**[Section: The Fatihah's Comprehensive Inclusion of the Principal Aims]**

Know that this surah comprises the principal lofty aims in the most complete manner, and contains them in the most perfect way.

It includes the introduction of the Worshipped, may He be blessed and exalted, through three names, to which all the Most Beautiful Names and the Sublime Attributes return and on which they depend. These names are: Allah, al-Rabb (the Lord), and al-Rahman (the Most Merciful). The surah is built upon divinity (al-ilahiyyah), lordship (al-rububiyyah), and mercy (al-rahmah). ﴿You alone do we worship﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] is founded on divinity; ﴿You alone do we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] is founded on lordship; and the request for guidance to the straight path is by the attribute of mercy. Praise (al-hamd) encompasses all three matters: He is praised in His divinity, His lordship, and His mercy. Commendation and glory are two perfections of His majesty.

It also includes the affirmation of the Return (al-ma'ad) and the recompense of the servants for their deeds, good and bad; the sole rule of the Lord, may He be exalted, over creation on that Day; and that His judgment is by justice. All of this falls under His words ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4].

It also includes the affirmation of prophethood (al-nubuwwat) from numerous aspects:

The first: His being the Lord of the worlds. It is not fitting for Him to leave His servants neglected and aimless, without informing them of what benefits them in their livelihood and their Return, and what harms them in both. To do so would be a diminishing of lordship and an attributing to the Lord, may He be exalted, of what does not befit Him. Whoever does this has not measured Him with His due measure.

The second: its being derived from the Name Allah, which means the One who is worshipped and adored. There is no way for the servants to know how to worship Him except through His messengers.

The third aspect is from His Name al-Rahman. His mercy prevents Him from neglecting His servants and from not informing them of what will bring them to the utmost of their perfection. Whoever gives the Name al-Rahman its due recognizes that it includes the sending of messengers and the sending down of books, far more than it includes the sending down of rain, the growing of pasture, and the bringing forth of grain. Mercy's requirement of that by which the life of hearts and spirits is attained is greater than its requirement of that by which the life of bodies and forms is attained. However, those who are veiled have only grasped from this Name the portion of beasts and animals, while people of understanding have grasped from it a matter beyond that.

The fourth aspect is from the mention of the Day of Religion (yawm al-din), for it is the Day on which God requites the servants for their deeds: He rewards them for good works and punishes them for sins and misdeeds. God would not punish anyone before the establishment of proof against him, and the proof was established through His messengers and His books. By them, reward and punishment are merited, and by them the market of the Day of Religion is set up, and the righteous are driven to bliss while the wicked are driven to Hellfire.

The fifth aspect is from His words ﴿You alone do we worship﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5]. What the Lord, may He be exalted, is worshipped with can only be that which He loves and is pleased with. Worship of Him, which is gratitude, love, and awe, is innate and intelligible to sound minds. However, the way of devotion and what He is worshipped with cannot be known except through His messengers and their explanation. This demonstrates that the sending of messengers is a matter firmly established in the intellects; it is impossible for the world to be left without it, just as it is impossible for it to be left without the Maker. Whoever denies the Messenger has denied the One who sent him and has not believed in Him. For this reason, God, glory be to Him, made disbelief in His messengers to be disbelief in Him.

**[Section]**

The first surah in the Qur'an is al-Fatihah, and it indicates that souls are created, in several respects:

- The first is His words, may He be exalted: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. Souls are part of the worlds, so He is their Lord.
- The second is His words, may He be exalted: ﴿You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help﴾. Souls worship Him and seek His help. If they were uncreated, they would be worshipped and sought for help.
- The third: they are in need of the guidance of their Originator and Lord, asking Him to guide them to His straight path.
- The fourth: they are bestowed upon and shown mercy, and they are also those upon whom wrath falls, who go astray and are wretched. This is the condition of the nurtured and the owned, not of the eternal, uncreated.

**[Section: The Conditions of Repentance]**

Since repentance (al-tawbah) is the servant's return to God and his departure from the path of those who earned wrath and of those who went astray, and this cannot be attained except by God's guidance to the straight path, and that guidance cannot be attained except by His help and by affirming His oneness (tawhid), the surah al-Fatihah encompasses all of this in the finest arrangement and includes it in the most eloquent manner. Whoever gives al-Fatihah its due, in knowledge, witnessing, state, and recognition, knows that its recitation as an act of servitude is not valid for him except with sincere repentance (al-tawbah al-nasuh). For complete guidance to the straight path does not exist alongside ignorance of sins, nor alongside persistence in them. The former is ignorance that contradicts knowledge of guidance, and the latter is error that contradicts one's aim and will. Therefore repentance is not valid except after knowing the sin, acknowledging it, and seeking deliverance from its evil consequences, first and last.

**[Benefit: The Human Being Has Two Faculties, a Theoretical Cognitive Faculty and a Volitional Practical Faculty]**

A person's complete felicity depends upon the perfecting of his two faculties: the cognitive and the volitional. The perfecting of the cognitive faculty comes only through knowing his Originator and Creator, knowing His names and attributes, knowing the path that leads to Him, knowing its hazards, knowing his own self, and knowing its defects. By these five kinds of knowledge the perfection of the cognitive faculty is attained, and the most knowledgeable of people are those who know them best and understand them most deeply. The perfecting of the volitional faculty is attained only by observing God's rights upon the servant and fulfilling them with sincerity, truthfulness, counsel, excellence, following, and witnessing His favor upon him, and witnessing his own shortcoming in fulfilling His right. He is ashamed to face Him with that service, knowing that it falls short of what He deserves, and far short of that. He has no way to perfect these two faculties except by His help, so he is compelled to ask that He guide him to the straight path that He guided His friends and elect to, and that He keep him from deviating from that path, either by corruption in his cognitive faculty, which leads him into error, or by corruption in his practical faculty, which brings upon him wrath.

Human perfection and felicity are not complete except by the totality of these matters, and the surah al-Fatihah includes them and arranges them in the most perfect order.

For His words ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ encompass the first foundation, which is knowledge of the Lord, may He be exalted, and knowledge of His names, attributes, and acts. The names mentioned in this surah are the roots of the Most Beautiful Names: they are the Name Allah, the Lord, and the Most Merciful. The Name Allah encompasses the attributes of divinity; the Name the Lord encompasses lordship; and the Name the Most Merciful encompasses the attributes of benevolence, generosity, and kindness. The meanings of His names revolve around these.

His words ﴿You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help﴾ encompass knowledge of the path that leads to Him, and that it is nothing but worshipping Him alone with what He loves and is pleased with, and seeking His help in that worship.

His words ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ show that the servant has no way to felicity except by remaining upright on the straight path, and that he has no way to uprightness except by his Lord's guidance to him, just as he has no way to worship Him except by His help. Therefore there is no way for him to remain upright on the path except by His guidance.

His words ﴿not of those who earned wrath, nor of those who went astray﴾ show the two extremes of deviation from the straight path: deviation toward either extreme is a deviation into error, which is corruption of knowledge and belief, and deviation toward the other extreme is a deviation into wrath, whose cause is corruption of intention and action.

Thus the beginning of the surah is mercy, its middle is guidance, and its end is blessing. A servant's share of blessing is according to his share of guidance, and his share of guidance is according to his share of mercy. So the whole matter returns to His blessing and His mercy. Blessing and mercy are necessary consequences of His lordship, so He is none but merciful and bountiful, and this is one of the requirements of His divinity. He is the true God, even if deniers deny Him and polytheists set up equals with Him. Whoever realizes the meanings of al-Fatihah in knowledge, recognition, action, and state has attained the greatest share of its perfection, and his servitude becomes the servitude of the elect, whose ranks are elevated above the common worshippers. And God is the One sought for help.

**[Section: His Guidance (ﷺ) Regarding Ruqyah for the One Stung, with al-Fatihah]**

Both al-Bukhari and Muslim transmitted in the Sahihayn, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "A group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) set out on a journey they undertook, until they stopped at a tribe among the tribes of the Arabs. They asked them for hospitality, but they refused to host them. Then the chief of that tribe was stung, so they tried every remedy for him, but nothing benefited him. Some of them said: 'If you went to those people who stopped here, perhaps some of them have something.' So they came to them and said: 'O company, our chief has been stung, and we have tried everything for him, but nothing has helped him. Does any of you have anything?' Some of them said: 'Yes, by God, I can perform ruqyah (healing by recitation). But we asked you for hospitality and you did not host us, so I will not perform ruqyah until you give us a reward.' So they agreed with them on a flock of sheep. He set off, spitting on him and reciting: 'All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.' It was as if he had been released from a tether. He got up and walked, with no ailment left in him." He said: "They paid them the reward they had agreed upon. Some of them said: 'Divide it.' The one who had performed the ruqyah said: 'Do not do so until we come to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and mention to him what happened, and see what he commands us.' So they came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and mentioned to him what had happened. He said: 'How did you know that it was a ruqyah?' Then he said: 'You have done right. Divide it, and set aside a share for me with you.'"

Ibn Majah also narrated in his Sunan, from the hadith of Ali, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The best medicine is the Qur'an."

It is well known that some speech has properties and beneficial effects that have been tested. So what is the presumption about the speech of the Lord of the worlds, whose excellence over all speech is like the excellence of God over His creation? It is the complete cure, the beneficial protection, the guiding light, and the all-encompassing mercy. Were it sent down upon a mountain, it would crumble from its greatness and majesty. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾ [al-Isra: 82].

The word "min" (of) here is for explaining the genus, not for partitioning. This is the more correct of the two opinions, as in His words: ﴿Allah has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Fath: 29]; and all of them are among those who believe and do righteous deeds. So what is the presumption about the Opening of the Book (fatihat al-kitab), for which there is no like in the Qur'an, nor in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms? It includes all the meanings of God's books, comprising the roots and summaries of the names of the Lord, may He be exalted: Allah, the Lord, and the Most Merciful. It affirms the Return (al-ma'ad), mentions the two tawhids (the oneness of lordship and the oneness of divinity), mentions the servant's need of the Lord, glory be to Him, in seeking help and seeking guidance, and singles Him out for that. It mentions the best of supplication absolutely, the most beneficial and most obligatory, and the thing that servants need most, which is guidance to His straight path. That guidance includes the complete knowledge of Him, His oneness, and His worship by doing what He commands, avoiding what He forbids, and remaining upright upon it until death. It also mentions the categories of creatures and their division into: one blessed with knowledge of the truth, acting upon it, loving it, and preferring it; one upon whom wrath falls for deviating from the truth after knowing it; and one who is astray for not knowing it.

These are the divisions of creation. Moreover, it includes the affirmation of predestination (al-qadar), of the Law (al-shar'), of the names and attributes, of the Return, and of prophethood; the purification of souls; the reform of hearts; the mention of God's justice and His benevolence; and the refutation of all the people of innovation (ahl al-bida') and falsehood. We have mentioned this in our large book Madarij al-Salikin (The Stages of the Travelers) in explaining it.

It is fitting for a surah with this much of its standing that one seeks healing through it from ailments, and that the one who was stung is treated by it with ruqyah.

In sum, what al-Fatihah contains of sincere devotion, praise of God, entrusting the whole matter to Him, seeking His help, relying upon Him, and asking Him for all the comprehensive blessings, which is the guidance that brings blessings and repels calamities, is among the greatest healing and sufficient remedies.

**[Chapter: The soul of the one who recites acts upon the soul of the one who is recited for, and by Allah's permission it repels the illness]**

It has been said that the place of the ruqyah (spiritual healing by recitation) within it is: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾. There is no doubt that these two phrases are among the most powerful components of this remedy, for they include, in their generality, entrusting, reliance, seeking refuge, seeking help, need and asking, and they combine the highest ends, which is worshipping the Lord alone, and the noblest means, which is seeking His help in worshipping Him, in a way that is not found in other phrases. There was a time for me in Mecca when I fell ill, and I lost both the physician and the medicine. So I used to treat myself with them: I would take a sip of Zamzam water and recite over it several times, then drink it, and I found complete recovery through that. Then I came to rely on this for many pains, and I benefited from it to the utmost degree.

**[Chapter: The effect of the ruqyah with al-Fatihah and other passages on treating venomous creatures]**

The effect of ruqyah with al-Fatihah and other passages in treating those with venom contains a wondrous secret. Venomous creatures act through the qualities of their wicked souls, as has preceded, and their weapon is the sting with which they bite. They do not bite until they become angry, and when they become angry the venom surges within them, and they discharge it through their instrument. God, glorified is He, has placed a remedy for every disease and an opposite for everything. The soul of the one who recites acts upon the soul of the one who is recited for, so there occurs between the two souls an action and a reaction, just as there occurs between the disease and the remedy. The soul of the one who recites, and its strength, become strengthened through the recitation against that disease, so it repels it by Allah's permission. The effect of medicines and diseases depends on action and reaction. Just as this occurs between the natural disease and the natural remedy, it also occurs between the spiritual disease and the spiritual remedy, and between the spiritual and the natural. In blowing (nafth) and spitting (tafl) there is a seeking of help through that moisture, air, and breath that directly accompanies the recitation, the remembrance and the supplication. For the recitation issues from the heart and mouth of the one who recites, so when some parts of his inner self accompany it, such as saliva, air and breath, it becomes more complete in effect, stronger in action and more penetrating. And through the combination of these there arises a effective quality similar to the quality that arises when medicines are compounded.

In sum: the soul of the one who recites confronts those wicked souls, and strengthens its quality with its own, and seeks help through the recitation and through blowing to remove that effect. Whenever the quality of the soul of the one who recites is stronger, the recitation is more complete. His seeking help through his blowing is like the seeking of help of those vile souls through their stinging.

There is another secret in blowing: it is among the things through which both good and evil spirits seek help. For this reason sorcerers do it, just as the people of faith do.

He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And from the evil of those who blow upon knots﴾ [al-Falaq: 4]. That is because the soul takes on the quality of anger and hostility, and sends out its breaths as arrows for itself, and supports them with blowing and spitting, which carries some saliva accompanying an effective quality. Sorcerers clearly seek help through blowing, even if it does not touch the body of the one bewitched. Rather, they blow over the knot and tie it, and speak the sorcery, and that acts upon the bewitched through the mediation of the lowly, evil spirits. The pure, righteous spirit confronts them with the quality of repelling, and with speaking the ruqyah, and it seeks help through blowing. Whichever of the two is stronger, the judgment belongs to it. The confrontation of spirits with one another, and their combat and their instruments, are of the same kind as the confrontation of bodies, and their combat and their instruments are alike. Indeed, the origin of combat and confrontation, for spirits and for bodies, is their instruments and their armies. But whoever is overcome by sense-perception does not perceive the effects of spirits, their actions and their reactions, because the authority of sense-perception has taken control over him, and he is distant from the world of spirits, its rulings and its actions.

The purpose is this: when the spirit is strong and takes on the meanings of al-Fatihah, and seeks help through blowing and spitting, it confronts the effect that arose from the wicked souls and removes it. And Allah knows best.

**[Chapter: On explaining that al-Fatihah includes the two healings, the healing of hearts and the healing of bodies]**

As for its including the healing of hearts: it includes it in the most complete manner. The basis of the ailments and sicknesses of hearts rests on two roots: corruption of knowledge and corruption of intention. From these two arise two deadly diseases, which are error (dalal) and anger (ghadab). Error is the result of corruption of knowledge, and anger is the result of corruption of intention. These two illnesses are the essence of all diseases of the heart. Guidance to the straight path therefore includes healing from the disease of error. For this reason, asking for this guidance is the most obligatory supplication upon every servant, and the most required of him every day and night in every prayer, because of the intensity of his need and his poverty toward the guidance sought. No other request can take its place.

Realizing ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5], in knowledge and recognition, and in action and state, includes healing from the disease of corruption of the heart and of intention. For the corruption of intention relates to ends and means. Whoever seeks an end that is cut off, perishing, and transient, and reaches it through every kind of means that lead to it, both kinds of his intention are corrupt. This is the case of everyone whose ultimate goal is other than God and His worship, such as the polytheists, the followers of desires, who have no end beyond them, and the people of leadership who follow after maintaining their leadership by any means, whether true or false. When the truth comes opposing their path of leadership, they crush it and trample it under their feet. If they are unable to do so, they repel it like an aggressor. If they are unable to do that, they imprison it on the road and turn aside from it to another path, while they are prepared to repel it as far as they can. When they find no escape from it, they give it the coinage and the sermon and remove it from control, judgment and execution. If the truth comes to support them, and they have a stake in it, they go about with it and parade it, and come to it submissively, not because it is true, but because it agrees with their aim and desires and serves their victory: ﴿And when they are called to God and His Messenger, that he may judge between them, behold, a party of them turn away. But if the right were theirs, they would come to him in submission. Is there a disease in their hearts, or do they have doubt, or do they fear that God and His Messenger will be unjust to them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Nur: 48].

The purpose is this: the intention of these people is corrupt in their ends and their means. When the ends they sought are nullified, dissolved and perished, they end up with the greatest loss and regrets. They are the most remorseful and grieving of people when the truth is established and falsehood is nullified, and the bonds of connection that were between them are cut, and they become certain that they are cut off from the caravan of success and felicity. This appears often in this world, and it appears even more strongly at the time of departing from it and arriving before God. It becomes most evident and certain in the barzakh (intermediate state), and it is fully unveiled on the Day of Meeting, when realities are made manifest, the people of truth prosper and the people of falsehood lose, and they know that they were liars, and were deceived and deluded. Alas for knowledge there that does not benefit its possessor, and for certainty that does not save the one who holds it.

Likewise, whoever seeks the highest end and the loftiest goal, but does not reach it through the means that lead to it and to Him, rather reaches for it through a means he thinks leads to it, while it is one of the greatest obstacles away from it, his condition is also like the condition of the first. Both are corrupt of intention. There is no healing from this disease except through the remedy of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5].

For this remedy is compounded of six components: (1) the worship of God alone and no other; (2) by His command and His law; (3) not by desire; (4) nor by the opinions of men, their conventions, their customs and their ideas; (5) by seeking help in His worship through Him; (6) not by the servant's own self, his strength, or his power, nor by anything other than Him.

These are the components of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5]. When the skilled physician who knows the disease compounds them, and the patient uses them, complete healing is achieved through them. Whatever lacks of healing is due to the absence of one of its components, or two, or more.

Then the heart is subject to two great diseases, which, if the servant does not remedy them, will inevitably lead it to ruin: they are ostentation (riya') and arrogance (kibr). The remedy for ostentation is ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5], and the remedy for arrogance is ﴿You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5].

I often heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may God sanctify his soul, say: ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] repels ostentation, and ﴿and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] repels haughtiness.

When one is healed from the disease of ostentation through ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5], and from the disease of haughtiness and self-admiration through ﴿You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5], and from the disease of error and ignorance through ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fatihah: 6], he is healed of his diseases and ailments, walks in the garments of well-being, has his blessing completed, and becomes one of those upon whom favour is bestowed, not those who have earned anger, who are the people of corrupt intention who recognized the truth and turned away from it, nor those who went astray, who are the people of corrupt knowledge, who were ignorant of the truth and did not recognize it.

It is right that a surah that includes these two healings should be used as a means of healing from every disease. For this reason, since it includes this healing, which is the greater of the two healings, obtaining the lesser healing through it is even more fitting, as we will explain. Nothing is more healing for hearts that have understood from God and His speech, and grasped from Him a special understanding, which He has singled them out with from the meaning of this surah.

God willing, we will explain its inclusion of refutation of all the people of innovation, with the clearest explanation and the best methods.

**[Its inclusion of the healing of bodies]**

As for its inclusion of the healing of bodies, we will mention from it what the Sunnah has brought, what the principles of medicine attest to, and what experience has confirmed.

As for what the Sunnah indicates: in the Sahih, from the hadith of Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: "Some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ passed by a tribe of the Arabs, but they did not host them nor entertain them. Then the chief of that tribe was stung. They came to them and said: 'Do you have any ruqyah, or is there among you anyone who performs ruqyah?' They said: 'Yes, but you did not host us, so we will not do it until you give us a reward.' So they gave them a flock of sheep as payment. Then a man among us began reciting over him with the Opening of the Book (al-Fatihah). He got up as though nothing had been wrong with him. We said: 'Do not hurry until we come to the Prophet ﷺ.' So we came to him and told him about that. He said: 'How did you know it was a ruqyah? Eat, and cast lots with me for a share.'"

This hadith includes the healing of this stung man through the recitation of al-Fatihah over him, so it sufficed him from medicine, and it may have achieved for his healing what medicine had not achieved.

This is despite the fact that the place was unreceptive, either because those people were not Muslims, or because they were stingy and base. How much more so when the place is receptive.

**[Chapter]**

As for what the principles of medicine testify to in this: know that stinging occurs from creatures with venom and poison, which are beings with wicked souls that take on a quality of anger, which stirs within them a fiery poisonousness, through which stinging takes place. These vary according to the variation in the wickedness, strength and quality of those souls. When their wicked souls take on that angry quality, it produces in them a poisonous nature, and they find ease and pleasure in discharging it into a receptive place, just as a wicked person among people finds ease and pleasure in delivering his evil to one he can reach. Many people cannot find peace in a day in which they do not harm anyone of their kind, and they feel within themselves a distress from carrying that poisonousness and evil, until they discharge it on others, whereupon their groaning cools and their soul is calmed. This resembles what befalls one whose desire for intercourse is intensified, so his temper worsens and his soul becomes heavy until he fulfils his need. The former is in the strength of desire, and the latter is in the strength of anger.

وقد أقام الله تعالى بحكمته السلطانَ (الحاكمَ والسلطةَ) رادعًا لهذه النفوس الغضبية، فلولاه لفسدت الأرض وخربت. ﴿وَلَوْلا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النّاسَ بَعْضَهم بِبَعْضٍ لَفَسَدَتِ الأرْضُ ولَكِنَّ اللَّهَ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلى العالَمِينَ﴾ [البقرة: ٢٥١] (﴿Had God not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would surely have been corrupted; but God is bounteous to the worlds.﴾). وأباح الله بلطفه ورحمته لهذه النفوس من الأزواج وملك اليمين ما يكسر حدّتها.

والمقصود أن هذه النفوس الغضبية إذا اتصلت بالمحل القابل أثّرت فيه، ومنها ما يؤثر في المحل بمجرد مقابلته له، وإن لم يمسّه، فمنها ما يطمس البصر، ويُسقط الحبل.

ومن هذا نظرُ العائن، فإنه إذا وقع بصره على المعين حدثت في نفسه كيفيةٌ سُمِّيَّةٌ أثّرت في المعين بحسب عدم استعداده، وكونه أعزلَ من السلاح، وبحسب قوة تلك النفس. وكثير من هذه النفوس يؤثر في المعين إذا وُصف له، فتتكيف نفسه وتقابله على البُعد فيتأثر به. ومنكر هذا ليس معدودًا من بني آدم إلا بالصورة والشكل. فإذا قابلت النفسُ الزكيةُ العلويةُ الشريفةُ التي فيها غضبٌ وحميةٌ للحق هذه النفوسَ الخبيثةَ السُّمِّيَّةَ، وتكيفت بحقائق الفاتحة وأسرارها ومعانيها، وما تضمنته من التوحيد والتوكل، والثناء على الله، وذكرِ أصول أسمائه الحسنى، وذكرِ اسمه الذي ما ذُكر على شر إلا أزاله ومحقه، ولا على خير إلا نمّاه وزاده، دفعت هذه النفسُ بما تكيفت به من ذلك أثرَ تلك النفس الخبيثة الشيطانية، فحصل البُرء، فإن مبنى الشفاء والبُرء على دفع الضد بضده، وحفظ الشيء بمثله، فالصحةُ تُحفظ بالمثل، والمرضُ يُدفع بالضد. أسبابٌ ربطها بمسبباتها الحكيمُ العليمُ خلقًا وأمرًا، ولا يتم هذا إلا بقوةٍ من النفس الفاعلة، وقبولٍ من الطبيعة المنفعلة. فلو لم تنفعل نفسُ الملدوغ لقبول الرقية، ولم تقوَ نفسُ الراقي على التأثير، لم يحصل البُرء.

فهنا أمورٌ ثلاثة: موافقةُ الدواء للداء، وبذلُ الطبيب له، وقبولُ طبيعة العليل. فمتى تخلّف واحدٌ منها لم يحصل الشفاء، وإذا اجتمعت حصل الشفاء ولا بد بإذن الله سبحانه وتعالى.

ومن عرف هذا كما ينبغي تبيّن له أسرارُ الرُّقى، وميّز بين النافع منها وغيره، ورقى الداء بما يناسبه من الرُّقى، وتبيّن له أن الرُّقية براقيها وقبولِ المحل، كما أن السيف بضاربه مع قبول المحل للقطع. وهذه إشارة مطلعة على ما وراءها لمن دقّ نظرُه، وحسُن تأملُه. والله أعلم.

وأما شهادة التجارب بذلك فهي أكثر من أن تُذكر، وذلك في كل زمان. وقد جرّبتُ أنا من ذلك في نفسي وفي غيري أمورًا عجيبة، ولا سيما مدةَ المقام بمكة، فإنه كان يعرض لي آلامٌ مُزعجة، بحيث تكاد تقطع الحركة مني، وذلك في أثناء الطواف وغيره، فأبادر إلى قراءة الفاتحة (al-Fatiha، فاتحة الكتاب، أي السورة الأولى)، وأمسح بها على محل الألم، فكأنه حصاةٌ تسقط. جربت ذلك مرارًا عديدة. وكنت آخذ قدحًا من ماء زمزم فأقرأ عليه الفاتحة مرارًا، فأشربه فأجد به من النفع والقوة ما لم أعهد مثله في الدواء، والأمر أعظم من ذلك، ولكن بحسب قوة الإيمان، وصحة اليقين. والله المستعان.

[فصلٌ: في اشتمال الفاتحة على الردّ على جميع المبطلين من أهل الملل والنحل، والردّ على أهل البدع والضلال من هذه الأمة]

وهذا يُعلم بطريقين: مجمَلٍ ومفصّلٍ.

أما المجمَل: فهو أن الصراط المستقيم متضمنٌ معرفةَ الحق، وإيثارَه، وتقديمَه على غيره، ومحبتَه والانقيادَ له، والدعوةَ إليه، وجهادَ أعدائه بحسب الإمكان.

والحقّ: هو ما كان عليه رسولُ الله (ﷺ) وأصحابُه، وما جاء به علمًا وعملًا، في باب صفات الرب سبحانه، وأسمائه وتوحيده، وأمره ونهيه، ووعده ووعيده، وفي حقائق الإيمان التي هي منازلُ السائرين إلى الله تعالى. وكلُّ ذلك مُسلَّمٌ إلى رسول الله (ﷺ)، دون آراء الرجال وأوضاعهم وأفكارهم واصطلاحاتهم.

فكلُّ علمٍ أو عملٍ أو حقيقةٍ، أو حالٍ أو مقامٍ خرج من مشكاة نبوّته، وعليه السكّة المحمدية، بحيث يكون من ضرب المدينة، فهو من الصراط المستقيم. وما لم يكن كذلك فهو من صراط أهل الغضب والضلال. فما ثَمّ خروجٌ عن هذه الطرق الثلاث: طريقِ الرسول (ﷺ) وما جاء به، وطريقِ أهل الغضب، وهي طريق مَن عرف الحق وعاندَه، وطريقِ أهل الضلال، وهي طريق مَن أضلّه الله عنه. ولهذا قال عبدُ الله بنُ عباسٍ وجابرُ بنُ عبد الله رضي الله عنهم: "الصراط المستقيم: هو الإسلام"، وقال عبدُ الله بنُ مسعودٍ وعليُّ بنُ أبي طالبٍ رضي الله عنهما: "هو القرآن"، وفيه حديثٌ مرفوعٌ في الترمذي وغيره. وقال سهلُ بنُ عبد الله: "طريقُ السنة والجماعة" (Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah، أهل السنة والجماعة)، وقال بكرُ بنُ عبد الله المزنيُّ: "طريقُ رسول الله (ﷺ)".

ولا رَيْب أنّ ما كان عليه رسولُ الله (ﷺ) وأصحابُه علمًا وعملًا، وهو معرفةُ الحقّ وتقديمُه، وإيثارُه على غيره، فهو الصراط المستقيم.

وكلُّ هذه الأقوال المتقدمة دالةٌ عليه جامعةٌ له.

فبهذا الطريق المجمَل يُعلم أن كلَّ ما خالفه فباطلٌ، وهو من صراط الأمتين: الأمةِ الغضبية، وأمةِ أهل الضلال.

[فصل]

وأما المفصَّل: فبمعرفة المذاهب الباطلة، واشتمالِ كلمات الفاتحة على إبطالها. فنقول:

الناسُ قسمان: مُقِرٌّ بالحق تعالى، وجاحدٌ له، فتضمنت الفاتحة إثباتَ الخالق تعالى، والردَّ على مَن جحده، بإثبات ربوبيته تعالى للعالمين.

وتأمّلْ حالَ العالَم كلِّه، علويِّه وسفليِّه، بجميع أجزائه: تجده شاهدًا بإثبات صانعه وفاطره ومليكه. فإنكارُ صانعه وجحدُه في العقول والفطر بمنزلة إنكار العِلم وجحدِه، لا فرقَ بينهما، بل دلالةُ الخالق على المخلوق، والفعّالِ على الفعل، والصانعِ على أحوال المصنوع عند العقول الزكية المشرقة العلوية، والفطر الصحيحة أظهرُ من العكس.

فالعارفون أربابُ البصائر يستدلّون بالله على أفعاله وصُنعه، إذا استدلّ الناسُ بصُنعه وأفعاله عليه. ولا ريبَ أنهما طريقان صحيحان، كلٌّ منهما حق، والقرآن مشتملٌ عليهما.

فأما الاستدلالُ بالصنعة فكثير، وأما الاستدلالُ بالصانع فله شأنٌ، وهو الذي أشارت إليه الرسلُ بقولهم لأممهم: ﴿أفِي اللَّهِ شَكٌّ﴾ [إبراهيم: ١٠] (﴿Is there doubt about God?﴾)، أي: أيُشَكُّ في الله حتى يُطلب إقامةُ الدليل على وجوده؟ وأيُّ دليلٍ أصحُّ وأظهرُ من هذا المدلول؟ فكيف يُستدلّ على الأظهر بالأخفى؟ ثم نبّهوا على الدليل بقولهم: ﴿فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ [الأنعام: ١٤] (﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾).

وسمعتُ شيخَ الإسلام تقيَّ الدين ابنَ تيمية قدّس الله روحَه يقول: كيف يُطلب الدليلُ على مَن هو دليلٌ على كل شيء؟ وكان كثيرًا ما يتمثّل بهذا البيت:

ولَيْسَ يَصِحُّ في الأذْهانِ شَيْءٌ ∗∗∗ إذا احْتاجَ النَّهارُ إلى دَلِيلِ

(Nothing can be established in minds / when daylight needs a proof.)

ومعلومٌ أن وجودَ الرب تعالى أظهرُ للعقول والفطر من وجود النهار، ومَن لم يرَ ذلك في عقله وفطرته فلْيَتّهمْهما.

وإذا بطل قولُ هؤلاء بطل قولُ أهل الإلحاد، القائلين بوحدة الوجود، وأنه ما ثَمّ وجودٌ قديمٌ خالقٌ ووجودٌ حادثٌ مخلوقٌ، بل وجودُ هذا العالم هو عينُ وجود الله، وهو حقيقةُ وجود هذا العالم. فليس عند القوم ربٌّ وعبدٌ، ولا مالكٌ ومملوكٌ، ولا راحمٌ ومرحومٌ، ولا عابدٌ ومعبودٌ، ولا مستعينٌ ومستعانٌ به، ولا هادٍ ولا مهديٌّ، ولا مُنعِمٌ ولا مُنعَمٌ عليه، ولا غضبانُ ومغضوبٌ عليه. بل الربُّ هو نفسُ العبد وحقيقتُه، والمالكُ هو عينُ المملوك، والراحمُ هو عينُ المرحوم، والعابدُ هو نفسُ المعبود. وإنما التغايرُ أمرٌ اعتباريٌّ بحسب مظاهر الذات وتجلّياتها، فتظهر تارةً في صورة معبود، كما ظهرت في صورة فرعون، وفي صورة عبدٍ، كما ظهرت في صورة العبيد، وفي صورة هادٍ، كما في صورة الأنبياء والرسل والعلماء. والكلُّ من عينٍ واحدة، بل هو العينُ الواحدة، فحقيقةُ العابد ووجودُه أو أنّيّتُه: هي حقيقةُ المعبود ووجودُه وأنّيّتُه.

والفاتحةُ من أولها إلى آخرها تبيّن بطلانَ قولِ هؤلاء الملاحدة وضلالَهم.

[فصلٌ: في تضمّنها الردَّ على الجهميّة (Jahmiyya، أتباع الجهم بن صفوان) معطّلةِ الصفات]

وذلك من وجوه:

أحدُها: من قوله: ﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ﴾ [الفاتحة: ٢] (﴿Praise belongs to God﴾)، فإنّ إثبات الحمد الكامل له يقتضي ثبوتَ كلِّ ما يُحمد عليه، من صفات كماله، ونعوت جلاله. إذ مَن عُدم صفاتِ الكمال فليس بمحمودٍ على الإطلاق، وغايتُه أنه محمودٌ من وجهٍ دون وجه، ولا يكون محمودًا بكل وجه، وبكل اعتبار، بجميع أنواع الحمد، إلا مَن استولى على صفات الكمال جميعِها، فلو عُدم منها صفةٌ واحدةٌ لنقص من حمده بحسبها.

وكذلك في إثبات صفة الرحمة له ما يتضمن إثبات الصفات التي تستلزمها من الحياة، والإرادة والقدرة، والسمع والبصر، وغيرها.

وكذلك صفةُ الربوبية تستلزم جميعَ صفات الفعل، وصفةُ الإلهية تستلزم جميعَ أوصاف الكمال ذاتًا وأفعالًا، كما تقدّم بيانُه.

فكونُه محمودًا، إلهًا ربًّا، رحمانًا رحيمًا، مَلكًا معبودًا، مستعانًا، هاديًا مُنعِمًا، يرضى ويغضب، مع نفيِ قيامِ الصفات به، جمعٌ بين النقيضين، وهو من أمحلِ المحال.

وهذه الطريقُ تتضمن إثباتَ الصفات الخبرية من وجهين:

أحدُهما: أنها من لوازم كماله المطلق، فإن استواءَه على عرشه من لوازم علوِّه، ونزولَه كلَّ ليلةٍ إلى سماء الدنيا في نصف الليل الثاني من لوازم رحمته وربوبيته، وهكذا سائرُ الصفات الخبرية.

الوجه الثاني: أن السمعَ ورد بها، ثناءً على الله ومدحًا له، وتعرّفًا منه إلى عباده بها، فجحدُها وتحريفُها عمّا دلّت عليه، وعمّا أُريد بها، مناقضٌ لما جاءت به. فلك أن تستدل بطريق السمع على أنها كمالٌ، وأن تستدل بالعقل كما تقدّم.

[فصلٌ: في تضمّنها للردّ على الجبرية (Jabriyya، القائلين بالجبر)]

وذلك من وجوه:

أحدُها: من إثبات عمومِ حمده سبحانه، فإنه يقتضي أن لا يعاقب عبيدَه على ما لا قدرةَ لهم عليه، ولا هو من فعلهم، بل هو بمنزلة ألوانهم، وطولِهم وقصرِهم، بل هو يعاقبهم على نفس فعلِه بهم، فهو الفاعلُ لقبائحهم في الحقيقة، وهو المعاقِبُ لهم عليها. فحمدُه عليها يأبى ذلك أشدَّ الإباء، وينفيه أعظمَ النفي، فتعالى مَن له الحمدُ كلُّه عن ذلك علوًّا كبيرًا. بل إنما يعاقبهم على نفس أفعالهم التي فعلوها حقيقةً، فهي أفعالُهم لا أفعالُه، وإنما أفعالُه العدلُ، والإحسانُ والخيراتُ.

الوجهُ الثاني: إثباتُ رحمته ورحمانيّته ينفي ذلك، إذ لا يُمكن اجتماعُ هذين الأمرين قطُّ: أن يكون رحمانًا رحيمًا ويعاقبَ العبدَ على ما لا قدرةَ له عليه، ولا هو من فعله، بل يكلّفه ما لا يُطيقه، ولا له عليه قدرةٌ ألبتّة، ثم يعاقبه عليه. وهل هذا إلا ضدُّ الرحمة، ونقضٌ لها وإبطالٌ؟ وهل يصحّ في معقول أحدٍ اجتماعُ ذلك والرحمةِ التامّةِ الكاملةِ في ذاتٍ واحدة؟

**Part 4 of 8 of the Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 1, Verse 1**

The third aspect: the affirmation of worship and seeking help for them, and their attribution to them through their saying "We worship, and We seek help." This attribution is real, not metaphorical. God cannot be described as performing worship and seeking help, which are actions of His servants. Rather, the servant in truth is the one who worships and seeks help, and God is the One who is worshipped and sought for help.

[Section: On how the verse contains a refutation of those who hold that the cause acts by its essence (al-qa'ilin bil-muwjab bil-dhat), without choice or will, and on the explanation that He, glory be to Him, is an agent who chooses (fa'il mukhtar).]

This is through several aspects:

First: from the affirmation of His praise. How can one be praised for what does not choose its existence, and is not by its own will and action? Is it valid to praise water for its effects and necessary consequences, or fire and iron and other things, by reason or by natural disposition? Praise is only due to an agent who chooses by his power and will for his praiseworthy actions. This is what is valid in intellects and natural dispositions, and nothing else. Whoever opposes this has left natural disposition and reason. Yet he does not deny his departure from the revealed laws and the prophethoods; rather he boasts of that and regards it as a source of pride.

Second: the affirmation of His lordship (rububiyyah) requires that He act by His will, choice, governance and power. Neither intellect nor natural disposition holds that the sun is lord because of its light, or water because of its cooling, or plants because they come from it. Nor is anything ever a lord over what has no power over it at all. Is this not a clear rejection of lordship itself?

Thus these people spoke in riddles to the ignorant, and spoke plainly to those of understanding.

Third: the affirmation of His ownership (mulk). It is not conceivable that ownership belongs to one who has no choice, no action and no will. Rather, every owned thing has will, choice and action more complete and perfect than this owner. ﴿Is He who creates like one who creates not? Will you not then take heed?﴾ [al-Nahl: 17].

Fourth: from His being the One sought for help. Seeking help from one who has no choice, no will and no power is impossible.

Fifth: from His being the One asked to guide His servants. Asking one who has no choice is impossible. The same applies to His being the Bestower of blessings.

[Section: On how the verse contains a refutation of those who deny that His knowledge encompasses particulars (juz'iyyat).]

This is through several aspects:

First: the perfection of His praise. How can one deserve praise who knows nothing of the world, its conditions and its details, nor the number of the spheres, nor the number of the stars, nor who obeys Him among those who disobey, nor who calls upon Him among those who do not?

Second: it is impossible for Him to be a god (ilah) and a lord (rabb) without knowing. The god who is worshipped and the lord who governs must know their worshipper and know his condition.

Third: from the affirmation of His mercy. It is impossible that He should show mercy to one He does not know.

Fourth: the affirmation of His ownership. A king who does not know any one of his subjects at all, nor anything of the conditions of his kingdom at all, is in no way a king.

Fifth: His being the One sought for help.

Sixth: His being the One asked to guide the one who asks Him and to answer him.

Seventh: His being the Guide.

Eighth: His being the Bestower of blessings.

Ninth: His being angry with whoever opposes Him.

Tenth: His being the Recompenser who requites people for their deeds on the Day of Judgment.

So denying His knowledge of particulars nullifies all of this.

[Section: On how the verse contains a refutation of those who deny the prophethoods (nubuwwat).]

This is through several aspects:

First: the affirmation of His complete praise. This requires the perfection of His wisdom, and that He not create His creation in vain, nor leave them neglected, neither commanded nor forbidden. For this reason God has declared Himself free of this in more than one place in His Book, and He informed us that whoever denies the messengership and prophethood, and denies that anything could be revealed to a human being, has not known Him with true knowledge, nor magnified Him as He deserves, nor measured Him with His true measure. Rather, he attributes to Him what is not fitting for Him, and what His praise and glory reject.

Whoever gives praise its due, in knowledge, understanding and insight, derives from it "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God" just as he derives from it "I bear witness that there is no god but God." He knows with certainty that the suspension of prophethoods (ta'til al-nubuwwat) contradicts praise, just as the negation of the attributes of perfection does, and just as the affirmation of partners and equals does.

Second: His divinity (ilahiyyah), and His being a god. This entails His being worshipped and obeyed. There is no way to know what He is to be worshipped with and obeyed with except through His messengers.

Third: His being Lord. Lordship requires commanding and forbidding His servants, rewarding the one who does good with His goodness, and requiting the one who does evil with His evil. This is the reality of lordship, and it is not complete except through messengership and prophethood.

Fourth: His being the All-Merciful, the Most Merciful. The perfection of His mercy requires that He make His servants know Himself and His attributes, guide them to what brings them near to Him and distances them from Him, reward them for their obedience, and recompense them with the best. This is not complete except through messengership and prophethood. So His mercy requires them.

Fifth: His ownership. Ownership requires disposal by speech, just as ownership requires disposal by action. The king is the one who disposes by His command and word, so His orders and decrees are executed wherever He wills. The owner is the one who disposes of his property by his action. God has the kingdom (al-mulk) and the ownership (al-milk), so He disposes of His creation by word and by action.

His disposal by His word is of two kinds: disposal by His cosmic words (kalimatuhu al-kawniyyah), and disposal by His religious words (kalimatuhu al-diniyyah). The perfection of His kingship is by both.

So sending the messengers is required by the perfection of His kingship and authority. This is the kingship that is intelligible in people's natural dispositions and intellects. Every king who has no messengers to disperse throughout the regions of his kingdom is not truly a king.

By this path the existence of His angels is known, and that belief in them is a necessary consequence of belief in His kingship, for they are the messengers of God among His creation and His command.

Sixth: the establishment of the Day of Judgment (yawm al-din), which is the Day of Recompense on which God requites His servants for their deeds, good and evil. This is not possible except after the establishment of messengership and prophethood, and the establishment of the proof by which the obedient and the disobedient are judged.

Seventh: His being worshipped. He is worshipped only by what He loves and is pleased with. There is no way for creatures to know what He loves and is pleased with except through His messengers. So denying His messengers is denying that He is worthy of worship.

Eighth: His being the Guide to the straight path (al-sirat al-mustaqim), which is knowing the truth and acting upon it. It is the nearest of the paths that lead to the sought goal, for the straight line is the shortest line connecting two points. This cannot be known except through the messengers. So its dependence upon the messengers is necessary, and more important than the dependence of the sensory path upon the soundness of the senses.

Ninth: His being the Bestower of blessings upon the people of guidance to the straight path. His bestowing upon them was completed only by sending the messengers to them, and by making them receptive to messengership and responsive to His call. By this He reminds them of His favour upon them and His blessing in His Book.

Tenth: the division of His creation into those upon whom blessings are bestowed, those upon whom wrath is incurred, and those who go astray. This division is necessary according to their division in knowing the truth and acting upon it: into one who knows it and acts by its requirements, who are the people of blessing; one who knows it but opposes it stubbornly, who are the people of wrath; and one who is ignorant of it, who are the ones who go astray. This division arose only after the sending of the messengers. Had there been no messengers, they would have been one community. So their division into these categories is impossible without messengership, and this division is necessary in actual fact. Therefore messengership is necessary.

It has become clear to you, by this path and the one before it, how the verse contains a refutation of whoever denies the bodily resurrection (al-ma'ad al-jusmani) and the resurrection of bodies. You have known that it necessarily requires the establishment of reward and punishment, command and prohibition. This is the truth for which the heavens and the earth were created, and for which the present world and the Hereafter exist. It is the requirement of creation and command, and to deny it is to deny both.

[Section: When the prophethoods and messengership are established, the attribute of speech (al-takallum) and of causing to speak (al-taklim) is established.]

The reality of messengership is conveying the speech of the sender. If there is no speech, what does the messenger convey? Indeed, how can his being a messenger be conceived? For this reason more than one of the early generations (al-salaf) said: whoever denies that God speaks, or that the Qur'an is His speech, has denied the messengership of Muhammad (ﷺ), indeed the messengership of all the messengers, whose reality is conveying the speech of God, blessed and exalted. For this reason, those who denied his messengership (ﷺ) said about the Qur'an: ﴿This is nothing but magic transmitted; this is nothing but the word of a human being﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 24-25]. They meant only the audible Qur'an that was conveyed to them and by which they were warned.

Whoever says that God has not spoken it has come to resemble their saying. ﴿Exalted is God above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation﴾.

[Section: On how the verse contains a refutation of whoever holds that the world is eternal (qidam al-'alam).]

This is through several aspects:

First: the affirmation of His praise. This requires the establishment of His acts, especially since most of the substance of praise in the Qur'an, or all of it, concerns acts. So it is here too: He praised Himself for His lordship, which includes His chosen acts. It is impossible for the act to be simultaneous with its agent. This is rejected by every sound intellect and upright natural disposition. The act is necessarily posterior to its agent.

Moreover, it is the object of will, influence and power, and its object cannot be eternal at all.

Second: the affirmation of His lordship over the worlds (al-'alamin). The reasoning mentioned above applies. The world is everything other than Him. It is established that everything other than Him is governed (marbub), and what is governed is necessarily created, and everything created is originated (hadith) after it was not. So His lordship over everything other than Him entails His priority over it and the originatedness of the governed. It cannot be conceived that the world is eternal while being governed forever. The eternal is self-sufficient by its eternity and needs no agent; while everything governed is poor in its essence. Nothing governed is self-sufficient, nor is there an eternal among them.

Third: the affirmation of His unity (tawhid). This requires that none of the world share with Him in the properties of lordship. Power is among the properties of lordship. So unity necessarily negates its being attributed to another, just as it negates the attribution of lordship and divinity to another.

[Section: On how this surah includes the three kinds of tawhid upon which all the messengers agreed, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them.]

Tawhid is of two kinds: one concerning knowledge and belief, and one concerning will and intention. The first is called scientific tawhid (al-tawhid al-'ilmi), and the second is called volitional, intentional tawhid (al-tawhid al-qasdi al-iradi). The first is related to information and knowledge, and the second to intention and will. This second kind is itself of two kinds: tawhid in lordship (tawhid al-rububiyyah), and tawhid in divinity (tawhid al-ilahiyyah). These are three kinds.

As for scientific tawhid, its foundation is the affirmation of the attributes of perfection, the negation of likeness and similitude, and the declaration of His transcendence above defects and deficiencies. This is indicated by two things: a general (mujmal) and a detailed (mufassal) indication.

The general one is the affirmation of praise to Him, glory be to Him. The detailed one is the mention of the attributes of divinity, lordship, mercy and kingship. On these four rests the foundation of the names and attributes.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 1, verse 1 (part 5 of 8):

As for the inclusion of the meaning of praise (hamd) in this: praise (hamd) includes commending the one who is praised for the attributes of his perfection and the descriptions of his majesty, together with loving him, being pleased with him, and submitting to him. Therefore one who denies the attributes of the one praised is not a praiser, nor is one who turns away from loving him and submitting to him. The more the attributes of perfection of the one praised are, the more complete his praise is, and the more his praise is diminished according to what is diminished of the attributes of his perfection. For this reason, all praise belongs to Allah, a praise that no one other than Him can enumerate, because of the perfection and multiplicity of His attributes. And for this reason no one of His creation can enumerate His praise, because of the attributes of perfection and descriptions of majesty that He has, which no one other than Him can enumerate. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, censured the gods of the disbelievers and found fault with them by denying them the attributes of perfection. He found fault with them for not hearing, not seeing, not speaking, not guiding, and not benefiting or harming. This is the attribute of the god of the Jahmiyyah, with which He found fault in the idols, and they attributed it to Him. Exalted is Allah far above what the wrongdoers and deniers say, a great exaltation. Allah, exalted is He, said, relating about His friend Ibrahim, peace be upon him, in his argument with his father: ﴿O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and does not avail you at all?﴾ [Maryam: 42]. If the god of Ibrahim were of this description and standing, Azar would have said to him: "And you have a god of this standing, so how do you object to me?" But he, despite his polytheism, was more knowing of Allah than the Jahmiyyah. Likewise, the disbelievers of Quraysh, despite their polytheism, acknowledged the attributes of the Creator, glorified is He, and His elevation above His creation. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the people of Musa made, after him, from their ornaments a calf, a body having a lowing. Did they not see that it could not speak to them or guide them to a way? They took it, and they were wrongdoers.﴾ [al-A'raf: 148]. If the God of creation, glorified is He, were like that, there would be no denunciation of them in this, nor evidence against the divinity of that by this.
If it is said: Allah, exalted is He, does not speak to His servants.
It is said: Rather, He has spoken to them. Among them is one whom Allah spoke to from behind a veil, speaking to him directly without an intermediary, like Musa. Among them is one to whom Allah spoke through His angelic messenger, and they are the prophets. And Allah spoke to all people through the tongues of His messengers. He sent down to them His speech, which His messengers conveyed from Him, and they said to them: "This is the speech of Allah with which He spoke, and He commanded us to convey it to you." From here the Salaf said: Whoever denies that Allah is a speaker has denied the message of all the messengers, because its reality is conveying His speech with which He spoke to His servants. So if His speech is negated, the message is negated. Allah, exalted is He, said in Surah Ta-Ha, concerning the Samiri: ﴿So he brought out for them a calf, a body having a lowing, and they said: This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot. Do they not see that it does not return to them a word, and it does not possess for them any harm or benefit?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 88]. Raj' al-qawl is speaking and causing speech. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah presents an example: two men, one of them mute, unable to do anything, and he is a burden upon his master; wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who orders justice while he is on a straight path?﴾ [al-Nahl: 76]. So He made the negation of the attribute of speech a cause for the invalidity of divinity. This is a matter known by natural disposition, sound intellects and the heavenly scriptures: that one who lacks the attributes of perfection is not a god, nor a governor, nor a lord; rather he is blameworthy, faulty, deficient, and has no praise, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Praise in this world and the Hereafter belongs only to the one who has the attributes of perfection and descriptions of majesty, for which he deserves praise. For this reason the Salaf named the books they composed on the Sunnah and the affirmation of the attributes of the Lord, His elevation above His creation, His speech and His causing speech, "Tawhid." This is because negating that, denying it and disbelieving in it is denial of the Creator and rejection of Him. Rather, His tawhid is the affirmation of the attributes of His perfection and His transcendence above likeness and deficiencies. The Mu'attilah made the rejection of the attributes and the divesting of the Creator from them "tawhid," and they made the affirmation of them for Allah "tashbih" (anthropomorphism), "tajsim" (corporealization) and "tarkib" (composition). Thus they named falsehood with the name of truth, to make it attractive, and an adornment with which they pass it off, and they named truth with the name of falsehood, to make people repelled from it. Most people are with the outward appearance of the coin, having none of the assayers' ability to test it. ﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the guided; and whomever He leaves astray, you will not find for him a guiding ally.﴾ [al-Kahf: 17]. The one who is praised is not praised for non-existence and silence at all, except when it is a negation of faults and deficiencies that includes the affirmation of their opposites from the perfections of affirmation. Otherwise, pure negation contains no praise, no commendation, and no perfection.
Likewise, His praising Himself for the absence of having a child includes the perfection of His self-sufficiency, His independence, His dominion, and the subjection of everything to Him. Taking a child contradicts that, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿They said: Allah has taken a son. Glorified is He; He is the Self-Sufficient. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.﴾ [Yunus: 68].
And His praising Himself for the absence of a partner includes His being singular in lordship and divinity, and His being unique in the attributes of perfection which no other can be described with, for otherwise a partner would exist with Him. If He lacked them, every existing thing would be more perfect than Him, since the existent is more perfect than the non-existent. For this reason He, glorified is He, does not praise Himself by a non-existence except when it includes the affirmation of a perfection. Just as He praised Himself by being one who does not die, because it includes the perfection of His life; and He praised Himself by being one whom drowsiness and sleep do not overtake, because that includes the perfection of His self-subsistence; and He praised Himself by saying that nothing escapes His knowledge, the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller than that nor greater, because of the perfection of His knowledge and encompassing; and He praised Himself by saying that He does not wrong anyone, because of the perfection of His justice and beneficence; and He praised Himself by saying that eyes do not perceive Him, because of the perfection of His greatness: He sees and is not seen, just as He knows and is not encompassed by knowledge. So the mere negation of being seen is not a perfection, because non-existence is not seen. There is no perfection at all in a thing's not being seen; rather the perfection lies in its not being encompassed by sight or perception, because of its greatness in itself and its transcendence above being perceived by the created. Likewise He praised Himself by the absence of heedlessness and forgetfulness, because of the perfection of His knowledge.
So every negation in the Qur'an by which Allah praised Himself is because of its opposition to the affirmation of its opposite, and because it includes the perfection of the affirmation of its opposite.
Thus I have come to know that the reality of praise follows the affirmation of the attributes of perfection, and that negating them is negating His praise, and negating praise necessitates the affirmation of its opposite.
[Chapter: Evidence for the Tawhid of the Names and Attributes]
As for the indication of the five names upon them, which are "Allah, al-Rabb, al-Rahman, al-Rahim, and al-Malik," it is based on two principles:
The first: the names of the Lord, blessed and exalted, indicate the attributes of His perfection. They are derived from the attributes; they are names and they are descriptions. Because of this they are "the most beautiful" (husna). For if they were mere words with no meanings in them, they would not be "the most beautiful," nor would they indicate praise or perfection, and it would be permissible for names of vengeance and anger to occur in the station of mercy and beneficence, and vice versa. So one says: "O Allah, I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for You are the Avenger," and "O Allah, give me, for You are the Harmful, the Preventer," and the like.
Denying the meanings of His most beautiful names is among the greatest forms of deviation (ilhad) regarding them. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names; they will be recompensed for what they used to do.﴾ [al-A'raf: 180]. Also, if they did not indicate meanings and attributes, it would not be permissible to report about Him by their verbal nouns (masadir) and to describe Him by them. But Allah reported about Himself by their verbal nouns, and affirmed them for Himself, and His messenger affirmed them for Him, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58]. So it is known that "the Strong" is one of His names, and its meaning is the One described with strength. Likewise His saying: ﴿So to Allah belongs all honor entirely.﴾ [Fatir: 10]. So "al-Aziz" is one who has honor. Had strength and honor not been affirmed for Him, He would not be named "Strong" or "Mighty." Likewise His saying: ﴿He sent it down with His knowledge﴾ [al-Nisa: 166], ﴿Know that it was sent down with the knowledge of Allah﴾ [Hud: 14], ﴿And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].
In the Sahih, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed Allah does not sleep, nor is it fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the night. His veil is light; were He to unveil it, the glories of His face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reaches." Here the verbal noun from which His name al-Basir (the All-Seeing) is derived is affirmed.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, from A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "Praise be to Allah, whose hearing encompassed all voices."
In the Sahih, the hadith of istikharah: "O Allah, I seek Your choice through Your knowledge, and I seek Your power through Your might." So He is Capable with power.
Allah, exalted is He, said to Musa: ﴿I have chosen you over the people by My messages and My speech﴾ [al-A'raf: 144]. So He is a Speaker with speech.
He is the Great, who possesses greatness, as in the Sahih from him ﷺ: "Allah, exalted is He, says: Greatness is My waist-wrapper, and pride is My cloak." He is the Wise, who possesses judgment: ﴿So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Great.﴾ [Ghafir: 12]. The Muslims agreed that if one swears by the life of Allah, or His hearing, or His sight, or His power, or His might, or His greatness, his oath is binding and requires expiation, because these are the attributes of His perfection from which His names are derived.
Also, if His names did not include meanings and attributes, it would not be proper to report about Him by their actions. One would not say: He hears and sees, He knows and is able and wills. For the establishment of the rulings of attributes is a branch of the establishment of the attributes; so when the root of the attribute is negated, the establishment of its ruling is impossible.
Also, if His names were not possessed of meanings and attributes, they would be frozen like pure proper names, which are not assigned to their referents on account of a meaning subsisting in them. Then they would all be equal, and there would be no difference between what they signify. This is clear obstinacy and manifest slander. For whoever makes the meaning of "the Capable" the same as the meaning of "the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing," and the meaning of "the Oft-Relenting" the same as "the Avenger," and the meaning of "the Giver" the same as "the Preventer," has indeed defied reason, language and natural disposition.
So denying the meanings of His names is among the greatest forms of deviation regarding them, and deviation regarding them has several kinds; this is one of them.
The second: naming idols with them, as they call them gods. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: "They diverted the names of Allah, exalted is He, from what they are upon, and named their idols with them. They added and subtracted: they derived al-Lat from Allah, al-Uzza from al-Aziz, and Manat from al-Mannan." It is narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿they deviate concerning His names﴾ [al-A'raf: 180]: "They lie about Him." This is an explanation by meaning.
The reality of deviation regarding them is diverting them from their correct application, introducing into them what is not among their meanings, and removing the real meanings from them. This is the reality of deviation, and whoever does that has lied against Allah. So Ibn Abbas explained deviation as lying, or it is the extreme of one who deviates regarding His names, exalted is He; for when one introduces into their meanings what is not of them, and takes them out of their realities, or some of them, he has diverted them from the correct and the truth, and this is the reality of deviation.
So deviation is either by denying them and rejecting them, or by denying their meanings and nullifying them, or by distorting them from correctness and removing them from truth through false interpretations, or by making them names for these created, made things, as in the deviation of the people of unification (ittihad), for they made them names of this existence, its praised and blameworthy alike, until their leader said: "He is the one named with every name praised by intellect, law and custom, and with every name blamed by intellect, law and custom." Exalted is Allah far above what the deviators say, a great exaltation.

(Section: On the comparison between the taste of listening (sama') and the taste of prayer, and the explanation that one of the two tastes is separate from the other.)
Indeed, whenever the taste of one of them and its dominance grows strong, the taste of the other and its dominance weakens.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 1, verse 1 (part 6 of 8):

There is no doubt that prayer is the coolness of the eyes of the lovers (of God), the delight of the spirits of the monotheists, the touchstone (mihakk) of the states of the truthful, and the scale (mizan) of the states of the wayfarers. It is His mercy bestowed upon His servants. He guided them to it and made them aware of it, out of mercy toward them and honour for them, so that they might attain through it the nobility of His favour and the success of nearness to Him. It is not that He has any need of them; rather it is a bounty from Him and a grace upon them. He made worship through it obligatory upon the heart and the limbs together, and He made the heart's share in it the more complete and the greater of the two shares. That share is its turning towards its Lord, glorified is He, its joy and delight in His nearness, its enjoyment of His love, its exultation in standing before Him, and its withdrawal, during the standing in servitude, from turning to other than its Worshipped One, and the perfecting of the rights of His servitude until it is performed in the manner He is pleased with.

When He, glorified is He, tested His servant with desires and their causes, from within him and from outside him, the completion of His mercy and His kindness toward him required that He prepare for him a banquet gathering every kind of dish, rare gift, robe of honour and bounty, and that He invite him to it five times every day. In every kind of that banquet He placed a pleasure, a benefit and an interest for this servant whom He invited to the banquet, which is not found in the other kind, so that the servant's delight in every kind of worship may be complete, and so that He may honour him with every category of honour. Every act of that worship becomes an expiation for a blameworthy matter which he used to dislike and which stood opposite it, so that He may reward him for it with a special light, a special strength in his heart and limbs, and a special reward on the day of his meeting with Him.

The one invited comes out from this banquet having been satisfied and quenched, and clothed with the robes of acceptance and made sufficient, because the heart had previously suffered from the drought, the barrenness, the hunger, the thirst, the nakedness and the sickness that it suffered. So He sends him away from His presence having been made independent of food, drink, clothing and gifts to the extent that suffices him.

Since the barrenness was continuous and the dryness of the souls was successive, He renewed the invitation to this banquet time after time, out of mercy toward him. So he never ceases to ask for water from the One in whose hand is the rain of the hearts and its watering, seeking the showers of His mercy, lest what that (banquet) has caused to grow for him of the pasture of faith, its herbage and its fruits, should wither, and lest the source of growth be cut off. The heart is always in this state of seeking water and seeking rain, complaining to its Lord of its dryness, its drought and its need for the watering of His mercy and the rain of His goodness. This is the constant practice of the servant throughout the days of his life.

For heedlessness that descends upon the heart is the drought and the barrenness. As long as it is in the remembrance of God and turning towards Him, the rain of mercy falls upon it like a copious rain. When it becomes heedless, it suffers drought in proportion to its heedlessness, little or much. When heedlessness takes hold and becomes firmly established, its land becomes dead, its year barren and dry, and the fire of desires blazes in it from every side like the scorching winds.

When the rain of mercy comes upon it again, its land stirs, swells and grows, and it brings forth every lovely pair. When drought and barrenness befall it, it is like a tree whose moisture, softness and fruits come from water. When water is withheld from it, its roots dry up, its branches wilt, its fruits are held back, and the branches and the tree may even dry out entirely. When you stretch a branch of it towards yourself, it does not extend and does not yield to you, and it breaks. Then the wisdom of the keeper of the orchard demands cutting that tree and making it fuel for the fire. Likewise the heart: it only dries up when it is empty of the Oneness of God, His love, His knowledge, His remembrance and His supplication. Then the heat of the self and the fire of desires strike it, and the branches of the limbs refuse to extend when you extend them and to yield when you lead them. Thereafter neither they nor the tree are fit for anything but the fire. ﴿So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of God; they are in manifest error﴾ [al-Zumar: 22].

When the heart is rained upon with the rain of mercy, the branches are soft, submissive and moist. When you stretch them towards the command of God, they yield with you and come forward swiftly, gentle and tranquil. You then pick from them the fruits of servitude which each branch carries, and their substance comes from the moisture and irrigation of the heart. The substance does its work in the heart and the limbs. When the heart dries up, the branches become idle from the works of righteousness, because the substance and life of the heart has been cut off from them, so it does not spread into the limbs, and each limb fails to bear its fruit of servitude.

For God has, in every limb of the servant, a servitude particular to it, and an obedience required of it. It was created for that and prepared for it.

People after this are of three categories:

The first: he who employs those limbs in what they were created for and what was intended of them. This is the one who trades with God for the most profitable trade and sells his soul to God for the most profitable sale. Prayer was instituted for the employment of all the limbs in servitude, following the standing of the heart in it.

The second: he who employs them in what they were not created for, and which they were not created for. This is the one whose effort has failed, whose trade has been lost, who has missed the good pleasure of his Lord and His abundant reward, and who has earned His wrath and painful punishment.

The third: he who idles his limbs and deadens them through inactivity. This one is also a loser, with the greatest loss, for the servant was created for worship and obedience, not for idleness. The most hateful of creatures to God is the idler who is neither occupied with the affairs of this world nor striving for the Hereafter. Such a one is a burden upon both this world and religion.

The first is like a man granted a vast tract of land, aided with the tools of ploughing and sowing, and given what suffices to irrigate it. He ploughed it and prepared it for cultivation, sowed in it various kinds of grain, and planted in it various kinds of fruits and differing fruit-trees. Then he did not neglect it; rather he set guards over it and protected it from corrupters. He kept inspecting it every day, repairing what had spoiled, planting in place of what had dried up, removing its weeds, cutting off its thorns, and using its produce to sustain its cultivation.

The second is like a man who took that land and made it a lair for beasts of prey and vermin, a dumping ground for carrion and stench, and a stronghold to which every corrupter, harmer and thief resorts. He took what had been given him to sow and improve it, and spent it as sustenance and livelihood for the people of evil and corruption who were in it.

The third is like a man who left it idle and neglected, and let that water go to waste in the deserts and wastelands. So he sits blameworthy and deprived. This is the example of the people of heedlessness, while the one before him is the example of the people of treachery and transgression, and the first is the example of the people of alertness and readiness for what they were created for.

The first, when he moves or is still, stands or sits, eats or drinks, sleeps or dresses, speaks or stays silent, all of that is for him and not against him, and it is in remembrance, obedience, nearness and increase.

The second, when he does that, it is against him and not for him, and it is in rejection, distance and loss.

The third, when he does that, is in heedlessness, idleness and negligence.

The first moves about in what he moves about in by the ruling of obedience and nearness.

The second moves about in it by the ruling of treachery and aggression, for God did not give him possession of what He possessed him with in order that he might use it to disobey Him. He is a transgressor, an aggressor, a traitor against God in His blessings, punished for enjoying them in other than His obedience.

The third moves about in it and partakes of it by the ruling of heedlessness and the delight and nature of the self. He does not seek by it the pleasure of God or nearness to Him. This is a manifest loss, for he has wasted the moments of his life, which have no value, away from the best profits and trades.

So God, glorified is He, called the monotheists to these five prayers out of mercy toward them, and prepared for them in them kinds of worship, so that the servant might attain from every word, deed, movement and stillness his share of His gifts.

The secret and the essence of prayer is the heart's turning towards God in it and its presence wholly before Him. When it does not turn to Him, and is occupied with other than Him, and is distracted by the talk of the self, it is like a delegate who came to the gate of a king, apologising for his error and fault, seeking the showers of His generosity and mercy, asking Him for sustenance to nourish his heart so that it may be strong enough to stand in His service. When he reached the gate and nothing remained but to converse with the King, he turned away from the King and deviated from him to the right or turned his back on him, and occupied himself with the thing most hateful to the King and of least worth in his sight, preferring it over Him, making it the direction of his heart, the place of his turning and the seat of his secret. He sent his servants and attendants to stand in obedience to the King on his behalf, to make excuses for him and to take his place in the service, while the King witnesses that and sees his condition. Yet the King's generosity, bounty and wide kindness refuse to turn those servants and followers away empty; they receive something of His mercy and kindness. But there is a difference between dividing the spoils among those entitled to shares of the booty and giving a gratuity to one who has no share: ﴿And for all there are degrees according to what they did, that He may fully repay them their deeds, and they will not be wronged﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 19].

God, glorified is He, created this human kind for Himself, chose it specially, and created for it everything, as in the divine saying: "Son of Adam, I created you for Myself, and I created everything for you. So by My right over you, do not occupy yourself with what I created for you from that for which I created you."

And in another narration: "I created you for Myself, so do not play; and I have undertaken your provision, so do not toil. Son of Adam, seek Me and you will find Me. If you find Me you will find everything, and if you miss Me you will miss everything, and I am better for you than everything."

He made prayer a means leading him to His nearness, His converse, His love and intimacy with Him. Between one prayer and another, heedlessness, neglect, aversion, slips and sins arise in him, which distance him from his Lord and remove him from His nearness. He becomes as though he were a stranger to servitude, not one of the servants. Perhaps he casts his hand into the captivity of the enemy, who takes him captive, shackles him, binds him and imprisons him in the prison of his self and his desire. His portion is then tightness of chest, the treatment of worries, griefs, sorrows and regrets, and he does not know the cause of that.

Thus the mercy of his Merciful Lord required that He give him a comprehensive servitude, varied in its parts and states, according to the variety of the events that come from the servant, and according to the intensity of his need for his share of each part of that servitude.

With ablution he purifies himself from filth and comes before his Lord purified. Ablution has an outward and an inward aspect. Its outward aspect is the purity of the body and the members of worship, and its inward aspect and secret is the purity of the heart from its filth and impurities through repentance. For this reason God, glorified is He, joins repentance and purification in His saying: ﴿Indeed, God loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 222].
