But His wisdom refuses that, and His justice refuses to punish anyone or seize him without proof. So He established the proof, turned the signs, struck the parables and diversified the proofs. Had all creatures been on one path of guidance, these matters would not have come about, these proofs and parables would not have been varied, and His might would not have appeared in His retribution against His enemies and His support of His friends over them, nor would His proofs have appeared which He established for the truthfulness of His prophets and messengers. There would not have been a sign for people in the two groups that met, one group fighting in the way of Allah and another disbelieving group whom they saw as twice their number with their own eyes. And there would not have been a lasting sign for creation as long as the world endures, in the matter of Moses and his people, and Pharaoh and his people, and the parting of the sea for them, their all entering it, then Moses and his people being saved with none of them drowned, while Pharaoh and his people were drowned with none of them surviving. This making Himself known to His servants, these signs, this might and this wisdom, cannot be nullified in any way and do not exist without their necessary consequences.

Furthermore, the reality of sovereignty is only completed through giving and withholding, honouring and humiliating, rewarding and punishing, anger and pleasure, appointing and dismissing, and the exalting of whoever deserves exaltation and the abasing of whoever deserves abasement. He, exalted, said: ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You strip sovereignty from whom You will. You exalt whom You will and You abase whom You will. In Your hand is the good. Indeed You are over all things competent. You cause the night to enter the day and You cause the day to enter the night. You bring the living out of the dead and You bring the dead out of the living. And You provide for whom You will without account﴾ [Al 'Imran: 26-27]. And He, exalted, said: ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him. Every day He is in an affair﴾ [al-Rahman: 29]. He forgives a sin, relieves a distress, removes a grief, supports the oppressed, seizes the oppressor, frees the captive, enriches the poor, mends the broken, heals the sick, accepts a slip, covers a fault, exalts the humbled, humbles the mighty, gives to the one who asks, takes away one dynasty and brings another, alternates the days among the people, raises up some peoples and lowers others. He drives the decrees which He determined fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and the earth, to their appointed times, so that none of them comes before its time or after it. Rather, He has counted each of them as His Book counted it, and His pen ran with it, His judgement took effect in it, and His knowledge preceded it. He alone disposes of all the kingdoms, with the disposal of a king who is powerful, dominant, just, merciful, complete in sovereignty, whom no contender disputes in his dominion and no opponent opposes in it. So His disposal of the kingdom revolves between justice, kindness, wisdom, benefit and mercy, and His disposal does not depart from these.

In the Tafsir of the Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Musa ibn Mardawayh, through the hadith of al-Hammani: "Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Mu'awiya ibn Yahya from Yunus ibn Maysara from Abu Idris from Abu al-Darda': that he was asked about the words of Allah, exalted, ﴿Every day He is in an affair﴾ [al-Rahman: 29], and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about it and said: 'Among His affairs is that He forgives a sin, relieves a distress, raises a people and lowers others.'" Also in it, through the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama: "al-Zubayr Abu 'Abd al-Salam narrated to us from Ayyub ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mikraz from his father, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: Your Lord, mighty and majestic, has neither night nor day with Him. The light of the heavens and the earth is from the light of His face. Your days with Him are twelve hours. Your deeds are presented to Him in the morning for three hours from the beginning of the day. He looks into them and becomes angry at what He dislikes. The first to know of His anger are the bearers of the Throne. The bearers of the Throne, the curtains of the Throne, the angels brought near and all the other angels glorify Him. Gabriel blows into the horn, and no creature of Allah in the heavens or on the earth remains without hearing it except the two weighty species. They glorify [for three hours] until the All-Merciful is filled with mercy. That is six hours. Then He calls for the wombs and looks into them for three hours: ﴿He forms you in the wombs as He wills. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [Al 'Imran: 6]; ﴿He grants to whom He wills females and He grants to whom He wills males﴾ [al-Shura: 49]. That makes nine hours. Then He calls for the provisions and looks into them for three hours: ﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts﴾ [al-Isra': 30]. That makes twelve hours.'"
Then 'Abd Allah recited: ﴿Every day He is in an affair﴾ [al-Rahman: 29], then said: "This is your affair and the affair of your Lord, mighty and majestic."
And al-Tabarani mentioned it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir through another route.

This is part of the completeness of His disposal over His kingdom, glory be to Him. Had His disposal been confined to one manner and one pattern, it would not have been a complete disposal.

The purpose here is that sovereignty (al-mulk) and praise (al-hamd) are inseparable in relation to Him. Whatever His sovereignty and power encompass, His praise also encompasses. He is praiseworthy in His sovereignty, and sovereignty and power belong to Him together with His praise. Just as it is impossible for any existent to fall outside His sovereignty and power, it is impossible for any of them to fall outside His praiseworthiness and wisdom. For this reason He praises Himself at the time of His creating and His commanding, to alert His servants that the source of His creation and command is His praiseworthiness. He is praiseworthy for everything He created and commanded, with the praise of gratitude and servitude, and the praise of laudation and commendation. Both are united in the word "tabaraka" (blessed be), so "tabaraka Allah" encompasses all of this. For this reason He mentioned this word after His saying: ﴿Surely, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-A'raf: 54].

Praise is the most comprehensive of the attributes and the most general of the laudations, and the paths to knowing it are very numerous. The ways to considering it in the smallest particles of the world, its details, and the particulars of commanding and forbidding are extremely broad, because all of His names, blessed and exalted is He, are praise; His attributes are praise; His acts are praise; His judgments are praise; His justice is praise; His vengeance upon His enemies is praise; and His bounty in His kindness to His allies is praise. Creation and command subsist through His praise, come into being through His praise, become manifest through His praise, and the end-purpose is His praise. Thus His praise is the cause of these things, their end, their manifestation, and their bearer. His praise is the spirit of everything, the subsistence of everything rests on it, and the pervasion of His praise in existents and the manifestation of its effects in them is a matter witnessed by sight and insight.

Among the ways that indicate the comprehensiveness of the meaning of praise and its extension over all knowable things is knowing His names and attributes, and the servant's affirmation that the world has a living God, who combines every attribute of perfection, every beautiful name, every lovely praise, and every noble act; that He has complete power, an executed will, an all-encompassing knowledge, a hearing that encompasses all voices, a sight that surrounds all visible things, a mercy that encompasses all creatures, a supreme sovereignty from which not even an atom of the atoms escapes, a complete and absolute independence from all aspects, a far-reaching wisdom whose effects are witnessed in beings, an overpowering might in all aspects and considerations, and complete words, executed and effective, which neither the righteous nor the wicked among all creatures can surpass. He is One, without partner in His lordship or in His divinity, without likeness in His essence, His attributes, or His acts. He has no one who shares with Him in an atom of His dominion, or who succeeds Him in the management of His creation, or who veils Him from His callers, supplicants, or askers, or who intercedes between them and Him through deception, fabrication, or lies, as happens between subjects and kings. Were that so, the order of existence would be corrupted and the whole world would be ruined: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya: 22]. So if there were other gods with Him, as His deniers who are in falsehood claim, there would occur in the management and the affair such deficiency and corruption that no state could remain stable upon it and no existence could be sound upon it.

Among His greatest blessings upon us, and what made His servants deserve to praise Him, is that He made us servants to Him alone, and did not make us, our Lord, divided among quarreling partners, nor make us servants of a god carved out by thoughts, who does not hear our voices, nor see our deeds, nor know our states, nor possess for his worshippers any harm or benefit, nor death nor life nor resurrection, who has never spoken, does not speak, does not command, and does not forbid, to whom hands are not raised, toward whom the angels and the Spirit do not ascend, to whom the good word does not rise, and to whom righteous deeds are not lifted; who is neither inside the world nor outside it, neither above it, nor to its right, nor to its left, nor behind it, nor in front of it, neither joined to it nor separated from it, neither opposite it nor distant from it; who is neither established upon His Throne nor above His servants, and whose share of the Throne is like the share of latrines and privies; from whom angels do not descend, nor does anything descend from Him, nor does anything ascend to Him, nor does anything draw near to Him; who neither loves nor is loved; whose believers do not delight in looking at His noble Face in the abode of reward; rather, He has no face that can be seen, nor a hand with which He grasps the heavens and another with which He grasps the earth; who has no act by which He is occupied and no wisdom by which He is characterized; who did not speak to Musa with speech; who did not manifest Himself to the mountain so that He made it crumble to dust; who will not come on the Day of Resurrection to judge; who does not descend every night to the lowest heaven and say, "I am not asked about My servants except Me"; who does not rejoice at the repentance of His servant when he repents to Him; and in whose wisdom it is permissible to punish His prophets, His messengers, His angels, and all the people of His obedience among the inhabitants of the heavens and the earths, and to bestow blessings upon His enemies among the disbelievers, those who wage war against Him, and those who deny Him and His messengers. All of them are equal in relation to Him, with no distinction whatsoever, except that He informed that He will not do that, so it is ruled out by the report that He will not do it, not because it is in itself contrary to His wisdom. Yet, His good pleasure is the very same as His anger, His anger the very same as His good pleasure, His love the very same as His dislike, and His dislike the very same as His love. These are nothing but pure will and absolute volition by which He wills, not for any wisdom, nor for any purpose, nor for any benefit. Yet He punishes His servants for what they did not do and for which they have no power, rather He punishes them for the very act He Himself performed and attributed to them, and He punishes them when they do not perform His act, and blames them for it. It is permissible in His wisdom that He punish men when they are not women, and women when they are not men, tall persons when they are not short, short persons when they are not tall, and the reverse, black persons when they are not white, and the reverse. Rather, His punishing them for opposing Him is of this same kind, since they have absolutely no power to do what they were commanded or to abandon what they were forbidden.

So to Him belong praise, gratitude, and the good, beautiful commendation, that He did not make us servants of one with such a nature, so that we would be lost. We have no Lord whom we aim to, no Eternal whom we turn to and worship, no god upon whom we rely, and no Lord to whom we return. Rather our hearts cry out in the paths of bewilderment: "Who guided us and gathered upon us a lost lord, who is neither inside the world nor outside it, neither separate from it nor opposite it, neither joined to it nor distant from it, from whom nothing descends and to whom nothing ascends, who has never spoken to anyone nor has anyone spoken to Him?" No one should mention His attributes or describe Him by them. Rather, one who mentions them with his tongue does not speak them, and with his heart does not comprehend them. It is required that whoever mentions them, reports them about Him, affirms them for Him, attributes them to Him, or describes Him by them be punished with death, or beating, or imprisonment. Rather, pure tawhid is denying them, stripping Him of them, negating their subsistence in Him and His characterization by them. Whatever of that our intellects do not grasp, it is obligatory to negate it, deny it, and declare disbelief in whoever affirms it, and make lawful his blood and wealth, or call him an innovator, misguided, and corrupt. The more emphatic the negation, the more complete the tawhid. Thus "He is not such-and-such, and He is not such-and-such" is more emphatic in tawhid than our saying "He is such-and-such and He is such-and-such."

So to Allah the Mighty belongs the greatest praise, the most complete and perfect, for what He bestowed upon us of knowing Him and affirming His oneness, and affirming His sublime attributes and beautiful names, and the affirmation of our hearts that He is Allah, there is no god but He, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Lord of the worlds, the Sustainer of the heavens and the earths, the God of the first and the last. He continues to be described with attributes of majesty, named with names of perfection, and exalted above their opposites of deficiencies, likeness, and similitude.

(Section)

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the Praised, the Beloved, the Exalted, the Possessor of majesty and honor, praised for everything He decreed and created, and for everything He commanded and legislated.

Whoever has a portion of knowing His beautiful names, and whose effects have settled in creation and command, sees creation and command arranged by them in the most perfect order. He sees their effects flowing in both, and knows, according to his knowledge of them, what befits His perfection and majesty to do and what does not. He infers from His names what He does and what He does not do, for He does not act contrary to the requirement of His praise and wisdom. Likewise he knows what befits Him to command and legislate and what does not, so he knows that He does not command contrary to the requirement of His praise and wisdom. So when he sees some rulings as tyranny and injustice, or foolishness and futility, or corruption, or things that do not necessitate praise or commendation, let him know that they are not among His rulings nor His religion, and that He and His messenger are free of them. For He commanded only justice, not injustice; benefit, not corruption; and wisdom, not futility and foolishness. He sent His messenger only with the tolerant hanifiyya (the pure monotheistic way), not with harshness and severity, and sent him with mercy, not cruelty, for He is the Most Merciful of the merciful, and His messenger is a mercy sent to the worlds. His whole religion is mercy, he is the prophet of mercy, and his nation is the merciful nation. All of that is the requirement of His beautiful names, His exalted attributes, and His praiseworthy acts. So He is not described except with praise, and not praised except with the best praise, just as He is not named except with the best names.

He, glorified is He, has alerted to the comprehensiveness of His praise over His creation and His command, by praising Himself at the beginning and the end of creation, at the time of command and legislation, praising Himself for His lordship over the worlds, praising Himself for His singularity in divinity and for His life, praising Himself for the impossibility of His being characterized by what is unbecoming to His perfection, such as taking a son or a partner, or allying with any of His creatures out of need for it, praising Himself for His exaltedness and His greatness, praising Himself in this life and the Hereafter, and reporting the pervasion of His praise in the upper and lower worlds. He alerted to all of this in His Book and praised Himself for it. Thus He diversified His praise and its causes, and at times gathered them and at other times separated them, so that He might make Himself known to His servants and teach them how to praise Him and how to commend Him, and so that He might make Himself beloved to them through that and love them when they know Him, love Him, and praise Him. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, Master of the Day of Judgment﴾. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿All praise is for Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 1]. And He said: ﴿All praise is for Allah, who revealed to His servant the Book and did not make in it any crookedness, [but made it] upright, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers﴾ [al-Kahf: 1-2]. And He said: ﴿All praise is for Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him is praise in the Hereafter, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted﴾ [Saba: 1]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿All praise is for Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four. He adds to creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ [Fatir: 1]. And He said: ﴿He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs praise in the first and the last, and to Him is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Qasas: 70]. And He said: ﴿He is the Living; there is no deity except Him, so invoke Him, sincere to Him in religion. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Ghafir: 65]. And He said: ﴿So exalted is Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning. And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you are at noon﴾ [al-Rum: 17-18].

He reported the praise of His creatures for Him after His separating between them and deciding for the people of His obedience with His reward and honor, and deciding for the people of His disobedience with His punishment and humiliation: ﴿And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [al-Zumar: 75].

He reported the praise of the people of Paradise for Him, and that they did not enter it except by His praise, just as the people of the Fire did not enter it except by His praise. The people of Paradise said: ﴿All praise is for Allah, who has guided us to this. And we would not have been [able] to find guidance if Allah had not guided us﴾ [al-A'raf: 43]. And ﴿Their call therein is, "Exalted are You, O Allah," and their greeting therein is, "Peace," and the last of their call is, "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Yunus: 10]. And He said about the people of the Fire: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will call to them, "Where are My partners, those you used to claim?" And We will extract from every nation a witness, and We will say, "Produce your proof." Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and lost from them is what they used to invent﴾ [al-Qasas: 74-75]. And He said: ﴿So they will admit their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk: 11].

They bore witness against themselves to disbelief and wrongdoing, and they knew that they had been liars in the world, deniers of the signs of their Lord, associators with Him, deniers of His divinity, and fabricators against Him. This is their acknowledgment of His justice concerning them, and of His seizing from them some of His right upon them, and that He is not unjust to them, and that they entered the Fire only by His justice and praise, and were punished only for their deeds and for what they were able to do or to abandon, not as the Jabriyya (those who deny human agency) say.

The detail of this wisdom is something human intellects have no way to encompass or to express. But in summary, every exalted attribute, beautiful name, lovely commendation, every praise, glorification, transcendence, sanctification, majesty, and honor belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the most perfect, complete, and enduring manner. Everything by which He is described, mentioned, or reported is a praise, commendation, glorification, transcendence, and sanctification for Him. So, glory be to Him and praise, no creature can count His praises. Rather He is as He praised Himself, and beyond what His creatures praise Him. So to Him belongs praise, first and last, abundant, good, and blessed in it, as befits the nobility of His Face, the might of His majesty, the loftiness of His glory, and the height of His grandeur.

This is an alert to one of the two kinds of His praise, namely the praise of attributes and names.

The second kind is the praise of blessings and favors. This is witnessed by all creation, the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever, in His abundant gifts, His vast bestowals, His generous favors, His beautiful kindnesses, His good treatment of His servants, His vast mercy toward them, His goodness, gentleness, and tenderness, His answering of the supplications of the distressed, His removing the afflictions of the afflicted, His rescuing of the distressed, His mercy toward the worlds, His beginning of blessings before being asked, and without any entitlement, but as a beginning from Him by the mere grace of His bounty and kindness, and His averting of trials and calamities after their causes have formed, and His turning them away after they have occurred.

And His subtle kindness, exalted is He, in that: by bringing to whoever He wills the best of kindnesses, and bringing him to what hopes cannot reach, and guiding His chosen ones and servants to the paths of the Abode of Peace, and defending them most excellently against harm, and protecting them from the pastures of sin. He made faith beloved to them and adorned it in their hearts, and made disbelief, immorality, and disobedience hateful to them. He made them among the rightly guided, wrote faith in their hearts, strengthened them with a spirit from Him, and named them "Muslims" before He created them. He mentioned them before they mentioned Him, gave to them before they asked Him, and made Himself beloved to them with blessings although He is free of them, and made them hateful to Him through sins while they are in need of Him. Despite all of this, He prepared for them a home and readied for them in it everything that souls desire and eyes delight in, filled it with every good, and deposited in it blessings, delight, joy, and brightness such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and nothing has occurred to a human heart. Then He sent messengers to them calling them to it, then facilitated for them the means that lead them to it and helped them to it, and He was content from them with little in this very short period compared to the permanence of the Abode of Bliss. He guaranteed for them that if they did good He would reward them tenfold for a good deed, and if they did evil and sought His forgiveness He would forgive them, and He promised that He would erase the bad deeds they had committed by the good deeds they would do afterward. He reminded them of His favors, made Himself known to them through His names, and commanded them with what He commanded them, out of mercy and kindness toward them, not because He needed them. He forbade them from what He forbade them, to protect and safeguard them, not out of miserliness toward them. He addressed them with the gentlest and sweetest address, advised them with the best advice, enjoined upon them the most perfect counsels, commanded them with the noblest qualities, and forbade them the ugliest words and deeds.

Ibn al-Qayyim, *al-Tafsir al-Qayyim*, on Surah 1, verse 2 (part 4 of 14):

He explained the signs to them, coined parables for them, widened for them the paths to knowing Him and recognizing Him, opened for them the doors of guidance, and made known to them the means that bring them near to His good pleasure and keep them far from His anger. He addresses them in the gentlest manner and calls them by their finest names, as in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers﴾ [An-Nur: 31], ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53], ﴿Say to My servants﴾ [Ibrahim: 31], ﴿And when My servants ask you about Me﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 186]. He addresses them with the speech of affection, love and tenderness, as in His saying: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous. Who has made for you the earth a bed and the sky a canopy, and sent down from the sky water and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know [the truth]﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 21-22]; ﴿O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the sky and the earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?﴾ [Fatir: 3]; ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah﴾ [Fatir: 5]; ﴿O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord, who created you and proportioned you and made you balanced?﴾ [Al-Infitar: 6-7]; ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except as Muslims. And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided. And remember the favor of Allah upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, and you became, by His favor, brothers. And you were on the brink of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs that you may be guided﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102-103]; ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as intimates other than your own, who will not spare you from ruin. They wish you would suffer. Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater. We have certainly made the signs clear to you, if you use reason﴾ [Al 'Imran: 118]; ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection, when they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, expelling the Messenger and you because you believe in Allah your Lord. If you have come out to strive in My way and seeking My pleasure, [do not] secretly show them affection, for I know best what you conceal and what you declare. And whoever of you does that has certainly strayed from the right way﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah: 1]; ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a person and his heart, and that to Him you will be gathered. And beware of a trial which will not afflict only those who have wronged among you exclusively. And know that Allah is severe in punishment. And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people would snatch you away, and He sheltered you and strengthened you with His help and provided you with good things, that you might be grateful﴾ [Al-Anfal: 24-26]; ﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke other than Allah could not create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. And if the fly should snatch away from them something, they could not retrieve it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought. They have not appraised Allah with the appraisal due to Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [Al-Hajj: 73-74]; ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis. He was of the jinn, so he defied the command of his Lord. Then would you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are enemies to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾ [Al-Kahf: 50]. In this address, you have been told: I have shown enmity to Iblis and cast him out of My heaven and removed him from My nearness, when he did not prostrate to your father Adam. Then you, O his children, take him and his descendants as allies besides Me, though they are enemies to you.

So let the intelligent person reflect on the placement of this address, its intense adherence to hearts, and its penetration into souls. Most of the Qur'an is in this mode of His addressing His servants with affection, tenderness, kindness, and sincere counsel. He informs His servants that He does not approve for them except the most noble means, the most excellent stations, and the most sublime knowledge and recognitions.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿If you disbelieve, indeed Allah is free from need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ [Az-Zumar: 7]. He says: ﴿This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 3]. He says: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 185]. He says: ﴿Allah wants to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you and to turn to you in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. And Allah wants to turn to you in forgiveness, but those who follow appetites want you to deviate into a great deviation. Allah wants to lighten [the burden] for you, and mankind was created weak﴾ [An-Nisa': 26-28].

He, the Exalted, disassociates Himself to His servants from the points of suspicion and accusation attributed to Him by those who do not know Him as He should be known, nor appraise Him with the appraisal due to Him: [such as] burdening His servants with what they cannot bear and have no ability at all to do, punishing them if they thank Him and believe in Him, creating the heavens and the earth and what is between them without wisdom or purpose, and that He did not create His creation out of any need for them, nor to multiply through them after scarcity, nor to strengthen Himself through them, as He said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 56-57]. So He informed that He did not create the jinn and mankind out of need for them, nor to profit from them, but He created them out of generosity and benevolence so that they would worship Him, and thereby they would gain every kind of profit from Him, as in His saying: ﴿If you do good, you do good for yourselves﴾ [Al-Isra': 7], and ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for themselves that they prepare﴾ [Ar-Rum: 44].

When He commanded them to perform ablution and to wash from major impurity, which removes their burdens, through which they enter into His presence and by which He raises their ranks, He said: ﴿Allah does not intend to make for you any difficulty, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 6]. He said concerning sacrificial animals and offerings: ﴿Their flesh will never reach Allah, nor their blood, but what reaches Him is piety from you﴾ [Al-Hajj: 37]. And He said, after commanding them to give charity and forbidding them from giving away bad wealth: ﴿And do not aim at the bad [part] of it to spend from it, while you would not take it yourselves except by closing your eyes to it. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 267].

He, the Exalted, says: I am free from need of what you spend, such that anything of it would reach Me. I am Praiseworthy, deserving of all praise. Your spending does not fill any need of Mine, nor does it necessitate praise for Me. Rather, He is Self-Sufficient in Himself, Praiseworthy in Himself, and in His names and attributes, and your spending benefits only you and returns its reward to you.

It is necessary for whoever has not tasted in his heart the sweetness of this address, its majesty, the subtlety of its placement, its attraction to hearts and souls, and its intimate contact with them, to treat his heart with piety, to purge from it the corrupt matters that have stood between him and his share of this, and to expose himself to the causes by which he may attain it: sincere desire, and turning to Allah that He may give life to his heart, purify it, and place in it faith and wisdom. For a dead heart does not taste the flavor of faith, nor find its sweetness, nor enjoy a good life, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

Whoever wishes to contemplate the roots of blessings, let him roam freely in the gardens of the Qur'an, and reflect on what Allah has enumerated in it of His blessings, and how He made Himself known through them to His servants from the beginning of the Qur'an to its end. [He did so] when He created the people of the Fire and tested them with Iblis and his party, and the domination of their enemies over them, and their trial with desires, wills and whims, so that the blessing upon them would be magnified by opposing and fighting them. [He did so so that] the enemies of Allah against His allies and servants would be the most complete and perfect blessing in everything He created, whether beloved or disliked, blessing or trial, and in everything He brought about on earth of His events against His enemies and His honoring of His allies, and in everything He decreed and ordained. The detailed account of this cannot be exhausted by the pens and papers of the world, nor by the powers of the servants. It is only a reminder and an indication.

Whoever surveys the Most Beautiful Names finds them to be praises and laudations, whose eloquence falls short of reaching their reality, and whose individual meanings the imaginations cannot encompass. Yet, beyond that, Allah, the Exalted, has praises, laudations, and kinds of commendation which no thought has stirred with, no suspicion has passed through the hearts, no perceptive mind has glimpsed, and no reflection has produced.

In the supplication of the one most knowing of his Lord among creation, most aware of His names, attributes and praises:
"I ask You by every name that is Yours, which You named Yourself with, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You, that You make the Qur'an the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the removal of my sorrow, and the departure of my worry and my grief."

In the authentic [collection] from him (ﷺ), in the hadith of intercession, when he prostrates before his Lord, he said: "Then He will open my heart to some of His praises which I do not know well now." And he used to say in his prostration: "I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself." So no one of His creation can enumerate praise of Him at all. He has names, attributes, praise and commendation which no close angel nor sent prophet knows. The comparison of what the servants know of that to what they do not know is like a sparrow's sip from the sea.

If it is said: "What then do you say about the trials, tests and pains that are witnessed among children and animals, and among those who are outside of obligation and have no reward or punishment upon them? And what do you say about the names that indicate this, such as the Avenger, the Restrainer, the Abaser, and similar?"

It is said: What has preceded of discussion on this matter suffices in part for one with a sound nature and a straight intellect. As for one whose nature is corrupt, whose heart is overturned, and whose insight of intellect is weak, even if every parable were coined for him, it would only increase him in blindness and bewilderment. We will add to what has preceded more clarification and explanation, since expanding on this topic is better than abbreviating it. So we say: You have known that all the names of the Lord, the Exalted, are beautiful, His attributes are perfection, His actions are wisdom and benefit, and to Him belongs every praise and commendation, and every good comes from Him, belongs to Him, and is in His hand. Evil is not attributed to Him in any way: not in His essence, not in His attributes, not in His actions, and not in His names. Even if it exists in what is produced by Him, it is good when attributed to Him and evil when attributed to whatever it proceeds from or befalls. So hold fast to this principle, and do not depart from it in any matter, minor or major, and judge by it everything that comes to you, and make it your ultimate reference, to which you return and on which you rely.

Know that Allah has specific distinctions in His creation, and mercy and grace which He bestows on whom He wills. This is required by His lordship, His divinity, His praiseworthiness and His wisdom. So beware, then beware, of listening to the whisperings of the devils of mankind and jinn and of the ignorant, wrongdoing self, [which say]: "Why did He not equalize His servants in those distinctions and divide them equally among them?" For this is the very essence of ignorance and foolishness on the part of the one who raises this objection. We have already shown earlier that His wisdom rejects and prevents that. But know that the matter is a division between His grace and His justice: He singles out whom He wills with His mercy, and He targets with His punishment whom He wills, and He is praised for this. The good among His creation are singled out for His grace and mercy, and the corrupt are targeted with His punishment. Each one has his portion of wisdom, trial and test, and each is employed for what he has been prepared and created for. All of that is good, benefit and mercy for the believers, for He created them for good deeds, so they act in them, and He employed them in them, and they could attain that only through Him and deserved it only through what preceded for them from His will and His division. Likewise, afflictions and poisons do not harm them. Rather, whenever the enemy whispers to them, or ambushes them with some of his schemes, or touches them with some phantom, they remember, and then they see clearly. Their brothers (the devils) extend them in error, then they do not stop. And when they fall into a minor or major sin, it returns upon them as mercy, turns into a remedy for them, and replaces a bad deed with sincere repentance and good deeds that erase [sins]. For He, the Exalted, made them know Himself, His grace, and that their hearts are in His hand, and their protection comes from Him, since He overturned their resolutions, though they had resolved not to disobey Him. He showed them His might in His decree, His goodness and benevolence in His pardon and forgiveness, and He made them witness their own selves and what is in them of deficiency, injustice and ignorance, and the extent of their need for Him, their dependence and their humility, and that if He does not pardon them and forgive them, they have no path to salvation ever. For when they gave of themselves the resolve not to disobey, and bound their hearts to it, then disobeyed Him by His will and His power, they came to know through that His great power, His beautiful concealment of them, His generous forbearance toward them, His vast forgiveness for them, the coolness of His pardon, His tenderness, compassion and kindness; and that He is Forbearing, possessing patience, not hastening; and Merciful, whose mercy precedes His wrath; and that whenever they return to Him in repentance, they find Him Forgiving, Merciful, Forbearing, Generous, who forgives their sins, excuses their slips, and loves them and befriends them after repentance.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 1, verse 2 (part 5 of 14):

They then turned to Him in supplication, seeking His favour with the humility of servants and acknowledging the might of His lordship. Glorified is He, so He made Himself known to them through His good response, His gracious kindness, and His excellent bounty, in that He inspired them to call upon Him and made it easy for them to repent and turn back to Him. They turned their hearts to Him after they had turned away from Him. Their disobedience and their sins did not prevent Him from showing compassion to them, from His goodness towards them, and from His kindness to them. He accepted their repentance before they repented to Him, and He gave to them before they asked Him. When they repented to Him, sought His forgiveness, and turned back to Him, He made Himself known to them in another way. He made them know His mercy, His good return, the vastness of His forgiveness, His generous pardon, His beautiful forgiving, His goodness, His bounty, His generosity, and His grace. He hastened to accept them after there had been from them what there had been of long evils, severe aversion, and rushing along the paths of His disobedience. Along with that, He let them witness His great praise and His abundant goodness, and His generosity in that He left them free to choose disobedience, so they attained it by His blessing and His help. Then He did not leave them to what it requires of destruction and corruption, after which no reform is hoped for. Rather, He took care of them with the healing cure, and He drew out from them a disease which, had it persisted with them, would have led to ruin. Then He took care of them by the spirit of hope, casting it into their hearts, and He informed them that He is according to their expectation of Him. Had He made them witness only the greatness of the offence, the ugliness of disobedience, and His anger and abhorrence towards those who disobey Him, it would have produced in them the deadly sickness or the incurable disease of despair of His mercy and despondency about His compassion, and that would have been their very destruction. But He had mercy on them before the trial, during the midst of the trial, and after the trial. He made those effects which His disobedience entails, of tribulations, trials and hardships, a mercy for them and a means to the elevation of their ranks and the attainment of nearness and honour with Him. So He made them witness, through the offence, the might of lordship and the humility of servitude, and He elevated them through its effects to the stations of His nearness and the attainment of His honour. Thus they profit in every state, turning in His generosity and goodness. Every decree He issues for the believer is good for him, leading him to His honour and reward. Likewise, His worldly gifts are blessings from Him to them. If He takes them back from them and deprives them of them, they become gifts of the Hereafter, as it is said: Allah bestows on His servants precious gifts, and when He takes them back, they become gifts of the Hereafter.

The Lord, glorified is He, has manifested Himself to the hearts of the believing knowers and appeared to them in His power, majesty, and greatness, the sovereignty of His will, the greatness of His authority, the loftiness of His station, His generosity, His goodness, His kindness, the vastness of His forgiveness and His mercy, and what He cast into their hearts of faith in His names and attributes, to the extent that human faculties can bear. Beyond that is what their powers cannot bear, and what does not occur to the mind or enter the imagination, and which has no comparison with what they have come to know of Him.

Know, then, that those whose share is the various kinds of sins and wickedness, and the many forms of disbelief and polytheism, who turn about in His anger and wrath, their hearts and souls bear witness against them with sins and disbelief, acknowledging that the proof is His against them and that His right is upon them. None of them mentions the Fire except that he bears witness to that, acknowledges it, and confesses it willingly, not under compulsion or oppression. This is their testimony against themselves. The testimony of His friends against them is another matter, and the believers bear witness about them with another testimony which His enemies do not bear. If they bore witness to it and acknowledged it, His mercy would be nearer to them than His punishment. They bear witness that they are His servants and His possession, and that He created them to manifest His glory, to execute His judgement in them, to carry out His justice, to fulfil His word upon them, to make true His threat concerning them, to make clear His prior knowledge concerning them, and to populate with them the abodes and dwellings which are the place of His justice and wisdom. His friends bear witness to the greatness of His dominion, the might of His authority, the truthfulness of His messengers, the perfection of His wisdom, the completeness of His blessing upon them, and the measure of what He has singled them out with. From what did He protect and shield them, and from what did He turn them away? They had no means to Him before His existence by which they could seek, that He would not make them among the companions of the left, and that He would make them among the companions of the right. They bear witness to Him, glorified is He, that what came from Him to them and in them, of what is required by the complete fulfilment of His words of truth and justice, is His saying and the realisation of what His names require, and so it is pure right belonging to Him.

All of that from Him is good and beautiful, and to Him belongs the most complete, perfect, and excellent praise. It is a just judgement and a decisive decree. He is praised for all of that, so no injustice, oppression, or futility touches Him. Rather, that is the very essence of wisdom, pure praise, perfection that He manifested in His right, might that He displayed, dominion that He proclaimed, and a will that He executed, just as He did with camels and the various kinds of livestock, by which He completed the rites of His friends and the sacrifices of His servants. Although that meant destruction and annihilation for the livestock, His enemies, the disbelievers who associate partners with Him and deny Him, are more deserving that their blood be the offerings of His friends and the sacrifices of those who strive in His way. As Hassan ibn Thabit said:

They purify themselves, taking it as their offering,
with the blood of those disbelievers who were hung up.

Likewise, when Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Qasri sacrificed al-Ja'd ibn Dirham, the leader of the Mu'attilah (those who deny the divine attributes) and the Pharaonic (deniers), he gave a sermon on the day of sacrifice. When he finished his sermon, he said: "O people, sacrifice, may Allah accept your sacrifices, for I am sacrificing al-Ja'd ibn Dirham. He claimed that Allah did not speak to Moses with real speech and did not take Abraham as a close friend, exalted is Allah far above what al-Ja'd says." Then he came down and slaughtered him, and he was his sacrifice. Al-Bukhari mentioned this in his book Khalq Af'al al-Ibad (The Creation of the Acts of Servants). So this is the witness of His friends regarding the affair of His enemies. But His enemies are heedless of this, neither witnessing it nor acknowledging it. Had they witnessed it and acknowledged it, His tenderness and mercy would have reached them. But when they were veiled from knowing Him, loving Him, affirming His oneness, affirming His beautiful names and sublime attributes, describing Him with what befits Him, and declaring Him free from what does not befit Him, they became worse off than livestock. They were struck with the veil, distanced far away from Him, and brought out from His light into darknesses. Their hearts were hidden in ignorance of Him, of His perfection, majesty, and greatness, in thick jungles, so that His term would be fulfilled upon them and His judgement executed against them. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise, and Allah knows best.

(Benefit)

Reflect upon the discourse of the Qur'an and you will find a King to whom belongs all dominion and all praise, in whose hand are the reins of all affairs, from whom they originate and to whom they return, seated upon the throne of His kingdom. Nothing is hidden from Him in the regions of His realm. He knows what is in the souls of His servants and is aware of their secrets and their public deeds. He alone manages the kingdom. He hears and sees, gives and withholds, rewards and punishes, honours and humiliates, creates and provides, causes to die and gives life, decrees, judges, and arranges. Affairs descend from Him, both the subtle and the great, and ascend to Him. Nothing stirs even an atom except by His permission, and not a leaf falls except with His knowledge.

Then reflect how you find Him praising Himself, glorifying Himself, and extolling Himself. He counsels His servants, guides them to what brings them happiness and success, encourages them to it, and warns them against what leads to their ruin. He makes Himself known to them through His names and attributes and draws them near to Himself through His blessings and favours. He reminds them of His blessings upon them and commands them to do what merits their completion. He warns them of His vengeance, reminds them of the honour He has prepared for them if they obey Him, and of the punishment He has prepared for them if they disobey Him. He informs them of His workings with His friends and His enemies, and how the end of these and those turned out. He praises His friends for their good deeds and best qualities, and He censures His enemies for their evil deeds and ugly attributes. He sets forth parables, varies the proofs and evidences, and answers the doubts of His enemies with the best answers. He confirms the truthful and refutes the liar, speaks the truth, guides to the path, and calls to the Abode of Peace, describing its qualities, goodness, and bliss. He warns against the Abode of Perdition, mentioning its torment, ugliness, and pains. He reminds His servants of their poverty before Him and their great need of Him in every respect, and that they cannot be independent of Him for the blink of an eye. He mentions His independence from them and from all created things, that He is self-sufficient in Himself, free of all that is other than Him, while everything other than Him is needy of Him in its very essence. He mentions that no one attains even an atom's weight of good, or more, except by His grace and mercy, and no atom's weight of evil, or more, except by His justice and wisdom. In His address, one witnesses the most delicate reproach towards His beloved ones. Yet along with that, He is the one who pardons their slips, forgives their sins, excuses their failings, rectifies their corruption, defends them, protects them, supports them, guarantees their welfare, saves them from every distress, and fulfils His promise to them. He is their Protector, besides whom they have no protector. He is their true Master and their Helper against their enemy. How excellent a Master, and how excellent a Helper!

When hearts witness from the Qur'an a great, merciful, generous, and beautiful King with such qualities, how could they not love Him and compete in drawing near to Him? How could they not spend their breaths in seeking His affection? He becomes dearer to them than everything else, His pleasure more precious to them than the pleasure of anything else. How could they not be occupied with His remembrance? His love, longing for Him, and intimacy with Him become their food, their sustenance, and their medicine, such that if they lose this, they are corrupted and destroyed, and their life brings them no benefit.

[Section: Those who acknowledge the Lord, glorified and exalted is He, as the Creator of the universe are of two kinds]

The first kind denies His separateness from His creation and says: He is neither separate nor immanent, neither inside the world nor outside it, neither above it nor below it, neither to its right nor its left, neither behind it nor in front of it, neither within it nor apart from it.

Al-Fatihah (the Opening chapter) refutes these people in two respects:

The first is the affirmation of His lordship over the universe. Pure lordship necessitates that the Lord be separate from the universe in His very essence, just as He is separate from it in lordship, attributes, and actions. Whoever does not affirm a Lord separate from the universe has not affirmed a Lord at all. For whoever denies separateness is necessarily bound by one of two matters, an inescapable necessity:

Either He is the very self of this universe, and in that case their statement holds, since the universe is not separate from His essence and self. From here entered the people of Oneness (Ahl al-Wahdah, the monists), who were first Mu'attilah (deniers of attributes) and then Ittihadiyyah (unionists).

Or he says: there is no Lord who is separate or immanent, neither inside nor outside, as the Dahriyyah (materialists) who deny the Creator have said.

As for this third statement, which combines two contradictories, affirming a Lord distinct from the universe while denying His separateness from it, and affirming a Creator who subsists in Himself, neither within the universe nor outside it, neither above nor below it, neither behind nor in front of it, neither to its right nor its left, it is a statement whose meaning is hidden. Minds cannot conceive it until they assent to it. When conceiving it is impossible for the mind, then assenting to it is even more impossible. It applies to pure non-existence and sheer negation, and its applicability to non-existence is more evident to minds and natural dispositions than its applicability to the Lord of the worlds.

Place this negation and these words that signify it upon impossible non-existence, then place them upon the exalted Essence, subsisting in Himself, who did not dwell in the universe and whom the universe did not contain. Then consider which of the two known things is more deserving of them.

Awaken yourself, and stand before Allah as one who reflects alone upon this matter, stripped of doctrines and their proponents, free of desire, partisanship, and tribal zeal, sincere in seeking guidance from Allah. Allah is too generous to disappoint a servant in this condition. This question requires no more than the affirmation of a Lord subsisting in Himself, separate from His creation. Indeed, this is the very substance of its meaning.

[Section: Those who affirm the Creator, exalted is He]

Then those who affirm the Creator, exalted is He, are of two kinds: people of monotheism (tawhid) and people of polytheism (shirk). The people of polytheism are of two kinds:

The first are those who associate partners with Him in His lordship and divinity, such as the Magians and those who resemble them among the Qadariyyah (those who deny divine decree). They affirm another creator alongside Allah, even if they do not say that he is equal to Him. The Magian Qadariyyah affirm creators of actions alongside Allah, whose actions are neither willed by Allah nor created by Him, and which proceed without His will. He has no power over them, and it is not He who made their doers agents of them. Rather, they themselves made their souls willing, desiring, and acting.

Thus the complete, absolute, and all-encompassing lordship of the universe refutes all these statements, for it necessitates His lordship over everything in it: its essences, attributes, movements, and actions.

The real position of the Magian Qadariyyah is that He, exalted is He, is not the Lord of the actions of living beings, and His lordship does not encompass them. How can it encompass what does not fall under His power, will, and creation? Moreover, in the generality of His praise there is what requires praising Him for the obedience of His creatures, since He is the one who helps them in it and grants them success in it. He is the one who willed it from them, as He said in more than one place in His Book: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾ [al-Insan 76:30]. So He is praised for having willed it for them and for having made them its doers by His power and will. He is therefore truly the one praised for it, while in their view they themselves are the ones praised for it, and praise for their actions belongs to them. In their view, there is no praise for Allah for the very act of their being its doers, nor for His reward and recompense for it.

As for the first point: their being its doers is by them, not by Him. As for the second: recompense is owed to Him as wages are owed by a hirer. So it is pure right belonging to them, which they have exchanged for it.

In His saying ﴿You alone we ask for help﴾ there is a clear refutation of them, for seeking help from Him can only be concerning something which is in His hand and under His power and will. How can one seek help from one in whose hand the act lies and who brings it into being, if He wills to bring it into being, and if He wills not to bring it into being, with one over whom that act is not in his hand, nor does it fall under his power or will?

In His saying ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ there is also a refutation of them. Absolute and complete guidance is what necessarily results in the attainment of being guided. Had it not been in His hand, exalted is He, and not theirs, they would not have asked Him for it. It includes guidance, clarification, success, empowerment, and making them guided. Their request is not merely the clarification and indication which the Qadariyyah supposed, for this alone does not bring about guidance nor save from ruin. It is available to others among the disbelievers, who preferred blindness to guidance and bought misguidance in exchange for guidance.

(Section)

Second category: those who associate partners with Him in His divinity (ilahiyyah). They acknowledge that He alone is the Lord of everything, its Sovereign and its Creator, and that He is their Lord and the Lord of their earliest forefathers, the Lord of the seven heavens, and the Lord of the Mighty Throne. Yet despite this, they worship other than Him, and they set up others alongside Him in love, obedience and veneration. These are the ones who "took rivals (andad) besides Allah." Such people have not fulfilled the due of "﴿You alone we worship﴾" (iyyaka na'budu). Although they have a share in "we worship You" (na'budu-ka), they have no share in "You alone we worship" (iyyaka na'budu), which implies: "We worship none but You, out of love, fear, hope, obedience and veneration." Thus "﴿You alone we worship﴾" is the realisation of this tawhid and the refutation of association in divinity (shirk fi al-ilahiyyah), just as "You alone we ask for help" (iyyaka nasta'in) is the realisation of tawhid of lordship (tawhid al-rububiyyah) and the refutation of associating others with Him in it. Likewise His saying: ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾. They are the people of tawhid, and they are the people who truly realise "﴿You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help﴾", whereas the people of association are the people of wrath and error.

(Section)

Reflect upon the secrets of the speech of the Lord, the Exalted, and the profound wisdom contained in the verses of the Glorious Book, which bears witness that it is the speech of the Lord of the worlds, and which bears witness for His Messenger that he is the truthful one whose truthfulness is confirmed. All of this follows from His wisdom and His praiseworthiness, and this is the meaning of His having created the heavens and the earth and what is between them "with truth" (bil-haqq). He did not create that in vain; rather He created it as an act proceeding from truth, leading to truth, and comprising truth. Truth thus precedes its creation, accompanies it, and is its ultimate end. For this reason He used the preposition "bi" (with), which indicates this meaning, rather than "li" (for), which by itself conveys the meaning of purpose. So "bi" conveys the meaning that the creation comprises truth which precedes it, accompanies it, and is its end. The truth that precedes it is that its issuing from His knowledge and wisdom; the source of His creation and command is the perfection of His knowledge and wisdom. By the perfection of these two attributes, what proceeds from the One characterised by them is entirely wise, beneficial and true. For this reason He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed you receive the Qur'an from One who is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾. He thus informed that the source of receiving it is the knowledge and wisdom of the Speaker, and whatever is of this kind is truth, justice, guidance and instruction.

Likewise the angels said to the wife of Abraham when she said: "Shall I give birth while I am an old woman, barren?" ﴿They said: "Thus says your Lord; indeed He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing."﴾ This refers back to His saying and His creation, namely the creation of a child for her in old age.

As for the accompanying truth of these created things, it is what they comprise of wisdoms, benefits, advantages, and signs that point servants to Allah, to His oneness, to His attributes, to the truthfulness of His messengers, and to the fact that meeting Him is true and beyond doubt. Whoever looks at existing things with the insight of his heart sees them like witnesses speaking of this; indeed their testimony is more complete than the testimony of mere report, because it is testimony of state which cannot admit falsehood. A discerning, insightful person does not contemplate any creature with true contemplation without finding it pointing to its Originator and Fashioner, to His oneness, to the perfection of His attributes and names, to the truthfulness of His messengers, and to the fact that meeting Him is true and beyond doubt. This is the Qur'an's method in guiding creatures to reason from the various kinds of created things and their conditions to establish the Maker, tawhid, the return (ma'ad), and prophethood. Sometimes it informs that He did not create His creation in vain or without purpose; sometimes it informs that He created them with truth; and sometimes it informs them and draws their attention to aspects of reflection and inference, by which to establish the truthfulness of what His messengers reported, until it makes clear to them that the messengers came to them only with what they witness as proofs of truth, and with what, if they contemplated it, they would find fixed in their innate nature and settled in their intellects; and that what they observe of His creation bears witness to what His messengers reported about His names, His attributes, His tawhid, meeting Him, and the existence of His angels. This is a great gate of faith, which Allah opens only for those for whom the precedence of happiness has been decreed; and it is the most noble knowledge a servant can attain in this abode.

I have clarified in another place that every movement observed in its various kinds is indicative of tawhid, prophethood and the return, by an easy, clear, demonstrative method. Likewise I mentioned in a letter to some companions, with clear proof, that the soul has fixed in the origin of its nature and creation the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger; and that if a person searched thoroughly, he would find this fixed in the essence of his soul, his self and his nature. So if a rational person contemplated the soul and its movement alone, he would extract from it faith in Allah, His attributes, the testimony that there is no god but Him, faith in His messengers, His angels and meeting Him. Only one upon whose heart the sun of guidance has shone, from whose heart the clouds of its unseen have cleared, and from whose heart the veil of ﴿Indeed we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾ has been removed, will believe this. Then there will appear to him a secret whose concealment had lasted long, and a dawn will shine for him whose night and darkness were his. So now pause at every word of His saying: ﴿Indeed in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers. And in your creation and what He disperses of living creatures are signs for a people who are certain ... And in the alternation of the winds are signs for a people who reason﴾.

Then reflect on the aspect of its being a sign, and upon what it was made a sign: is it for one single objective or for several objectives? Likewise with the rest of the Qur'an of this pattern, such as the end of Surah Al 'Imran, His saying in Surah al-Rum: ﴿And of His signs...﴾ to its end, His saying in Surah an-Naml: ﴿Praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen﴾ to the end of the verses, and many times that in the Qur'an. And like His saying in Surah adh-Dhariyat: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those who are certain, and in yourselves; will you not then see?﴾ ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾. All of this is part of the truth by which He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them. It is a truth existing in the existence of these creatures, inscribed in their pages, which every successful person reads, whether a writer or not, as it has been said:

Reflect upon the lines of existing things, for they
Are messages to you from the Supreme Assembly.
And He has inscribed in them, if you reflect on its inscription:
"Surely everything other than Allah is vain."

As for the truth which is the ultimate end of their creation, it is an end desired from the servants and an end desired for them. What is desired from them is that they know Allah, the Exalted, and the attributes of His perfection, the Mighty and Majestic, and that they worship Him and associate nothing with Him, so that He alone is their god, their object of worship, the one they obey and the one they love. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth their like; the command descends among them that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾.

He thus informed that He created the world so that His servants would know the perfection of His power and the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, and this entails knowing Him, knowing His names and attributes, and His tawhid.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾.

This end is what is desired from the servants: that they know their Lord and worship Him alone.

As for the end desired for them, it is recompense with justice and grace, reward and punishment. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did and recompense those who did good with the best﴾.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed the Hour is coming; I am almost concealing it, so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives﴾.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿That He may make clear to them that about which they differ, and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars﴾.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne, arranging the affair. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not remember? To Him is your return, all of you, as a promise of Allah, true. Indeed He originates creation and then repeats it that He may recompense those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice; and those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾.

So reflect now on how the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them comprised truth at the beginning, the end and the middle, and that they were created with truth, for truth, and as witnesses to truth.

He, the Exalted, denounced whoever supposed otherwise, saying: ﴿Did you then suppose that We created you in vain and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ Then He exalted Himself above this supposition, which contradicts His wisdom, His knowledge and His praiseworthiness, saying: ﴿So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth﴾. Reflect on what is in these two names, "the King, the Truth," of refutation of this supposition which His enemies imagined; for it contradicts the perfection of His kingship and His being the Truth, since the true King is the one to whom command and prohibition belong, who disposes of His creation by His word and His command. This is the difference between the King (malik) and the Owner (malik/malik), for the Owner is the one who disposes by his action, while the King is the one who disposes by his action and command. The Lord, the Exalted, is the Owner of the kingdom, so He disposes by His action and command. Whoever supposes that He created His creation in vain, without commanding or forbidding them, has impugned His kingship and has not measured Him with the measure due to Him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they did not measure Allah with His true measure when they said, "Allah did not send down anything upon a human being."﴾ Whoever denies the law of Allah, His command and His prohibition, and makes creatures like unregulated cattle, has impugned Allah's kingship and has not measured Him with His true measure. Likewise His being the God of creation requires the perfection of His essence, attributes and names, and the occurrence of His acts in the most perfect and complete manner. Just as His essence is the Truth, His word is true, His promise is true, His command is true, His acts are all true, and His recompense, which entails His law, His religion, and the Last Day, is true; whoever denies any of this has not described Allah as the Absolute Truth in every respect and from every standpoint. His being the Truth entails His law, His religion, His reward and His punishment. How then could one suppose of the King, the Truth, that He would create His creation in vain and leave them neglected, not commanding them, not forbidding them, not rewarding them, and not punishing them, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected?﴾

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Unregulated, not commanded and not forbidden."

Someone else said: "Not recompensed for good and evil, not rewarded, not punished." The two statements are mutually entailing: al-Shafi'i mentioned the cause of recompense, reward and punishment, which is command and prohibition; the other mentioned the purpose of command and prohibition, which is recompense, reward and punishment.

Then reflect on His saying afterwards: ﴿Did He not used to be a sperm-drop emitted? Then he became a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned﴾.

Whoever does not leave him neglected while he was a drop of sperm, but rather turned the drop and transformed it until it became more perfect than it was, which is the clot; then turned the clot until it became more perfect than it was, until He created it and proportioned its creation, arranging it by His direction and wisdom through the stages of its perfections, until its perfection ended in a complete human being; how then would He leave him neglected, not driving him to the end of the perfection for which he was created?

So when a rational, insightful person contemplates the states of the drop from its beginning to its end, they guide him to the return and to prophethood, just as they guide him to establishing the Maker, His tawhid and His attributes of perfection. Just as the states of the drop from its beginning to its end show the perfect power of the Originator and Fashioner of man, they likewise show the perfection of His wisdom, His knowledge and His kingship, and that He is the King, the Truth, exalted above creating it in vain and leaving it neglected after the perfection of its creation.

Reflect how, when His disbelieving enemies claimed that He did not command them or forbid them through His messengers, and that He would not resurrect them for reward and punishment, this claim of theirs amounted to saying that the creation of the heavens and the earth was vain. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieved, so woe to those who disbelieved from the Fire﴾.

When His enemies supposed that He had not sent a messenger to them and had not appointed a term for meeting Him, that supposition was their assumption that He created His creation in vain. Hence He, the Exalted, praised His servants who reflect upon His creatures, because their reflection led them to bear witness that He did not create them in vain; and when they knew and witnessed this, they knew that its creation entails His command, His prohibition, His reward and His punishment. So in their supplication they mentioned these two matters, saying: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You; so protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced; and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾.

When they knew that the creation of the heavens and the earth entails reward and punishment, they sought refuge in Allah from His punishment. Then they mentioned the faith to which their reflection upon the creation of the heavens and the earth led them, saying: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith, "Believe in your Lord," so we believed﴾. The fruit of their reflection on the creation of the heavens and the earth was acknowledgment of Him, the Exalted, of His oneness, of His religion, of His messengers, of His reward and of His punishment. They therefore sought a means to Him through their faith, which is among the greatest of His favours upon them, toward the forgiveness of their sins, the expiation of their evil deeds, and their admission among the righteous into His Garden which He promised them; and that is the completion of His blessing upon them. Thus they sought a means through His earlier blessing upon them to His later blessing upon them; and that is a means, through obedience, to His honour, and it is one of the means to Him, the means He commanded them to seek in His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and seek the means (wasilah) to Him﴾. He also informed about the distinguished of His servants, that they seek the means to Him, when He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means to their Lord, which of them is nearest﴾.

Moreover, in these two verses there are wonderful secrets which I have mentioned in the book (al-Tuhfah al-Makkiyyah fi Bayan al-Millah al-Ibrahimiyyah).

Thus their sound reflection on the creation of the heavens and the earth yielded that He did not create them in vain, and yielded faith in Allah, His messenger, His religion, His law, His reward and His punishment, and seeking a means to Him through obedience and faith in Him.

What we have mentioned in this section is a drop from a sea without shore, so do not consider it long, for it is a treasure from the treasures of knowledge which does not suit every soul, nor does every deprived person accept it, and Allah singles out whom He wills with His mercy.

(Section: on the dispute among people regarding which is superior, patience or gratitude)

Ibn al-Jawzi relates three opinions on this:

The first: that patience is superior.
The second: that gratitude is superior.
The third: that they are equal, as 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If patience and gratitude were two camels, I would not mind which of them I rode."

We shall mention what each group argued, and what supports or weakens its argument, with the help and success of Allah.

Section: The proponents of patience said: Allah, glorified is He, has praised patience and those who possess it, commended it, commanded it, and tied to it the good of this world and the Hereafter. Allah mentions it in His Book in about ninety places. And the texts and hadiths already cited about it and its excellence indicate that it is superior to gratitude. It suffices for its excellence the saying of the Prophet: "The one who eats and is grateful is like the one who fasts and is patient." He mentioned this in the context of preferring patience and elevating its rank over gratitude, for he equated the grateful with the patient and likened him to it, and the rank of the compared-to is higher than the rank of the one compared. This is like his saying: "The one who persists in wine is like a worshipper of idols," and similar examples. They said: When we weigh the texts about patience against those about gratitude, we find the texts about patience to be many times more numerous. For this reason, since prayer and jihad are the best deeds, the hadiths about them occur in all chapters; you will not find more prophetic hadiths in any chapter than in the chapters on prayer and jihad. They also said: Patience enters every chapter, indeed every issue of religion, and for this reason it is to faith as the head is to the body. They also said: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, attached increase to gratitude, saying: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed, "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you"﴾, and attached reward without reckoning to patience. Also, He, glorified is He, stated the reward of the grateful without qualification, saying: "And Allah will reward the grateful," and He restricted the reward of the patient by good conduct, saying: ﴿And We will surely reward those who were patient with their best reward for what they used to do﴾. They also said: It has been authentically reported from the Prophet that he said: Allah, the Exalted, says:

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 1, verse 2 (part 7 of 14):

"Every deed of the son of Adam is his own, except fasting, for it is Mine and I will reward it for it."

In another wording:
