"Every deed of the son of Adam is multiplied, a good deed being credited tenfold. Allah the Exalted said: Except fasting, for it is Mine and I will reward it for it."

This is only because fasting is patience of the soul (sabr, patient endurance) and its restraint from its desires, as in the same hadith: he gives up his desire, his food and his drink for My sake. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said to the one who asked him about the best deeds: "Upon you is fasting, for there is nothing equal to it."

Since patience is the restraining of the soul from answering the call of desire, and this is the essence of fasting, for fasting is the restraining of the soul from answering the call of the desire for food, drink and intercourse, the patience mentioned in His saying ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ was interpreted as fasting, and Ramadan was named the month of patience.

Some of the early generations (al-salaf) said: "Fasting is half of patience." This is because patience is the restraining of the soul from answering the call of desire and anger. The soul desires a thing for the pleasure of attaining it, and gets angry out of aversion to what pains it. Fasting is patience only against the demand of desire, namely the desire of the belly and the private parts, not the demand of anger. But the completeness and perfection of fasting is the soul's patience against answering the call of both. The Prophet ﷺ indicated this in the sound hadith, his saying: "When one of you is fasting on a day, let him not behave foolishly or shout. If someone reviles him or fights with him, let him say: I am fasting." So he guided to the moderation of the powers of desire and anger, and that the fasting person should guard himself against the corruption of both for the sake of his fast. The one corrupts his fast, and the other nullifies its reward, as he said in another hadith: "Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need that he give up his food and drink."

They said: The superiority of patience over gratitude is sufficient in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today for their patience; they are the triumphant.﴾ So He made their triumph the reward of their patience. He also said: ﴿And Allah is with the patient.﴾ Nothing equals His companionship with His servant. As one of the gnostics ('arifun) said: "The patient have gone with the good of this world and the Hereafter, for they have attained the companionship of Allah."

He said: ﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord, for indeed you are before Our eyes.﴾ This includes protection, guardianship and preservation for the one who is patient with His judgment.

He promised the patient three things, each of which is better than this world and all that is in it: His prayers upon them, His mercy toward them, and His singling them out for guidance in His saying: ﴿Those upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and those are the guided.﴾ This implies that guidance is confined to them. He also informed that patience is among the matters of resolve (azm al-umur) in two verses of His Book, and He commanded His Messenger to emulate the patience of the Messengers of firm resolve, and this has been mentioned before.

They said: The evidence has shown that renouncing the world and being content with little of it, as far as possible, is better than accumulating from it. Renunciation of it is the state of the patient, and accumulation of it is the state of the grateful. They said: The Messiah, upon him blessings and peace, was asked about two men who passed by a treasure: one of them went past it without turning to it, and the other took it and spent it in obedience to Allah the Exalted. Which of them is better? He said: "The one who did not turn to it and turned away from it is better in the sight of Allah."

They said: What confirms this is that the keys to the treasures of the earth were offered to the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not take them, and said: "Rather, I would be hungry one day and full one day." Had he taken them, he would have spent them in seeking Allah's pleasure and obedience to Him. So he preferred the station of patience over them and renunciation of them.

They said: It is known that human perfection lies in three matters: knowledge that one knows, deeds that one performs, and states (ahwal) that follow from one's knowledge and deeds.

The best of knowledge, deed and state is knowledge of Allah, His names, attributes and actions, and acting in accordance with His pleasure, and the heart's attraction toward Him through love, fear and hope. This is the most noble of what is in this world, and its reward is the most noble of what is in the Hereafter. The most exalted aims are knowing Allah and loving Him, delight in His nearness, longing for meeting Him, and savoring His remembrance. This is the greatest happiness of this world and the Hereafter, and it is the end that is sought for its own sake. The servant perceives fully that this is the very essence of happiness only when the veil is lifted for him, he departs this world and enters the Hereafter. Otherwise, in this world, even if he perceives something of it, his perception is not complete, because of the obstacles he faces and the trials with which he is tested. Otherwise, happiness in reality is nothing but that.

All knowledge and cognition follows this knowledge, being desired for its sake. Knowledge varies in its excellence according to how far it leads to this knowledge and how far it is from it. Every knowledge that leads more closely to the knowledge of Allah, His names and attributes is higher than what is below it. Likewise with the state of the heart: every state that is closer to the goal for which it was created is more noble than what is below it. Likewise with deeds: every deed that is closer to attaining this goal is better than other deeds. For this reason prayer and jihad are among the best deeds, being the most conducive to the goal. So it must be, for whatever thing is closer to the end is better than what is far from it. So the deed that prepares the heart and readies it for knowing Allah, His names and attributes, and for loving Him, fearing Him and hoping in Him, is better than what is not so. When several deeds share in this leading, the best of them is the closest to this destination. For this reason acts of obedience share in this leading and are therefore sought by Allah, while sins share in veiling the heart and cutting it off from this end, and so they are forbidden. The effect of acts of obedience and sins is according to their degrees.

Here is a matter that must be noticed: a particular deed may be better for one person than for another. A wealthy man who has much wealth, whose soul does not allow him to give up any of it, his giving charity and preferring others over himself is better for him than standing in night prayer and fasting by day voluntarily. A brave man whom the enemy fears for his might, standing in the ranks for an hour and fighting Allah's enemies, is better than Hajj, fasting and voluntary charity. A scholar who knows the Sunnah, the lawful and the unlawful, and the paths of good and evil, mixing with people, teaching them and advising them in their religion, is better than withdrawing from them and emptying his time for prayer, recitation of the Qur'an and glorification. A ruler whom Allah has appointed to judge among His servants, who sits for an hour to examine injustices, to give the wronged his right against the wrongdoer, to establish the prescribed punishments, to support the righteous and suppress the falsifier, is better than years of worship by someone else. And one whose desire for women dominates him, his fasting is more beneficial to him and better than the remembrance and charity of another. Consider the Prophet's appointment of Amr ibn al-As and Khalid ibn al-Walid and others among his commanders and agents, and his not appointing Abu Dhar, but saying to him: "I see you are weak, and I love for you what I love for myself. Do not be put in charge of two people, nor take charge of an orphan's property." He commanded him and others to fast, and said: "Upon you is fasting, for there is nothing equal to it." And he commanded another not to become angry, and a third to keep his tongue moist with the remembrance of Allah.

Whenever Allah wills perfection for a servant, He enables him to exert his full effort in what he is prepared for and suited to, which has been readied for him. When he exerts his full effort in it, he surpasses others in it, as it has been said:

"He kept outstripping until his envier said: This is a short path to the heights."

This is like a patient who complains of stomach pain, for example. If he uses the medicine for that ailment, he benefits from it. If he uses the medicine for headache, it does not reach his illness. A tyrannical stinginess, for example, is one of the destructive things, and fasting for a hundred years or standing in its night prayer will not remove it. Likewise, the disease of following desire and self-admiration is not suited by abundant recitation of the Qur'an, exerting effort in knowledge, remembrance and asceticism. It is removed only by expelling it from the heart with its opposite. If one were asked which is better, bread or water, the answer would be that in its place this is better, and in its place that is better.

When you know this principle, giving wealth in gratitude is a righteous deed through which a state is produced in the heart. It is a remedy for the disease in the heart that prevents it from its goal. As for the poor ascetic, he has been freed from this disease and this remedy, and his strength is free to exert full effort in attaining the goal.

Then they raised an objection to themselves, saying: "If it is said that the Law has urged deeds, they answered it by saying: When a physician praises a medicine, this does not show that the medicine is desired for its own sake, nor that it is better than the healing it produces. Rather, deeds are a cure for the diseases of the hearts, and the diseases of the hearts are generally not perceived. So the urging was directed toward the deed that is intended, which is the healing of the heart. The poor man who takes your charity draws out from you the disease of stinginess, as the cupper draws from you the deadly blood."

They said: When this is understood, it becomes clear that the state of the patient is like the state of one who guards his health and strength, and the state of the grateful is like the state of one who treats himself with various medicines to remove the sources of sickness.

Chapter: The grateful said: "You have overstepped your station, and you have preferred a station other than the better one. You have put the means before the end, what is sought for another before what is sought for itself, the complete deed before the more complete, and the excellent before the most excellent. You have not known the due right of gratitude, nor have you fulfilled its rank. He, the Exalted, has joined His remembrance, which is the purpose of creation, with His remembrance, and both are the purpose of creation, while patience is a servant to them, a means to them, and a help toward them." He said: ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you; and be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.﴾

He joined gratitude with faith, and informed that He has no purpose in punishing His creatures if they are grateful and believe in Him. He said: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?﴾ That is, if you fulfill that for which you were created, which is gratitude and faith, then what would I do with your punishment?

Moreover, He informed that the people of gratitude are those singled out for His favor among His servants. He said: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others that they might say: Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us? Is not Allah most knowing of the grateful?﴾ He divided people into the grateful and the ungrateful. The most hateful things to Him are disbelief and its people, and the most beloved things to Him are gratitude and its people. He said concerning man: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way, whether he is grateful or ungrateful.﴾

And His prophet Solomon said: ﴿This is from the favor of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful, his gratitude is only for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous.﴾ He said: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you; but if you deny, indeed My punishment is severe.﴾ He said: ﴿If you deny, indeed Allah is free of need from you, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief; and if you are grateful, He approves it for you.﴾

This is abundant in the Qur'an. He, the Exalted, contrasts gratitude with disbelief, as its opposite. He said: ﴿And Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all, and Allah will reward the grateful.﴾ The grateful are those who remained firm upon the blessing of faith and did not turn back on their heels. He, the Exalted, tied increase to gratitude, and His increase has no end, just as His gratitude has no end. He, the Exalted, made many rewards subject to His will, as in His saying: ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills.﴾ And His saying concerning the answering of prayer: ﴿So He removes that for which you call upon Him, if He wills.﴾ And His saying concerning provision: ﴿He gives provision to whom He wills.﴾ Concerning forgiveness: ﴿He forgives whom He wills.﴾ And repentance: ﴿And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills.﴾ But the reward of gratitude He stated without qualification wherever it was mentioned, as in His saying: ﴿And We will reward the grateful,﴾ and ﴿And Allah will reward the grateful.﴾

When the enemy of Allah, Iblis, recognized the status of gratitude, that it is among the greatest and highest stations, he made his aim to strive to cut people off from it. He said: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and behind them, from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful.﴾

Allah, the Exalted, described the grateful as few among His servants. He said: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful.﴾

Imam Ahmad reported from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard a man saying: "O Allah, make me among the few." He said: "What is this?" The man said: "O Commander of the Faithful, Allah said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few,﴾ and He said: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful,﴾ and He said: ﴿Except those who believed and did righteous deeds, and few are they.﴾" Umar said: "You have spoken the truth."

Allah, the Exalted, praised the first messenger He sent to the people of the earth for his gratitude. He said: ﴿Offspring of those whom We carried with Noah; indeed, he was a grateful servant.﴾

The specific mention of Noah here and the addressing of the servants as his descendants is an indication of following him, for he is their second father, since Allah the Exalted did not make for the creation after the Flood any offspring except from his descendants, as He said: ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors.﴾ So the descendants were commanded to imitate their father in gratitude, for he was a grateful servant.

He, the Exalted, informed that He is worshipped only by those who are grateful to Him, so whoever does not give thanks to Him is not among the people of His worship. He said: ﴿And be grateful to Allah, if it is Him that you worship.﴾ (2:172)

He commanded His servant Moses to receive what He gave him of prophethood, messengership and speaking directly with gratitude. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O Moses, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and My speech, so take what I have given you and be among the grateful.﴾

The first command Allah enjoined upon man, after he came to understand, was gratitude to Him and to his parents. He said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man concerning his parents; his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years: Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final destination.﴾

He informed that His pleasure lies in His being thanked. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if you are grateful, He is pleased with it for you.﴾

Allah praised His intimate friend Abraham for thanking His blessings. He said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. Grateful for His favors; He chose him and guided him to a straight path.﴾

He informed about him that he was "a nation," that is, an exemplar to be followed in goodness; that he was "devoutly obedient" (qanitan) to Allah, and the qanit is one who is obedient and persistent in his obedience; and that the hanif is one who turns to Allah and turns away from all else. Then He concluded for him with these attributes by saying that he was grateful for His favors, thus making gratitude the goal of His intimate friend.

He, the Exalted, informed that gratitude is the purpose of His creation and His command, indeed the very goal for which He created His servants. ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing, sight and hearts, that you might be grateful.﴾

So this is the goal of creation and the goal of command. He said: ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were humble; so fear Allah that you may be grateful.﴾

It is possible that His saying "that you may be grateful" is a reason for His decree of victory for them, and for His command to them to be mindful of Him, and for both together. This is the apparent meaning. So gratitude is the goal of creation and of command. He has explicitly stated that it is the goal of His command and of His sending of the Messenger, in His saying: ﴿Just as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, reciting to you Our verses, purifying you, teaching you the Book and wisdom, and teaching you what you did not know. So remember Me, I will remember you, and be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.﴾

They said: Gratitude is desired for its own sake, while patience is desired for something else. Patience is praised only because it leads to and delivers to gratitude; so it is a servant of gratitude.

It is established in the two Sahihs from the Prophet ﷺ that he stood in prayer until his feet swelled. It was said to him: "Do you do this when Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins?" He said: "Should I not be a grateful servant?"

It is established in the Musnad and in al-Tirmidhi that the Prophet ﷺ said to Mu'adh: "By Allah, I love you, so do not forget to say at the end of every prayer: O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya and Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, who said: "Among the supplications of the Prophet ﷺ was: O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well."

He said: Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, saying: Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Talq ibn Habib, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever is given four things has been given the good of this world and the Hereafter: a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, a body patient in trials, and a wife who does not betray him in herself or in his property."

He also mentioned, from a hadith of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aisha, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah does not bestow a blessing upon a servant and then he knows that it is from Allah, except that Allah records his gratitude for it. And Allah does not know a servant to feel remorse for a sin, except that Allah forgives him before he asks forgiveness. A man buys a garment for a dinar, wears it and praises Allah; it does not reach his knees before he is forgiven."

It is established in Sahih Muslim from him ﷺ that he said: "Indeed Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a morsel and praises Him for it, and drinks a draught and praises Him for it."

Thus this great reward, which is the greatest kind of reward, comes in return for his gratitude through praise, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the good pleasure of God is greater﴾.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Salih, who said: Abu Zuhayr Yahya ibn Atarid al-Qurashi narrated to us, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:
"God does not grant a servant gratitude and then deprive him of increase." Because God, exalted is He, says: ﴿If you give thanks, I will surely increase you﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said:
"God lets one enjoy a blessing for as long as He wills. If he is not thankful for it, it turns into a punishment for him."
For this reason, they used to call gratitude the preserver, because it preserves existing blessings, and the attractor, because it attracts lost blessings.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said to a man from Hamadhan:
"Blessing is connected to gratitude, and gratitude is linked to increase. The two are yoked together, so the increase from God will never cease until the gratitude from the servant ceases."

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said:
"Bind God's blessings with the gratitude to God."
He used to say: Gratitude is the fetter of blessings.

Mutarrif ibn Abdullah said: "To be granted well-being and be thankful is dearer to me than to be tested and be patient."

Al-Hasan said: "Frequently mention these blessings, for mentioning them is gratitude."

God commanded His Prophet to speak of his Lord's blessing, saying: ﴿As for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾.

God, exalted is He, loves that His servant be seen to bear the mark of His blessing, for that is gratitude for it through the tongue of circumstance.

Ali ibn al-Ja'd said: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri say: David, peace be upon him, said: "Praise be to God, praise as is fitting to the nobility of His face and the majesty of His glory." Then God revealed to him: "O David, you have fatigued the angels."

Shu'ba said: Al-Muffadal ibn Fadala narrated to us, from Abu Raja' al-Utaridi, who said: Imran ibn Husayn came out to us, wearing a khazz (silk) cloak which we had never seen him wear before or after, and he said: The Messenger of God said:
"When God bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant."

In the Sahifa of Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet, who said:
"Eat, drink, and give charity without pride or extravagance, for God loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant."

Shu'ba mentioned from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from his father, who said:
"I came to the Messenger of God while I was in shabby appearance. He said: Do you have any wealth? I said: Yes. He said: What kind of wealth? I said: Every kind; God has given me camels, horses, slaves, and sheep. He said: When God has given you wealth, let it be seen upon you."

In some mursal (hadiths whose chain omits a companion) reports: "God loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant in his eating and drinking."

Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Maqri narrated from Abu Ma'mar, from Bukayr ibn Abdullah, raising it (to the Prophet):
"Whoever is given good and it is seen upon him is called the beloved of God, one who speaks of God's blessing. Whoever is given good and it is not seen upon him is called the hated of God, one who opposes God's blessing."

Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: "It used to be said: whoever recognizes God's blessing in his heart and praises Him with his tongue has not completed that until he sees the increase, because of God's saying: ﴿If you give thanks, I will surely increase you﴾."
He also said: "Among the gratitude for a blessing is to speak of it."

God, exalted is He, has said (in a hadith qudsi):
"O son of Adam, when you wallow in My blessings while you wallow in My disobedience, beware of Me, lest I strike you down among your sins. O son of Adam, fear Me and sleep wherever you wish."

Al-Sha'bi said: "Gratitude is half of faith, and certainty is all of faith." Abu Qilaba said: "The worldly life you have thanked God for will not harm you."

Al-Hasan said: "When God bestows blessings upon a people, He asks them for gratitude. If they give thanks to Him, He is able to increase them; if they deny Him, He is able to send His blessing upon them as punishment." God, glorified is He, has censured the ingrate (kanud), who is the one who does not give thanks for His blessings.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord﴾ (100:6): he counts the calamities and forgets the blessings.

The Prophet informed that women are most of the people of the Fire for this reason. He said:
"If you were kind to one of them all your life, and then she saw something from you (she disliked), she would say: I have never seen any good from you."

If this is the case with abandoning gratitude for the blessing of a husband, which in reality is from God, then how about one who abandons gratitude for God's blessing?

O you who oppress in your deeds, while oppression is returned upon the oppressor,
How long will you, and how long, complain of calamities and forget the blessings?

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of God said:
"Speaking of blessings is gratitude, and leaving them is disbelief. Whoever does not give thanks for little does not give thanks for much. Whoever does not thank people does not thank God. Community is blessing, and division is punishment."

Mutarrif ibn Abdullah said: "I considered well-being and gratitude, and I found in them the good of this world and the Hereafter. To be granted well-being, and to be granted well-being and be thankful, is dearer to me than to be tested and be patient."

Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani saw a porter carrying his load, and he was saying: "Praise be to God, I seek God's forgiveness."
He (Bakr) said: "I waited until he set down what was on his back, and I said to him: Can you not do better than this?"
He said: "Yes, I do much better: I recite the Book of God. But the servant is between a blessing and a sin, so I praise God for His abundant blessings and seek His forgiveness for my sins."
I said: "The porter is more learned in jurisprudence than Bakr."

Al-Tirmidhi mentioned from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, who said:
"The Messenger of God went out to his companions and recited to them Surat al-Rahman from its beginning to its end. They were silent. He said: I recited it to the jinn on the night of the jinn, and they gave a better response than you. Every time I came to His saying ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾ (55:13), they said: 'None of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny. To You be praise.'"

Mash'ar said: When it was said to the family of David, ﴿Work, O family of David, in gratitude﴾ (34:13), there was not an hour during which there was not someone from them standing in prayer.

Awn ibn Abdullah said: Some jurists said: "I have seen in my affairs that I have not seen any good except that it was accompanied by evil, except well-being and gratitude. For many a grateful person is in trial, and many a person enjoying well-being is not grateful. So when you ask God, ask for both of them together."

Abu Mu'awiya said: Umar ibn al-Khattab wore a shirt, and when it reached his collarbone, he said: "Praise be to God who clothed me with what conceals my nakedness and with which I adorn myself in my life." Then he stretched out his hands and saw something extending beyond his hands, so he cut it off. Then he began to narrate, saying: I heard the Messenger of God say:
"Whoever wears a garment which I think is new, and says when it reaches his collarbone, or he said before it reaches his knees, the like of that, and then takes his worn garment and clothes a poor man with it, will remain in the protection of God, in the safeguard of God, and in the shelter of God, alive and dead, for as long as any of that garment remains."

Awn ibn Abdullah said: A man wore a new shirt and praised God, and he was forgiven. Another man said: "Let me go back until I buy a shirt, then I will wear it and praise God."

Shurayh said: "No servant is afflicted with a calamity except that God has three blessings upon him in it: that it was not in his religion; that it was not greater than it was; and that it was inevitable, and it has happened."

Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said: "Whenever Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz turned his gaze to a blessing God had bestowed upon him, he would say: O God, I seek refuge in You from exchanging Your blessing for disbelief, from denying it after I have known it, and from forgetting it and not praising You for it."

Rawh ibn al-Qasim said: A man became an ascetic, and said: "I will not eat khabisa (a sweet confection); I cannot give thanks for it." Al-Hasan said: "This man is a fool. Can he give thanks for cold water?"

In some of the divine reports, God, mighty and majestic is He, says:
"Son of Adam, My good comes down to you, and your evil ascends to Me. I show affection to you with blessings, and you show hatred to Me with sins. A noble angel does not cease to ascend to Me from you with an ugly deed."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Abu Ali narrated to me, who said: I used to hear a neighbour of mine saying at night:
"O my God, Your good descends upon me, and my evil ascends to You. How many a noble angel has ascended to You from me with an ugly deed! Yet You, despite Your self-sufficiency from me, show affection to me with blessings, while I, despite my poverty and need of You, show hatred to You with sins, and in that You protect me, conceal me, and provide for me."

When Abu al-Mughira was asked, "How have you risen, Abu Muhammad?" he would say: "We have risen drowned in blessings, unable to give thanks. Our Lord shows affection to us though He is independent of us, and we show hatred to Him though we are in need of Him."

Abdullah ibn Tha'laba said: "My God, from Your generosity is that You are obeyed and not disobeyed; and from Your forbearance is that You are disobeyed and it is as if You do not see. What era has passed in which the inhabitants of Your earth did not disobey You, while You are constantly doing good?"

Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, whenever he wore a new garment, would say: "In the name of God, and praise be to God."

Anas ibn Malik said: "No servant devotes himself to worshipping God except that God commands the heavens and the earth to convey his provision, and places it in the hands of the children of Adam, who work for it, until it is delivered to him. Indeed, the servant before Him has made it obligatory upon Him to give thanks, and his father found the Rich, the Praiseworthy, having servants who are poor, who take His provision and give thanks to Him."

Yunus ibn Ubayd said: A man said to Abu Tamima, "How have you risen?" He said: "I have risen between two blessings, and I do not know which of them is greater: sins which God has concealed, so no one can reproach me for them; and affection which God has cast into the hearts of His servants, which my deeds cannot reach."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated from Sa'id al-Maqbari, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Salam, that Musa, peace be upon him, said:
"O Lord, what is the gratitude that is fitting for You?"
He said: "Your tongue will not cease to be moist with My remembrance."

Suhayl ibn Abi Salih narrated from his father, from Abu Hurayra, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man of the Ansar from the people of Quba invited the Prophet, and we went with him. When he had eaten and washed his hands, he said: "Praise be to God who feeds and is not fed, who has guided us and fed us and given us drink, and every good trial He has tested us with. Praise be to God, not one who is left or dispensed with, nor one who is ungrateful, nor one who is independent of Him. Praise be to God who feeds from food, gives drink from drink, clothes from nakedness, guides from error, gives sight from blindness, and has favoured us above many of His creatures with a clear favour. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds."

In the Musnad of al-Hasan ibn al-Salah, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God said:
"God does not bestow a blessing upon a servant in his family, his wealth, or his children, and then he says: 'What God wills; there is no power except with God,' and then he sees in it a calamity other than death."

It is mentioned from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Prophet entered upon her and saw a fallen piece of bread. He wiped it and said: "O Aisha, honour the neighbourhood of God's blessings, for they are the ones that flee from a household, and they nearly return to them."
Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned it.

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Salih, from Abu Imran al-Juni, from Abu al-Khald, who said: I read in the matter of David that he said: "O Lord, how can I give thanks, when I cannot reach Your thanks except through Your blessings?"
He said: Then revelation came to him: "O David, do you not know that what you have of blessings is from Me?" He said: "Yes, my Lord." He said: "Then I am content with that from you as thanks."

Abdullah ibn Ahmad said: Abu Musa al-Ansari narrated to us, from Abu al-Walid, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: Among the supplications of David was: "Glory be to Him who draws out gratitude through giving, and draws out supplication through trial."

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, who said: God revealed to David: "Love Me, and love My worship, and make Me beloved to My servants." He said: "My Lord, this is Your love and the love of Your worship. How can I make You beloved to Your servants?" He said: "Remind them of Me, for they do not mention of Me except what is good." Exalted is the majesty of our Lord, blessed is His name, high is His majesty, sanctified are His names, glorified is His praise, and there is no god but He.

Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq ibn Imran narrated to us, who said: I heard Wahb say: "I found in the book of the family of David: By My might, whoever holds fast to Me, even if the heavens with those in them and the earths with those in them plot against him, I will make for him a way out from among them. And whoever does not hold fast to Me, I will cut off his hands from the means of the heavens, and cause the earth to swallow him from beneath his feet, and place him in the air, then leave him to himself. Sufficient is Me for My servant, when My servant is in My obedience: I give him before he asks Me, and I respond to him before he calls upon Me. I know his need better than he does, and what is gentle to him from himself."

Ahmad said: Yasar narrated to us, Hafs narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, who said: David, peace be upon him, had divided the hours of the night and day among his family, so that there was not an hour of night or day but that someone from the family of David was standing in prayer during it. He said: So God, blessed and exalted is He, mentioned them in this verse: ﴿Work, O family of David, in gratitude; but few of My servants are grateful﴾ (34:13).

Ahmad said: Jabir ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Mughira ibn Uyayna, who said: David said: "My Lord, has any of Your creatures spent the night remembering You longer than I have?" God revealed to him: "Yes, the frog." And God sent down upon him: ﴿Work, O family of David, in gratitude; but few of My servants are grateful﴾. He said: "My Lord, how can I bear to give You thanks, when You are the One who bestows blessings upon me, then You grant me, upon the blessing, the gratitude, then You increase me blessing after blessing? The blessings are from You and the gratitude is from You, so how can I bear to give You thanks?" He said: "Now you have known Me, O David."

Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Subayh, from al-Hasan, who said: The Prophet of God, David, said:
"My God, if every hair of mine had two tongues glorifying You night, day, and for all time, I would not fulfil the right of one blessing."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from Abu Imran al-Juni, from Abu al-Khald, who said: Musa said: "O Lord, how can I give thanks to You, when the smallest blessing You have placed with me from Your blessings is not repaid by my entire deed?" He said: Then revelation came to him: "O Musa, now you have given Me thanks."

Bakr ibn Abdullah said: "No servant has ever said 'Praise be to God' except that a blessing became due upon him by his saying 'Praise be to God.' Its recompense is that he says 'Praise be to God,' and then another blessing comes, and the blessings of God do not run out."

Al-Hasan said: The Prophet of God heard a man say "Praise be to God for Islam," and he said: "Indeed, you praise God for a great blessing."

Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: I heard Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan say:
"No servant has said a word more beloved to God, or more complete in gratitude in His sight, than saying: 'Praise be to God who has bestowed blessings upon us and guided us to Islam.'"

Sulayman al-Taymi said: God, glorified is He, bestows blessings upon His servant according to his capacity, and obliges them to give thanks according to their ability. Al-Hasan, whenever he began his speech, would say: "Praise be to God. O Allah, our Lord, to You be praise for creating us, providing for us, guiding us, teaching us, rescuing us, and relieving us. To You be praise for Islam and the Qur'an. To You be praise for family, wealth, and well-being. You have humbled our enemy, expanded our provision, manifested our security, united our division, and made our well-being good. And for all that we have asked You, our Lord, You have given us; so to You be praise for that, abundant praise. To You be praise for every blessing You have bestowed upon us, in the past or the present, in secret or in public, in particular or in general, for the living or the dead, for the present or the absent. To You be praise until You are pleased, and to You be praise when You are pleased."

Al-Hasan said: Musa said: "O Lord, how can the son of Adam render the gratitude due for what You did for him? You created him with Your hand, breathed into him of Your spirit, lodged him in Your garden, and commanded the angels, so they prostrated to him." He said: "O Musa, he knows that this is from Me, so let him praise Me for it. That is the gratitude for what I did for him."

Sa'd ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi said: God named Nuh a grateful servant (17:3) only because he did not wear a new garment or eat food without praising God. Ali ibn Abi Talib, whenever he came out of the toilet, would rub his belly with his hand and say: "How great a blessing! If only the servants knew its gratitude."

Mukhallad ibn al-Husayn said: It used to be said: gratitude is abandoning sins.

Abu Hazim said: "A blessing that does not bring one near to God is a trial." Sulayman said: "Remembering blessings begets love for God."

Hammad ibn Zayd said: Layth narrated to us, from Abu Burda, who said: I came to Madina and met Abdullah ibn Salam, who said to me: "Would you not enter a house which the Prophet entered, and we will feed you sawiq (a mash of barley or wheat) and dates?" Then he said: "When God gathers the people tomorrow, He will remind them of what He bestowed upon them. The servant will say: 'What is the sign of that?' He will say: 'The sign of that is that you were in such and such distress, and you called upon Me, and I relieved it. The sign of that is that you were on such and such a journey, and you asked Me for company, and I accompanied you.'" He continues reminding him until he remembers, then He says: "The sign of that is that you proposed to such and such a woman, daughter of such and such, and others proposed to her along with you, and I married her to you and turned them away." He stands His servant before Him and enumerates His blessings upon him. He wept, then wept again, and said: "I truly hope that God will not seat a servant before Him and then punish him."

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Uthman, from Ibn Sirin, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God said:
"On the Day of Resurrection, blessings, good deeds, and bad deeds will be brought. God, mighty and majestic is He, will say to one of His blessings: 'Take your right from his good deeds.' Not a good deed will be left for him except that it is carried off by it."

Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani said: A matter befalls the servant, and he asks God, and it is averted from him. Then Satan comes to him and weakens his gratitude, saying: "The matter was easier than you think." Or he says: "Does not the servant say: 'The matter was harder than I thought, but God averted it from me'?"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned from Sadaqa ibn Yasar, who said: While David, peace be upon him, was in his prayer niche, an ant passed by him. He looked at it, reflected on its creation, and marvelled at it, and said: "God does not care for this." So God gave it speech, and it said: "O David, does your self make you proud? By Him in whose hand is my soul, I am more grateful for what God has given me of His bounty than you are for what God has given you of His bounty."

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 1, verse 2 (part 9 of 14)**

Ayyub said: Among the greatest of Allah's blessings upon His servant is that he be trusted with what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: It used to be said, "No one is a faqih (jurist) who does not regard affliction as a blessing and ease as a calamity."

Zazan said: Among what is owed to Allah by the one who possesses a blessing, in recognition of His blessing, is that he not use it as a means to disobedience.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Mahmud al-Warraq recited to me:

*If my gratitude is itself a blessing from Allah,*
*then how can gratitude come about except by His grace?*

*For a blessing of this kind, gratitude is owed to Him,*
*when it touches you with happiness, its joy spreads.*

*Though the days grow long and life continues,*
*in each of them there is a favor from Him.*

*And if it touches you with hardship, it brings reward after it,*
*though illusions and land and sea grow narrow with it.*

Al-Darawardi related from Amr ibn Abi Amr, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, meaning Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said:

"Indeed, the believer in My sight is like every good: he praises Me, and I take his soul from between his two flanks."

Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir passed by a young man who was flirting with a woman, and said: "O young man, this is not the recompense for the blessings of Allah upon you."

Hammad ibn Salama related from Thabit, who said: Abu al-'Aliya said: "I truly hope that no servant will perish between two things: a blessing for which he praises Allah, and a sin for which he seeks forgiveness."

Ibn al-Sammak wrote to Muhammad ibn al-Hasan when he was appointed judge in al-Raqqa: "As to what follows: let taqwa (God-consciousness) be your concern in every situation, and fear Allah regarding every blessing He has bestowed upon you, lest you be ungrateful for it while using it in disobedience. For blessings carry both a proof and a consequence. Their proof is the obedience they bring; their consequence is a lack of gratitude for them. So may Allah pardon you for every gratitude you neglected, every sin you committed, and every right you fell short of."

Al-Rabi' ibn Abi Rashid passed by a man afflicted with a chronic disability. He sat and began praising Allah and weeping. He was asked, "What makes you weep?" He said: "I remembered the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, and I likened the people of Paradise to the people of well-being and the people of the Fire to the people of affliction. That is what made me weep."

Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) related from the Prophet (ﷺ):

"If one of you wishes to see the measure of Allah's blessing upon him, let him look at one who is below him, and not look at one who is above him."

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Yahya ibn Abdullah informed me, saying: I heard Abu Hurayra and he mentioned it.

Ibn al-Mubarak said: Yazid ibn Ibrahim related to us from al-Hasan, who said: Abu al-Darda' said: "Whoever does not recognize Allah's blessing upon him except in his food and drink, his deeds have diminished and his punishment is near."

Ibn al-Mubarak said: Malik ibn Anas informed us, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talha, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) greet a man, and the man returned the greeting. Umar said to him, "How are you?" The man said, "I praise Allah to you." Umar said, "This is what I wanted from you."

Ibn al-Mubarak said: Mas'ud related to us, from Alqama ibn Martad, from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "We may meet many times in a single day, and one of us asks the other about his condition, and he intends by that only that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, be praised."

Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah, ﴿and He has lavished upon you His favors, outward and inward﴾, said: "It is 'there is no god but Allah.'"

Ibn 'Uyayna said: "Allah has not bestowed upon the servants any blessing better than making them know 'there is no god but Allah.'" He said: "And 'there is no god but Allah' is for them in the Hereafter like water is in this world."

One of the al-Salaf (the earlier generations of pious predecessors) said in his sermon on the day of 'Id: "You have become radiant, and people have become dusty. People weave, and you wear. People give, and you take. People breed, and you ride. People sow, and you eat." He wept, and he made them weep.

Abdullah ibn Qurt al-Azdi, who was among the Companions, said on the pulpit on a day of Adha, seeing the colorful garments of the people: "How great a blessing, how profusely given, and how manifest a favor! Nothing has departed from a people that is more severe than a blessing they cannot return. Blessings are only secured by the gratitude of the one who receives them toward the Bestower."

Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him) said: A man had worldly provision extended to him, and then it was taken from his hands. He began to praise Allah and extol Him until he had nothing left but a mat (bariya). He continued praising Allah and extolling Him until he had no bed except the mat. Then, to another man, worldly provision was extended, and he said to the owner of the mat: "Tell me, for what do you praise Allah?" He said: "I praise Him for what, if I were given in exchange for it what all creation has been given, I would not give it to them." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "Tell me, your sight, your tongue, your hands, your feet..."

A man came to Yunus ibn Ubayd complaining of his straitened circumstances. Yunus said to him: "Would you be pleased to exchange your sight for a hundred thousand dirhams?" The man said, "No." He said: "Your hands for a hundred thousand?" He said, "No." "Your feet for a hundred thousand?" He said, "No." Yunus said: "Then He mentioned Allah's blessings upon him. I see with you hundreds of thousands, and you complain of need." Abu al-Darda' used to say: "Health is kingship."

Ja'far ibn Muhammad (may Allah be pleased with him) lost a mule of his. He said: "If Allah returns it to me, I will praise Him with praises He is pleased with." It was not long before someone brought its saddle and bridle. He mounted it, and when he settled upon it and gathered his garments about him, he raised his head to the sky and said: "Praise be to Allah," and did not add to it. He was asked about that, and he said: "Have I left anything, or kept anything back? I have made all praise belong to Allah."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya related from the narration of Sa'd ibn Ishaq ibn Ka'b ibn 'Ujra, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:

"The Messenger of Allah sent a military expedition of the Ansar and said: 'If Allah grants them safety and spoils, then for Allah I owe Him gratitude for that.' They had not been long before they gained spoils and were safe. One of his Companions said: 'We heard you say, "If Allah grants them safety and spoils, then for Allah I owe Him gratitude for that."' He said: 'I have done so. O Allah, to You belongs praise in gratitude, and to You belongs favor in generosity.'"

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said to Abu Hazim: "O Abu Hazim, how many people meet me and supplicate for me with good, and I do not know them, and I have never done good to them." Abu Hazim said: "Do not think that this comes from you. Rather, look at the one from whom it comes, and thank him." And Abu Abd al-Rahman recited: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will endow them with love.﴾

Ali ibn al-Ja'd related to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salama al-Majishun related to me from one whom I trust that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say in his supplication: "I ask You for the completion of blessing in all things, and gratitude to You for them, until You are pleased, and after being pleased, and for goodness in all matters in which goodness is sought, with the ease of all affairs and not their difficulty, O Generous One."

Al-Hasan said: "Whenever Allah bestows a blessing upon a servant and he says, 'Praise be to Allah,' what has been given to him is greater than what he has taken."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: It has reached me from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna that he said: "This is a mistake; the deed of a servant cannot be better than the deed of Allah." Then he said: Some of the people of knowledge said: "The explanation of this is that when a man is bestowed a blessing by Allah, and he is among those obligated to praise Him, He makes him aware of what was done for him, so he thanks Allah as he ought to thank Him, and so praise for it is better."

I say: What Ibn 'Uyayna mentioned does not necessarily apply to al-Hasan's statement. His saying "Praise be to Allah" is itself one of Allah's blessings, and the blessing for which Allah is praised is also one of Allah's blessings. Some blessings are more excellent than others. The blessing of gratitude is more excellent than the blessing of wealth, rank, children, a spouse, and the like, and Allah knows best. This does not require that the servant's act be better than the act of Allah. It only shows that the servant's act of gratitude may be better than some of what Allah has done. The servant's act is itself something Allah has done, and there is no doubt that some of His acts are better than others.

Some of the people of knowledge said: "The blessings of Allah upon us in what He has withheld from us of the world are better than His blessings upon us in what He has extended to us of it. This is because Allah did not approve of this world for His Prophet. So my being in what Allah approved for His Prophet and loved for him is more beloved to me than being in what He disliked for him and was angry at."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: It has reached me from some scholars that he said: "It is fitting for the scholar to praise Allah for what He has withheld from him of the desires of this world, just as he praises Him for what He has given him. And how can what Allah has given compare to the reckoning that will come upon him? Compare it to His giving him well-being and not testing him with what would occupy his heart, tire his limbs, so that he thanks Allah for the tranquility of his heart and the gathering of his resolve."

It is related from Ibn Abi al-Hawari, who said: Fudayl ibn Iyad and Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna sat one night until morning discussing blessings. Sufyan kept saying: "Allah has blessed us in such and such, Allah has blessed us in such and such, Allah has done such and such for us." Abdullah ibn Dawud related to us from Sufyan regarding the words of Allah, ﴿We will lead them step by step from where they do not know﴾, he said: "He lavishes blessings upon them and prevents them from gratitude." Others besides Sufyan said: "Every time they commit a sin, He gives them a new blessing."

Thabit al-Bunani was asked about al-Istidraj (gradual leading into ruin), and he said: "It is the deception of Allah against the negligent servants."

Yunus said in explaining it: If a servant has a station with Allah, and he preserves it and remains upon it, then thanks Allah for what he was given, He gives him something nobler than it. But if he neglects gratitude, Allah leads him gradually, and his neglect of gratitude is itself istidraj.

Abu Hazim said: "Allah's blessing in what He has withheld from me of the world is greater than His blessing in what He has given me of it. I have seen Him give it to peoples, and they perished. Every blessing that does not bring you closer to Allah is a trial. And when you see Allah continuing His blessings upon you while you disobey Him, beware of Him."

Dhakara Katib al-Layth, from Hiql, from al-Awza'i, that he admonished them, and in his admonition he said: "O people, strengthen yourselves with these blessings in which you find yourselves, to flee from the fire of Allah, which is kindled and rises over the hearts. For you are in an abode where your stay is short, and you are expected to be successors after the generations who came before you, who received from the world its most beneficial and its brightest. They were longer-lived than you, greater in bodies, and mightier in their traces. They cut through mountains, hewed rocks, and dug through lands, supported by strong might and bodies like pillars. But the days and nights did not delay in folding up their terms, effacing their traces, emptying their dwellings, and erasing their remembrance, so that you do not sense from them any one, nor hear from them a whisper. They used to play, secure, in the night-raids upon a heedless people, or at the dawn upon a regretful people. Then you have known what befell them in their courtyards by night, the punishment of Allah, so that many of them in their homes were found prostrate in death, and the rest remained looking upon their traces, with vengeance and the removal of blessings, and their dwellings empty, in which there is a sign for those who fear the painful punishment, and a lesson for whoever fears. You have become, after them, in a limited term, a world that has been withdrawn, and a time whose pardon has passed and whose ease has gone, leaving nothing of it but the protectors of evil, the remnants of turbidity, the terrors of lessons, punishments and divine chastisements, the sending of trials, successive earthquakes, and humiliation after which the corruption appeared on land and sea. Do not be like those whom hope deceived, whom a long term deluded, and who were pleased by long wishes. We ask Allah to make us and you among those who heed His warning and understand His good tidings, and so prepare for themselves."

It used to be said: "Gratitude is abandoning disobedience."

Ibn al-Mubarak said: Sufyan said: "He is not a faqih who does not regard affliction as a blessing and ease as a calamity."

When Marwan ibn al-Hakam mentioned Islam, he would say: "By the blessing of my Lord, it reached me, not by what my hands have sent forth, nor by my own will. Indeed, I was a sinner."

*How many an entrance, had I died in it,*
*would have made me an example among my kin.*

*I was protected from evil and harm within it,*
*and I gained from it a great blessing.*

*How many a blessing from Allah is there that goes by in the evening,*
*and in the morning is visible in appearance and within the heart.*

Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) was summoned to a people engaged in suspicious conduct. He set out to seize them, but they dispersed before he reached them. So he freed a slave in gratitude to Allah that no disgrace of a Muslim had come about at his hands.

Yazid ibn Harun said: Asbagh ibn Yazid informed us that when Nuh (peace be upon him) came out of the lavatory, he would say: "Praise be to Allah who let me taste its pleasure, kept its benefit in my body, and removed its harm from me." So he was named "a grateful servant."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Al-Abbas ibn Ja'far related to me from al-Harith ibn Shibl, who said: Umm al-Nu'man told us that A'isha told her that the Prophet (ﷺ) never rose from the lavatory except that he said this.

A man said to Abu Hazim: "What is the gratitude of the eyes, O Abu Hazim?" He said: "If you see good with them, you proclaim it; if you see evil with them, you conceal it." He said: "And what is the gratitude of the ears?" He said: "If you hear good with them, you retain it; if you hear evil with them, you repel it." He said: "And what is the gratitude of the hands?" He said: "You do not take with them what is not theirs, and you do not withhold a right of Allah that is in them." He said: "And what is the gratitude of the belly?" He said: "That its lower part be food and its upper part knowledge." He said: "And what is the gratitude of the private parts?" He said: Allah said: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their spouses or what their right hands possess, for then they are not blameworthy. But whoever seeks beyond that, it is those who are the transgressors.﴾ He said: "And what is the gratitude of the feet?" He said: "If you know someone dead whom you envy, you employ them in his deeds; and if you hate him, you turn away from his deeds, and you are thankful to Allah."

As for one who thanks with his tongue but does not thank with all his limbs, his example is like the example of a man who has a cloak, takes hold of its edge, and does not wear it. Such a thing does not benefit him against heat, cold, snow, or rain.

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak mentioned that the Negus (al-Najashi) once sent for Ja'far and his companions. They entered upon him while he was in a house wearing worn garments and sitting on the dust. Ja'far said: "We were alarmed when we saw him in that state. When he saw what was in our faces, he said: 'I bring you good news that will gladden you. A messenger of mine has come to me from the direction of your land and informed me that Allah has granted victory to His Prophet and destroyed his enemy, and that so-and-so and so-and-so were taken captive, and so-and-so and so-and-so were killed, and they met in a valley called Badr, abundant in arak trees, as if I were looking at it. I used to tend there for my master, a man of the Banu Dhamra.'" Then Ja'far said to him: "Why are you sitting on the dust, with no carpet beneath you, and wearing these worn garments?" He said: "We find in what Allah revealed to Isa (peace be upon him) that it is a right upon the servants of Allah to show humility to Allah for what He has newly bestowed upon them of His blessings. So when Allah has newly granted me the victory of His Prophet, I have shown this humility to Allah."

Habib ibn Ubayd said: "Allah does not test a servant with an affliction except that in it there is a blessing for him: that it is not worse than it."

Abd al-Malik ibn Ishaq said: "No one among people is not tested, either with well-being to see how he gives thanks, or with calamity to see how he endures."

Sufyan al-Thawri said: "Allah has blessed a servant in a need more than his supplicating to Him for it."

When something that pleased him came to him, the Prophet (ﷺ) would fall down in prostration to Allah in thanks to Him, the Mighty and Majestic. Ahmad mentioned it.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (may Allah be pleased with him) said:

"The Prophet came out to us and turned toward his place of charity, then entered, faced the qibla, and fell in prostration, prolonging the prostration. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you prostrated a prostration that I thought Allah may have taken your soul in it.' He said: 'Jibril came to me and gave me good news that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Whoever sends blessings upon you, I send blessings upon him, and whoever greets you with peace, I greet him with peace. So I prostrated to Allah in gratitude.'" Ahmad mentioned it.

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "We set out with the Prophet from Makkah, intending Madinah. When we were near 'Azwar, he dismounted, then raised his hands and supplicated to Allah for a while, then fell into prostration and remained a long time. Then he rose and raised his hands for a while, then fell into prostration again. He did this three times, and said: 'I asked my Lord and interceded for my community, and He gave me a third of my community, so I fell prostrate in gratitude to my Lord. Then I raised my head and asked my Lord for my community, and He gave me a third of my community, so I fell prostrate to my Lord. Then I raised my head and asked my Lord, my Lord, and He gave me the remaining third, so I fell prostrate to my Lord.'" Related by Abu Dawud.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the book *al-Futuh*: When the bringer of good news came on the day of Badr with the killing of Abu Jahl, the Messenger of Allah made him swear three oaths by Allah, besides whom there is no god: "Did you truly see him slain?" He swore to him, and the Messenger of Allah fell in prostration.

Sa'id ibn Mansur mentioned that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) prostrated when news of the killing of Musaylima came to him. Ahmad mentioned that Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) prostrated when he found Dhu al-Thudayya among the Khawarij (the seceders). Ka'b ibn Malik also prostrated during the time of the Prophet when he was given the good news that Allah had accepted his repentance, and the story is in the Two Sahihs.

If it is said: "The blessings of Allah upon the servant are constant and continuous, so what required the singling out of the newly arising blessing for gratitude, rather than the enduring one, when the enduring one may be greater?"

It is answered in several respects:

First, the newly arising blessing reminds one of the enduring one, and man is entrusted with the lesser.

Second, this newly arising blessing calls for a renewed act of servitude, and the easiest of that for a human being, and the most beloved to Allah, is prostration in gratitude to Him.

Third, the newly arising blessing has an impact upon souls and hearts, and it is more attached to them. For this reason one is congratulated upon it and condoled upon its loss.

The fourth [point]: the occurrence of blessings produces joy and expansiveness of the soul, and this often leads to insolence (al-ashr), exultation (al-batar), and prostration, which is humility to Allah, servitude, and submission. So when he receives His blessing with gladness, the joy and expansiveness of his soul, he is worthy of the continuation of that blessing. But when he receives it with the joy that Allah does not love, with insolence and exultation, as the ignorant do when Allah bestows blessings upon them, it is swiftly lost and quickly transferred, and it turns into a punishment and becomes a gradual deception (istidraj). The matter of al-Najashi has already been mentioned, for when Allah bestows a blessing upon His servant, He loves that the servant should respond to it with humility. Al-'Ala' ibn al-Mughira said: "I gave the good news of al-Hasan's death to al-Hajjaj while he was hidden, so he fell down in prostration to Allah."

(Section)

Among the subtle blessings of Allah upon the servant, which he hardly notices, is that he closes his door upon himself, and then Allah sends to him someone who knocks on his door asking him for some food, so that He makes him aware of His blessing upon him.

Salam ibn Abi Muti' said: "I went in to visit a sick man, and he was groaning. I said to him: 'Remember those cast out on the road, remember those who have no shelter and no one to serve them.' He said that. Then I went in to him again afterwards and heard him saying to himself: 'Remember those cast out on the road, remember the one who has no shelter and no one to serve him.'"

Abd Allah ibn Abi Nuh said: A man on some of the coasts said to me: "How many times have you acted towards Him, blessed is His name, in ways He dislikes, and He has dealt with you in ways you love?"

I said: "I cannot count it, it is so much."

He said: "Have you ever turned to Him in a matter of your distress, and He forsook you?"

I said: "No, by Allah, but He has been kind to me and helped me."

He said: "Have you ever asked Him for anything and He did not give it to you?"

I said: "Has He ever withheld from me anything I asked? I have never asked Him for anything except that He gave it to me, and I have never sought His help except that He helped me."

He said: "Tell me, if one of the sons of Adam had done to you some of these qualities, what would be your reward for him?"

I said: "I could not repay him or compensate him."

He said: "Your Lord is more deserving and more fitting that you should exert yourself in giving thanks to Him, for He has been kind to you from of old and now. By Allah, thanking Him is easier than repaying His servants. He, blessed and exalted, is content from the servants with praise as thanks."

Sufyan al-Thawri said: "Allah would not bestow a blessing upon a servant in this world and then disgrace him in the Hereafter. It is incumbent upon the Bestower to complete the blessing upon the one whom He has blessed."

Ibn Abi al-Hawwari said: "I said to Abu Mu'awiya: 'How great is the blessing upon us in tawhid; we ask Allah not to deprive us of it.' He said: 'It is incumbent upon the Bestower to complete the blessing upon the one whom He has blessed, and Allah is too generous to bestow a blessing and not complete it, or to employ someone in a deed and not accept it.'"

Ibn Abi al-Hawwari said: "A woman said to me: 'I am in my house, and my heart is preoccupied.' I said: 'With what?' She said: 'I want to know Allah's blessings upon me in the blink of an eye, or to know my shortcoming in giving thanks for His blessing upon me in the blink of an eye.' I said: 'You want what our minds cannot grasp.'"

Ibn Zayd said: "A single man in a gathering may praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and as a result the needs of everyone in that gathering are fulfilled."

He said: "In some of the books that Allah sent down, He says: 'Gladden My believing servant,' and nothing comes to him but he says: 'Praise be to Allah, as Allah wills.' 'Terrify My believing servant,' and no sign of an adversity appears to him but he says: 'Praise be to Allah, praise be to Allah.' Allah, blessed and exalted, says: 'My servant praises Me when I terrify him as he praises Me when I gladden him. Enter My servant into the house of My might, as he praises Me in all his states.'"

Wahb said: "A servant of Allah worshipped for fifty years, and Allah revealed to him: 'I have forgiven you.' He said: 'My Lord, how can You forgive me when I have not sinned?' So Allah permitted a vein in his neck to throb, and he could neither sleep nor pray. Then it calmed down and he slept. Then an angel came to him, and he complained to him, saying: 'What I have suffered from the throbbing of the vein!' The angel said: 'Your Lord says: Your worship for fifty years equals the calm of the vein.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned that Dawud said: "My Lord, inform me of the least of Your blessings upon me." Allah revealed to him: "O Dawud, breathe." He breathed, and Allah said: "This is the least of My blessings upon you."

(Section) This clarifies the meaning of the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud from the report of Zayd ibn Thabit and Ibn Abbas: "If Allah were to punish the inhabitants of His heavens and the inhabitants of His earth, He would punish them without being unjust to them; and if He were to show them mercy, His mercy would be better for them than their deeds." And the hadith in the Sahih: "None of you will be saved by his deed." They said: "Not even you, Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace, for the deeds of a servant do not match any of the blessings of Allah upon him."

As for the statement of some jurists that whoever swears to praise Allah with the best kinds of praise, his oath is fulfilled by saying: "Praise be to Allah, a praise that matches His blessings and compensates for His increase," this is not a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) nor from any of the Companions. It is rather an Isra'iliyy (a narrative of Israelite origin) from Adam. More correct than it is the saying: "Praise be to Allah, a praise that is not repaid, not left behind, and not dispensed with, our Lord." It is not possible for the praise and gratitude of a servant to match any one of Allah's blessings, let alone match all of His blessings. Nor is the servant's action and praise able to compensate for the increase. Rather, it must be understood in a sense that is correct: that the praise which Allah, glorified is He, deserves is praise that matches His blessings and compensates for His increase, even if the servant cannot produce it. For example, if one says: "Praise be to Allah, as much as the heavens are full, as much as the earth is full, as much as what is between them is full, as much as whatever else You will after that is full, as much as the number of the sands, the dust, the pebbles and the drops of rain, as much as the number of the breaths of creation, and as much as the number of what Allah has created and what He will create." This is an informing about the praise He deserves, not about the praise that the servant actually offers.

(Section)

Abu al-Mulayh said: Musa said: "My Lord, what is the best gratitude?" He said: "That you thank Me in every state."

Bakr ibn Abd Allah said: "I said to a brother of mine: 'Advise me.' He said: 'I do not know what to say, except that this servant should not slacken in praise and seeking forgiveness, for the son of Adam is between a blessing and a sin. A blessing is only made right by praise and gratitude, and a sin is only made right by repentance and seeking forgiveness. So give me as much knowledge as you wish.'"

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Dawud said: "I saw a sore on the hand of Muhammad ibn Wasi', and it seemed as if he saw that it distressed me. He said to me: 'Do you know what blessing Allah has given me in this sore? He did not place it in my eye, nor on the tip of my tongue, nor on the edge of my memory.' So the sore became light for him."

Al-Jurayri narrated from Abu al-Ward, from al-Hallaj, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by a man who was saying: "O Allah, I ask You for the completion of blessing." He said: "Son of Adam, do you know what the completion of blessing is?" He said: "Messenger of Allah, I made a supplication hoping for good in it." He said: "The completion of blessing is deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise."

Sahm ibn Salama said: "I have been told that when a man mentions the name of Allah at the beginning of his food and praises Him at its end, he will not be asked about the bounty of that food."

(Section)

That gratitude is superior to patience is shown by the fact that Allah, glorified is He, loves to be asked for well-being (al-'afiyah), and He is not asked for anything more beloved to Him than well-being. As in the Musnad, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood on the pulpit and said: "Ask Allah for well-being, for He has not given a servant, after certainty, anything better than well-being."

In another hadith: "People have not been given anything better in this world than pardon and well-being, so ask Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for them." And he said to his uncle al-Abbas: "O uncle, increase your supplication for well-being." In al-Tirmidhi: "I said: 'Messenger of Allah, teach me something to ask Allah for.' He said: 'Ask Allah for well-being.' I remained for some days, then came and said: 'Teach me something to ask Allah for.' He said to me: 'O Abbas, O uncle of the Messenger of Allah, ask Allah for well-being in this world and the Hereafter.'" In his supplication on the day of al-Ta'if he said: "If You are not angry with me, I do not mind, but Your well-being is more expansive for me." So he sought refuge in His well-being, as he sought refuge in it in his saying: "I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath, and I seek refuge in Your forgiveness from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You."

In another hadith: "Ask Allah for pardon, well-being, and safety (al-mu'afah)." This request includes pardon for what has passed, well-being in the present, and safety in the future through the continuance and lastingness of well-being.

Abd al-A'la al-Taymi used to say: "Increase your request to Allah for well-being, for the afflicted, however severe his affliction, is no more deserving of supplication than the one at ease who does not feel safe from affliction. The afflicted today were only among the people of well-being yesterday, and the afflicted after today will only be among the people of well-being today. If affliction led to good, we would have been among the men of affliction. How many an affliction has exhausted one in this world and disgraced him in the Hereafter! Whoever lingers in disobedience to Allah cannot be sure that there remains for him in the rest of his life an affliction that will exhaust him in this world and disgrace him in the Hereafter. Then, after that, he says: 'Praise be to Allah, who, if we count His blessings, we cannot enumerate them; and if we strive for Him in deeds, we cannot repay them; and if we live long in them, we cannot reach their end.'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by a man who was asking Allah for patience. He said: "You have asked for affliction, so ask for well-being."

In Sahih Muslim, he visited a man who had become emaciated, meaning wasted away so that he became like a chick. He said: "Did you used to supplicate Allah for anything, or ask Him for something?" He said: "Yes, I used to say: 'O Allah, whatever You were going to punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You cannot bear it and cannot endure it. Why did you not say: 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire'?" So he supplicated Allah for him, and He healed him.

In al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "A supplication I memorized from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which I will never abandon: 'O Allah, make me the greatest of Your thankers, the most abundant in Your remembrance, the most faithful follower of Your counsel, and the best keeper of Your commandment.'"

Shaybān said: "When al-Hasan sat in a gathering, he would say: 'To You is praise for Islam, to You is praise for the Qur'an, to You is praise for family and wealth. You have expanded our provision, shown us security, and been good to us in well-being. And from everything we have asked You, You have given us. So to You is abundant praise, as You bestow abundantly. You have given much good, and You have turned away much evil. So to Your Majestic, Enduring, Everlasting Face is the praise.'"

Some of the early generation (al-salaf) used to say: "O Allah, whatever blessing, well-being, or honour in religion or in worldly life has come upon us in the past and is still coming upon us in the future, it is from You alone, with no partner. So to You is the praise for that upon us, to You is the favour, to You is the grace, and to You is the praise as many times as You have blessed us and all Your creation. There is no god but You."

Mujahid said: "When Ibn Umar was on a journey and the dawn rose, he raised his voice and called out: 'Let the hearer hear praise of Allah, His blessings, and His good trial upon us,' three times. 'O Allah, accompany us and bestow favour upon us. I seek refuge in Allah from the Fire,' and 'There is no might nor power except by Allah,' three times."

Imam Ahmad mentioned that Allah, glorified is He, revealed to Musa ibn Imran, peace be upon him: "O Musa, be alert, seeking for yourself companions. Every companion who does not agree with you in what gladdens Me, do not keep company with him, for he is an enemy to you, and he hardens your heart. Remember Me often until you deserve gratitude and complete the increase."

Al-Hasan said: "When Allah created Adam, He brought forth the people of Paradise from his right side and the people of the Fire from his left side. They spread over the surface of the earth: among them the blind, the deaf, and the afflicted. Adam said: 'My Lord, why did You not make my children equal?' He said: 'O Adam, I wish to be thanked.'"

In the Sunan, from him (al-Hasan): whoever says in the morning: "O Allah, whatever blessing has come upon me, or upon anyone of Your creation, is from You alone, with no partner. So to You is the praise and to You is the thanks," has fulfilled the thanks due for that day; and whoever says it in the evening has fulfilled the thanks due for that night.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever is afflicted and is patient, given and is grateful, wronged and forgives, wrongs and seeks forgiveness, those are the ones who have security and are guided." It is also related from him that he advised a man with three things: "Remember death much, for it will occupy you from everything else. Make supplication incumbent upon you, for you do not know when your supplication will be answered. And be thankful incumbent upon you, for thanks is an increase."

It is also related from him that when he ate he said: "Praise be to Allah who has fed me and given me drink and guided me, and every good trial with which He has tested me. Praise be to Allah, the Provider, the Possessor of strong power. O Allah, do not take away from us any good You have given us, nor any good You have provided us, and make us among those who are grateful to You."

It is also related from him that when he ate he said: "Praise be to Allah who has fed and given drink and made it palatable and made a way out for it."

When food was brought to Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, he would not stop being covered until he said these words: "Praise be to Allah who has guided us, fed us, given us drink, and blessed us. Allah is greatest. O Allah, Your blessing has surrounded us while we are in every evil; so we have risen and passed the evening in goodness. We ask You for its completion and its thanks. There is no good but Your good, and no god other than You, the God of the righteous and the Lord of the worlds. Praise be to Allah. There is no god but Allah. As Allah wills. There is no power except by Allah. O Allah, bless us in what You have provided us, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."
