In reality, the world is not to be blamed. Blame is directed only to the servant's actions within it. It is a bridge or a crossing to Paradise or to the Fire. But because desires, appetites, heedlessness, and turning away from Allah and the Last Abode have overcome it, and this has become dominant among its people and in what is in it, and dominant in its name, it acquired the name of blame upon its unqualified mention. Otherwise, it is the foundation of the Hereafter, its farm, and from it comes the provision for Paradise. In it souls acquired faith, knowledge of Allah, love of Him, His remembrance, and the pursuit of His pleasure. The best life that the people of Paradise attained in Paradise came only from what they sowed in it. It is enough as praise and virtue that for the friends of Allah in it are the coolness of the eyes, the joy of hearts, the delight of souls, the pleasure of spirits, and a bliss that nothing else resembles: through His remembrance, knowledge, love, worship, reliance upon Him, turning to Him, intimacy with Him, rejoicing in His nearness, humbling oneself before Him, the delight of intimate conversation with Him, turning fully to Him, and being occupied with Him rather than with anyone else. In it is His speech, His revelation, and His guidance, and His Spirit which He cast by His command, and He informed whom He willed of His servants with it. For this reason Ibn 'Aqīl and others preferred this over the bliss of Paradise, and they said: "This is Allah's right over them, and that is their share and their bliss, and His right is better than their right." They said: "Faith and obedience are better than their reward." The verification is that comparison cannot be validly made between two matters in two different abodes. If they could be combined in one abode, then it would be possible to seek the comparison. Faith and obedience in this abode are the best of what is in it, and entering Paradise, looking at the face of Allah, the Majestic, hearing His speech, and winning His pleasure are the best of what is in the Hereafter. So this is the best of this abode, and that is the best of the other abode. It is not valid to say: "Which of the two is better?" This is the best of the means, and that is the best of the ends. And with Allah is success.

(Section)
When He, glorified is He, described the reality of this world, explained its ultimate purpose and its end, and its transformation in the Hereafter into severe punishment, forgiveness from Allah, and reward, He commanded His servants to race and hasten toward what is better and more lasting, and to prefer it over the perishable, the cut off, the mixed with grief and disturbance. Then He informed that this is His bounty, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty. The Exalted said: ﴿And strike for them the likeness of the life of this world: it is like water that We sent down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingled with it, then it became dry stalks that the winds scatter. Allah is ever Capable of all things﴾.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned that wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world, and that the enduring good deeds, which are the righteous actions and sayings whose reward remains and whose recompense lasts, are better in hope and reward for the servant. The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of the life of this world is like water that We sent down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingled with it, of which people and livestock eat, until the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified, and its people think they are capable of it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it a harvested field as though it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who reflect﴾.

When He informed His servants about the calamities of this abode, He called His servants to the Abode of Peace, which is free from change, transformation, cessation, and extinction. He called all His servants to it, out of justice, and specified whom He willed for guidance to its path, out of bounty.

He, glorified is He, informed that wealth and children do not bring people closer to Him. What brings them closer to Him is the fear of Allah and dealing with Him in them. He warned His servants that their wealth and children should not distract them from His remembrance. He informed that whoever does that is the real loser, not the one whose wealth and children are small in this world. He forbade His Prophet to extend his eyes to what the people of this world were given for enjoyment, as a trial for them and a test. He informed that His provision which He has prepared for him in the Hereafter is better and more lasting than what they were given to enjoy.

He, glorified is He, informed that He gave him the seven oft-repeated (al-sab' al-mathānī) and the Great Qur'an, and that this is better and more excellent than what the people of this world were given in their world. He made what He gave him a barrier from extending his eyes toward that. So this giving in this world, and what He has stored for him of the provision of the Hereafter, is better than what the people of this world were given. So do not extend your eyes.

Section: When it is known that wealth and poverty, affliction and well-being, are a trial and test from Allah for His servant, by which He examines his patience and gratitude, it is known that patience and gratitude are two mounts for faith, and faith is carried only upon them, and every believer must have both. Each of them is more excellent in its own place. Patience is more excellent in situations of patience, and gratitude is more excellent in situations of gratitude. This is if it is valid to separate each of them from the other. As for when patience is part of the designation of gratitude, and gratitude is part of the designation of patience, and each of them is in reality composed of the two together, as explained earlier, then preference between them is not valid unless one is stripped of the other. That is a mental supposition that the mind imagines and does not exist externally. But it is valid in one respect: that a servant's patience may overcome his gratitude, which is an amount beyond mere patience, consisting of outward and inward sayings and actions. So no room remains in him except for the patience of the soul in what it is in, because of the strength of what descends upon it and the narrowness of the place, so all its powers turn toward restraining the soul and holding it back for Allah. And his gratitude may overcome his patience, through outward and inward sayings and actions, over the strength of his restraint of his soul and holding it back for Allah, so the strength of his will and his action becomes stronger than the strength of his restraint and holding back of himself.

Consider this through two persons. One of them has authority over himself, able to hold it back from desires, rarely complaining about calamities, and that is most of his work. The other gives much for doing good, both the limited and the far-reaching, generous of soul in spending goodness, and a third is weak of soul in the strength of patience. The soul has two powers: the power of patience and restraint, and holding the soul back, and the power of giving, doing good, and advancing to do what perfects it. Its perfection is by the combination of these two powers in it. People in this are in four classes. The highest is the one in whom both powers are combined, and the lowest is the one in whom both powers are lacking. Some have a patience stronger than their action and giving, and some are the opposite. So when gratitude is preferred over patience, either it is by considering the preference of one station over another, or it is by considering the stripping of each of the two from the other and disregarding its consideration. The complete clarification of this is through the question of the rich grateful one and the poor patient one, so we shall mention for it a chapter devoted to it which uncovers the truth regarding it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 1, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ carries a particular servitude (ʿubudiyyah) proper to it, which is witnessing the comprehensiveness of His mercy, its vastness encompassing everything, and every existent taking its share of it; especially the special mercy that has set His servant before Him in service, conversing with Him through His speech, seeking His favor, asking Him for mercy, asking Him for guidance, and the completion of His blessing upon him. This is from His mercy to His servant. So His mercy encompasses everything, just as His praise encompasses everything.

[Chapter: The Mention of Allah's Names After the Praise]

In mentioning these names after the praise, and in directing the praise toward their meaning and what they require, there is that which indicates that He is praised in His divinity (ilahiyyah), praised in His lordship (rububiyyah), praised in His mercy (rahmaniyyah), and praised in His kingship (mulk); and that He is a praiseworthy God (ilah), a praiseworthy Lord (rabb), a praiseworthy Most Merciful (Rahman), and a praiseworthy King (malik). Thus to Him belong all the categories of perfection: a perfection from each of these names individually, a perfection from the other individually, and a perfection from the conjunction of one with the other.

An example of this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is Rich, Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Taghabun: 6], ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ [al-Nisa: 26], ﴿And Allah is Capable﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 7], ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 218]. Richness is an attribute of perfection, praise is an attribute of perfection, and the conjunction of His richness with His praiseworthiness is also perfection. His knowledge is perfection, His wisdom is perfection, and the conjunction of knowledge with wisdom is also perfection. His power is perfection and His forgiveness is perfection, and the conjunction of power with forgiveness is perfection; likewise pardoning after power: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning, Forgiving﴾ [al-Nisa: 43], and the conjunction of knowledge with forbearance: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, Forbearing﴾ [al-Nisa: 12].

The bearers of the Throne are four: two of them say, "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; to You is the praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge," and two say, "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; to You is the praise for Your pardoning after Your power." For not everyone who has power pardons, nor does everyone who pardons do so from power; not everyone who knows is forbearing, nor is every forbearing one knowing. No thing is joined to another more beautiful than forbearance joined to knowledge, pardoning joined to power, kingship joined to praise, and might joined to mercy: ﴿And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 9].

From this is the saying of the Messiah, peace be upon him: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 118]. This is better than saying, "And if You forgive them, indeed You are the Forgiving, the Merciful," meaning: if You forgive them, the source of Your forgiveness is from might, which is the perfection of power, and from wisdom, which is the perfection of knowledge. For whoever forgives out of incapacity and ignorance of the offender's crime, You do not forgive except from complete power, complete knowledge, and wisdom by which You place things in their right places. So this is better than mentioning "the Forgiving, the Merciful" in this context, since its mention would indicate an allusion to seeking forgiveness at other than its appropriate time, when it has already passed. For if he had said, "And if You forgive them, indeed You are the Forgiving, the Merciful," there would have been in this a supplication for compassion and an allusion to seeking forgiveness for one who does not deserve it, which is what the station of the Messiah, peace be upon him, would be above. Especially since the situation is one of greatness and majesty, and a situation of retribution against those who ascribed a son to Allah and took him as a god besides Him. So the mention of might and wisdom here is more fitting than the mention of mercy and forgiveness.

This is unlike the saying of the Friend (Khalil), peace be upon him: ﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols. My Lord, indeed they have led many of the people astray. So whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Ibrahim: 35–36].

He did not say, "Indeed You are Mighty and Wise," because the station is one of supplication for compassion and an allusion to a request, meaning: if You forgive them and have mercy upon them, by granting them success to return from polytheism to monotheism and from disobedience to obedience, as in the hadith: "O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know."

In this is the clearest indication that the names of the Lord, exalted is He, are derived from attributes and meanings that subsist in Him, and that every name corresponds to what is mentioned with it and conjoined to it, from His act and His command. And Allah is the Granter of success to what is correct.

[Chapter: The Connection of Creation to Allah's Names]

Reflect on the connection of creation and command to these three names, which are Allah, the Lord, and the Most Merciful: how creation, command, reward and punishment arose from them, and how they gathered creation and separated them. To them belongs the gathering, and to them belongs the separation.

The name Lord has the gathering that unites all created beings: He is the Lord and Creator of everything, and the One capable over it. Nothing lies outside His lordship, and everyone in the heavens and earth is a servant of His, in His grip and under His subjugation. They are gathered by the attribute of lordship and separated by the attribute of divinity. So the happy ones single Him out alone in worship and voluntarily acknowledge that He is Allah, there is no god but Him, to whom alone worship, reliance, hope and fear, love, turning in repentance, humility, reverence, and submission are fitting.

Here people separated and became two groups: a group of polytheists in the Blaze, and a group of monotheists in Paradise.

So divinity is what separated them, just as lordship is what gathered them.

Religion and law, command and prohibition, are manifested through it, and their establishment comes from the attribute of divinity. Creation, bringing into being, governance and action come from the attribute of lordship. Recompense through reward and punishment, Paradise and Fire, comes from the attribute of kingship, for He is "King of the Day of Judgment." So He commands them by His divinity, helps them, grants them success, guides them, and leads them astray by His lordship, and rewards and punishes them by His kingship and justice. Each of these matters does not separate from the others.

As for mercy, it is the bond and the means between Allah and His servants. Worship on their part toward Him, and lordship on His part toward them, and mercy is the connecting cause between Him and His servants. By it He sent His messengers to them, sent down His books upon them, by it He guided them, by it He made them dwell in the abode of His reward, and by it He provided for them, granted them well-being and bestowed blessings upon them. Between them and Him is the cause of servitude, and between Him and them is the cause of mercy.

The conjunction of His lordship with His mercy is like the conjunction of His istiwa' (settling) upon His Throne with His mercy: ﴿The Most Merciful settled upon the Throne﴾ [Taha: 5] corresponds to His saying ﴿Lord of the worlds, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [al-Fatihah: 2–3]. For the comprehensiveness and breadth of lordship, such that nothing lies outside it, is the utmost comprehensiveness and breadth of mercy. So He encompassed everything with His mercy and His lordship. Yet in His being Lord of the worlds there is what indicates His elevation above His creation, and His being above everything, as its explanation will come, God willing.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 1, verse 4:

It is the Day on which Allah requites His servants for their deeds: He rewards them for good works, and punishes them for disobedience and evil deeds. Allah would not punish anyone before the proof (hujjah) is established against him, and the proof has been established only through His messengers and His books. By them the reward and the punishment are merited, and by them the market of the Day of Religion is set up, and the righteous are driven to bliss and the wicked to the Hellfire.

He said in the book (al-Kalam ala Masalat al-Sama'):

Then he gives His saying ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ its due of servitude, and reflects on how it contains the affirmation of the Return (al-ma'ad), the Lord's sole authority to judge among His creatures, and that it is a Day on which the servants are requited for their deeds, good and evil. That is among the details of His praise and what it necessitates.

Since His saying ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ is a report of His praise, Allah said: "My servant has praised Me." And since His saying ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ is a repetition and reiteration of the attributes of His perfection, He said: "My servant has extolled Me." Praise (thana') is only through repeating the commendations and enumerating the attributes of the one praised. And since He described Himself, glory be to Him, with sole sovereignty over the Day of Religion, which is the true sovereignty, containing the manifestation of His justice, His greatness, His majesty, His oneness and the truthfulness of His messengers, He named this praise "glorification" (majd), saying: "My servant has glorified Me." For glorification is praise with attributes of greatness and majesty.

(Benefit: on the specialisation of the King (al-Malik) with the Day of Religion)

The attributes of justice, of grasping and extending, of lowering and raising, of giving and withholding, of honouring and humbling, of subjugation and judgment, and the like, are more particular to the name al-Malik, and He specified it with the Day of Religion, which is recompense with justice, because of His sole judgment in it, because it is the true Day, and what precedes it is like an hour, and because it is the ultimate end, while the days of this world are stages leading to it.

Surat al-Fatiha contains the affirmation of the Return, and the recompense of the servants for their deeds, good and bad, and the Lord's sole judgment among the creation on that day, and that His judgment is with justice. All of this falls under His saying ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾.

(Section)

Ad-din (religion/judgment) carries the sense of humbling and subjugation, and it also carries the sense of submission, obedience and servitude. Therefore it may go from the high to the low, as one says: "dintuhu fa-dan," meaning, "I subdued him so he submitted."

The poet said:

He subdued the Rabab when they disliked the religion (al-din), so they became in might and prowess.

And it may go from the low to the high, as one says: "dintu Allah" and "dintu li-Allah," and "fulan la yadinu Allaha dinan" and "la yadinu Allaha bi-dinin." So "dana Allah" means: he obeyed Allah, loved Him and feared Him; and "dana Allah" also means: he humbled himself before Him, submitted, abased himself and yielded.

Inward religion necessarily involves love and submission, just as worship does, unlike outward religion, which does not necessarily entail love, although it involves yielding and outward humility.

Allah, glorified is He, named the Day of Resurrection [the Day of Religion], because it is the Day on which people are requited for their deeds: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. That includes their recompense and their reckoning. Therefore the exegetes explained it as the Day of Recompense and the Day of Reckoning.

(Benefit)

When the worshipper says ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, he witnesses here the glory that befits none but the true, manifest King. He witnesses a dominating King to whom creation submits, before whom faces are humbled, before whose majesty the tyrants are abased, and before whose might every mighty one yields. He witnesses with his heart a King upon the throne of heaven, dominant in His might, before whom faces bow and prostrate. If he does not nullify the reality of the attribute of kingship, he is granted the witnessing of the realities of the Names and Attributes, whose nullification is nullification of His kingship and denial of it. For the true, complete King can only be living, self-subsisting, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, governing, powerful, speaking, commanding and forbidding, established upon the throne of His kingdom, sending His messengers to the farthest reaches of His realm with His commands. He is pleased with whoever deserves His pleasure, rewards, honours and draws him near; and He is angry with whoever deserves His anger, punishes, humiliates and distances him. He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, gives to whom He wills, draws near whom He wills and distances whom He wills. He has an abode of punishment, which is the Fire, and an abode of great felicity, which is Paradise. Whoever nullifies any part of this, or denies it, or denies its reality, has indeed impugned His kingship, glory be to Him and exalted is He, and negated His perfection and completeness.

Likewise, whoever denies the comprehensiveness of His decree and destiny has denied the comprehensiveness of His kingship and perfection. So the worshipper witnesses the glory of the Lord, exalted is He, in His saying ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾.

[Section: Religion is of two kinds]

Religion (din) is of two kinds: a legislative, commanding religion, and a reckoning, recompensing religion. Both belong to Allah alone. So all religion belongs to Allah, whether as command or as recompense. Love is the root of each of the two kinds of religion. For what He, glorified and exalted, legislated and commanded, He loves and is pleased with; and what He forbade, He hates and abhors, because it is contrary to what He loves and is pleased with, so He loves its opposite. Thus His entire commanding religion returns to His love and His good pleasure.

The servant's religion to Allah is accepted only when it proceeds from His love and pleasure, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever has tasted the flavour of faith is one who is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as messenger." So this one is a worshipper sustained by love, by reason of which it was legislated, for the sake of which it was legislated, and upon which it was founded. Likewise His recompensing religion includes requiting the doer of good with his goodness and the doer of evil with his evil. Each of the two matters is beloved to the Lord, for they are His justice and His grace, and both are attributes of His perfection. He, glorified is He, loves His attributes and His names, and loves those who love them. Each of the two religions is His straight path, upon which He Himself is. Thus He is upon a straight path in His command and prohibition, His reward and punishment, as Allah, exalted is He, said, reporting about His prophet Hud, peace be upon him, when he said to his people: ﴿Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and bear witness, you, that I am free from what you associate - other than Him. So scheme against me, all of you, and give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path﴾ [Hud: 54-56].

When the prophet of Allah, Hud, peace be upon him, knew that his Lord is upon a straight path in His creation, His command and prohibition, His reward and punishment, His decree and destiny, His withholding and giving, His well-being and trial, His granting of success and forsaking, He does not depart in any of that from the requirement of His holy perfection, which His names and attributes demand: justice, wisdom, mercy, goodness and grace; placing reward in its proper places; punishment in its fitting place; placing success and forsaking, giving and withholding, guidance and misguidance, each in its appropriate position and station. All of this is due to Him, meriting complete praise and commendation. This knowledge and recognition gave him strength, so he proclaimed before the chiefs of his people, with a firm heart and an unafraid soul, rather one stripped bare for Allah: ﴿Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and bear witness, you, that I am free from what you associate...﴾

Then he informed of the comprehensiveness of His power and dominance over all else, and the submission of everything before His majesty, saying: ﴿There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾ So how should I fear one whose forelock is in another's hand, while he is under His domination, His grip, and beneath His dominion and authority? Is this anything but the most profound ignorance and the vilest injustice?

Then he informed that He, glorified is He, is upon a straight path, so whatever He decrees and destines, the servant does not fear His tyranny or His injustice. So I do not fear what is beneath Him, for its forelock is in His hand, and I do not fear His tyranny or injustice, for He is upon a straight path. He, glorified is He, His judgment proceeds upon His servant, and His decree is just in regard to him. Kingship is His, and praise is His. In His dealings with His servants He does not depart from justice and grace: if He gives, honours, guides and grants success, it is by His grace and mercy; and if He withholds, humiliates, misguides, forsakes and makes wretched, it is by His justice and wisdom. He is upon a straight path in this and in that.

In the authentic hadith: "No servant is ever afflicted by distress or grief, and says: 'O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your female servant. My forelock is in Your hand. Your judgment over me proceeds, Your decree over me is just. I ask You by every name that is Yours, by which You named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You: that You make the Mighty Qur'an the spring of my heart, the light of my breast, the removal of my grief, and the departure of my distress and sorrow,' except that Allah removes his distress and sorrow and replaces them with relief." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not learn these words?" He said: "Yes, it is fitting for whoever hears them to learn them."

This encompasses the Lord's cosmic (kawni) and commanding (amri) judgment, and His decree which occurs both by the servant's choice and without his choice. Both judgments proceed upon His servant, and both decrees are just concerning him. Thus this hadith is derived from this verse; between them is the closest kinship.

[Benefit: on remembrance at meeting the enemy, and for one who fears a ruler or other]

In the Sunan of Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, from Abu Musa, that the Prophet ﷺ, when he feared a people, would say: "O Allah, we place You against their necks, and we seek refuge in You from their evils."

It is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he would say at the meeting with the enemy: "O Allah, You are my arm, You are my helper, and by You I fight."

And from him ﷺ, that he was on a campaign and said: "O Master of the Day of Judgment, You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help." Anas said: "I indeed saw men being struck down by the angels from before and behind them."

From Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If you fear a ruler or other, say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but You; the might of Your protection is great, and Your praise is exalted.'"

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Hasbuna Allah wa ni'ma al-wakil (Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs)" was said by Ibrahim when he was thrown into the fire, and it was said by Muhammad ﷺ when people said to him: ﴿Indeed, the people have gathered against you﴾.

When he says, ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾, he waits for his Lord's response: "This is between Me and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks." Let him reflect on the servitude (ubudiyya) in these two phrases and their rights, distinguish the phrase that belongs to God from the phrase that belongs to the servant, and understand the secret of why one of them is for God and the other for the servant. Let him distinguish between the monotheism (tawhid, the affirmation of God's oneness) required by "You alone we worship" and the tawhid required by "You alone we ask for help." Let him understand the wisdom of these two phrases being placed in the middle of the surah, between the two kinds of praise before them and the supplication after them. Let him understand the precedence of "You alone we worship" over "You alone we ask for help," and the precedence of the object over the verb while the verb comes later, which is more concise and brief, and the wisdom of repeating the pronoun again and again. Let him know what each of the two phrases averts of the calamity that opposes servitude, how the two phrases bring him into the pure form of servitude, and how the entire Qur'an, from its beginning to its end, revolves around these two phrases. Indeed, creation, command, reward, punishment, this world and the hereafter all revolve around them. Let him know how they encompass the noblest ends and the most complete means, and why they came with the pronoun of direct address and presence rather than the pronoun of the absent third person.

This is a subject that calls for a large book. Were it not for digressing from our purpose, we would have clarified it and expanded on it. Whoever wishes to examine it, we have mentioned it in the book "Stages of the Travelers Between the Stations of 'You Alone We Worship and You Alone We Ask for Help'" (Madarij al-Salikin) and in the book "al-Risala al-Misriyya."

[Benefit]
When the servant resolves to do a matter, he must first know whether it is an act of obedience to God or not. If it is not an act of obedience, he should not do it unless it is permissible, so that he may use it as an aid to obedience, and then it becomes an act of obedience. When it becomes clear to him that it is an act of obedience, he should not proceed with it until he considers whether it is being helped (by God) or not. If it is not being helped, he should not proceed, lest he humiliate himself. If it is being helped, there remains another consideration: that he approach it through its proper gate. If he approaches it from other than its gate, he will waste it, neglect it, or spoil some part of it. These three matters are the foundation of the servant's happiness and success, and they are the meaning of the servant's saying: ﴿You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path﴾.

The happiest of creatures are the people of worship, of seeking help, and of being guided to the sought goal. The most wretched are those who lack these three matters. Among people, some have a share of "You alone we worship" that is nonexistent or weak, and a share of "You alone we ask for help" that is also nonexistent or weak. These are forsaken, humiliated, and grieved. Others have a strong share of "You alone we ask for help" and a weak or absent share of "You alone we worship." These have influence, dominion, and strength, but they have no good end. Rather, their end is the worst of ends. Still others have a share of "You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help," but their share of being guided to the intended goal is very weak, like the condition of many worshippers and ascetics who have little knowledge of the realities of the guidance and the religion of truth with which God sent His Messenger ﷺ.

The saying of ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him: "Whoever's intention is sincere in the truth, even if it is against himself," is an indication that his standing for the truth for God is not sufficient if it is against others, unless he is the first to stand for it against himself. Then his standing for it against others is accepted. Otherwise, how can the truth be accepted from one who neglects to stand for it against himself?

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab once delivered a sermon while wearing two garments. He said: "O people, do you not hear?" Salman said: "We do not hear." ʿUmar said: "Why, O Abu ʿAbd Allah?" He said: "You distributed to us one garment each, and you have two garments." He said: "Do not hurry. O servant of God, O servant of God," but no one answered him. Then he said: "O ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar," and he said: "At your service, O Commander of the Faithful." He said: "I adjure you by God, is the garment with which I wrapped myself your garment?" He said: "Yes, by God, yes." Salman said: "Now, speak and we will listen."

[Section: For Every Person There Is Servitude to God According to His Rank]
His saying: "Judging in matters of truth is among the things by which God makes the reward obligatory and by which He makes the treasure good."

This is the servitude of judges and rulers that is required of them. For God, the Exalted, every person has a servitude according to his rank, apart from the general servitude in which He made His servants equal. So for the scholar, from his servitude is spreading the Sunnah and the knowledge with which God sent His Messenger, which is not required of the ignorant. He has the servitude of patience in that, which is not required of others. For the ruler, from the servitude is establishing the truth, enforcing it, and compelling those who are bound by it to comply, along with patience in that and striving for it, which is not required of the mufti. For the wealthy, from the servitude is discharging the rights that are in his wealth, which is not required of the poor. For the one able to enjoin good and forbid evil with his hand and tongue, there is what is not required of the one unable to do either.

Yahya ibn Muʿadh al-Razi once spoke about jihad and enjoining good and forbidding evil. A woman said to him: "This is an obligation that has been lifted from us." He said: "Suppose the weapons of the hand and tongue have been lifted from you, but the weapon of the heart has not been lifted from you." She said: "You have spoken the truth. May God reward you with good."

Iblis has deceived most of creation by making them think it is good to perform some kind of remembrance, recitation, prayer, fasting, asceticism in the world, and withdrawal, while they neglect these servitudes and do not move their hearts to perform them. Such people, in the view of the heirs of the prophets, are among the least religious of people. For religion is standing up for God in what He has commanded. So the one who abandons the rights of God that are obligatory upon him is in a worse state before God and His Messenger than the one who commits sins. For abandoning a command is greater than committing a prohibited act, for more than thirty reasons, which our shaykh, may God have mercy on him, mentioned in some of his works. Whoever has experience of what God sent His Messenger ﷺ with, and of what he and his Companions were upon, sees that most of those who are pointed to as religious are the least religious of people. And God is the One sought for help. What religion and what good is there in one who sees the sanctities of God violated, His limits neglected, His religion abandoned, and the Sunnah of the Messenger of God ﷺ shunned, while he is cold of heart and silent of tongue? He is a mute devil, just as the one who speaks falsehood is an articulate devil. Is the calamity of religion anything but from such people, who, if you grant them their food and their leadership, do not care about what happens to religion? The best of them is one who is grieved and anguished. Even if he were challenged in some matter that wounded his standing or wealth, he would exert himself, strive, and apply the three levels of denunciation according to his capacity. Yet these people, despite their fall in God's eyes and God's hatred toward them, have been afflicted in this world with the greatest affliction, and they do not perceive it. It is the death of the hearts. For whenever the life of the heart is more complete, its anger for God and His Messenger is stronger, and its support for religion is more perfect.

Imam Ahmad and others have mentioned a report that God, the Exalted, revealed to one of the angels: "Cause the village of such-and-such to be swallowed up." He said: "My Lord, how can that be, when there is such-and-such worshipper among them?" God said: "Begin with him, for his face has never once changed (in anger for My sake)."

Abu ʿUmar mentioned in the book "al-Tamhid" that God, the Exalted, revealed to one of His prophets: "Say to such-and-such ascetic: As for your asceticism in the world, you have hastened your rest by it. As for your devotion to Me, you have gained honor by it. But what have you done regarding what is due to Me from you?" He said: "My Lord, and what is due to You from me?" He said: "Have you befriended My friend or taken My enemy as an enemy?"

[Section: The Secret of Creation, Command, and the Laws]
The secret of creation, command, the books, the laws, reward, and punishment all comes down to these two phrases, and upon them revolves servitude and monotheism. It has been said: God sent down one hundred and four books, and He gathered their meanings in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. He gathered the meanings of these three books in the Qur'an, gathered the meanings of the Qur'an in the Mufassal (the final short surahs), gathered the meanings of the Mufassal in al-Fatiha, and gathered the meanings of al-Fatiha in ﴿You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5].

These are the two phrases divided between the Lord and His servant, in halves. Half of them is for Him, the Exalted, which is "You alone we worship," and half is for His servant, which is "You alone we ask for help." The secret of this and its meaning will come, God willing, in its proper place.

Worship (ʿibada) comprises two roots: the utmost love together with the utmost humility and submission. The Arabs say: "a paved road" (ṭariq muʿabbad), meaning one made smooth and level. Ta'abbud means humbling oneself and submitting. So whoever you love but are not submissive to, you are not worshipping him. And whoever you submit to without love, you are not worshipping him either, until you are both loving and submissive. For this reason, those who deny the love of the servants for their Lord deny the reality of servitude, and those who deny that He is beloved to them, indeed that He is the ultimate object of their seeking, and the highest goal of their desire, while denying that He is God (ilah), even if they acknowledge that He is Lord of the worlds and Creator of them, this is the extent of their monotheism. It is the monotheism of lordship (tawhid al-rububiyya) which the idolaters of the Arabs acknowledged, and by which they did not leave polytheism. As God, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "God"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87], and He said: ﴿If you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "God"﴾ [Luqman: 25], and ﴿Say: To whom belong the earth and whoever is in it?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 84], up to His saying ﴿They will say, "To God." Say: Then how are you deluded?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 89]. For this reason, they are argued against with it concerning the oneness of His divinity, and that none should be worshipped other than Him, just as there is no creator other than Him and no lord besides Him.

Seeking help (isti'āna) comprises two roots: trust in God (thiqa) and reliance upon Him (iʿtimad). For a servant may trust a person without relying on him in his affairs, because he is independent of him. And he may rely on a person without trusting him, because he needs him and there is no one else to take his place, so he must rely on him even though he does not trust him.

Tawakkul (complete reliance on God) is a meaning composed of two roots: trust and reliance. It is the reality of "﴿You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5]." These two roots, tawakkul and worship, are mentioned in the Qur'an in several places, in which He joined them together. This is the first.

The second: the saying of Shuʿayb: ﴿My success is only through God. In Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn in repentance﴾ [Hud: 88].

The third: His saying: ﴿To God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter returns, so worship Him and rely upon Him﴾ [Hud: 123].

The fourth: His saying, quoting the believers: ﴿Our Lord, in You we have put our trust, and to You we turn, and to You is the final return﴾ [al-Mumtahana: 4].

The fifth: His saying: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion. Lord of the East and the West, there is no god but He, so take Him as Guardian﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 8–9].

The sixth: His saying: ﴿Say: He is my Lord; there is no god but He. In Him I have put my trust, and to Him is my return﴾ [al-Ra'd: 30].

These are six places in which the two roots, "﴿You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5]," are combined.

The precedence of "worship" over "seeking help" in al-Fatiha is by way of giving precedence to ends over means. For "worship" is the end for which the servants were created, and "seeking help" is a means toward it. Also, "﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5]" relates to His divinity and to the name "Allah," while "﴿You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5]" relates to His lordship and to the name "Lord" (al-Rabb). So He placed "You alone we worship" before "You alone we ask for help," just as He placed the name "Allah" before "Lord" at the beginning of the surah. Also, "You alone we worship" is the portion of the Lord, and so it belongs to the first half, which is praise of God, the Exalted, since it is more fitting for Him. And "You alone we ask for help" is the portion of the servant, so it belongs to the half that is for him, which is "﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fatiha: 6]" to the end of the surah.

Also, "worship" in its absolute sense includes "seeking help," but not vice versa. Every servant who worships God with complete servitude seeks help from Him, but the converse does not hold, because the person of desires and appetites may seek help from Him to fulfil his appetites. Thus worship is more complete and perfect, and for this reason it is the portion of the Lord.

Also, "seeking help" is a part of "worship" but not vice versa. And also, "seeking help" is a request from Him, while "worship" is a devotion to Him.

And because worship ('ibadah) can only come from one who is sincere, whereas seeking help (istia'anah) can come from one who is sincere and from one who is not.

And because worship is His right, which He has made obligatory upon you, while seeking help is asking for aid in worship. It is an acknowledgment of His bounty, which He has bestowed upon you, and fulfilling His right is more important than dwelling on His bounty.

And because worship is thanks for His blessing upon you, and God loves to be thanked, whereas help is His action toward you and His enabling you. When you commit yourself to His servitude and enter under His dominion, He helps you to perform it. So committing to it and entering under His dominion is the cause of obtaining help, and the more complete the servant's servitude, the greater God's help to him.

Servitude is surrounded by two kinds of help: help before it, to commit to it and carry it out, and help after it, toward another act of servitude, and so on forever, until the servant fulfils his term.

And because "You alone we worship" is for Him, and "You alone we seek help from" is through Him. What is for Him takes precedence over what is through Him, because what is for Him is connected to His love and His pleasure, while what is through Him is connected to His will. What is connected to His love is more perfect than what is connected only to His will. For the whole of existence is connected to His will: the angels, the devils, the believers, the disbelievers, obedience and disobedience. But what is connected to His love is their obedience and their faith. So the disbelievers are the people of His will, and the believers are the people of His love. For this reason nothing for God ever settles in the Fire, and everything in it is through Him, the Exalted, and by His will.

These secrets clarify the wisdom in placing "You alone we worship" before "You alone we seek help from."

As for placing the object of worship and the object of seeking help before the two verbs, it contains: their courtesy toward God by placing His name before their act; it contains concern and intense care for Him; and it contains the indication of exclusivity, called restriction (hasr). So it has the force of: "We worship none but You, and we seek help from none but You." The judge in this is the taste of Arabic and understanding of it, and the induction of the places where this construction is used before the verb. Sibawayh stated the concern (ihtimam) and did not negate anything else.

And because it would be ugly for one who has freed ten slaves, for example, to then say to one of them, "It is you alone I have freed," and whoever hears him would reject this from him, saying, "You have freed others as well." Had the understanding of exclusivity not existed, this speech would not be considered ugly, nor would its rejection be fitting.

Reflect on His saying: ﴿And fear Me alone﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:40], ﴿And be wary of Me alone﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:41]. See how you find it has the force of: "Do not fear other than Me, and do not be wary of other than Me." Likewise "You alone we worship and You alone we seek help from" has the force of: "We do not worship other than You, and we do not seek help from other than You." Every person of sound taste understands this exclusivity from the reason of the context.

No weight is given to the disputation of one whose understanding is weak and who has been opened the door of doubt and sowing doubt. Such people are the plague of knowledge and the affliction of minds and understandings. Moreover, the pronoun "iyyaka" (إيّاكَ) contains an indication of the very essence and reality that the attached pronoun does not contain. In "iyyaka qasadtu wa-ahbabtu" (it is You I intended and loved) there is an indication of the meaning of Your reality and essence, my intention, which is not in your saying "qasadtuka wa-ahbabtuka" (I intended You and loved You). And in "iyyaka a'nI" (it is You I mean) there is the meaning: I mean Your self, Your essence, and Your reality.

From here some grammarians have said that "iyya" (إيّا) is a noun (ism zahir) with the attached pronoun as its annex, and this has not been refuted with a sufficient refutation.

Had I not been occupied with something beyond this, I would have extensively discussed this issue, mentioned the positions of the grammarians on it, supported the preferred view, and perhaps, God willing, I will return to this.

In repeating "iyyaka" a second time there is an indication that these matters are connected to each of the two verbs. In repeating the pronoun there is a strength of implication that is not present in omitting it. So if you say to a king, for example, "It is you I love, it is you I fear," there is in it, from the exclusivity of love and fear to his essence and the concern with mentioning it, what is not present in your saying, "It is you I love and fear."

[Section: The Categories of People Regarding Worship and Seeking Help]

Having understood this, people, regarding these two foundations, which are worship and seeking help, are of four categories.

The most excellent and noblest of them are the people of worship who seek help from God in it. The worship of God is the ultimate aim of their desire, and their request from Him is that He help them in it and enable them to perform it. For this reason, among the most excellent things the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, is asked for is help in pleasing Him. This is what the Prophet ﷺ taught to his beloved Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, when he said: "O Mu'adh, by God, I truly love you. Do not neglect to say after every prayer: 'O God, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well.'"

So the most beneficial supplication is asking for help in pleasing Him, and the most excellent gift is His granting this requested thing. All the transmitted supplications revolve around this, and around repelling what opposes it, and around perfecting it and facilitating its means. So reflect upon them.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may God sanctify his soul, said: "I contemplated the most beneficial supplication, and it is the request for help in pleasing Him. Then I found it in al-Fatihah in ﴿You alone we worship and You alone we seek help from﴾ [al-Fatihah 1:5]."

Opposite these is the second category: those who turn away from worshipping Him and from seeking help from Him. For them there is neither worship nor seeking help. Rather, if one of them asks Him and seeks His help, it is for his own portions and desires, not for the pleasure of his Lord and His rights. For He, Glorified is He, is asked by whoever is in the heavens and the earth. His allies and His enemies ask Him, and He provides for these and those. The most hateful of His creatures to Him is Iblis, yet he asked Him for something and He gave it to him and let him enjoy it. But since it was not a help for him in pleasing Him, it became an increase in his wretchedness, his distance from God, and his expulsion from Him. And likewise, everyone who seeks help from Him for a matter and asks Him for it, and it is not a help for obeying Him, it distances him from His pleasure and cuts him off from it, without doubt.

Let the intelligent person reflect on this regarding himself and others, and let him know that God's answering those who ask Him is not because of the askers' honour before Him. A servant asks Him for a need and He grants it, and in it lies his destruction and wretchedness. His granting it to him is due to his humiliation before Him and his fall from His regard. And His withholding from him is due to His honour for him and His love for him. He withholds it out of protection, safeguarding, and preservation, not out of stinginess. This is only what He does with His servant whom He wishes to honour and love, and treats with His kindness. Yet in his ignorance he thinks that God does not love him or honour him, and he sees Him granting the needs of others, so he thinks ill of his Lord. This is the filler of his heart, and he does not perceive it. The one protected is the one God protects, and "man is a witness against himself" (basirah).

The sign of this is that he blames the decrees (aqdar) and inwardly reproaches them, as it is said:

"The helpless in judgment squanders his opportunity,
until, when the matter has passed, he blames fate."

By God, if he uncovered his inner reality and secret, he would see there the reproach of fate and the accusation against it, and that it should have been such-and-such. But what can I do, and the matter is not in my hands? The intelligent person is the adversary of his own self, and the ignorant person is the adversary of the decrees of his Lord.

So beware with the utmost caution of asking Him for a specific thing whose outcome and consequence are hidden from you. If you find no alternative to asking Him, then make it conditional on His knowledge, in which the choice lies, and precede your request with istikharah (the prayer seeking divine guidance). Let not your istikharah be merely with the tongue without knowledge. Rather, it should be the istikharah of one who has no knowledge of his own interests, has no power over them, has no guidance to their details, and does not control harm or benefit for himself. Indeed, if he is left to himself, he will be utterly ruined, and his affairs will fall apart.

And when He gives you what He gives without your asking, ask Him to make it a help for you in obeying Him and a means to reach His pleasure, and not a cause of cutting you off from Him or a distancing from His pleasure. Do not think that all His giving is due to His servant's honour before Him, nor that all His withholding is due to his servant's humiliation before Him. Rather, His giving and His withholding are a trial and a test, by which He tests His servants. God, the Exalted, said:

﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him, honouring him and blessing him, he says, "My Lord has honoured me." But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me." No!﴾ [al-Fajr 89:15–17]

That is, not everyone to whom I give, bless, and provide has been honoured by Me, nor is that due to his honour before Me. Rather, it is a trial from Me and a test for him: will he thank Me so that I give him more than that, or will he disbelieve Me so that I take it from him and give it to another? And not everyone whom I test by restricting his provision, and whose provision I make limited with a measure beyond which there is no surplus, is so because of his humiliation before Me. Rather, it is a trial and test from Me for him: will he be patient so that I give him many times over what he missed of the abundance of provision, or will he be discontented so that his share is discontent?

Thus God, Glorified is He, refuted those who thought that abundance of provision is honour and poverty is humiliation, and He said: "I did not test My servant with wealth because of his honour before Me, nor did I test him with poverty because of his humiliation before Me." He informed that honour and humiliation do not revolve around wealth, abundance of provision, or its measure. For He, Glorified is He, grants abundance to the disbeliever, not out of honour for him, and restricts provision to the believer, not out of humiliation of him. He honours whoever honours Him through knowledge of Him, love for Him, and obedience to Him, and He humiliates whoever humiliates Him through turning away from Him and disobeying Him. So to Him belongs praise for this and for that, and He is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.

Thus the happiness of this world and the Hereafter returns to ﴿You alone we worship and You alone we seek help from﴾ [al-Fatihah 1:5].

The third category: those who have some form of worship without seeking help. These are of two types.

The first: the Qadariyyah, who claim that God has done for the servant all of what was within His power of kindnesses, and that nothing within His power remains to help him to act. They say He has helped him by creating the instruments and their soundness, by making the path known, by sending the messengers, and by enabling him to act. So after this there remains no help within His power for which he would ask Him. Rather, He has made His allies and His enemies equal in help: He helps these as He helps those. But His allies chose faith for themselves, and His enemies chose disbelief for themselves, without God having granted these a special enabling that necessitated faith for them, and forsaken those with another matter that necessitated disbelief for them. So these have a deficient share of worship, with no help accompanying it. They are left to themselves, and the path of seeking help and of tawhid (monotheism) is closed to them. Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, said: "Belief in qadar (divine decree) is the order of tawhid. Whoever believes in God and denies His decree, his denial nullifies his tawhid."

The second type: those who have acts of worship and litanies, but their share of tawakkul (trust in God) and seeking help is deficient. Their hearts have not been broad enough to encompass the connection of means with decree, and the dissolving of means within it, and their subsistence through it, and that without decree the means are like dead matter that has no effect, indeed like non-existence that has no being, and that decree is like the spirit that moves them, and the reliance is upon the first mover.

Thus the faculties of their insight have not penetrated from the moving to the mover, from the cause to the effect, from the instrument to the agent. So their resolve weakens and their aspirations fall short. Their share of "You alone we seek help from" [al-Fatihah 1:5] is diminished, and they do not find the taste of devotion through tawakkul and seeking help, even if they find its taste in litanies and duties.

For these there is a share of success, effectiveness, and influence in proportion to their seeking help and tawakkul, and for them there is a share of abandonment, weakness, humiliation, and incapacity in proportion to the scarcity of their seeking help and tawakkul. If the servant were to truly rely on God in removing a mountain from its place, and he were commanded to remove it, He would indeed remove it.

If you say: "What then is the meaning of tawakkul and seeking help?"

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 1, verse 5 (part 3 of 14):

I say: It is a state of the heart that arises from knowing God and believing in His sole authority over creation and governance, over harm and benefit, over giving and withholding, and that whatever He wills comes to be even if people do not will it, and whatever He does not will does not come to be even if people will it. This belief necessitates reliance upon Him, entrusting oneself to Him, tranquillity in Him, trust in Him, and certainty that He suffices for whatever one places one's trust in Him for, and that He is capable of it, and that nothing happens except by His will, whether people will it or their fathers do.

Its state resembles the state of a child with his two parents in what he desires of hope and fear, when they are the ones who hold sway over these things. So consider the detachment of his heart from turning to anyone other than his parents, and the confining of his concern to bringing about what he desires through them. This is the state of the one who relies upon God (al-mutawakkil), and whoever is like this with God, God will suffice him without fail. God the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever relies upon God, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [al-Talaq: 3], meaning He is sufficient for him, and ḥasb means the sufficient. If, along with this, he is among the people of taqwa, then the praiseworthy outcome is his, and if he is not among the people of taqwa, then he is [in a state of deficiency].

The Fourth Category: This is the one who witnesses God's sole authority over benefit and harm, and that whatever He wills comes to be and whatever He does not will does not come to be, yet he does not heed what He loves and is pleased with. So he relies upon Him, seeks His help in attaining his portions, his desires and his aims, asks Him for them, and brings them down through Him, and they are granted to him and he is helped to attain them. Whether these be wealth, leadership, or standing in the eyes of people, or spiritual states of unveiling, influence, power and establishment, yet for him there is no outcome, for these are of the same kind as apparent kingship, and wealth does not entail Islam, let alone closeness to God and being one of His friends. Kingship, standing, wealth and states are given to the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever. Whoever takes any of that as evidence of God's love for the one to whom He has given it, and of His pleasure with him, and that he is among His close friends, then he is among the most ignorant of the ignorant, and the furthest of them from knowledge of God and knowledge of His religion, and from distinguishing between what He loves and is pleased with, and what He hates and is angered by. The state [of spiritual experience] is of this world, and it is like kingship and wealth: if it helps its possessor to obey God and seek His pleasure and carry out His commands, it joins him with the just and righteous kings; otherwise it is a burden upon its possessor, distancing him from God, and joining him with the oppressive kings and the wicked rich.

[Chapter: One does not become truly realised in "You alone we worship" except by following the Messenger and sincerity, and the divisions of people in this regard]

When this is understood, the servant is not truly realised in ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5] except by two great foundations:
One of them: following the Messenger ﷺ.
The second: sincerity toward the One worshipped. This is the realisation of ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5].
People are also divided according to these two foundations into four categories:
The first: the people of sincerity toward the One worshipped and of following, and they are the people of ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5] in truth. Their deeds are all for God, their words are for God, their giving is for God, their withholding is for God, their love is for God, and their hatred is for God. Their dealings, outwardly and inwardly, are for the sake of God alone; they do not seek from people any reward or gratitude, nor the pursuit of standing with them, nor the seeking of praise and a position in their hearts, nor fleeing from their blame. Rather, they regard people as being in the position of the occupants of graves, who possess no power to harm or benefit them, nor to cause death or life or resurrection. So acting for the sake of people, seeking standing and position with them, and hoping for harm or benefit from them, never comes from one who knows them at all, but from one ignorant of their true state and ignorant of his Lord. Whoever knows people assigns them their proper places, and whoever knows God makes his deeds and words sincerely for Him, and his giving and withholding, and his love and hatred. He does not deal with any of creation apart from God except out of ignorance of God and ignorance of creation. Whenever he knows God and knows people, he prefers dealing with God over dealing with them.
Likewise, all their deeds and acts of worship conform to God's command and to what He loves and is pleased with, and this is the deed which God does not accept from any doer other than it, and it is the deed by which He tests His servants in life and death, as God the Exalted said: ﴿He who created death and life that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [al-Mulk: 2], and He made what is on the earth an adornment for it, to test them as to which of them is best in deed. Al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyad said: "The good deed is the most sincere of it and the most correct of it." They said: "O Abu ʿAli, what is its most sincere and most correct?" He said: "Indeed, if a deed is sincere but not correct, it is not accepted; and if it is correct but not sincere, it is not accepted, until it is both sincere and correct. The sincere is what is for God, and the correct is what is according to the Sunnah." This is what is meant in His saying ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110], and in His saying ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God while being a doer of good﴾ [al-Nisa: 125]. So God accepts from deeds only what is purely for His sake, upon following His command. Whatever else is so, it is rejected upon its doer, and it is returned to him in the state in which he most needs it, as scattered dust. In the Sahih, from the hadith of ʿAisha from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our affair, it is rejected." And every deed without emulation of the Prophet only increases its doer in distance from God, for God is worshipped only by His command, not by opinions and desires.

(Chapter)
The second type: one who has neither sincerity nor following. His deed does not conform to the Law, nor is it purely for the One worshipped. Such are the deeds of those who adorn themselves before people and show off to them with what God and His Messenger did not legislate. These are the worst of creation and the most detested by God, Mighty and Majestic, and they have the greatest share of His saying: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done—do not think them safe from punishment, and for them is a painful punishment﴾ [Al ʿImran: 188]. They rejoice in what they have done of innovation, misguidance and shirk, and they love to be praised for following the Sunnah and for sincerity.
This type is common among those of the people who claim knowledge, poverty and worship but have deviated from the straight path; they commit innovations and misguidance, showing off and seeking reputation, and they love to be praised for what they have not done of following, sincerity and knowledge. They are the people of wrath and misguidance.

[One who is sincere in his deeds but they are not in accordance with following the command]
The third type: one who is sincere in his deeds, but they are not in accordance with following the command, like ignorant worshippers, those who claim the path of asceticism and poverty, and everyone who worships God without His command and believes that this worship of his is a means of drawing near to God. This is his state, like one who thinks that listening to whistling and clapping is a means of nearness, or that seclusion in which one abandons Friday and congregational prayer is a means of nearness, or that continuous fasting from day into night is a means of nearness, or that fasting on the day when all people break their fast is a means of nearness, and similar things.

[One whose deeds are in accordance with following the command but are for other than God]
(Chapter)
The fourth type: one whose deeds are in accordance with following the command, but are for other than God, like the obedience of those who show off, and like the man who fights for show, zeal and bravery, or who performs Hajj so that it may be said of him, or who recites the Qur'an so that it may be said of him. Their deeds, outwardly, are righteous deeds commanded, but they are not righteous, so they are not accepted. ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship God, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyina: 5]. Thus everyone is only commanded to worship God by what He commanded, and to be sincere to Him in worship, and they are the people of ﴿You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5].

(Chapter: The people of the station of "You alone we worship" have four paths regarding the best worship, its most beneficial form, and what is most worthy of preference and specification)
Then the people of the station of ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5] have, regarding the best worship, its most beneficial form, and what is most worthy of preference and specification, four paths, and they are in this four groups:
The first group: in their view, the most beneficial and best acts of worship are those most difficult for the souls and hardest for them.
They said: because it is furthest from its desires, and it is the very reality of devotion.
They said: and the reward is according to the degree of hardship, and they related a hadith with no basis: "The best of deeds is the most arduous (aḥmazuhā)", meaning the hardest and most difficult.
These are the people of striving (mujahadat) and of pressing hard upon the souls.
They said: the souls are only set right by this, since their nature is laziness and abasement and inclination to the earth, so they are not set right except by mounting dangers and bearing hardships.
The second group said: the best acts of worship are detachment, asceticism in this world, minimising from it as far as possible, casting off concern for it, and not caring for anything that belongs to it.
Then these are two sorts:
Their common folk thought this was the ultimate goal, so they strove toward it, acted upon it, called people to it, and said: it is better than the rank of knowledge and worship, and they regarded asceticism in this world as the ultimate goal and head of every worship.
Their elite regarded this as sought for something else, and that what is intended by it is the heart's devotion to God, the gathering of aspiration upon Him, emptying the heart for love of Him, turning to Him in repentance, trusting in Him, and occupying oneself with seeking His pleasure. So they saw that the best worship is collectedness upon God, and constant remembrance of Him with the heart and the tongue, and occupation with watching over Him, above everything that scatters the heart and disperses it.
Then these are two sorts: the knowers who follow, when command and prohibition come, hasten to them even if it scatters them and takes away their collectedness; and the deviants among them say: the purpose of worship is the heart's collectedness upon God, so when something comes that separates it from God, it is not heeded; and perhaps one of them says:
"One is asked for litanies who is heedless, so how of a heart whose every moment is a litany?"
Then these again are two sorts: some of them abandon obligatory duties and obligations for the sake of their collectedness, and some of them perform them and abandon the sunnas and supererogatory acts, and the learning of beneficial knowledge, for the sake of their collectedness.
One of these asked a knowing shaykh, saying: "When the muezzin calls to prayer while I am in my collectedness upon God, if I rise and go out, I am lost, and if I remain as I am, I remain in my collectedness. What is better for me?"
He said: "When the muezzin calls to prayer and you are beneath the Throne, rise and answer the caller of God, then return to your place. This is because collectedness upon God is the share of the spirit and the heart, and answering the caller is the right of the Lord, and whoever prefers the share of his spirit over the right of his Lord is not among the people of ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5]."

The third group: they saw that the most beneficial and best acts of worship are those in which there is far-reaching benefit, so they regarded them as better than those whose benefit is limited to oneself. So they regarded serving the poor, occupying oneself with people's interests, fulfilling their needs, and assisting them with wealth, standing and benefit, as better. They therefore devoted themselves to it, acted upon it, and argued with the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "All creation are the dependants of God, and the most beloved of them to Him are those most beneficial to His dependants." Related by Abu Yaʿla.
They argued too that the worship of the worshipper is confined to himself, whereas the deed of the one who benefits extends to others, and where is the one of these from the other?
They said: for this reason the superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon over the rest of the stars.
They said: the Messenger of God ﷺ also said to ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: "That God guides a single man through you is better for you than red camels." This preference is only for far-reaching benefit. They also argued with his saying ﷺ: "Whoever calls to guidance has a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without any of their rewards being diminished." They argued with his saying ﷺ: "Indeed God and His angels send blessings upon those who teach the good to people," and with his saying ﷺ: "Indeed the scholar—those in the heavens and those on the earth seek forgiveness for him, even the fish in the sea and the ant in its hole."
They argued too that when the worshipper dies his deed is cut off, whereas the one whose benefit continues does not have his deed cut off, for as long as the benefit attributed to him continues.

واحْتَجُّوا بِأنَّ الأنْبِياءَ إنَّما بُعِثُوا بِالإحْسانِ إلى الخَلْقِ وهِدايَتِهِمْ، ونَفْعِهِمْ في مَعاشِهِمْ ومَعادِهِمْ، لَمْ يُبْعَثُوا بِالخُلْواتِ والِانْقِطاعِ عَنِ النّاسِ والتَّرَهُّبِ، ولِهَذا أنْكَرَ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ) عَلى أُولَئِكَ النَّفَرِ الَّذِينَ هَمُّوا بِالِانْقِطاعِ لِلتَّعَبُّدِ، وتَرْكِ مُخالَطَةِ النّاسِ، ورَأى هَؤُلاءِ التَّفَرُّقَ في أمْرِ اللَّهِ، ونَفْعَ عِبادِهِ، والإحْسانَ إلَيْهِمْ، أفْضَلَ مِنَ الجَمْعِيَّةِ عَلَيْهِ بِدُونِ ذَلِكَ.

الصِّنْفُ الرّابِعُ، قالُوا: إنَّ أفْضَلَ العِبادَةِ العَمَلُ عَلى مَرْضاةِ الرَّبِّ في كُلِّ وقْتٍ بِما هو مُقْتَضى ذَلِكَ الوَقْتِ ووَظِيفَتُهُ، فَأفْضَلُ العِباداتِ في وقْتِ الجِهادِ: الجِهادُ، وإنْ آلَ إلى تَرْكِ الأوْرادِ، مِن صَلاةِ اللَّيْلِ وصِيامِ النَّهارِ، بَلْ ومِن تَرْكِ إتْمامِ صَلاةِ الفَرْضِ، كَما في حالَةِ الأمْنِ.

والأفْضَلُ في وقْتِ حُضُورِ الضَّيْفِ مَثَلًا القِيامُ بِحَقِّهِ، والِاشْتِغالُ بِهِ عَنِ الوِرْدِ المُسْتَحَبِّ، وكَذَلِكَ في أداءِ حَقِّ الزَّوْجَةِ والأهْلِ.

والأفْضَلُ في أوْقاتِ السَّحَرِ الِاشْتِغالُ بِالصَّلاةِ والقُرْآنِ، والدُّعاءِ والذِّكْرِ والِاسْتِغْفارِ.

والأفْضَلُ في وقْتِ اسْتِرْشادِ الطّالِبِ، وتَعْلِيمِ الجاهِلِ الإقْبالُ عَلى تَعْلِيمِهِ والِاشْتِغالِ بِهِ.

والأفْضَلُ في أوْقاتِ الأذانِ تَرْكُ ما هو فِيهِ مِن وِرْدِهِ، والِاشْتِغالُ بِإجابَةِ المُؤَذِّنِ.

والأفْضَلُ في أوْقاتِ الصَّلَواتِ الخَمْسِ الجِدُّ والنُّصْحُ في إيقاعِها عَلى أكْمَلِ الوُجُوهِ، والمُبادَرَةُ إلَيْها في أوَّلِ الوَقْتِ، والخُرُوجُ إلى الجامِعِ، وإنْ بَعُدَ كانَ أفْضَلَ.

والأفْضَلُ في أوْقاتِ ضَرُورَةِ المُحْتاجِ إلى المُساعَدَةِ بِالجاهِ، أوِ البَدَنِ، أوِ المالِ الِاشْتِغالُ بِمُساعَدَتِهِ، وإغاثَةُ لَهْفَتِهِ، وإيثارُ ذَلِكَ عَلى أوْرادِكَ وخَلْوَتِكَ.

والأفْضَلُ في وقْتِ قِراءَةِ القُرْآنِ جَمْعِيَّةُ القَلْبِ والهِمَّةِ عَلى تَدَبُّرِهِ وتَفَهُّمِهِ، حَتّى كَأنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى يُخاطِبُكَ بِهِ، فَتَجْمَعُ قَلْبَكَ عَلى فَهْمِهِ وتَدَبُّرِهِ، والعَزْمُ عَلى تَنْفِيذِ أوامِرِهِ أعْظَمُ مِن جَمْعِيَّةِ قَلْبِ مَن جاءَهُ كِتابٌ مِنَ السُّلْطانِ عَلى ذَلِكَ.

والأفْضَلُ في وقْتِ الوُقُوفِ بِعَرَفَةَ الِاجْتِهادُ في التَّضَرُّعِ والدُّعاءِ والذِّكْرِ دُونَ الصَّوْمِ المُضْعِفِ عَنْ ذَلِكَ.

والأفْضَلُ في أيّامِ عَشْرِ ذِي الحِجَّةِ الإكْثارُ مِنَ التَّعَبُّدِ، لاسِيَّما التَّكْبِيرُ والتَّهْلِيلُ والتَّحْمِيدُ، فَهو أفْضَلُ مِنَ الجِهادِ غَيْرِ المُتَعَيَّنِ.

والأفْضَلُ في العَشْرِ الأخِيرِ مِن رَمَضانَ لُزُومُ المَسْجِدِ فِيهِ والخَلْوَةِ والِاعْتِكافِ دُونَ التَّصَدِّي لِمُخالَطَةِ النّاسِ والِاشْتِغالِ بِهِمْ، حَتّى إنَّهُ أفْضَلُ مِنَ الإقْبالِ عَلى تَعْلِيمِهِمُ العِلْمَ، وإقْرائِهِمُ القُرْآنَ، عِنْدَ كَثِيرٍ مِنَ العُلَماءِ.

والأفْضَلُ في وقْتِ مَرَضِ أخِيكَ المُسْلِمِ أوْ مَوْتِهِ عِيادَتُهُ، وحُضُورُ جِنازَتِهِ وتَشْيِيعُهُ، وتَقْدِيمُ ذَلِكَ عَلى خَلْوَتِكَ وجَمْعِيَّتِكَ.

والأفْضَلُ في وقْتِ نُزُولِ النَّوازِلِ وأذاةِ النّاسِ لَكَ أداءُ واجِبِ الصَّبْرِ مَعَ خُلْطَتِكَ بِهِمْ، دُونَ الهَرَبِ مِنهُمْ، فَإنَّ المُؤْمِنَ الَّذِي يُخالِطُ النّاسَ لِيَصْبِرَ عَلى أذاهم أفْضَلُ مِنَ الَّذِي لا يُخالِطُهم ولا يُؤْذُونَهُ.

والأفْضَلُ خُلْطَتُهم في الخَيْرِ، فَهي خَيْرٌ مِنَ اعْتِزالِهِمْ فِيهِ، واعْتِزالُهم في الشَّرِّ، فَهو أفْضَلُ مِن خُلْطَتِهِمْ فِيهِ، فَإنْ عَلِمَ أنَّهُ إذا خالَطَهم أزالَهُ أوْ قَلَّلَهُ فَخُلْطَتُهم حِينَئِذٍ أفْضَلُ مِنِ اعْتِزالِهِمْ.

فالأفْضَلُ في كُلِّ وقْتٍ وحالٍ إيثارُ مَرْضاةِ اللَّهِ في ذَلِكَ الوَقْتِ والحالِ، والِاشْتِغالُ بِواجِبِ ذَلِكَ الوَقْتِ ووَظِيفَتِهِ ومُقْتَضاهُ.

وَهَؤُلاءِ هم أهْلُ التَّعَبُّدِ المُطْلَقِ، والأصْنافُ قِبَلَهم أهْلُ التَّعَبُّدِ المُقَيَّدِ، فَمَتى خَرَجَ أحَدُهم عَنِ النَّوْعِ الَّذِي تَعَلَّقَ بِهِ مِنَ العِبادَةِ وفارَقَهُ يَرى نَفْسَهُ كَأنَّهُ قَدْ نَقَصَ وتَرَكَ عِبادَتَهُ، فَهو يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ عَلى وجْهٍ واحِدٍ، وصاحِبُ التَّعَبُّدِ المُطْلَقِ لَيْسَ لَهُ غَرَضٌ في تَعَبُّدٍ بِعَيْنِهِ يُؤْثِرُهُ عَلى غَيْرِهِ، بَلْ غَرَضُهُ تَتَبُّعُ مَرْضاةِ اللَّهِ تَعالى أيْنَ كانَتْ، فَمَدارُ تَعَبُّدِهِ عَلَيْها، فَهو لا يَزالُ مُتَنَقِّلًا في مَنازِلِ العُبُودِيَّةِ، كُلَّما رُفِعَتْ لَهُ مَنزِلَةٌ عَمِلَ عَلى سَيْرِهِ إلَيْها، واشْتَغَلَ بِها حَتّى تَلُوحَ لَهُ مَنزِلَةٌ أُخْرى، فَهَذا دَأْبَهُ في السَّيْرِ حَتّى يَنْتَهِيَ سَيْرُهُ، فَإنْ رَأيْتَ العُلَماءَ رَأيْتَهُ مَعَهُمْ، وإنْ رَأيْتَ العُبّادَ رَأيْتَهُ مَعَهُمْ، وإنْ رَأيْتَ المُجاهِدِينَ رَأيْتَهُ مَعَهُمْ، وإنْ رَأيْتَ الذّاكِرِينَ رَأيْتَهُ مَعَهُمْ، وإنْ رَأيْتَ المُتَصَدِّقِينَ المُحْسِنِينَ رَأيْتَهُ مَعَهُمْ، وإنْ رَأيْتَ أرْبابَ الجَمْعِيَّةِ وعُكُوفِ القَلْبِ عَلى اللَّهِ رَأيْتَهُ مَعَهُمْ، فَهَذا هو العَبْدُ المُطْلَقُ، الَّذِي لَمْ تَمْلِكْهُ الرُّسُومُ، ولَمْ تُقَيِّدْهُ القُيُودُ، ولَمْ يَكُنْ عَمَلُهُ عَلى مُرادِ نَفْسِهِ وما فِيهِ لَذَّتُها وراحَتُها مِنَ العِباداتِ، بَلْ هو عَلى مُرادِ رَبِّهِ، ولَوْ كانَتْ راحَةُ نَفْسِهِ ولَذَّتُها في سِواهُ، فَهَذا هو المُتَحَقِّقُ بِ"﴿إيّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وإيّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ﴾ [الفاتحة: ٥]" حَقًّا، القائِمُ بِهِما صِدْقًا، مَلْبَسُهُ ما تَهَيَّأ، ومَأْكَلُهُ ما تَيَسَّرَ، واشْتِغالُهُ بِما أمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ في كُلِّ وقْتٍ بِوَقْتِهِ، ومَجْلِسُهُ حَيْثُ انْتَهى بِهِ المَكانُ ووَجَدَهُ خالِيًا، لا تَمْلِكُهُ إشارَةٌ، ولا يَتَعَبَّدُهُ قَيْدٌ، ولا يَسْتَوْلِي عَلَيْهِ رَسْمٌ، حُرٌّ مُجَرَّدٌ، دائِرٌ مَعَ الأمْرِ حَيْثُ دارَ، يَدِينُ بِدِينِ الآمِرِ أنّى تَوَجَّهَتْ رَكائِبُهُ، ويَدُورُ مَعَهُ حَيْثُ اسْتَقَلَّتْ مَضارِبُهُ، يَأْنَسُ بِهِ كُلُّ مُحِقٍّ، ويَسْتَوْحِشُ مِنهُ كُلُّ مُبْطِلٍ، كالغَيْثِ حَيْثُ وقَعَ نَفَعَ، وكالنَخْلَةِ لا يَسْقُطُ ورَقُها وكُلُّها مَنفَعَةٌ حَتّى شَوْكُها، وهو مَوْضِعُ الغِلْظَةِ مِنهُ عَلى المُخالِفِينَ لِأمْرِ اللَّهِ، والغَضَبِ إذا انْتُهِكَتْ مَحارِمُ اللَّهِ، فَهو لِلَّهِ وبِاللَّهِ ومَعَ اللَّهِ، قَدْ صَحِبَ اللَّهَ بِلا خَلْقٍ، وصَحِبَ النّاسَ بِلا نَفْسٍ، بَلْ إذا كانَ مَعَ اللَّهِ عَزَلَ الخَلائِقَ عَنِ البَيْنِ، وتَخَلّى عَنْهُمْ، وإذا كانَ مَعَ خَلْقِهِ عَزَلَ نَفْسَهُ مِنَ الوَسَطِ وتَخَلّى عَنْها، فَواهًا لَهُ! ما أغْرَبَهُ بَيْنَ النّاسِ! وما أشَدَّ وحْشَتَهُ مِنهُمْ! وما أعْظَمَ أُنْسَهُ بِاللَّهِ وفَرَحَهُ بِهِ، وطُمَأْنِينَتَهُ وسُكُونَهُ إلَيْهِ! واللَّهُ المُسْتَعانُ، وعَلَيْهِ التُكْلانُ.

[فَصْلٌ: مَنفَعَةُ العِبادَةِ وحِكْمَتُها ومَقْصُودُها وانْقِسامُ النّاسِ في ذَلِكَ لِأرْبَعَةِ أصْنافٍ]

[نُفاةُ التَّعْلِيلِ]

ثُمَّ لِلنّاسِ في مَنفَعَةِ العِبادَةِ وحِكْمَتِها ومَقْصُودِها طُرُقٌ أرْبَعَةٌ، وهم في ذَلِكَ أرْبَعَةُ أصْنافٍ.
