الصِّنْفُ الأوَّلُ: نُفاةُ الحُكْمِ والتَّعْلِيلِ (ta'līl: attributing acts to causes and wisdom)، الَّذِينَ يَرُدُّونَ الأمْرَ إلى مَحْضِ المَشِيئَةِ، وصِرْفِ الإرادَةِ، فَهَؤُلاءِ عِنْدَهُمُ القِيامُ بِها لَيْسَ إلّا لِمُجَرَّدِ الأمْرِ، مِن غَيْرِ أنْ تَكُونَ سَبَبًا لِسَعادَةٍ في مَعاشٍ ولا مَعادٍ، ولا سَبَبًا لِنَجاةٍ، وإنَّما القِيامُ بِها لِمُجَرَّدِ الأمْرِ ومَحْضِ المَشِيئَةِ، كَما قالُوا في الخَلْقِ: إنَّهُ لَمْ يَخْلُقْ ما خَلَقَهُ لِعِلَّةٍ، ولا لِغايَةٍ هي المَقْصُودَةُ بِهِ، ولا لِحِكْمَةٍ تَعُودُ إلَيْهِ مِنهُ، ولَيْسَ في المَخْلُوقاتِ أسْبابٌ مُقْتَضِياتٌ لِمُسَبَّباتِها، ولا فِيها قُوًى ولا طَبائِعُ، فَلَيْسَتِ النّارُ سَبَبًا لِلْإحْراقِ، ولا الماءُ سَبَبًا لِلْإرْواءِ والبَرْدِ وإخْراجِ النَّباتِ، ولا فِيهِ قُوَّةٌ ولا طَبِيعَةٌ تَقْتَضِي ذَلِكَ، وحُصُولُ الإحْراقِ والرِّيِّ لَيْسَ بِهِما، لَكِنْ بِإجْراءِ العادَةِ الاقْتِرانِيَّةِ عَلى حُصُولِ هَذا عِنْدَ هَذا لا بِسَبَبٍ ولا بِقُوَّةٍ قامَتْ بِهِ، وهَكَذا الأمْرُ عِنْدَهم في أمْرِهِ الشَّرْعِيِّ سَواءٌ، لا فَرْقَ في نَفْسِ الأمْرِ بَيْنَ المَأْمُورِ والمَحْظُورِ، ولَكِنَّ المَشِيئَةَ اقْتَضَتْ أمْرَهُ بِهَذا ونَهْيَهُ عَنْ هَذا، مِن غَيْرِ أنْ يَقُومَ بِالمَأْمُورِ بِهِ صِفَةٌ اقْتَضَتْ حُسْنَهُ، ولا المَنهِيِّ عَنْهُ صِفَةٌ اقْتَضَتْ قُبْحَهُ.

وَلِهَذا الأصْلِ لَوازِمُ وفُرُوعٌ كَثِيرَةٌ فاسِدَةٌ، وقَدْ ذَكَرْناها في كِتابِنا الكَبِيرِ المُسَمّى "مِفْتاحُ دارِ السَّعادَةِ ومَطْلَبُ أهْلِ العِلْمِ والإرادَةِ" وبَيَّنّا فَسادَ هَذا الأصْلِ مِن نَحْوِ سِتِّينَ وجْهًا، وهو كِتابٌ بَدِيعٌ في مَعْناهُ، وذَكَرْناهُ أيْضًا في كِتابِنا المُسَمّى "سَفَرُ الهِجْرَتَيْنِ وطَرِيقُ السَّعادَتَيْنِ".

وَهَؤُلاءِ لا يَجِدُونَ حَلاوَةَ العِبادَةِ ولا لَذَّتَها، ولا يَتَنَعَّمُونَ بِها، ولَيْسَتِ الصَّلاةُ قُرَّةَ أعْيُنِهِمْ، ولَيْسَتِ الأوامِرُ سُرُورَ قُلُوبِهِمْ، وغِذاءَ أرْواحِهِمْ وحَياتِهِمْ، ولِهَذا يُسَمُّونَها تَكالِيفَ، أيْ قَدْ كُلِّفُوا بِها، ولَوْ سَمّى مُدَّعٍ لِمَحَبَّةِ مَلِكٍ مِنَ المُلُوكِ أوْ غَيْرِهِ ما يَأْمُرُهُ بِهِ تَكْلِيفًا، وقالَ: إنِّي إنَّما أفْعَلُهُ بِكُلْفَةٍ، لَمْ يَعُدَّهُ أحَدٌ مُحِبًّا لَهُ، ولِهَذا أنْكَرَ هَؤُلاءِ أوْ كَثِيرٌ مِنهم مَحَبَّةَ العَبْدِ لِرَبِّهِ، وقالُوا: إنَّما يُحِبُّ ثَوابَهُ وما يَخْلُقُهُ لَهُ مِنَ النَّعِيمِ الَّذِي يَتَمَتَّعُ بِهِ، لا أنَّهُ يُحِبُّ ذاتَهُ، فَجَعَلُوا المَحَبَّةَ لِمَخْلُوقِهِ دُونَهُ، وحَقِيقَةُ العُبُودِيَّةِ هي كَمالُ المَحَبَّةِ، فَأنْكَرُوا حَقِيقَةَ العُبُودِيَّةِ ولُبَّها، وحَقِيقَةُ الإلَهِيَّةِ كَوْنُهُ مَأْلُوهًا مَحْبُوبًا بِغايَةِ الحُبِّ، المَقْرُونِ بِغايَةِ الذُّلِّ والخُضُوعِ، والإجْلالِ والتَّعْظِيمِ، فَأنْكَرُوا كَوْنَهُ مَحْبُوبًا، وذَلِكَ إنْكارٌ لِإلَهِيَّتِهِ، وشَيْخُ هَؤُلاءِ هو الجَعْدُ بْنُ دِرْهَمٍ الَّذِي ضَحّى بِهِ خالِدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ القَسْرِيُّ في يَوْمِ أضْحى، وقالَ: إنَّهُ زَعَمَ أنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يُكَلِّمْ مُوسى تَكْلِيمًا، ولَمْ يَتَّخِذْ إبْراهِيمَ خَلِيلًا، وإنَّما كانَ إنْكارُهُ لِكَوْنِهِ تَعالى مَحْبُوبًا مُحِبًّا، لَمْ يُنْكِرْ حاجَةَ إبْراهِيمَ إلَيْهِ، الَّتِي هي الخُلَّةُ عِنْدَ الجَهْمِيَّةِ، الَّتِي يَشْتَرِكُ فِيها جَمِيعُ الخَلائِقِ، فَكُلُّهم أخِلّاءُ لِلَّهِ عِنْدَهم.

وَقَدْ بَيَّنّا فَسادَ قَوْلِهِمْ هَذا، وإنْكارِهِمْ مَحَبَّةَ اللَّهِ مِن أكْثَرَ مِن ثَمانِينَ وجْهًا في كِتابِنا المُسَمّى "قُرَّةُ عُيُونِ المُحِبِّينَ، ورَوْضَةُ قُلُوبِ العارِفِينَ" وذَكَرْنا فِيهِ وُجُوبُ تَعَلُّقِ المَحَبَّةِ بِالحَبِيبِ الأوَّلِ مِن جَمِيعِ طُرُقِ الأدِلَّةِ النَّقْلِيَّةِ والعَقْلِيَّةِ والذَّوْقِيَّةِ والفِطْرِيَّةِ وأنَّهُ لا كَمالَ لِلْإنْسانِ بِدُونِ ذَلِكَ ألْبَتَّةَ، كَما أنَّهُ لا كَمالَ لِجِسْمِهِ إلّا بِالرُّوحِ والحَياةِ، ولا لِعَيْنِهِ إلّا بِالنُّورِ الباصِرِ، ولا لِأُذُنِهِ إلّا بِالسَّمْعِ، وأنَّ الأمْرَ فَوْقَ ذَلِكَ وأعْظَمُ.

[القَدَرِيَّةُ النُفاةُ]

الصِّنْفُ الثّانِي: القَدَرِيَّةُ النُفاةُ (al-Qadariyyah al-nufāh: those who deny divine decree in the sense of God's creation of acts, here used for those who affirm wisdom but deny it inheres in God)، الَّذِينَ يُثْبِتُونَ نَوْعًا مِنَ الحِكْمَةِ والتَّعْلِيلِ ولَكِنْ لا يَقُومُ بِالرَّبِّ، ولا يَرْجِعُ إلَيْهِ، بَلْ يَرْجِعُ إلى مُجَرَّدِ مَصْلَحَةِ المَخْلُوقِ ومَنفَعَتِهِ.

فَعِنْدَهُمْ: أنَّ العِباداتِ شُرِعَتْ أثْمانًا لِما يَنالُهُ العِبادُ مِنَ الثَّوابِ والنَّعِيمِ، وأنَّها بِمَنزِلَةِ اسْتِيفاءِ أُجْرَةِ الأجِيرِ.

قالُوا: ولِهَذا يَجْعَلُها اللَّهُ تَعالى عِوَضًا كَقَوْلِهِ ﴿وَنُودُوا أنْ تِلْكُمُ الجَنَّةُ أُورِثْتُمُوها بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [الأعراف: ٤٣]، أيْ: "وأُنْدوا أنَّ تلكم الجنةُ أُعطيتموها بسبب ما كنتم تعملون"، وقَوْلِهِ ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [النحل: ٣٢]، وقَوْلِهِ ﴿هَلْ تُجْزَوْنَ إلّا ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [النمل: ٩٠]، وقَوْلِهِ ﷺ فِيما يَحْكِي عَنْ رَبِّهِ عَزَّ وجَلَّ: «يا عِبادِي، إنَّما هي أعْمالُكم أُحْصِيها لَكُمْ، ثُمَّ أُوَفِّيكم إيّاها» وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى ﴿إنَّما يُوَفّى الصّابِرُونَ أجْرَهم بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ﴾ [الزمر: ١٠].

قالُوا: وقَدْ سَمّاهُ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ جَزاءً وأجْرًا وثَوابًا، لِأنَّهُ يَثُوبُ إلى العامِلِ مِن عَمَلِهِ، أيْ يَرْجِعُ إلَيْهِ مِنهُ.

قالُوا: ولَوْلا ارْتِباطُهُ بِالعَمَلِ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِتَسْمِيَتِهِ جَزاءً ولا أجْرًا ولا ثَوابًا مَعْنًى.

قالُوا: ويَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ الوَزْنُ، فَلَوْلا تَعَلُّقُ الثَّوابِ والعِقابِ بِالأعْمالِ واقْتِضاؤُها لَها، وكَوْنُها كالأثْمانِ لَها لَمْ يَكُنْ لِلْوَزْنِ مَعْنًى، وقَدْ قالَ تَعالى ﴿والوَزْنُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الحَقُّ فَمَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ المُفْلِحُونَ - ومَن خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَأُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسَهم بِما كانُوا بِآياتِنا يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ [الأعراف: ٨-٩].

وَهاتانِ الطّائِفَتانِ مُتَقابِلَتانِ أشَدَّ التَّقابُلِ، وبَيْنَهُما أعْظَمُ التَّبايُنِ.

فالجَبْرِيَّةُ (al-Jabriyyah: those who hold that human beings are compelled in their acts, with no real connection between deeds and reward) لَمْ تَجْعَلْ لِلْأعْمالِ ارْتِباطًا بِالجَزاءِ ألْبَتَّةَ، وجَوَّزَتْ أنْ يُعَذِّبَ اللَّهُ مَن أفْنى عُمْرَهُ في طاعَتِهِ، ويُنَعِّمَ مَن أفْنى عُمْرَهُ في مَعْصِيَتِهِ، وكِلاهُما بِالنِسْبَةِ إلَيْهِ سَواءٌ، وجَوَّزَتْ أنْ يَرْفَعَ صاحِبَ العَمَلِ القَلِيلِ عَلى مَن هو أعْظَمُ مِنهُ عَمَلًا، وأكْثَرُ وأفْضَلُ دَرَجاتٍ، والكُلُّ عِنْدَهم راجِعٌ إلى مَحْضِ المَشِيئَةِ، مِن غَيْرِ تَعْلِيلٍ ولا سَبَبٍ، ولا حِكْمَةٍ تَقْتَضِي تَخْصِيصَ هَذا بِالثَوابِ، وهَذا بِالعِقابِ.

The Qadariyya (advocates of free will, who held that God is obliged to do what is best for His servants) made it binding upon God to care for what is most beneficial, and they made all of that a mere exchange for deeds, a price paid for them. They argued that if reward reached the servant without his works, it would be spoiled by the possibility of a favour bestowed on him without any price.

May God fight them! How ignorant they are of God, and how deluded! They treated God's grace and kindness toward His servant as if it were a servant's charity to another servant, to the point that they said: His giving a person what He gives him as a wage for his work is more beloved to the servant and more pleasant for him than His giving it to him as a bounty without any work.

The Jabriyya (determinists, who denied any real causal role for human actions) opposed them in the most extreme way, and did not grant works any effect on the recompense whatsoever.

Both groups are unjust and have deviated from the straight path upon which God created His servants, which the messengers brought and which the books revealed. That path is that deeds are causes that lead to reward and punishment, necessitating them just as all causes necessitate their effects. The good deeds are from God's guidance, bounty, favour, and charity toward His servant, if He helps him to do them, enables him to do them, creates in him the will to do them and the power over them, makes them beloved to him, adorns them in his heart, and makes their opposites hateful to him. Yet despite all this, they are not a price for His recompense and reward, nor are they commensurate with it. Rather, the most that can be said is that when the servant exerts his sincere effort and striving in them and performs them in the most perfect manner, they amount to thanks to Him for some of His blessings upon him. If He were to demand from him his full due, there would remain for him some part of the thanks owed for that blessing that he had not fulfilled. Therefore, if He were to punish the inhabitants of His heavens and the inhabitants of His earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them. And if He were to show them mercy, His mercy would be better for them than their deeds, as has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ).

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) denied that anyone enters Paradise by deeds, as he said: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deed alone." In another wording: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deed." In another wording: "None of you will be saved by his deed." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I, unless God covers me with His mercy and bounty."

And God, glorified is He, affirmed entry into Paradise by deeds, as in His saying: ﴿Enter Paradise for what you used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 32]. There is no contradiction between them, because the negation and the affirmation are not with respect to one and the same meaning. What is negated is that one deserves Paradise merely by deeds, and that deeds are a price and a return for it. This is a refutation of the Qadariyya Majusiyya (the "Magian" Qadariyya), who claimed that bestowing reward as an initial favour implies a repetition of obligation (on the servant's part).

This group is among the most ignorant of creation regarding God, and the most thickly veiled from Him. They deserve to be called the Magians of this Ummah. Sufficient evidence of their ignorance of God is that they did not know that the inhabitants of His heavens and His earth are in His favour, and that among the completeness of joy, delight, pleasure and happiness is their rejoicing in the favour of their Master and Lord, the True One, and that they only find their life pleasant through this favour. The most elevated of them in rank with Him, and the closest to Him, are those who know this favour best, who most affirm it, mention it, thank Him for it, and love Him because of it. Is there anyone who ever moves about except within His favour? ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: Do not consider your Islam a favour to me. Rather, God bestows a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17].

The acceptance of a creature's favour is only a deficiency because the creature is like the one it favours; when he confers a favour upon him, he exalts himself over him, and the one who receives the favour sees himself as lower than him. This is so even though it is not found in every creature. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has a favour over his Ummah, and his Companions used to say: "God and His Messenger are more bountiful." There is no deficiency in a father's favour upon his child, nor any shame for him in accepting it. Likewise a master's favour toward his slave. How then could it be a deficiency for the Lord of the Worlds, in whose ocean of favour creatures move about, and in whose pure charity toward them they live, without any return from them whatsoever? Even if their deeds are causes for what they receive of His generosity and munificence, He is the one who bestows favour upon them by enabling them to do those causes, guiding them to them, helping them to perform them, completing them for them, and accepting them from them despite their imperfections. And this is the meaning by which He established entry into Paradise in His saying: ﴿for what you used to do﴾ [al-A'raf: 43].

So this is the "ba" of causation (bi-ma: "for what"), a refutation of the Qadariyya and the Jabriyya who say: there is no connection between deeds and recompense, and deeds are not causes for it; their utmost role is to be signs.

They also say: this connection is not consistent, since recompense does not always follow deeds, both in good and in evil. So nothing remains except the bare cosmic command and the divine will.

The texts refute the view of these people, just as they refute the view of those others. The rational and natural proofs also refute the positions of both parties, and make clear to whoever has a heart and intellect the true value of the position of the People of the Sunnah, who are the middle sect: those who affirm the universality of God's will and power, His creation of servants and their actions, and His perfect wisdom, which includes linking causes to their effects, and their being established by them both legally and cosmically, and their consequences following upon them, both in this world and the next.

Each of the two deviant groups abandoned a kind of truth and committed a kind of falsehood on its account, indeed many kinds. God guided the People of the Sunnah to the truth in what the others differed about, by His permission: ﴿God guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ [al-Baqarah: 213], and ﴿That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Owner of great bounty﴾ [al-Hadid: 21].

[Those who claimed that the purpose of worship is the discipline of the souls]

The third category: those who claimed that the benefit of worship is the disciplining of the souls and preparing them to receive the overflow of knowledge upon them, and bringing their powers out of the powers of the predatory and bestial souls. If they were deprived of acts of worship, they would be of the same nature as the souls of beasts and cattle. Acts of worship take them out of their habits and customs and move them to resemble pure intellects, so that they become knowing and receptive to the imprinting of forms of knowledge and gnosis upon them. This is said by two groups:

The first: those who came close to the prophethoods and the revealed laws among the philosophers, who held the eternity of the world, the non-splitting of the spheres, and the absence of a free-choosing agent.

The second: those among the Sufis of Islam who philosophized and drew close to the philosophers. They claim that acts of worship are exercises to prepare the souls and free them, to detach them from the sensible world, and for inspirations and knowledge to descend upon them.

Among these people are some who make acts of worship obligatory only for this purpose. Once they have achieved it, the person remains free to preserve it, to let it go, or to occupy himself with what comes to him from it. Others among them make it obligatory to observe the litanies and duties, and not to neglect them. These also are of two kinds:

One: those who make it obligatory as a means of keeping the law and disciplining the souls.

The others: those who make it obligatory to preserve the inspiration, and out of fear that the soul, by abandoning it, will slide back to its earlier bestial state.

This is the ultimate reach of the steps of the theologians on the path of spiritual wayfaring, and the extent of their knowledge of the wisdom of worship and what it was legislated for. You will hardly find in the books of these people any approaches other than these three, whether combined or as alternatives.

[The Muhammadan Abrahamic group]

As for the fourth category: they are the Muhammadan Abrahamic group, followers of the two Friends (Abraham and Muhammad, peace be upon them), who know God and His wisdom in His command, His law, and His creation, and who possess insight into worship and into what God intends by it.

The three groups are veiled from them by the false doubts they hold and the corrupt foundations they rely on. They think there is nothing beyond what they have. They rejoice in what they have of falsehood, and they are content with the illusions to which they are accustomed. If they knew that beyond it there is something more sublime and greater, they would not be satisfied with less. But their intellects fell short of it, they were not guided to it by the light of prophethood, they did not perceive it so as to strive to seek it, and they saw that what they have is better than ignorance, and they saw the contradiction and corruption in what others have.

From these matters there results the preference for what they have over everything else. This is the affliction of the sects, and the one who is spared is the one whom God spares.

[Section: The secret of servitude, its goal and its wisdom]

Know that the secret of servitude, its goal and its wisdom, is only comprehended by one who knows the attributes of the Lord, mighty and majestic, without denying them, and who knows the meaning of divinity (ilahiyya) and its reality, and the meaning of His being God. Indeed He is the True God, and every god other than Him is false, indeed the most false of falsehoods. The reality of divinity is fitting only for Him, and worship is the necessary consequence of His divinity, its effect and its requirement. Its connection to it is like the connection of the object of attributes to the attributes, like the connection of the known to knowledge, the capable to power, sounds to hearing, benevolence to mercy, and giving to generosity.

So whoever denies the reality of divinity and does not know it, how can he correctly know the wisdom of acts of worship, their goals, their purposes, and what they were legislated for? How can he correctly know that they are the ultimate aim for which creation was made, for which they were created, for which the messengers were sent and the books revealed, and for which Paradise and Hell were created? And that supposing the creation to be idle with respect to them is an attribution to God of what is not fitting for Him, and God is exalted above what the one who created the heavens and the earth in truth, and did not create them in vain, and did not create man in vain or leave him neglected, is exalted above. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115], meaning: for nothing and without wisdom, and not for My worship and My recompensing you. He, exalted is He, stated this explicitly in His saying: ﴿I did not create jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56]. So worship is the goal for which He created the jinn, humankind, and all creation.

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected?﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 36], meaning: unattended. Al-Shafi'i said: he is not commanded and not forbidden. Others said: he is not rewarded and not punished. The correct view is both, for reward and punishment follow upon command and prohibition, and command and prohibition are the request for worship and its willing. The reality of worship is the fulfillment of both.

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿They reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth: Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You, so save us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ [Al 'Imran: 191]. And He said: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 85]. And He said: ﴿God created the heavens and the earth with truth, and that every soul may be recompensed for what it earned﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 22].

So He informed us that He created the heavens and the earth with truth, which includes His command and His prohibition, His reward and His punishment.

If the heavens and the earth and what is between them were created for this, and it is the ultimate goal of creation, how can it be said that there is no cause for it and no intended wisdom which is its goal? Or that it was only so that the servants might be hired, lest the reward be spoiled for them by favour? Or only so that souls might be prepared for intellectual knowledge and trained by opposing habits?

Let the discerning person reflect on the distinction between these statements and what the clear revelation indicates. He will find that the proponents of these statements did not measure God with His due measure, nor did they know Him with His due knowledge.

God, exalted is He, created creation only for His worship, which comprises the perfection of His love together with submission to Him and obedience to His command.

So the foundation of worship is the love of God; indeed, it is the singling out of Him with love, so that all love is for God alone. One does not love anything alongside Him, but loves for His sake and in Him, as one loves His prophets, messengers, angels and friends. Our love for them is part of the perfection of His love, and not love alongside Him, unlike the love of one who takes rivals besides God and loves them as he loves Him.

And when love for Him is the true reality of worship and its essence, it is only realized by following His command and avoiding His prohibition. When one follows the command and avoids the prohibition, the reality of worship and love becomes evident. For this reason, Exalted is He, made following His Messenger a sign of it and a witness for whoever claims it. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 31]. So He made following His Messenger conditional upon their love for Allah, and a condition for Allah's love for them. The existence of the conditioned thing is impossible without the existence of its condition, and its realization is by the realization of its condition. Thus it is known that love is absent when following is absent. Therefore the absence of their love for Allah necessarily follows from the absence of following His Messenger, and the absence of following is necessarily linked to the absence of Allah's love for them. Hence it is impossible for their love for Allah to be established, or Allah's love for them to be established, without following His Messenger.

It also indicates that following the Messenger ﷺ is the love of Allah and His Messenger, and obedience to his command. That is not sufficient for worship until Allah and His Messenger are more beloved to the servant than anything else. So there must not be anything in his heart more beloved to him than Allah and His Messenger. Whenever there is something in his heart more beloved to him than these two, that is the shirk which Allah will never forgive its possessor, and which Allah will not guide. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kinsfolk, the wealth you have acquired, the commerce whose slackness you fear, and the dwellings you are pleased with are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah brings His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [al-Tawbah: 24].

Whoever gives precedence to the obedience of any of these over the obedience of Allah and His Messenger, or the words of any of them over the words of Allah and His Messenger, or the pleasure of any of them over the pleasure of Allah and His Messenger, or fear of any of them, hope in them, and reliance upon them over fear of Allah, hope in Him, and reliance upon Him, or dealing with any of them over dealing with Allah, then he is among those for whom Allah and His Messenger are not more beloved than anything else. Even if he says it with his tongue, it is a lie from him and a report contrary to what he actually is. Likewise, whoever gives precedence to the judgment of anyone over the judgment of Allah and His Messenger, that person whom he prefers is more beloved to him than Allah and His Messenger. However, the matter may be confused for one who prefers the words, judgment, obedience, or pleasure of someone, thinking that such a person never commands, judges, or says anything except what the Messenger said. So he obeys him, refers disputes to him, and accepts his sayings on that basis. Such a person is excused if he is unable to do otherwise. But if he is able to reach the Messenger, and he knows that someone other than the one he follows has more right to be followed, absolutely or in some matters, and he does not turn to the Messenger nor to the one who has more right, then this is the one to be feared for, and he falls under the threat. If he then considers it lawful to punish whoever opposes him, and humiliates him, and does not agree with him in following his shaykh, then he is among the oppressive transgressors. Allah has set a measure for everything.

[Section: The structure of ﴿You alone we worship﴾ upon four foundations]

He built ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] upon four foundations: realizing what Allah and His Messenger love and are pleased with, in words of the tongue and the heart, and in deeds of the heart and the limbs.

Worship ('ubudiyyah) is a comprehensive term for these four levels. Those who truly fulfill ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] are its true people.

The speech of the heart is belief in what Allah, Glorified is He, has told about Himself, His names, attributes, actions, angels, and meeting with Him, through the tongues of His messengers.

The speech of the tongue is reporting that, calling to it, defending it, clarifying the falsehood of innovations that oppose it, engaging in its remembrance, and conveying His commands.

The deeds of the heart are such as love for Him, reliance upon Him, turning to Him in repentance, fear of Him, hope in Him, sincerity of religion for Him, patience with His commands, His prohibitions, and His decrees, contentment with Him and with what comes from Him, loyalty for His sake, enmity for His sake, humility and submission before Him, lowliness toward Him, tranquility in Him, and other deeds of the heart. Their obligatory aspect is more obligatory than the deeds of the limbs, and their recommended aspect is more beloved to Allah than the recommended aspect of the deeds of the limbs. The deeds of the limbs without them are either of no benefit or of little benefit.

The deeds of the limbs are such as prayer, striving, walking to Friday and congregational prayers, helping the weak, doing good to creation, and similar things.

So ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] is a commitment to the rulings of these four, and an affirmation of them. ﴿And You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5] is a request for help in them and for success in them. And ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fatihah: 6] includes the definition of the two matters in detail, and the inspiration to establish them, and to follow the path of those who travel to Allah through them.

[Section: The call of all the Messengers to ﴿You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help﴾]

All the Messengers called only to ﴿You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5]. They all called to the oneness of Allah and sincerity of His worship, from the first of them to the last. Noah, peace be upon him, said to his people: ﴿Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 59]. Likewise Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb, and Ibrahim, peace be upon them, said the same. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying]: Worship Allah and avoid the false deities﴾ [al-Nahl: 36]. He said: ﴿We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]. And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteousness; indeed I am Knowing of what you do. And indeed, this your nation is one nation, and I am your Lord, so fear Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 51-52].

[Section: Allah made worship the attribute of His most perfect creation]

Allah, Exalted is He, made worship the attribute of His most perfect creation and those closest to Him. He said: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the favored angels. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant - He will gather them all to Himself﴾ [al-Nisa': 172]. He said: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord do not disdain His worship; they glorify Him and to Him they prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf: 206]. This indicates that the complete pause in His saying in Surat al-Anbiya' ﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Anbiya': 19] is here, and then one begins with ﴿And those who are with Him do not disdain His worship, nor do they tire; they glorify the night and the day, never slackening﴾ [al-Anbiya': 19-20]. These are two complete, independent sentences. That is, to Him belong those in the heavens and on the earth as servants and possession. Then He began another sentence: ﴿And those who are with Him do not disdain His worship﴾, meaning that the angels who are with Him do not disdain His worship, that is, they do not refuse it, nor become proud, nor grow weary, becoming exhausted and stopping. It is said: ḥasira and istaḥsara, when one becomes tired and exhausted. Rather their worship and glorification are like breathing for the children of Adam. The first is a description of the servants of His lordship, and the second is a description of the servants of His divinity.

He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan: 63] through the end of the surah. He said: ﴿A spring from which the servants of Allah drink; they make it gush forth in abundance﴾ [al-Insan: 6]. He said: ﴿And remember Our servant Dawud﴾ [Sad: 17]. He said: ﴿And remember Our servant Ayyub﴾ [Sad: 41]. He said: ﴿And remember Our servants Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Ya'qub﴾ [Sad: 45]. He said about Sulayman: ﴿An excellent servant; indeed he was one who turned back in repentance﴾ [Sad: 30]. He said about the Messiah: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 59]. So He made his ultimate status worship, not divinity, as his enemies the Christians say. He described His most noble creation and the highest in rank with Him by worship, in the most honorable of their stations. He said: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾ [al-Baqarah: 23]. He, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾ [al-Furqan: 1]. He said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who sent down upon His servant the Book﴾ [al-Kahf: 1]. So He mentioned him with worship in the station of the descent of the Book upon him, and in the station of the challenge to produce something like it. He said: ﴿And when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they almost became crowded around him﴾ [al-Jinn: 19]. So He mentioned him with worship in the station of calling to Him. He said: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra': 1]. So He mentioned him with worship in the station of the Night Journey. In the Sahih, it is reported from him ﷺ that he said: "Do not exceed the bounds in praising me as the Christians exceeded in praising the son of Maryam (Mary), the Messiah; I am only a servant, so say: the servant of Allah and His Messenger." And in a hadith: "I am a servant; I eat as a servant eats, and I sit as a servant sits." In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is reported from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr who said: "I read in the Torah the description of Muhammad ﷺ: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, My servant and My Messenger. I named him al-Mutawakkil (the one who relies upon Allah). He is not harsh nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, nor does he repay evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives."

Allah, Glorified is He, made the unrestricted glad tidings for His servants. He said: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾ [al-Zumar: 17]. He made unrestricted security for them. He said: ﴿O My servants, no fear will be upon you today, nor will you grieve - those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 68-69]. He removed Satan from his authority over them specifically, and made his authority over whoever takes him as a protector and associates others with Allah. He said: ﴿Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them, except those who follow you of the misguided﴾ [al-Hijr: 42]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾ [al-Nahl: 99-100].

The Prophet ﷺ made excellence in the worship of servanthood the highest level of religion, which is ihsan (excellence). He said in the hadith of Jibril, when he asked him about ihsan: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you."

[Section: On the obligation of ﴿You alone we worship﴾ for every servant until death]

Allah, Exalted is He, said to His Messenger: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾ [al-Hijr: 99]. The people of the Fire said: ﴿And we used to deny the Day of Recompense until there came to us the certainty﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 46]. Al-yaqin (the certainty) here is death, by the consensus of the people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis). In the Sahih, in the story of the death of 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, may Allah be pleased with him, the Prophet ﷺ said: "As for 'Uthman, the certainty from his Lord has come to him", that is, death and what is in it. So the servant is never free of worship as long as he is in the abode of obligation. Rather, in the barzakh (intermediate state) there is another worship for him when the two angels ask him: Who did you worship? What do you say about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? They seek an answer from him. There is another worship for him on the Day of Resurrection, the day when Allah calls all creation to prostration. The believers will prostrate, while the disbelievers and hypocrites remain unable to prostrate. When they enter the abode of reward and punishment, the obligation ends there, and the worship of the people of reward becomes glorification joined with their breaths, without finding any weariness or fatigue in it.

Whoever claims that he reaches a station where worship falls away from him is a heretic (zindiq), a disbeliever in Allah and His Messenger. He has only reached the station of disbelief in Allah and departure from His religion. Rather, the more firmly a servant is established in the stations of worship, the greater his worship becomes, and the obligation upon him from it is greater and more than the obligation upon one below him. For this reason, the obligation upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and indeed upon all the Messengers, is greater than the obligation upon their nations. The obligation upon the Ulu al-'Azm (the Messengers of firm resolve) is greater than upon those below them, and the obligation upon the people of knowledge is greater than upon those below them. And each person is according to his rank.

[Section: On the division of worship into general and specific]

**The general servitude** is the servitude of all the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth to God, the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever alike. This is the servitude of compulsion and dominion (*ʿubūdiyyat al-qahr wa-l-mulk*). God the Exalted said: ﴿They say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced something monstrous. The heavens nearly rupture from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is none in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 19:88–93]. This includes both the believer and the disbeliever among them.

And God the Exalted said: ﴿And the day He will gather them and what they worship other than God, and He will say, "Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?"﴾ [al-Furqan 25:17]. He called them His servants despite their misguidance, but this is a designation restricted by the pointing (of the demonstrative "these"). As for the unrestricted designation, it does not come except for the people of the second category, as will be explained, God willing.

And God the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "O God, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ."﴾ [al-Zumar 39:46]. He said: ﴿And God does not want injustice for the servants﴾ [Ghafir 40:31], and He said: ﴿Indeed, God has judged between the servants﴾ [Ghafir 40:48]. This encompasses both the specific and the general servitude.

As for the second category, it is the servitude of obedience, love, and following the commands. God the Exalted said: ﴿O My servants, no fear will there be upon you today, nor will you grieve﴾ [al-Zukhruf 43:68]. He said: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants who listen to speech and follow the best of it﴾ [al-Zumar 39:17]. He said: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"﴾ [al-Furqan 25:63]. And God the Exalted said, concerning Iblis: ﴿And I will surely mislead them all, except Your servants among them, the sincere ones﴾ [al-Hijr 15:39]. Then God the Exalted said concerning them: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾ [al-Hijr 15:42].

So all of creation are servants of His lordship (*ʿabīd rubūbiyyatihi*), and the people of His obedience and His guardianship (*walāyatihi*) are servants of His divinity (*ʿabīd ilāhiyyatihi*).

The addition of "servants" (*ʿibād*) to Him in an unqualified manner does not occur in the Qur'an except for these people.

As for describing the servants of His lordship with servitude, it does not come except in one of five ways. First, indefinitely, as in His saying: ﴿There is none in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 19:93]. Second, definite with the article "al-," as in His saying: ﴿And God does not want injustice for the servants﴾ [Ghafir 40:31] and ﴿Indeed, God has judged between the servants﴾ [Ghafir 40:48].

Third, restricted by a demonstrative or the like, as in His saying: ﴿Did you lead these, My servants, astray?﴾ [al-Furqan 25:17].

Fourth, that they be mentioned within the generality of His servants, so that they are grouped together with the people of His obedience in the mention, as in His saying: ﴿You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ﴾ [al-Zumar 39:46].

Fifth, that they be mentioned described by their action, as in His saying: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God"﴾ [al-Zumar 39:53].

It may be said that He called them "His servants" only because they did not despair of His mercy, turned back to Him in repentance, and followed the best of what was sent down to them from their Lord. Thus they become among the servants of divinity and obedience.

The servitude was divided into the specific and the general because the original meaning of the word is humility and submission. It is said, "a path that is *muʿabbad*" when it has been made smooth by the treading of feet, and "love has enslaved him" (*ʿabbadahu al-ḥubb*) when it has subdued him. But His friends submit to Him and are humbled by choice and willingly, in compliance with His command and prohibition, whereas His enemies submit to Him by compulsion and against their will.

The division of servitude into the specific and the general has a parallel in the division of devotion (*qunūt*) into specific and general, and likewise prostration (*sujūd*). God the Exalted said of the specific devotion: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord?﴾ [al-Zumar 39:9]. He said concerning Maryam: ﴿And she was among the devoutly obedient﴾ [al-Tahrim 66:12]. This is frequent in the Qur'an.

And He said of the general devotion: ﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [al-Rum 30:26], meaning, submissive and humbled.

And He said of the specific prostration: ﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not disdain His worship; they exalt Him, and to Him they prostrate﴾ [al-Aʿraf 7:206]. And He said: ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down prostrating and weeping﴾ [Maryam 19:58]. This is frequent in the Qur'an.

And He said of the general prostration: ﴿And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows at morning and evening﴾ [al-Raʿd 13:15].

For this reason, this unwilling prostration is other than the prostration mentioned in His saying: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures, and many of mankind?﴾ [al-Hajj 22:18]. Here He singled out "many of mankind" for prostration, while in Surat al-Nahl He encompassed them all in prostration: ﴿And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels﴾ [al-Nahl 16:49]. This is the prostration of humility, compulsion, and submission. Thus every being is submissive to His lordship, humbled before His might, and subdued under His dominion, exalted is He.

[Section: On the levels of "You alone we worship" (*iyyāka naʿbud*), in knowledge and action]

Servitude has levels according to knowledge and action. As for its levels in knowledge, there are two:

The first is knowledge of God, and the second is knowledge of His religion.

As for knowledge of Him, glorified is He, there are five levels: knowledge of His essence, His attributes, His acts, His names, and His transcendence above whatever is not befitting to Him.

Knowledge of His religion has two levels. The first is His religion of command and law (*al-dīn al-amrī al-sharʿī*), which is the straight path that leads to Him.

The second is His religion of recompense (*al-dīn al-jazāʾī*), which includes His reward and His punishment. Within this knowledge is included knowledge of His angels, His books, and His messengers.

As for its levels in action, there are two: a level for the companions of the right (*aṣḥāb al-yamīn*), and a level for the foremost, the near ones (*al-sābiqīn al-muqarrabīn*).

As for the level of the companions of the right, it is the performance of obligations and the abandonment of prohibitions, together with the commission of permissible things and some disliked things, and the abandonment of some recommended things.

As for the level of the near ones, it is the performance of obligations and recommended acts, and the abandonment of prohibitions and disliked things, while being detached from what does not benefit them in their return (to God), and scrupulous about what they fear may harm them.

For their elite, permissible things have turned into acts of obedience and means of drawing near through intention. So for them there is no permissible act whose two sides are equal; rather, all their deeds are weighted toward merit. Whoever is below them abandons permissible things, occupied away from them by acts of worship, whereas these perform them as acts of obedience and means of nearness. The people of these two levels have ranks that none can count except God.

[Section: The levels of servitude, which are fifteen levels]

[Servitude of the heart]

The axis of servitude revolves around fifteen principles. Whoever perfects them perfects the levels of servitude.

Their explanation is that servitude is divided among the heart, the tongue, and the limbs, and each of these has a servitude specific to it.

The rulings that apply to servitude are five: obligatory, recommended, forbidden, disliked, and permissible, and these apply to each of the heart, the tongue, and the limbs.

The obligatory acts of the heart are of two kinds: those whose obligation is agreed upon, and those about which there is disagreement.

Those whose obligation is agreed upon are such things as sincerity (*ikhlāṣ*), trust in God (*tawakkul*), love (*maḥabba*), piety (*birr*), turning back in repentance (*ināba*), fear (*khawf*), hope (*rajāʾ*), firm affirmation (*taṣdīq al-jāzim*), and intention in worship (*niyya fī al-ʿibāda*). This last is an addition beyond sincerity, for sincerity is singling out the one worshipped from others.

The intention of worship has two levels: the first is distinguishing worship from habit; the second is distinguishing the degrees of acts of worship from one another.

These three categories are obligatory.

Likewise truthfulness (*ṣidq*). The difference between it and sincerity is that the servant has an object sought (*maṭlūb*) and a seeking (*ṭalab*). Sincerity is the unifying of the object sought, while truthfulness is the unifying of the seeking. Sincerity is that the object sought should not be divided; truthfulness is that the seeking should not be divided. Truthfulness is the exerting of effort, and sincerity is the singling out of the object sought.

The community (*umma*) has agreed on the obligation of these acts upon the heart in general terms.

Likewise sincere counsel (*nuṣḥ*) in servitude, on which the religion depends. It is exerting effort in performing servitude in the manner loved by the Lord and pleasing to Him. The root of this is obligatory, and its perfection is the level of the near ones.

Likewise each of these obligatory acts of the heart has two sides: an obligatory side that is required, which is the level of the companions of the right, and a perfected recommended side, which is the level of the near ones.

Likewise patience (*ṣabr*) is obligatory by the consensus of the community. Imam Ahmad said: God mentioned patience in ninety places in the Qur'an, or some ninety. It too has two sides: an obligatory required side and a recommended perfected side.

As for what is disputed, such as contentment (*riḍā*), there are two opinions among the jurists and the Sufis, and the two opinions exist among the followers of Ahmad. Whoever considers it obligatory says: displeasure (*suخṭ*) is forbidden, and there is no escape from it except through contentment, and whatever escape from the forbidden depends upon, is obligatory.

They argued with the report: "Whoever does not endure My trial, and is not content with My decree, let him take a lord other than Me."

Whoever says it is recommended says: the command concerning it has not come in the Qur'an or the Sunnah, unlike patience, for God commanded it in many places in His Book. Likewise trust (*tawakkul*): He said: ﴿If you have believed in God, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims﴾ [Yunus 10:84]. He commanded turning back (*ināba*): He said: ﴿And turn back to your Lord﴾ [al-Zumar 39:54]. He commanded sincerity, as in His saying: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyina 98:5]. Likewise fear: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers﴾ [Al ʿImran 3:175]; His saying: ﴿So do not fear them but fear Me﴾ [al-Baqara 2:150]; and His saying: ﴿And of Me, fear[only] Me﴾ [al-Baqara 2:40]. Likewise truthfulness: He said: ﴿O you who have believed, fear God and be with the truthful﴾ [al-Tawba 9:119]. Likewise love, which is the most obligatory of the obligations, since it is the heart of the worship commanded, its marrow and its spirit.

As for contentment, it came in the Qur'an as praise of its people and commendation of them, not as a command to it.

They said: As for the report mentioned, it is an Israelite narrative (*isrāʾīlī*) and is not to be used as evidence.

They said: And in the well-known hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: "If you are able to do contentment along with certainty, then do it; but if you are not able, then in patience upon what the soul dislikes there is much good," and it is in some of the Sunan.

They said: As for your saying, "There is no escape from displeasure except by it," this does not follow, for the levels of people regarding what is decreed are three: contentment, which is the highest; displeasure, which is the lowest; and patience upon it without contentment with it, which is the middle. The first is for the near, foremost ones; the third is for the moderate (*muqtaṣidūn*); and the second is for the wrongdoers. Many people are patient with what is decreed and do not feel displeasure, yet they are not content with it. So contentment is a different matter.

It has been unclear to some people how contentment can coexist with pain, and they thought the two are contradictory, but it is not as they imagined. The sick person drinking a bitter medicine feels pain from it and is content with it; the fasting person in the heat of Ramadan feels pain from his fast and is content with it; the stingy person feels pain at paying the zakat on his wealth and is content with it. So just as pain does not contradict patience, it does not contradict contentment with it.

This disagreement among them is only about contentment with His cosmic decree (*qaḍāʾ al-kawnī*). As for contentment with Him as Lord and God, and contentment with His religious command (*amr dīnī*), its obligation is agreed upon. Indeed, a servant does not become a Muslim except through this contentment: that he be content with God as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as messenger.

From this also is their disagreement about humility (*khushūʿ*) in prayer, and there are two opinions among the jurists about it, and both exist in the school of Ahmad and others.

Upon these two opinions is their disagreement about the obligation of repeating the prayer for one whose whisperings (*waswās*) predominate in his prayer. Ibn Hamid among the followers of Ahmad required it, as did Abu Hamid al-Ghazali in his *Ihya'*, but most jurists did not require it.

And they argued that the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded the one who forgot in his prayer to perform the prostrations of forgetfulness (sujud al-sahw) and did not command him to repeat the prayer. [They also cited] his saying (ﷺ): "Indeed, Satan comes to one of you during his prayer and says: 'Remember such-and-such, remember such-and-such,' regarding what he had not been remembering, until the person does not know how many [units] he has prayed." However, there is no dispute that this prayer is rewarded only to the extent of the presence of the heart and its humility, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a servant may finish the prayer and only a half of it is recorded for him, or a third, or a quarter, until it reaches a tenth." Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "You gain from your prayer only what you understood of it." Thus it is called valid (sahih) with regard to the fact that we do not command him to repeat it, but it is not proper to attach the term validity to it in the sense that it is said to be a "valid prayer" while its performer receives no reward for it.

The point is that these acts, whether obligatory or recommended, are the servitude of the heart. Whoever neglects them has neglected the servitude owed to the King, even if he performs the servitude of his subjects, which are the limbs.

The aim is that the king of the limbs, which is the heart, should stand in its servitude to Allah, the Exalted, and so should its subjects.

As for the prohibited deeds that concern the heart: they are arrogance (kibr), showing off (riya'), self-admiration ('ujb), envy (hasad), heedlessness (ghaflah), and hypocrisy (nifaq). They are of two types: disbelief (kufr) and disobedience (ma'siyah).

Disbelief includes doubt (shakk), hypocrisy (nifaq), polytheism (shirk), and what follows from them.

Disobedience is of two types: major sins (kaba'ir) and minor sins (sagha'ir).

Major sins include showing off, self-admiration, arrogance, boasting (fakhr), vanity (khuyala'), despair of Allah's mercy (qunut min rahmat Allah), despair of Allah's comfort (ya's min rawh Allah), feeling secure from Allah's plan (amn min makr Allah), rejoicing and delight in harming the Muslims, gloating over their misfortune, loving that indecency spread among them, envying them for what Allah has given them of His bounty, wishing that this bounty be removed from them, and the consequences of these matters. These are more severely forbidden than fornication, drinking wine, and other manifest major sins. There is no soundness for the heart or the body except by avoiding them and repenting from them; otherwise the heart is corrupt, and when the heart is corrupt the body is corrupt.

These afflictions arise only from ignorance of the servitude of the heart and from abandoning its performance.

The duty of "You alone we worship" (﴿Iyyaka na'budu﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5]) falls upon the heart before the limbs. So when it is ignorant of this and abandons its performance, it will inevitably be filled with the opposites of it. In proportion to its performance of it, it is freed from their opposites.

These matters and their like may be minor sins in one's case, or may be major sins, according to their strength, severity, subtlety, or lightness.

Among the minor sins also: the desire for forbidden things and wishing for them. The degrees of desire vary in greatness and smallness according to the degrees of what is desired. So desire for disbelief and polytheism is disbelief; desire for innovation (bid'ah) is wickedness; desire for major sins is disobedience. If one abandons it for Allah's sake while being able to do it, he is rewarded. If he abandons it out of inability after exerting his capacity to attain it, he deserves the punishment of the doer, because he is placed in his rank regarding the rulings of reward and punishment, even though he is not placed in his rank regarding the rulings of the Sharia. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When two Muslims confront each other with their swords, the killer and the killed are in the Fire." They said: "This is the killer, O Messenger of Allah, but what about the killed?" He said: "He was eager to kill his companion." So he placed him in the rank of the killer because of his eagerness to kill his companion, in sin but not in ruling. There are many similar examples regarding reward and punishment.

By this, the recommended (mustahabb) and permitted (mubah) matters of the heart are also known.

[Section: The Worship of the Tongue]

As for the five servitudes of the tongue: its obligatory part is pronouncing the two testimonies (al-shahadatayn), reciting what it is required to recite of the Qur'an, that upon which the validity of the prayer depends, and uttering the obligatory remembrances in the prayer which Allah and His Messenger commanded, such as glorifying (tasbih) in bowing and prostration, saying "Our Lord, and to You belongs all praise" after rising from bowing, reciting the tashahhud, and the takbir.

Among its obligations is returning the greeting of peace, and there are two opinions regarding initiating it.

Among its obligations is commanding right and forbidding wrong, teaching the ignorant, guiding the one who has gone astray, giving the testimony that is required, and speaking the truth.

As for its recommended part: reciting the Qur'an, constant remembrance of Allah, discussing beneficial knowledge, and what follows from these.

As for its forbidden part: it is uttering everything that Allah and His Messenger detest, such as speaking innovations that oppose what Allah sent His Messenger with, calling to them, beautifying and strengthening them; as well as slander, reviling and harming a Muslim by any speech, lying, false testimony, and speaking about Allah without knowledge, which is the most severely forbidden of these.

Its disliked (makruh) part is speaking what it is better to leave unsaid, without punishment for it.

The early scholars (salaf) differed as to whether there is permissible speech in regard to the tongue that is equally balanced between its two sides (i.e., neither good nor bad), in two opinions, mentioned by Ibn al-Mundhir and others. One of them: every word one speaks is either for him or against him, and nothing is neither for him nor against him.

They argued with the well-known hadith: "Every speech of the son of Adam is against him, not for him, except enjoining good, forbidding evil, and remembering Allah and what is related to it."

They also argued that all his speech is recorded for him, and only good and evil are recorded.

Another group said: rather, this speech is permissible, neither for him nor against him, just as with the movements of the limbs.

They said: because much speech is not connected with any command or prohibition, and this is the nature of what is permissible.

The truth is that the movement of the tongue with speech is not equally balanced between its two sides. Rather it is either preponderantly good or preponderantly bad, because the tongue has a status that the other limbs do not have. When the son of Adam rises in the morning, all the limbs humble themselves before the tongue, saying: "Fear Allah regarding us, for we are only with you. If you are upright, we are upright, and if you are crooked, we are crooked." Most of what throws people face-down into the Fire are the harvests of their tongues. Everything the tongue utters is either something that pleases Allah and His Messenger or not. If it is so, it is preponderantly good; if it is not, it is preponderantly bad. This is unlike the movements of the other limbs, for their possessor benefits from moving them in permissible matters that are equally balanced, due to the comfort and benefit he gains from them. So he is permitted to use them for what benefits him, and there is no harm upon him in the Hereafter for it. But moving the tongue with what gives no benefit yields only harm. So reflect on this.

If it is said: the tongue may move with what has a permissible worldly benefit that is equally balanced, so the ruling on its movement would be the ruling on that action.

It is answered: its movement with it is preponderantly good when there is need for it, and when there is no need for it, it is preponderantly bad, bringing him no benefit, so it is against him and not for him.

If it is said: when the action is equally balanced, the movement of the tongue which is the means to it is likewise equally balanced, since means follow the intended goal in ruling.

It is answered: this does not necessarily follow. Something may be permissible, or even obligatory, while its means is disliked, like fulfilling a vowed act of obedience, which is obligatory, while its means, the vow itself, is disliked and prohibited. Likewise, a disliked oath is preponderantly bad, even though fulfilling it or expiating it is obligatory. Likewise, asking people when in need is disliked, yet he may benefit from what the request brought him. This is very common. A means may include a corruption for which it is disliked or forbidden, while what it was made a means to is neither forbidden nor disliked.

[Section: The Worship of the Limbs]

As for the five servitudes of the limbs: they also come to twenty-five levels, since the senses are five, and each sense has five servitudes.

For hearing, there is the obligation to listen quietly and attentively to what Allah and His Messenger obligated upon it, such as listening to Islam and faith and their obligations. Likewise listening to the recitation in prayer when the imam recites aloud, and listening to the sermon for Friday prayer according to the more correct of the two opinions of the scholars.

It is forbidden for him to listen to disbelief and innovations, except where there is a preponderant benefit in listening, such as refuting it, bearing witness against its speaker, or increasing the strength of faith and the Sunnah by knowing their opposites of disbelief and innovation and the like. Likewise listening to the secrets of one who flees from you with his secret and does not want you to know it, unless it includes a right of Allah that must be fulfilled, or harm to a Muslim whose advice and warning against it is required.

Likewise, listening to the voices of non-mahram women whose voices are feared to cause temptation, when no need calls for it, such as testimony, transaction, asking for a legal opinion, litigation, treatment, or the like.

Likewise, listening to musical instruments and instruments of merriment and play, such as the lute (ud), the nabur, the flute (yara'), and the like. He is not obligated to plug his ears if he hears the sound while not intending to listen to it, unless he fears being drawn to it and attentive to it; then, to avoid hearing it, blocking the means (sadd al-dharai') becomes obligatory.

Similar to this: the one in ihram may not deliberately smell perfume, and if the wind carries its fragrance and casts it into his nostrils, he is not obligated to block his nose.

Similar to this: a glance by chance (nazrat al-fuja'ah) is not forbidden to the one who glances, but the second glance is forbidden to him if he does it deliberately.

As for recommended hearing: such as listening to recommended knowledge, the recitation of the Qur'an, the remembrance of Allah, and listening to everything Allah loves, though it is not obligatory.

The disliked is the opposite of this, namely listening to everything that is disliked without punishment for it.

The permissible is clear.

As for obligatory seeing: looking into the Mushaf and books of knowledge when learning the obligatory part from them is required, and looking when it is necessary to distinguish the lawful from the unlawful in the things he eats, spends, or enjoys, and in the trusts he delivers to their owners so that he distinguishes between them, and the like.

Forbidden seeing: looking at non-mahram women with desire in any case, and looking at them without desire unless there is a need, such as the glance of a suitor, a buyer or dealer, a witness, a judge, a physician, and a mahram.

Recommended seeing: looking into books of knowledge and religion by which a man increases in faith and knowledge; looking into the Mushaf; looking at the faces of righteous scholars and parents; and looking at the visible signs of Allah in order to be guided by them to His oneness, knowledge of Him, and His wisdom.

Disliked is the excessive looking that has no benefit in it, for the eye has excesses just as the tongue has excesses. How often the excesses of these have led to excesses from which it is hard to be freed and whose remedy is difficult. One of the early scholars said: "They used to dislike the excess of looking just as they disliked the excess of speech."

Permissible seeing is that which has no harm in it in the present or the future and no benefit.

Among forbidden looking is looking at the 'awrahs (intimate parts), which are of two kinds: an 'awrah behind clothing and an 'awrah behind doors.

If someone looks into an 'awrah behind a door and the owner of the 'awrah throws something at him and blinds his eye, there is no liability on him, and it is lost without compensation, according to the explicit statement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the hadith agreed upon as authentic. Even if some jurists weakened it, because the text did not reach them, or they interpreted it otherwise.

This applies when the looker has no cause that permits looking, such as an 'awrah there that he is looking at, or a suspicion for which he is commanded or permitted to inspect.

As for tasting: the obligatory is taking food and drink when one is compelled to it and fears death. If he leaves it until he dies, he dies as a sinner who killed himself. Imam Ahmad and Tawus said: "Whoever is forced to eat carrion and does not eat until he dies, enters the Fire."

From this is taking medicine when one is certain of being saved from destruction by it, according to the more correct of the two opinions. If he only expects a cure from it, is it recommended, permissible, or is it better to leave it? There is a well-known dispute about this between the early and later scholars.

Forbidden tasting: such as tasting wine, deadly poisons, and tasting what is prohibited for the obligatory fast.

As for the disliked (makruh) kind: it includes tasting doubtful things (al-mushtabihat), eating beyond need, and tasting the food of "surprise" (ta'ām al-fujā'a), which is food that someone eats after it has come upon them unexpectedly, when the host did not intend to invite you to it. It also includes eating the food of show-offs at weddings, invitations and the like. The Sunan report that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) "forbade the food of those who compete (in showing off)." It also includes tasting the food of someone who feeds you out of shyness toward you rather than with a willing heart.

The recommended (mustahabb) kind of tasting is eating what helps you obey God, the Mighty and Majestic, from what God has permitted. It also includes eating together with a guest so that he enjoys his meal and achieves his purpose, and eating from the food of the host of a banquet whose invitation is obligatory to accept or recommended to accept.

Some jurists have made eating from an obligatory wedding banquet (walima) obligatory, because of the command to do so from the Lawgiver.

The permissible (mubah) kind of tasting is that which involves neither sin nor merit.

As for the connection of the five rulings to the sense of smell: the obligatory smelling is every smelling that becomes the required means of distinguishing lawful from unlawful, such as smelling a substance to know whether it is pure or impure, and whether it is a deadly poison or harmless, or to distinguish what one is entitled to benefit from from what one is not. This includes the smelling of an appraiser (muqawwim) and an expert (rabb al-khibra) when judging a valuation, the smelling of slaves, and the like.

As for forbidden smelling: it is deliberately smelling perfume while in ihram, smelling perfume that is usurped (maghsub) or stolen, and deliberately smelling the perfume of unrelated women, for fear of being tempted by what lies behind it.

As for recommended smelling: it is smelling what helps you obey God, strengthens the senses, and opens the soul to knowledge and action. Among this is accepting a gift of perfume and sweet basil (rayhan) when it is given to you. In Sahih Muslim, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever is offered sweet basil should not refuse it, for it is pleasant in scent and light to carry."

The disliked kind is like smelling the perfume of oppressors and people of doubtful conduct, and the like.

The permissible kind is that in which there is no prohibition from God, no accountability, and no religious benefit, and which has no connection to the Law.

As for the connection of these five rulings to the sense of touch: obligatory touching is like touching one's wife when intercourse with her becomes obligatory, and touching a slave-woman whose chastity one is obliged to protect.

Forbidden touching is touching what is not lawful to touch of unrelated women.

Recommended touching is when it involves lowering one's gaze, restraining oneself from what is forbidden, and protecting the chastity of one's family.

Disliked touching is touching one's wife for pleasure while in ihram, and likewise while in i'tikaf, and while fasting if one cannot be sure of oneself.

From this is touching the body of a dead person by someone other than the one who washes it, because the body has come to be in the position of the awrah (private parts) of the living, out of honor for it. For this reason it is recommended to cover it from eyes, and to wash it in its shirt according to one of the two opinions. Also touching a man's thigh, if we say it is awrah.

The permissible kind is that in which there is no harm and no religious benefit.

These levels are also arranged according to the act of striking with the hand and walking with the foot, and their examples are not hidden.

Earning a livelihood that one is able to do, to support oneself, one's family and dependents, is obligatory. Regarding its obligation for the purpose of paying one's debts, there is disagreement; the sound view is that it is obligatory, so that one may be able to pay one's debt. It is not obligatory for the purpose of paying zakat. Regarding its obligation for performing the obligatory Hajj, there is consideration; the stronger view on the evidence is that it is obligatory, because it enters into the condition of capability (istita'a) and enables one through it to perform the rite; but the well-known view is that it is not obligatory.

From obligatory striking (of the hand): helping someone in dire need, throwing the pebbles at the jamarat, and performing wudu' and tayammum.

The forbidden kind: like killing a soul that God has forbidden to kill, plundering protected property, striking someone who may not be struck, and the like. Also the kinds of forbidden play established by the text, such as backgammon (nard), or what is even more strictly forbidden according to the people of Madina, such as chess (shatranj), or its equivalent according to the jurists of hadith like Ahmad and others, or less than that according to some of them. Also the like of writing innovations (bida') that oppose the Sunna, whether by composing or copying them, unless accompanied by refuting and disproving them; writing falsehood and injustice; an unjust ruling; slander, and amatory poetry about unrelated women; and writing anything that harms the Muslims in their religion or their worldly affairs, especially if you earn money by it: ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from God," to exchange it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:79). Likewise, a mufti writing a fatwa that contradicts the ruling of God and His Messenger is forbidden, unless he is a mujtahid who has erred, in which case the sin is lifted from him.

As for the disliked kind: it is like idle play and frivolity that is not forbidden, and writing what has no benefit in writing it, and no advantage in this world or the Hereafter.

The recommended kind is writing everything that has benefit for the religion or benefit for a Muslim. Also doing good with one's hand, such as helping a craftsman, making something for someone who is clumsy, pouring from one's bucket into the bucket of someone seeking water, carrying a load for him on one's animal, holding the animal until he is loaded onto it, or assisting him with one's hand in whatever he needs, and the like. From this is touching the corner (of the Ka'ba) with one's hand during tawaf, and kissing the hand after touching it, on which there are two opinions.

The permissible kind is that in which there is no harm and no reward.

As for obligatory walking: walking to the Friday prayer and to congregational prayers, according to the more correct of the two opinions, for twenty-some proofs mentioned elsewhere; walking around the House for obligatory tawaf; walking between al-Safa and al-Marwa, whether on foot or on one's mount; walking to the ruling of God and His Messenger when one is called to it; walking to maintain the ties of kinship; walking to be dutiful to one's parents; walking to the sessions of knowledge whose seeking and learning is obligatory; and walking to Hajj when the distance is near and there is no harm to him in it.

The forbidden kind: walking toward disobedience of God, and it is from the "foot" (rajl) of Satan. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And incite against them with your cavalry and your infantry﴾ (Al-Isra 17:64). Muqatil said: "Seek help against them from the riders and the foot-soldiers of your army." So every rider and walker in disobedience of God is from the army of Iblis.

Likewise, these five rulings are connected to riding as well.

Its obligatory form is riding in battle, in jihad, and in obligatory Hajj.

Its recommended form is riding for the recommended purposes of those things, for seeking knowledge, for maintaining the ties of kinship, and for being dutiful to parents. Regarding standing at 'Arafa, there is a dispute whether riding there is superior or standing on the ground. The verified view is that riding is superior if it includes a benefit, such as teaching the rites and having people follow the example, and if it helps one to supplicate, and there is no harm to the animal.

Its forbidden form: riding in disobedience of God, the Mighty and Majestic.

Its disliked form: riding for amusement and play; and everything whose abandonment is better than doing it.

Its permissible form: riding for purposes that do not involve losing a reward or acquiring a burden.

So these are fifty levels across ten things: the heart, the tongue, the hearing, the sight, the nose, the mouth, the hand, the foot, the private parts, and sitting upon the back of the animal.

[Section: The Ultimate Goal of the Wayfarers is the Perfection of the Station of Servanthood, Purely]

If your heart does not accept that repentance is the ultimate goal of the stations (maqamat) of the wayfarers (salikin), and you do not give ear to anything of what we have mentioned, and you insist that the ultimate goal is the vanishing of the final stage of union (ittisal) into the very essence of existence, annihilation (mahq), the vanishing of the sciences of witnessing (shawahid) into pure divine knowledge (al-'ilm al-ladunni), and that the unity of existence (jam' al-wujud) and unity of the essence (jam' al-'ayn) is the final stage of the wayfarers toward God, in a way that includes every wayfarer: know that this so-called unity, taken alone, does not give servanthood ('ubudiyya) or faith (iman), let alone being the ultimate goal of every prophet, saint and knower. For this unity is attained by both the sincere believer (siddiq) and the heretic (zindiq), and the atheists and the monists (ittihadiyya) have a great share in it. Around it they hover, and for them it is the final stage of realization. So where is the realization of servanthood, the bearing of its burdens, the carrying out of its obligations and recommended acts and their performance, the struggle against God's enemies, the call to God, commanding the good and forbidding the evil, and enduring harm for God's sake, within this unity?! Where is the knowledge of the Names and Attributes in detail within it? Where is the knowledge of what the Lord, the Exalted, loves and hates in detail? Where is the knowledge of the better of the two goods and the worse of the two evils within it? And where is the knowledge of the levels and stations of servanthood within it?!

The truth is that the ultimate goal of the wayfarers is the perfection of the station of servanthood in its pure form. This is something no path leads to for the children of nature (bani al-tabi'a). It was only singled out for the two Friends (al-Khalilan), upon them both be blessings and peace, from among all creation. As for Ibrahim the Friend of God, may the blessings of God and His peace be upon him, God, the Mighty and Majestic, bore witness that he fulfilled (his covenant). As for the master of the children of Adam, may the blessings of God and His peace be upon him, he perfected the station of servanthood, and so deserved precedence over all creatures. He was the possessor of the Wasila (intercession station) and the intercession, from which all the messengers will hold back, and he himself says: "I am its (the one for it)." For this reason God, glorified and exalted, mentioned him with servanthood at the highest of his stations and the noblest of his states, as in His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night﴾ (Al-Isra 17:1); and His saying: ﴿And when the servant of God stood up calling upon Him﴾ (Al-Jinn 72:19); and His saying: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:23); and His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:1). For this reason, when people beg Jesus for intercession, he says: "Go to Muhammad, a servant whose past and future sins God has forgiven." So he deserved that supreme rank by perfecting his servanthood to God, and by the perfection of God's forgiveness toward him.

So the matter returns to this: the ultimate goal and final stage of the stations is repentance and pure servanthood, not the unity of the essence, nor the unity of existence, nor the annihilation of union.

If you say: this unity only comes to those who have truly established repentance and servanthood.

It is said: this is not so. Rather, the unity that comes to those who establish that is the unity of the messengers and their successors. It is the unification of aspiration upon God, glorified be He, through love, turning back to Him, reliance, fear, hope, and watchfulness; and the unification of aspiration upon executing God's commands among creation through calling to Him and striving (jihad). So there are two unities: the unity of the heart upon the One God alone worshipped, and the unity of concern for Him upon the purity of His servanthood.

If you say: where is the witness of these two unities? I say: it is in the whole Qur'an. Take it from the Opening of the Book, in His saying: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ (Al-Fatiha 1:5). Reflect on what is in His saying "iyyaka" (You alone): the restriction of worship and seeking help to His holy essence; and what is in His saying "na'budu" (we worship), which is for the present and future tense, and for both outward and inward worship, encompassing all kinds of worship, in the present and future, in speech and deed, outwardly and inwardly; and seeking help in that from Him alone and not from anything else. For this reason the entire path is in these two words, and this is the meaning of their saying: "The path is in: 'You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help' — with what You desire, I desire." Thus the desire is gathered into one, and the will is gathered into His desired object which He loves and is pleased with. To this the messengers called, from the first of them to the last; toward it the doers strove, and the seekers turned; and all states and stations, from their beginning to their end, are contained within it and are among its fruits and requirements.

The servitude ('ubudiyya) combines the perfection of love with the perfection of humility, and the perfection of submission to the Beloved's pleasure and commands. It is therefore the goal beyond which there is no goal. If there is no way to fulfil its reality as it should be fulfilled, then repentance (tawba) is the lever and the means of return. You have come to know, through this and other things, that the need for repentance at the end of the journey is greater than the need for it at the beginning. Were it not for the breath of its spirit, despair would stand between the son of water and clay and reaching the Lord of the worlds. This would be so even if he fulfilled what he is obliged to fulfil toward his Master of rights. How much more so when there is heedlessness, shortcoming, neglect, and laxity, and when he prefers his own portions (huzuz) over the rights of his Lord at many times, from which he can hardly free himself. This is especially true for the wayfarer on the path of annihilation (fana') and gathering (jam'). His Lord demands servitude from him, while his soul demands gathering and annihilation. If he examined his soul closely and called it to a sound account, he would see clearly that it wants its own portion and seeks its own pleasure. Yes, everyone seeks that. But the matter lies in distinguishing between one whose portion has become the very pleasure and love of God, whether his soul loves that or dislikes it, and one whose portion is what he wants from his Lord. The first one's portion is the desire of his Lord for him in religious and legal terms, and this is his portion, his desire from his Lord. And success is from God.
