If it is said: "This matter is accepted for the people of spiritual taste (dhawq), and you speak in the language of knowledge, not the language of taste. The one who tastes is one who finds, and the one who finds cannot deny what he finds. So he does not refer to the man of knowledge, but calls him to taste what he has tasted, and says:

"I say to the blaming censurer who offers his blame,
Taste passion, and if you can, then blame."

It is said: One who refers to taste has not been fair, for this is a referral to one who is himself judged, not to the judge; to one who is himself witnessed, not to the witness; and to what is weighed, not to the scale.

Glory be to God! Does the mere taste of a thing indicate its ruling, that it is true or false? Did God and His Messenger make tastes and ecstatic findings (mawajid) into proofs and evidences, by which one distinguishes between what He loves and approves and what He hates and is displeased with? If that were so, every falsifier would argue for his falsehood by taste and finding, as you find among many people of falsehood and heresy. These are the Monists (al-ittihadiyya), who are the most disbelieving of creation, and they argue for their disbelief and heresy by taste and finding, until one of them says:

"O my companion, you forbid me and command me,
But finding is more truthful as a forbidder and commander.
If I obey you and disobey finding, I go astray,
Away from certainty toward the illusions of reports.
And the very thing you call me to, when I verify it,
Changes the forbidden into the permitted, O neighbour."

This speaker also says: "There has been established for us, through unveiling (kashf) and taste, what contradicts the plain intellect. Every believer in a matter he holds with certainty finds its taste pleasing. The atheist tastes the taste of monism and the loosening of religion; the Rafidi tastes the taste of rejection and enmity toward the best of creation; the Qadari tastes the taste of denying destiny and marvels at one who affirms it; the Jabari is the opposite; and the polytheist tastes the taste of polytheism, to the point that he rejoices when his deity and object of worship is mentioned besides God, and his heart recoils when God alone is mentioned."

This argument has been followed by the people of the newly invented, satanic audition (sama'), which is pure desire of the soul and its passion. They argue for the permissibility of this audition by what it contains of taste, finding, and pleasure. You will find the Christian who has, in his trinitarianism, a taste, a finding, and longing, such that if the most severe punishment were presented to him, he would choose it rather than abandon his trinity, because of the taste he has in it.

At this point it is said: Suppose the matter is as you say, and that the denying speaker did not speak in the language of taste. Would it be valid for the taster's taste to be a sound and beneficial proof for him between himself and God? Suppose this denier said: "Yes, I am veiled from reaching what I deny, not tasting it, and you are a taster who has arrived. So what is the sign of what you have tasted and arrived at? And what is the evidence for it? I do not deny your taste or your finding of it. But the matter lies in what is tasted, not in the tasting. When the lover in love tastes the flavour of his love and passion for his beloved, the most that this shows is the existence of his love and passion, not that this is beneficial or harmful to him, or that it makes him perfect or deficient." And success is from God.

[Chapter: The Correct Gathering is the Gathering of the Tawhid of Lordship and the Gathering of the Tawhid of Divinity]

So the one who holds this gathering witnesses the Lord, exalted, as the Sustainer (al-Qayyum) above His Throne, who alone governs the affairs of His servants. There is no creator, no provider, no giver, no withholder, no one who causes death or gives life, and no governor of the affairs of the kingdom, outwardly or inwardly, other than Him. What He wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be. No atom moves except by His permission, no occurrence takes place except by His will, and no leaf falls except by His knowledge. Nothing is hidden from Him, the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller or greater than that, except that His knowledge encompasses it, His power surrounds it, His will executes it, and His wisdom requires it. This is the gathering of the Tawhid of Lordship.

As for the gathering of the Tawhid of Divinity, it is that one gathers his heart, his aspiration, and his resolve upon God, and directs his will and movements toward fulfilling His right and establishing His servitude, glorified is He. Thus the aspects of his will are gathered upon His religious and legal desire.

These two gatherings are the reality of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾. The servant witnesses from His saying "You" (iyyaka) the Essence that gathers all the attributes of perfection, to which belong all the Most Beautiful Names. Then he witnesses from His saying "we worship" (na'budu) all kinds of worship, outward and inward, by intention, speech, action, state, and orientation. Then he witnesses from His saying "and You alone we ask for help" (wa iyyaka nasta'in) all kinds of seeking help, reliance, and entrusting. Thus he witnesses from it the gathering of Lordship, and from "﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5]" the gathering of Divinity, and from "You" the Essence that gathers all the Most Beautiful Names and the Supreme Attributes.

[Section: The Characteristic of Worship (ta'abbud)]

The characteristic of worship is love together with submission and humility toward the Beloved. Whoever loves a beloved and submits to him has made his heart a servant to him. Indeed, worship is the final stage of love, and it is also called tatayyum (enslavement by love). Its first stage is 'alaqa (attachment), named so because the lover is attached to the beloved.

The poet said:
"I was attached to Layla, while she wore amulets,
And her breast had not yet shown its swelling among her peers."

Another said:
"Attachment to the mother of al-Walid, after
Your head's locks were like the thighs of the white-haired, stripped one."

Then after it comes sababa (passionate longing), named so because the heart pours itself out toward the beloved. The poet said:
"The lovers complained of passion; would that I
Had borne alone what they suffer from their separation."
"So all the delight of love was for my heart,
And no lover before me or after me has reached it."

Then gharam (ardent, enduring love), which is the adherence of love to the heart so that it never departs from it. From this the creditor is called gharim, because he clings to his debtor. From this is His saying, exalted: ﴿Indeed its punishment was gharam﴾ [al-Furqan: 65].

Later writers have become fond of using this word for love, and you rarely find it in the poetry of the Arabs.

Then 'ishq (passionate love), which is excess in love. For this reason the Lord, blessed and exalted, is not described by it, nor is it applied to Him.

Then shawq (longing), which is the heart's journey to the beloved with the swiftest journey. Its use regarding the Lord, exalted, has come, as in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad from 'Ammar ibn Yasir: that he prayed a prayer and shortened it, and he was asked about that, and he said: "Indeed I supplicated in it with supplications that the Prophet, peace be upon him, used to supplicate with: 'O God, I ask You by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation: give me life if life is better for me, and cause me to die if death is better for me. O God, I ask You for Your fear in the unseen and the witnessed, and I ask You for the word of truth in anger and in contentment, and I ask You for moderation in poverty and in wealth, and I ask You for a bliss that does not end, and I ask You for a coolness of the eye that does not cease, and I ask You for the coolness of life after death, and I ask You for the delight of gazing upon Your Face, and I ask You for longing for meeting You, without harmful distress or misleading trial. O God, adorn us with the adornment of faith, and make us guides who are guided.'"

In another narration: "The longing of the righteous for My meeting has lasted long, and I am more longing for their meeting."

This is the meaning that the Prophet (ﷺ) expressed by his saying: "Whoever loves meeting God, God loves meeting him."

Some people of insight said regarding His saying, exalted: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting of God, then indeed the term of God is coming﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 5]: When He, glorified is He, knew the intensity of His friends' longing for His meeting, and that their hearts would not be guided except through meeting Him, He set for them a term and an appointment for meeting Him, and their souls find rest in it. The most pleasant and sweetest life, absolutely, is the life of the loving, longing, intimate lovers. Their life is the true good life, and there is no life for the heart that is better, more pleasant, or more wholesome than it. This is the good life in His saying, exalted: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ [al-Nahl: 97].

What is meant by it is not the life shared between believers and disbelievers, the righteous and the wicked, in the goodness of food, clothing, drink, and marriage. Indeed, the enemies of God may exceed His friends in that many times over. God, glorified is He, has guaranteed for everyone who does righteousness that He will give him a good life. He is the truthful in promise, who does not break His promise. And what life is better than the life of one whose concerns have all been gathered and become one concern in pleasing God, whose heart is not scattered, but who turns toward God, and whose will and thoughts, which were divided among every valley, become one stream toward God? So his remembrance of his Supreme Beloved, his love, his longing for meeting Him, and his intimacy with His nearness become what dominates him. Upon this his concerns, his will, and his intentions revolve, with every thought of his heart. If he is silent, he is silent by God; if he speaks, he speaks by God; if he hears, he hears by Him; if he sees, he sees by Him; by Him he grasps, by Him he walks, by Him he dwells, by Him he lives, by Him he dies, and by Him he is raised. This is as in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from him (ﷺ), relating from his Lord, blessed and exalted, that He said: "My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks. By Me he hears, by Me he sees, and by Me he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him, and if he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely protect him. I do not hesitate about anything I am going to do as I hesitate about taking the soul of My believing servant, who dislikes death, and I dislike to hurt him, though he must have it."

This noble divine hadith, whose meaning and intent is forbidden to the coarse-natured and the hard-hearted to understand, includes the restriction of the causes of His love to two things: performing His obligations, and drawing near to Him through voluntary acts.

He, glorified is He, informed us that performing His obligations is the most beloved thing by which those who draw near draw near to Him, and that after it come voluntary acts. The lover continues to increase in voluntary acts until he becomes beloved of God. When he becomes beloved of God, God's love for him produces another love from Him, above the first love. This love occupies his heart and preoccupies it from thinking about and caring for anything other than his Beloved. It takes possession of his spirit, and there is no room left in it for anything other than his Beloved at all. The remembrance of his Beloved, his love for Him, and His Supreme Exemplar become his, and He holds the reins of his heart and dominates his spirit, with the dominion of the Beloved over the love of the sincere lover in his love, in which all the powers of his love have gathered toward Him.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary, al-Tafsir al-Qayyim, on surah 1, verse 5 (part 11 of 14):

There is no doubt that this lover, if he hears, hears with his beloved; if he sees, he sees with Him; if he strikes, he strikes with Him; if he walks, he walks with Him. He is in his heart, with him, his companion and his close friend. So the bā' here denotes accompaniment (al-muṣāḥabah), and it is an accompaniment without parallel, which cannot be grasped merely by reporting about it or knowing it. The matter is therefore one of states (ḥāliyyah), not a purely cognitive matter.

If the created being finds this in love for a created being, for which he was not created nor made to be disposed, as one of the lovers said:

"Your image is in my eye, your remembrance is in my mouth, and your abode is in my heart, so where could you be absent?"

And another said:

"And it is a wonder that I yearn for them; I ask about them of whoever I meet, while they are with me.
And my eye seeks them while they are in its blackness, and my heart longs for them while they are between my ribs."

This is more subtle than the words of another:

"If I say you are absent, my heart does not believe me, since you are in it as the secret's place, never absent.
Or if I say you are not absent, the glance says this is a lie, so I am bewildered between truth and falsehood."

Nothing is closer to the lover than his beloved. Love may take such firm hold of him that the beloved becomes closer to him than his own self, so that he forgets himself while he is not forgotten, as one said:

"I wish to forget her remembrance, yet it is as though Layla is presented to me on every path."

Another said:

"The heart is asked to forget you, but natures refuse the transmitter."

In the hadith, He specified the hearing, the sight, the hand and the foot for mention, for these are the instruments of perception and the instruments of action. Hearing and sight bring to the heart will and aversion, and they bring to it love and hatred, and then it employs the hand and the foot. When the servant's hearing is by Allah and his sight is by Allah, he is preserved in the instruments of his perception, and he is preserved in his love and hatred, so he is preserved in his striking and his walking.

Consider how He sufficed with mentioning hearing, sight, hand and foot, rather than the tongue. For perception by hearing happens sometimes by choice and sometimes without choice, and likewise sight may fall suddenly without intention, and likewise the movement of the hand and foot, which the servant cannot avoid. So how about the movement of the tongue, which occurs only with intention and choice? And the servant may dispense with it except where he is commanded to use it.

Also, the tongue's responsiveness to the heart is more complete than the responsiveness of the other limbs, for it is its interpreter and its messenger.

Consider how He affirmed the servant's being with Him, his hearing, sight, striking and walking, in His saying: "I was his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks," affirming that He is with His servant, and that His servant is in his perceptions, by his hearing, his sight, and his movements by his hands and feet.

Consider how He said: "By Me he hears, and by Me he sees," and did not say: "For Me he hears, and for Me he sees." Some who speculate may think that the lām is more fitting in this place, since it indicates purpose, and that these acts occur for Allah, which is more specific than occurring by Him. This is an error and a mistake, for the bā' here is not merely that of assistance. The movements and perceptions of the righteous and the wicked are only by Allah's help to them. The bā' here denotes accompaniment, meaning: he hears, sees, strikes and walks while I am his companion, with him. This is like His saying in another hadith: "I am with My servant when he remembers Me and his lips move with Me." This is the special companionship mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: "Do not grieve, indeed Allah is with us" [al-Tawbah: 40].

And the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "What do you think of two whose third is Allah?" And His saying, exalted is He: "And indeed Allah is with the doers of good" [al-'Ankabut: 69].

And His saying: "Indeed Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good" [al-Nahl: 128].

And His saying: "And be patient; indeed Allah is with the patient" [al-Anfal: 46].

And His saying: "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me" [al-Shu'ara': 62].

And His saying to Musa and Harun: "Indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing" [Ta-Ha: 46].

So this bā' conveys the meaning of this companionship, and not the lām. The servant cannot attain sincerity, patience and reliance upon Allah, nor reach the stations of servanthood, except by this bā' and this companionship.

So whenever the servant is by Allah, hardships become easy for him and fears are turned in his favour. By Allah every difficulty is made light, every hardship is made easy, and every distance is brought near. By Allah worries, distresses and sorrows vanish. There is no concern with Allah, and no grief or sadness, except where the servant loses the meaning of this bā'. Then his heart becomes like a fish when it leaves water: it leaps and writhes until it returns to it.

When this agreement from the servant with his Lord in what He loves is achieved, agreement from the Lord with His servant in his needs and requests is achieved, so He said: "If he asks Me, I will surely give him; and if he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely grant him refuge."

That is: just as he agreed with Me in what I desire by complying with My commands and drawing near by what I love, so I agree with him in his desire and his fear regarding what he asks Me to do for him, and what he seeks refuge in Me from befalling him. This agreement grows strong on both sides, to the extent that it requires the Lord, glorified is He, to hesitate regarding the death of His servant, because he dislikes death, and the Lord, exalted is He, dislikes what His servant dislikes and dislikes his distress. Thus, from this aspect, it requires that He not cause him to die, but his benefit lies in his death, for He caused him to die only so that He might give him life, He afflicted him with sickness only so that He might heal him, He made him poor only so that He might enrich him, He withheld from him only so that He might give to him, and He did not expel him from Paradise in his father's loins except that He would return him to it in the best of his states. He did not say to his father, "Go down from it," except while intending to return him to it. This is the true Beloved, not anyone else. Indeed, even if every hair-root of the servant contained complete love for Allah, it would be only a part of what He deserves from His servant.

"Shift your heart wherever you wish in desire; love is only for the first Beloved.
How many a dwelling place on earth the youth grows fond of, yet his longing is always for the first dwelling."

[Section: The final stage of love]

Then comes tatayyum (devotion), which is the last of the stages of love. It is the lover's servitude to his beloved. One says: "Love enslaved him" (tayyamahu al-ḥubb) when it made him a servant, and from this comes "Taym Allah," meaning the servant of Allah. The real meaning of ta'abbud is humiliation and submission to the beloved. From it comes the expression "a paved road" (ṭarīq mu'abbad), meaning one made smooth, which feet have worn down. So the servant (ʿabd) is the one whom love has made submissive and who submits to his beloved. For this reason, the most noble of the servant's states and stations are those of servanthood, and there is no station nobler than it.

Allah, glorified is He, has mentioned the most honoured of creation to Him and the most beloved to Him, His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, with servanthood in his most noble stations: the station of calling to Him, the station of challenge through prophethood, and the station of the Night Journey. He, glorified is He, said: "And when the servant of Allah stood calling Him, they almost became crowded around him" [al-Jinn: 19].

And He said: "And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it" [al-Baqarah: 23].

And He said: "Glory be to the One who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque" [al-Isra': 1].

The hadith of intercession: "Go to Muhammad, a servant whom Allah forgave his past and future sins." So he attained the station of intercession through the perfection of his servanthood and the perfection of Allah's forgiveness of him. Allah, glorified is He, created creation to worship Him alone, with no partner, and this worship is the most perfect kind of love together with the most perfect kind of submission. This is the reality of Islam and the religion of Ibrahim, and whoever turns away from it has indeed made himself foolish. He, exalted is He, said:

"And who would turn away from the religion of Ibrahim except one who makes himself a fool? And We had chosen him in this world, and indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous. When his Lord said to him, 'Submit,' he said, 'I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.' And Ibrahim instructed his sons in it, and so did Ya'qub: 'O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.' Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, 'What will you worship after me?' They said, 'We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and to Him we are Muslims'" [al-Baqarah: 130–133].

For this reason, the greatest sin in the sight of Allah is shirk.

[Shirk in love]

The root of shirk is associating others with Allah, including in love, as He, exalted is He, said: "And among people are those who take others besides Allah as equals, loving them as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah" [al-Baqarah: 165].

He, glorified is He, informed that among people are those who associate with Him rivals whom they love as they love Allah, and He informed that those who believe are stronger in love for Allah than the owners of rivals are for their rivals.

It has been said: rather, the meaning is that they are stronger in love for Allah. For although they love Allah, when they associate others with Him in love, their love for Allah weakens. And the monotheists, since their love for Allah is purified, is stronger than that of those others. Equating the Lord of the worlds with rivals in this love is what is meant, as previously mentioned.

Since Allah's purpose from His creation is the purity of this love for Him, He strongly denounced those who take guardians or intercessors besides Him, and He combined this at times and separated one from the other. He, exalted is He, said: "Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself above the Throne, arranging the affair. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not remember?" [Yunus: 3].

He, exalted is He, said: "Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then established Himself above the Throne. You have not, besides Him, any guardian or intercessor. Will you not remember?" [al-Sajdah: 4].

He said, in separation: "Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say: 'Even though they possess nothing and do not reason?' Say: 'To Allah belongs all intercession'" [al-Zumar: 43–44].

He, exalted is He, said: "And warn by it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no guardian and no intercessor, that they might become righteous" [al-An'am: 51].

He, exalted is He, said: "Behind them is Hell, and what they earned will not avail them at all, nor what they took as protectors besides Allah. And for them is a great punishment" [al-Jathiyah: 10].

So when the servant takes his Lord alone as his ally, He establishes intercessors for him and makes the bond of allegiance between him and His believing servants, so they become his allies in Allah. This contrasts with one who takes a created being as an ally besides Allah.

This is one kind and that is another kind, just as shirk-based intercession, which is false, is one kind, while true intercession, which is established and is attained only through tawhid, is another kind. This is the point of distinction between the people of tawhid and the people of shirk, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.

The point is that the reality of servanthood is not attained together with associating others with Allah in love, unlike love for Allah, which is among the necessary requirements and obligations of servanthood. The love of the Messenger, indeed placing him above oneself, parents and children in love, is not complete faith except with it, for his love is part of the love of Allah. Likewise every love for the sake of Allah and for Allah, as in the Two Sahihs, where he ﷺ said: "Whoever has three qualities will find in them the sweetness of faith."

In another wording in the Two Sahihs: "None will find the sweetness of faith except one who has three qualities: that Allah and His Messenger be dearer to him than anything else; that he loves a person only for Allah's sake; and that he hates to return to disbelief after Allah has rescued him from it, just as he hates to be thrown into the Fire."

In the hadith in the Sunan: "Whoever loves for Allah's sake, hates for Allah's sake, gives for Allah's sake, and withholds for Allah's sake, has perfected his faith."

In another hadith: "Two men do not love each other for Allah's sake except that the better of them is the one who loves his companion more intensely."

Indeed this love is among the necessary requirements of and obligations arising from the love of Allah, exalted is He, and whenever it is stronger, its root is likewise.

[Section]

The Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 1, Verse 5 (Part 12 of 14):

Since a human being, and indeed every living creature that moves by will, cannot be free of knowledge, of will, and of acting on that will, and has a desired goal, and a path and a means that leads to it and helps him reach it, sometimes the means comes from himself, sometimes from outside and separate from him, and sometimes from both himself and the outside, the living creature is naturally disposed to intend something and desire it, and to seek help from something and rely on it to attain what he desires.

What is desired is of two kinds. The first is what is desired for its own sake. The second is what is desired for the sake of something else.

What is sought as help is also of two kinds. The first is what is sought as help for its own sake. The second is what is a follower of that and an instrument.

These are four matters: what is desired for its own sake, what is desired for the sake of something else, what is sought as help for its own sake, and what is sought as help by being an instrument and a follower of what is sought as help for its own sake.

The heart must have a goal in which it finds rest, and in which its love comes to an end. It must also have something by which it reaches its goal and which it seeks as help in attaining what it desires. The one sought as help is called upon and asked. Worship and seeking help are often inseparable. Whoever the heart relies on for his provision, his victory, his benefit and his advantage, submits to him, humbles itself to him, obeys him, and loves him for this reason, even if it does not love him for his own essence. But the state may dominate it until it loves him for his own essence and forgets the purpose for which it loved him. As for the one the heart loves, wills and intends, it may not seek help from him, but seek help from another to attain it, like one who loves wealth, a position, or a woman. If he knows that the beloved is able to achieve his aim, he seeks help from him, and so his love and his seeking help from him are combined.

So the categories are four: what is loved for its own essence and sought as help in itself. This is the highest category, and it belongs to Allah alone. Everything other than Him should only be loved as a follower of His love, and sought as help because it is an instrument and a means.

The second: what is loved for the sake of something else and also sought as help, like a beloved who is able to achieve the aim of the one who loves him.

The third: what is loved but is sought as help against something else.

The fourth: what is sought as help but is not loved in itself.

When this is understood, it becomes clear who among these four categories deserves worship and seeking help, and that loving other than Him and seeking help from other than Him, if they are not a means to loving Him and seeking help from Him, will harm the servant, and their harm is greater than their benefit. And Allah is the One sought for help, and upon Him is reliance.

[Chapter: The Sixth Witnessing, the Witnessing of Tawhid]

This is that one witnesses the Lord, blessed and exalted, as alone in creating and in judging, that whatever He wills comes to be and whatever He does not will does not come to be, that not an atom stirs except by His permission, that creation is subdued under His grip, and that there is no heart except that it is between two of His fingers: if He wills to make it stand firm, He makes it stand firm, and if He wills to make it swerve, He makes it swerve. So the hearts are in His hand, and He is their turner and director however He wills and however He intends. And He is the One who granted the souls of the believers their piety, and He is the One who guided them and purified them, and He inspired the souls of the wicked with their wickedness and their misery: "Whomever Allah guides, there is no misleader for him, and whomever Allah leaves to stray, there is no guide for him" (cf. 7:186). He guides whom He wills by His bounty and mercy, and He leads astray whom He wills by His justice and wisdom. This is His bounty and His gift, and the bounty of the Generous is not withheld. And this is His justice and His decree: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya: 23].

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Belief in qadar (divine decree) is the system of tawhid (oneness of Allah). Whoever denies qadar, his denial breaks his tawhid, and whoever believes in qadar, his belief confirms his tawhid."

In this witnessing, the station of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ is realized for the servant, in knowledge and in state. The servant's foot becomes firm in tawhid al-rububiyyah (oneness of Lordship), and then he rises from it upward to tawhid al-uluhiyyah (oneness of divinity). When he is certain that harm and benefit, giving and withholding, guidance and misguidance, happiness and misery are all in the hand of Allah and not in the hand of any other, and that He is the One who turns the hearts and directs them as He wills, and that no one is granted success except whom He grants success and helps, and no one is forsaken except whom He forsakes, humiliates and abandons, and that the healthiest, safest, straightest, softest, purest and most tender hearts are those that take Him alone as God and object of worship, so that He is more beloved to them than everything else, more feared by them than everything else, and more hoped in by them than everything else. Then His love precedes all loves in the heart, so all loves follow it, as an army follows a sultan. His fear precedes all fears in the heart, so all fears follow his fear. His hope precedes all hopes in the heart, so every hope follows his hope.

This is the sign of tawhid al-uluhiyyah in this heart, and the door through which it entered is tawhid al-rububiyyah. That is, the door to tawhid al-uluhiyyah is tawhid al-rububiyyah.

[Chapter: That there is no happiness for the heart, no pleasure, no bliss, and no well-being except by Allah being its God, its Creator alone, its object of worship and the ultimate goal of its seeking, and more beloved to it than everything else.]

It is known that every living being other than Allah, the Glorified, whether an angel, a human, a jinn or an animal, is in need of acquiring what benefits it and repelling what harms it, and this is not completed for it except by its perception of the beneficial and the harmful. The benefit is of the kind of bliss and pleasure, and the harm is of the kind of pain and punishment.

So it must have two things. The first is knowing what is the beloved goal that benefits it and gives it pleasure when attained. The second is knowing the helper who connects it to that goal and achieves it. Corresponding to these are two other matters: the first is what is hated, detestable and harmful, and the second is the helper who repels it. These are four things:

First: a matter that is loved and whose existence is sought.
Second: a matter that is hated and whose non-existence is sought.
Third: the means to attaining the desired, beloved goal.
Fourth: the means to repelling the hated.

These four matters are necessary for the servant, and indeed for every animal, whose existence and well-being are not established except by them.

When this is established, Allah, the Exalted, is the One who must be the intended, invoked, sought goal, the One whose face is sought, whose nearness is pursued, and whose pleasure is desired, and He is the helper in attaining all of this. Worshipping other than Him and turning to it and attaching oneself to it is the hated harm, and Allah is the helper in repelling it. So He, the Glorified, combines these four matters, and none other does.

So He is the worshipped, beloved, desired One. He is the helper of His servant in reaching Him and worshipping Him. The hated and detestable happens only by His will and power, and He is the helper of His servant in repelling it from him, as the one most knowledgeable of Him among creation (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, and I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You." And he said: "O Allah, I have submitted myself to You, and I have turned my face to You, and I have entrusted my affair to You, and I have leaned my back upon You, out of desire and fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You."

So from Him is the escape, and to Him is the refuge, and by Him is the seeking of protection from the evil of what occurs by His will and power. So the granting of protection is His act, and the thing from which protection is sought is His act, or His created effect that He created by His will.

So the command is all His, the praise is all His, the dominion is all His, and all good is in His hands. None of His creation can count His praises; rather He is as He praised Himself, and beyond what any of His creatures can praise Him.

For this reason the servant's well-being and happiness lie in realizing the meaning of His saying: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5].

For worship includes the desired goal, but in its most perfect forms, and the one sought for help is the One by whom the goal is sought.

So the first (worship) is from the meaning of His divinity, and the second (seeking help) is from the meaning of His lordship. For the God (ilah) is the One whom hearts worship with love, submission, reverence, honoring, exalting, humbling, subjugation, fear, hope and trust. And the Lord, the Exalted, is the One who nurtures His servant, giving him his creation, then guiding him to his interests. There is no God but Him and no Lord but Him. Just as the lordship of other than Him is the greatest falsehood, so too is the divinity of other than Him.

Allah, the Glorified, has combined these two foundations in several places in His Book, such as His saying: ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾ [Hud: 123]. And His saying about His Prophet Shu'ayb: ﴿And my success is not but through Allah; upon Him I rely, and to Him I turn back﴾ [Hud: 88]. And His saying: ﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and glorify Him with His praise﴾ [al-Furqan: 58]. And His saying: ﴿And devote yourself to Him with complete devotion. Lord of the east and the west; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Trustee﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 8-9]. And His saying: ﴿Say, He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I rely, and to Him is my return﴾ [al-Ra'd: 30]. And His saying about the monotheists, the followers of Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned back, and to You is the destination﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4].

These are seven places that encompass these two foundations, which combine the two meanings of tawhid, without which the servant has no happiness at all.

The second aspect: Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, created creation for His worship, which comprises knowing Him, turning to Him, loving Him, and sincerity toward Him. By remembering Him their hearts find rest and their souls are tranquil, and by seeing Him in the Hereafter their eyes are delighted and their bliss is complete. He will not give them anything in the Hereafter better for them, more beloved to them, more delightful to their eyes, or more pleasing to their hearts, than looking at Him and hearing His speech directly without an intermediary. And He did not give them in this world anything better for them, more beloved to them, or more delightful to their eyes, than believing in Him, loving Him, longing to meet Him, being intimate with His nearness, and delighting in His remembrance.

The Prophet (ﷺ) combined these two matters in the supplication that al-Nasa'i and Imam Ahmad narrated, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and others, from the hadith of 'Ammar ibn Yasir: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate with it: "O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, give me life as long as You know life is good for me, and cause me to die when death is good for me. I ask You for fear of You in secret and in public, and I ask You for the word of truth in contentment and in anger, and I ask You for moderation in poverty and wealth, and I ask You for a bliss that never ends, and I ask You for a coolness of the eye that never ceases, and I ask You for contentment after decree, and I ask You for the coolness of life after death, and I ask You for the pleasure of looking at Your Face, and I ask You for longing to meet You, without a harmful adversity or a misleading trial. O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of faith, and make us guides who are guided."

In this great supplication, he combined the best thing in this world, which is longing to meet Him, the Glorified, and the best thing in the Hereafter, which is looking at His Face, the Glorified.

Since the perfection and completion of this was dependent on the absence of what harms in this world and tempts one in religion, he said: "without a harmful adversity or a misleading trial."

Since the perfection of the servant lies in being knowledgeable of the truth, following it, and teaching it to others as a guide, he said: "and make us guides who are guided."

Since the beneficial contentment that achieves the goal is contentment after the decree has occurred, not before it, for before it is a resolve to be content, and when the decree occurs that resolve is dissolved, he asked for contentment after it. The decreed is encompassed by two matters: seeking guidance (istikharah) before it occurs, and contentment after it occurs. So it is part of the servant's happiness to combine both, as in the Musnad and others, from him (ﷺ): "Indeed, among the happiness of the son of Adam is seeking Allah's guidance, and his contentment with what Allah has decreed. And indeed, among the misery of the son of Adam is abandoning seeking Allah's guidance, and his anger at what Allah has decreed."

Since fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the head of every good, in public and in private, he asked Him for fear of Him in secret and in public.

Since most people speak the truth only when they are content, and when they are angry their anger drives them to falsehood, and their contentment may also lead them into falsehood, he asked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for success in speaking the truth in anger and in contentment. For this reason some of the Salaf said: "Do not be one who, when content, his contentment leads him into falsehood, and when angry, his anger drives him out of the truth."

Since poverty and wealth are two trials and two afflictions by which Allah tests His servant, for in wealth He extends His hand and in poverty He withholds it, he asked Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for moderation in both states, which is the balance that has neither extravagance nor stinginess.

Since bliss has two kinds, one for the body and one for the heart, which is the coolness of the eye, and its perfection is in its permanence and continuity, he combined them in his saying: "I ask You for a bliss that never ends, and a coolness of the eye that never ceases."

Since adornment has two kinds, adornment of the body and adornment of the heart, and the adornment of the heart is greater in worth and more significant in value, and since the adornment of the body is attained in its most perfect form in the Hereafter, he asked his Lord for the inner adornment and said: "Adorn us with the adornment of faith."

Since life in this abode is never cool for anyone, whoever he may be, but is filled with choking grief and distress, and surrounded by inner and outer pains, he asked for the coolness of life after death.

The point is that he combined in this supplication the best of what is in this world and the best of what is in the Hereafter.

The servants' need for their Lord in their worship and in deifying Him is like their need for Him in creating them, providing for them, granting health to their bodies, concealing their faults, and securing their fears. Indeed their need for His divinity, love and servitude is greater, for that is the ultimate goal intended for them. There is no well-being for them, no bliss, no success, no pleasure, and no happiness without that in any way.

For this reason "There is no god but Allah" is the best of good deeds, and the tawhid of divinity is the head of the matter. As for the tawhid of lordship, which both the Muslim and the disbeliever acknowledge, and which the theologians (ahl al-kalam) established in their books, it is not sufficient on its own. Rather it serves as proof against them, as He, the Glorified, explained in His noble Book in several places. For this reason the right of Allah over His servants is that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. As in the authentic hadith narrated by Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Do you know what Allah's right over His servants is?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "His right over His servants is that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. Do you know what the servants' right over Allah is if they do that?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Their right over Him is that He does not punish them with the Fire."

And for this reason He, the Glorified, loves His believing, monotheist servants and rejoices in their repentance. Just as in that lies the greatest pleasure, happiness and bliss of the servant. There is nothing in existence other than Allah, the Glorified, to which the heart can find rest, be tranquil and feel intimacy, and enjoy turning to Him. Whoever worships other than Him and gains from it some benefit and pleasure, his harm from that is many times greater than his benefit, and it is like eating poisoned food that is delicious. And just as the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted if there were gods in them other than Him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would both have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya: 22].

Likewise, when the heart has an object of worship other than Allah, the Exalted, it becomes corrupt with a corruption whose rectification is not hoped for, except by removing that object of worship from the heart, and having Allah, the Exalted, alone as its God and object of worship, whom it loves, hopes in, fears, relies upon, and turns to.

The third aspect: the servant's need to worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him, has no parallel that could be used as an analogy. It does, however, resemble in some respects the body's need for food and drink, and the soul's need, so it is compared to them. There are nonetheless many differences between them. The true reality of the servant is his heart and his spirit, and he has no wellbeing except through his true God, there is no god but Him. He is not at peace except by remembering Him, and he does not find rest except by knowing and loving Him. He is toiling toward Him, laboring toward Him, and so he will meet Him, and he must meet Him. He has no wellbeing except through the singling out of Allah in love, worship, fear and hope. Even if he obtains pleasures and joys from other than Him, those do not last for him. Rather, he moves from one kind to another and from one person to another, enjoying this at one time and that at another. Very often, the very thing he enjoys becomes the greatest cause of his pain and harm. As for his true God, he needs Him at every time and in every state. Wherever he is, the very act of faith in Him, loving Him, worshipping Him, glorifying Him and remembering Him is the nourishment and strength of the human being, and his wellbeing and sustenance. This is what the people of faith hold, and what the Sunnah and the Qur'an indicate, and what the natural disposition and the heart bear witness to. It is not as those say whose share of realization and gnosis is small, and whose portion of excellence (ihsan) has been diminished, who claim that worshipping Him, remembering Him and thanking Him is a burden and a hardship imposed merely as a trial and test, or merely for the sake of a compensation of reward separate from the deed, like an exchange for prices, or merely for the discipline and refinement of the self so that it rises above the level of the beasts of the animal kingdom. This is what is found in the statements of one whose share of knowledge of the Most Merciful has been diminished, whose portion of tasting the realities of faith is small, and who rejoices in the scum of ideas and the refuse of minds. Rather, worship of Him, knowledge of Him, His oneness (tawhid) and thanking Him are the delight of the human being's eyes, the finest pleasure for the spirit, the heart and the inner being, and the most pure bliss attained by one who is worthy of this station. And Allah is the One sought for help, and upon Him is reliance.

The worship and commands are not intended primarily to be hardship and burden, even though that does occur incidentally and as a consequence in some of them, for reasons that necessitate it and are inescapable, and which belong to the requirements of this world.

His commands, the right He has made obligatory upon His servants, and the laws He has prescribed for them, are the coolness of the eyes and the delight of the hearts, the bliss and joy of the spirits. Through them comes their healing, their happiness and their success, and their perfection in this life and the next. Indeed, there is in reality no joy, no delight, no pleasure and no bliss for them except through this. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an instruction from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers. Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ [Yunus: 57-58].

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: "The bounty of Allah is the Qur'an, and His mercy is that He made you among its people." Hilal ibn Yasaf said: "By Islam, which guided you to it, and by the Qur'an, which taught it to you; it is better than what you accumulate of gold and silver." Likewise Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "His bounty is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an." And a group of the early generations said: "His bounty is the Qur'an, and His mercy is Islam."

The verified position is that each of them contains both qualities, bounty and mercy. These are the two matters with which Allah favoured His Messenger (ﷺ), when He said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor [what] faith [was].﴾ [al-Shura: 52].

Allah, the Exalted, only raises up whoever is raised by means of the Book and faith, and debases whoever is debased by the lack of both.

If it is said: the Qur'an has indeed named this a "taklif" (obligation), as in His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286], and His saying: ﴿We do not burden a soul except to its capacity﴾ [al-An'am: 152].

It is answered: Yes, but that occurred only in the negative form. Allah, the Exalted, never named His commands, His injunctions and His laws a "taklif." Rather, He named them a spirit and a light, a healing, a guidance, a mercy, a life, a covenant, a charge, and similar terms.

The fourth aspect: the best and most sublime of the blessings of the Hereafter, the highest of them absolutely, is looking at the Face of the Lord, majestic is His majesty, and hearing His speech. As in Sahih Muslim, from Suhayb (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise, you have a promise with Allah which He wishes to fulfil for you.' They will say: 'What is it? Has He not made our faces bright, weighed our scales heavy, admitted us into Paradise, and saved us from the Fire?' He said: 'Then the veil will be lifted for them, and they will look at Him. He will not have given them anything more beloved to them than looking at Him.'" And in another hadith: "They will not turn to anything of the bliss as long as they are looking at Him." So the Prophet (ﷺ) made clear that, despite their complete enjoyment of what their Lord has given them in Paradise, He has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking at Him. That is more beloved to them because the pleasure, bliss, joy, delight and coolness of eye they obtain through it exceed what they obtain from enjoying food, drink and the wide-eyed maidens (hur al-'ayn). There is absolutely no comparison between the two pleasures and the two blessings. For this reason, the Exalted said regarding the disbelievers: ﴿No! Indeed, they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord. Then indeed, they will [enter] the Hellfire.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15-16].

So He combined for them two kinds of punishment: the punishment of the Fire and the punishment of being veiled from Him, the Exalted. Likewise, He combined for His friends two kinds of bliss: the bliss of enjoying what is in Paradise and the bliss of enjoying the sight of Him. In this surah He mentioned these four kinds, saying regarding the righteous: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, on couches, observing.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 22-23].

Whoever said that the meaning of the verse is that they look at their enemies being punished, or look at their palaces and gardens, or that some of them look at others, has diminished the meaning of the verse. All of this is a deviation from the intended meaning to something else. The meaning is rather that they look at the Face of their Lord, in contrast to the state of the disbelievers, who are veiled from their Lord.

﴿Then indeed, they will [enter] the Hellfire.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 16].

Reflect on how the Exalted set against what the disbelievers said about the believers in the world, and mocked them for, its opposite in the Hereafter. The disbelievers, when the believers passed by them, would wink at one another and laugh at them: ﴿And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are the astray."﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 32]. Then He said: ﴿So today, those who believed will be laughing at the disbelievers﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 34], as a counterpart to their winking and laughing at them. Then He said, "[they are] observing," leaving the looking unrestricted, not qualifying it with one object over another. The highest, most sublime and greatest thing they look at is Allah, the Exalted. Looking at Him is the most sublime and excellent kind of looking, and it is the highest rank of guidance. So He answered their saying: ﴿Indeed, these are the astray﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 32].

Therefore, looking at the Lord, the Exalted, is intended in these two places without doubt, either specifically or through generality and absoluteness. Whoever reflects on the context will find that the two verses cannot bear any meaning other than this, whether specifically or generally.

Just as there is no comparison between the blessings in Paradise and the blessing of looking at the Face of the Most High, the Exalted, so too there is no comparison between the blessings of this world and the blessing of loving Him, knowing Him, longing for Him and being intimate with Him. Rather, the pleasure of looking at Him, the Exalted, follows from their knowledge of Him and their love for Him, for pleasure follows awareness and love. Whenever the lover knows his beloved more and loves him more intensely, his enjoyment of nearness to Him, seeing Him and reaching Him is greater.

The fifth aspect: created beings have, for the servant, neither benefit nor harm, neither giving nor withholding, neither guidance nor misguidance, neither victory nor abandonment, neither lowering nor raising, neither honour nor humiliation. Rather, Allah alone owns all of that for him. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to the people - none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds - none can release it after Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ [Fatir: 2]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And if Allah touches you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He intends for you good, there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ [Yunus: 107]. And the Exalted said: ﴿If Allah helps you, no one can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, then who is there that can help you after Him?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 160]. And the Exalted said, regarding the man of Ya-Sin: ﴿Shall I take gods other than Him? If the Most Merciful should intend me some harm, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 23]. And the Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, remember the favour of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no god but Him, so how are you deluded?﴾ [Fatir: 3]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Who is it that is an army for you to support you other than the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are not but in delusion. Or who is it that could provide for you if He withheld His provision? But they persist in arrogance and aversion.﴾ [al-Mulk: 20-21].

He, the Exalted, combined victory and provision. The servant needs someone who will repel his enemy by His victory and bring him benefits by His provision, so he must have a helper and a provider. Allah alone is the One who helps and provides, for He is the Provider, the Possessor of strong power. From the perfection of the servant's understanding and knowledge is that he knows that if Allah touches him with harm, no one else can lift it from him, and if He bestows on him a blessing, no one else can grant it to him. It is related that Allah, the Exalted, revealed to one of His prophets:

"Acquire for Me subtle understanding and hidden gentleness, for I love that. He said: 'O Lord, what is subtle understanding?' He said: 'If a fly lands on you, know that I am the One who made it land, so ask Me to remove it.' He said: 'And what is hidden gentleness?' He said: 'If a grain comes to you, know that I am the One who caused it to reach you, and that I remembered you by it.'" And the Exalted said regarding the sorcerers: ﴿And they could not harm anyone thereby except by the permission of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 102].

So He alone is the One who suffices His servant, helps him, provides for him and protects him.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ma'mar informed us, he said: I heard Wahb say: Allah, the Exalted, said in some of His books:

"By My might, whoever holds fast to Me, even if the heavens with those in them and the earths with those in them plot against him, I will make for him a way out from that. And whoever does not hold fast to Me, I will cut off his hands from the means of the heaven, and I will cause the earth to sink beneath his feet, and I will place him in the air, then I will leave him to himself. My hand is full for My servant: when My servant is obedient to Me, I give him before he asks Me, and I respond to him before he calls upon Me, for I know his need, which is more gentle to him than he knows it himself."

Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us, Abu Sa'id al-Mu'addib related to us, from one who heard 'Ata al-Khurasani, who said: I met Wahb ibn Munabbih while he was circumambulating the House, so I said to him: "Relate to me a hadith that I can memorize from you in this place of mine, and be brief." He said: "Yes:

"Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed to Dawud: 'O Dawud, by My might and My majesty, no servant of Mine holds fast to Me to the exclusion of My creation - I know that from his intention - except that the seven heavens and whoever is in them, and the seven earths and whoever is in them, will plot against him, but I will make for him an exit from among them. And by My might and My majesty, no servant of Mine holds fast to a created being to the exclusion of Me - I know that from his intention - except that I will cut the means of the heaven from his hand, and make the earth sink from beneath his feet, then I will not care in which valley he perishes.'"

This aspect is more apparent to the common people than the previous one. For this reason they were addressed with it in the Qur'an more than the first, and it is from this that the messengers called to the first aspect. When the discerning person reflects upon the Qur'an, he finds that Allah, the Exalted, calls His servants by this aspect to the first aspect. This aspect requires reliance upon Allah, the Exalted, seeking help from Him, calling upon Him and asking Him alone, to the exclusion of all else. It also requires love of Him and worship of Him, because of His goodness to His servant and His abundant favours upon him. So when they love Him, worship Him and rely upon Him from this aspect, they enter through it into the first aspect.

A parallel to this is one who is struck by a great calamity, or severe poverty, or a distressing fear. He begins to call upon Allah, the Exalted, and to humble himself before Him, until He opens to him the sweetness of intimate conversation with Him, the great faith in Him, and turning to Him, which is more beloved to him than the need he initially intended. But he did not know that at first, until he sought it and longed for it. In a similar sense, a poet said:

"May Allah reward the day of terror with good, for it showed us - in all its harshness - Umm Thabit,
It showed us maidens veiled behind their curtains, whom we would not see except at the time of the rushing women's cries."

The sixth aspect: the servant's attachment to other than Allah, the Exalted, is harmful to him if he takes from it beyond the surplus over his need, without seeking help from it in obedience to Him. If he obtains food, drink, marriage and clothing beyond his need, that harms him, and if he loves other than Allah as much as he loves, he will inevitably be deprived of it and separated from it. If he loves it for other than Allah, its love will necessarily harm him, and he will be punished by what he loves, either in this world or in the Hereafter, and most often he will be punished by it in both abodes. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment, on the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 34-35].

And the Exalted said: ﴿So let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in this world, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 55].

The seventh aspect: the servant's reliance upon a created being, and his trust in him, necessarily brings harm upon him from that very source, contrary to what he hoped from him. He will inevitably be forsaken from the direction from which he expected to be helped, and blamed from the direction from which he expected to be praised. This too is established by the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and it is known through inductive observation and experience. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they have taken gods other than Allah that they might be for them a source of might. No! They will deny their worship of them and will be against them as opponents.﴾ [Maryam: 81-82]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And they have taken gods other than Allah, that perhaps they might be helped. They are unable to help them, while they are a force brought forward for them.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 74-75].

That is, they will be angry on their behalf and fight, as an army is angry and fights on behalf of its commanders, yet they are unable to help them, rather they are a burden upon them. And the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. Their gods, which they invoked besides Allah, did not avail them at all when the command of your Lord came, and they added nothing to them but ruin.﴾ [Hud: 101]. That is, [they added nothing but] loss. And the Exalted said: ﴿So do not invoke with Allah another god, lest you be among those punished.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 213]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Do not make with Allah another god, lest you sit reproached and forsaken.﴾ [al-Isra: 22].

Indeed, the polytheist hopes through his polytheism for victory at times, and for praise and commendation at other times. So Allah, the Exalted, informed us that his aim is turned back upon him, and he ends up forsaken and blamed.

The point is: these two aspects regarding the created being are the opposite of what is true regarding the Creator, the Exalted. So the soundness, happiness and success of the heart lie in worshipping Allah, the Exalted, and seeking His help. Its destruction, misery and harm, both immediate and deferred, lie in worshipping the created being and seeking his help.

The eighth aspect: Allah, glorified is He, is Rich, Generous, Mighty, Merciful. He is kind to His servant although He has no need of him. He wills good for him and removes harm from him, not to bring any benefit to Himself from the servant, nor to repel any harm, but out of mercy and kindness from Him. He, glorified is He, did not create His creation so that He would increase in number through them after scarcity, nor so that He would be strengthened by them after humiliation, nor so that they would give Him strength, nor so that they would benefit Him, nor so that they would defend Him, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me. I do not want provision from them, nor do I want them to feed Me. Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56-58]
And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And say, "All praise is due to Allah, who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in dominion, and who has no ally out of weakness. And magnify Him with [full] magnification."﴾ [al-Isra: 111].
He, glorified is He, does not take as an ally anyone who would need Him out of humiliation, as a created being takes an ally among created beings. Rather, He takes as allies His friends out of kindness, mercy and love for them. As for the servants, they are as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Allah is the Rich, and you are the poor.﴾ [Muhammad: 38].

The ninth aspect: the created servant does not know your interest unless Allah, exalted is He, makes him know it, and he cannot achieve it for you unless Allah empowers him to do so, and he does not will it unless Allah creates in him will and volition. So the matter returns entirely to the One from whom it began, the One in whose hand is all good, and to whom the whole affair returns. Therefore, attaching the heart to other than Him in hope, fear, trust and servitude is pure harm with no benefit in it. Whatever benefit comes through that is by Him alone, who decreed it, facilitated it, and delivered it to you.

The tenth aspect: most of creation only wants to have its needs fulfilled by you, even if that harms your religion and your worldly life. Their aim is the fulfilment of their needs, even at your expense. The Lord, blessed and exalted is He, wants you for your own sake, wants to do good to you for your own sake and not for His benefit, and wants to repel harm from you. So how can your hope, your expectation and your fear be attached to other than Him? The sum of this is that you should know:
"That all of creation, if they gathered together to benefit you with something, would not benefit you except with something that Allah, Most High, has written for you; and if they all gathered together to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with something that Allah, Most High, has written against you." Allah, Most High, said: ﴿Say: "Nothing will afflict us except what Allah has decreed for us. He is our Protector, and upon Allah let the believers rely."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 51].

Then contemplate his need and dependence upon His words: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾, whose content is knowing the truth, intending it, desiring it, acting upon it, remaining steadfast in it, calling others to it, and bearing patiently the harm of those who are called. By completing these five levels guidance is completed, and whatever is lacking from them is lacking from one's guidance.

Since the servant is in need of this guidance outwardly and inwardly, in everything he does and leaves undone:

Among matters he has done without guidance, in knowledge, action, or intention, he is in need of repentance from them, and his repentance from them is itself guidance.

Among matters he has been guided to in their root but not in their details, he is in need of guidance in their details.

Among matters he has been guided to from one aspect but not another, he is in need of the completion of guidance in them, so that guidance is perfected for him and more guidance is added to his guidance.

Among matters in which he needs to attain in the future guidance like what he attained in the past.

Among matters in which he believes the opposite of what they are, he is in need of a guidance that abrogates that belief from his heart and establishes its opposite in it.

Among matters of guidance, he is capable of them but has not been created with the will to do them, so he is in need, for the completion of guidance, of the creation of a will by which he does them.

Among matters, he is incapable of doing them while being willing, so he is in need in his guidance of being empowered to do them.

Among matters, he is incapable of them and does not desire them, so he is in need of the creation of capability and will in him, so that guidance may be completed for him.

Among matters he is standing upon in the manner of guidance in belief, will, and action, he is in need of steadfastness in them and their continuance.

His need for asking for guidance became the greatest of needs, and his dependence upon it the most intense of dependencies. The Merciful Lord made this request obligatory upon him every day and night, in his best states, which are the five prayers, in multiple repetitions, due to the great intensity of his necessity and dependence upon this sought matter.

(Section)
His saying ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ includes seeking guidance from one who is capable of it, and it is in His hand: if He wills, He gives it to His servant, and if He wills, He withholds it from him. Guidance is knowledge of the truth and acting upon it. Whoever Allah, the Exalted, has not made knowing the truth and acting upon it has no way to being guided. He, glorified is He, alone is the One who grants the guidance that necessarily results in being guided and from which it does not fail: which is making the servant desirous of guidance, loving it, preferring it, and acting upon it. This guidance does not belong to an angel brought near nor to a prophet sent. It is the guidance of which He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾, along with His saying: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾. The latter is the guidance of calling, teaching and direction, and by it Thamud were guided, but they preferred blindness over it. And it is of which He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah would not mislead a people after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should fear﴾. So He guided them with the guidance of clarification by which His proof is established against them, and He withheld from them the guidance necessarily leading to being guided, by which no one whom He guides goes astray. That is His justice toward them, and this is His wisdom: He gave them what establishes the proof against them, and withheld from them what they are not fit for and what does not befit them.

(Section)
Guidance is knowledge of the truth together with intending it and preferring it over other than it. The one who is guided is the one who acts upon the truth and desires it. It is the greatest blessing of Allah upon the servant, and for this reason He, glorified is He, commanded us to ask Him for guidance to the straight path every day and night in our five prayers. The servant is in need of knowing the truth that pleases Allah in every outward and inward movement. When he knows it, he is in need of One who inspires in him the intention to seek the truth, placing his will in his heart, and then of One who empowers him to perform it. It is known that what the servant does not know is many times more than what he knows, and that whatever he knows to be true, his soul does not obey him in willing it, and even if he willed it, he would be unable to do much of it. So he is compelled at every time to guidance concerning the past, the present, and the future.

As for the past, he needs to take account of himself regarding it: whether it occurred in rectitude, so that he thanks Allah for it and seeks its continuance, or whether he departed from the truth in it, so that he repents to Allah, the Exalted, from it, seeks His forgiveness, and resolves never to return to it.

As for guidance in the present, it is required of him, for he is the son of his moment, so he needs to know the ruling on the actions he is engaged in: whether they are right or wrong.

As for the future, his need of guidance is more evident, so that his journey may be on the path. When this is the nature of guidance, it becomes known that the servant is the most compelled of all things to it, and that what some people raise of the corrupt question, namely: "If we are guided, what need do we have to ask Allah to guide us?" Is this not seeking to obtain what is already obtained? It is the most corrupt question and the furthest from correctness, and it is evidence that its asker has not attained the meaning of guidance nor comprehended its reality and name. For this reason, whoever tried to answer it said that the meaning is "make us firm in guidance and continue it for us."

Whoever comprehends the reality of guidance and the servant's need for it knows that what he has not yet attained of it is many times more than what he has attained, and that he is at every time in need of renewed guidance, especially since Allah, the Exalted, is the Creator of the actions of hearts and limbs, so at every time he is in need of Allah creating for him a specific guidance. Then, unless the obstacles and diverting forces that prevent the effect of guidance and turn it away are removed from him, he will not benefit from the guidance, and its purpose will not be fulfilled for him, for the ruling is not sufficed by the existence of its cause alone; rather, the absence of its impediment and what opposes it is also necessary.

It is known that the servant's whisperings, thoughts, and desires of error in his heart are each an obstacle preventing the effect of guidance from reaching him. If Allah does not turn them away from him, he will not be fully guided. So his need of Allah's guidance is linked to his every breath, and this is the greatest need of the servant.

[Section: Allah taught His servants how to ask Him for guidance to the straight path]

Since asking Allah for guidance to the straight path is the most exalted of requests, and attaining it is the most noble of gifts, Allah taught His servants how to ask Him, and commanded them to precede their request with His praise, extolling Him, and glorifying Him, then mentioning their servitude and their monotheism. These two are means to their goal: a means of approach to Him through His names and attributes, and a means of approach to Him through their servitude to Him. These two means are such that supplication is hardly rejected with them, and they are reinforced by the two means mentioned in the two hadiths of the Greatest Name, which Ibn Hibban narrated in his Sahih, as did Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi.

The first: the hadith of Abdullah ibn Buraydah from his father, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) heard a man supplicating and saying: 'O Allah, I ask You, by my testifying that You are Allah, there is no god but You, the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad), who has not begotten nor been begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.' He said: 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, he has asked Allah by His Greatest Name, which when He is called upon by it, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives.'" Al-Tirmidhi said: this is a sahih hadith.

This is a means of approach to Allah through His oneness, and the supplicant's testimony to His unity, and the affirmation of His attributes indicated by the name al-Samad. Ibn Abbas said of it: "The Knower whose knowledge is perfect, the Capable whose power is perfect." In another narration from him: "He is the Lord (al-Sayyid) in whom all kinds of lordship are perfected." Abu Wa'il said: "He is the Lord whose lordship has reached its end." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He is the one perfect in all His attributes, His actions, and His words, and by negating resemblance and likeness from Him through His saying: ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾.

This is the expression of the creed of the People of the Sunnah, and the means of approach by believing in that and testifying to it is the Greatest Name.

The second: the hadith of Anas: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a man supplicating: 'O Allah, I ask You, because to You belongs all praise, there is no god but You, the Bestower (al-Mannan), Originator of the heavens and the earth, Possessor of majesty and honour, O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting.' He said: 'He has asked Allah by His Greatest Name.'" This is a means of approach to Him through His names and attributes.

Al-Fatihah has gathered both means: the means of approach through praise, extolling and glorifying Him, and the means of approach to Him through His servitude and monotheism. Then comes the request for the most important of goals and the most successful of desires, which is guidance, after the two means. So the one who supplicates with it is worthy of being answered.

A parallel to this is the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ) that he would say when he stood to pray at night, narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih from the hadith of Ibn Abbas: "O Allah, to You belongs praise. You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. To You belongs praise. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. To You belongs praise. You are the Truth, and Your promise is true, and Your meeting is true, and Paradise is true, and the Fire is true, and the Prophets are true, and the Hour is true, and Muhammad is true. O Allah, to You I submit, in You I believe, upon You I rely, to You I turn in repentance, by You I contend, and to You I refer for judgment. So forgive me what I have sent forward and what I have delayed, what I have concealed and what I have made public. You are my God; there is no god but You." Here he mentioned the means of approach to Him through His praise, extolling Him, and through His servitude to Him, then asked Him for forgiveness.

[Section: On the levels of guidance]

Then from "Guide us" one witnesses ten levels, and when they are combined, guidance is attained for him.

The first level: the guidance of knowledge and clarification, that He makes him knowing of the truth, perceiving it.

The second: that He empowers him to it, otherwise he is not capable of it by himself.

The third: that He makes him desirous of it.

The fourth: that He makes him one who performs it.

The fifth: that He makes him steadfast upon that and continuing in it.

The sixth: that He turns away from him the obstacles and the hindrances opposed to it.

The seventh: that He guides him in the very path itself with a specific guidance, more particular than the first, for the first is guidance to the path in general, and this is guidance within it and within its stages in detail.

The eighth: that He makes him witness the goal along the path, and alerts him to it, so that he is one who keeps it in view in his journey, attentive to it, not veiled by the means from it.

The ninth: that He makes him witness his poverty and his need of this guidance above every need.

The tenth: that He makes him witness the two deviant paths that diverge from it: the path of those who incurred anger, who turned away from following the truth deliberately and stubbornly, and the path of those who went astray, who turned away from it through ignorance and error. Then he witnesses the gathering of the straight path into one way, upon which are all the prophets of Allah and His messengers, and their followers among the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous.

This is the unity upon which the messengers of Allah and their followers are, and whoever attains this unity has attained the straight path. And Allah knows best.

(Section)
