Among its knowledge: when snow covers the ground, it considers the thin spot that has sunk in, and knows that beneath it is a hare's burrow, so it digs it out and hunts the hare, knowing that the heat of her breath melts some of the snow and makes it thin. Among the knowledge of the wolf: when it sleeps, it makes sleep alternate between its eyes, so it sleeps with one while the other remains alert, and when the other grows drowsy it sleeps with it, and opens the one that slept. As some Arabs said: ﴿He sleeps with one of his eyes and guards with the other against death; he is awake and asleep.﴾

And among the wonders of the knowledge of the sparrow: when its chick falls, it cries out, and no sparrow remains nearby without coming, and they fly around the chick and move it by their actions, and they give it strength, resolve and movement until it flies with them. Some hunters said: "Often I have seen a sparrow on the wall, and I gesture with my hand as if I were throwing at it, and it does not fly. Often I lower my hand toward the ground as if I were picking something up, and it does not move. But if my hand touches even a small pebble, a stone or a date-pit, it flies before my hand can reach it."

And among the knowledge of the dove: when she is carrying eggs, she and the male take part in building the nest, and they set up for it foundations resembling a wall, then they warm it and give it another quality, then they turn the eggs over during the days. And they divide between them the sitting and the toil: most of the hours of sitting fall to the female, and most of the hours of seeking food fall to the male. When the chick hatches, they know that its crop is too narrow for food, so they blow into it repeatedly until its crop widens. Then they feed it saliva or something similar before the food, which is like milk for a child. Then they teach it that the crop needs tanning, so they feed it from the base of the walls some substance between salt and earth, by which the crop is tanned. When it is tanned, they feed it grain. When they know that it is able to pick up food, they stop feeding it gradually. When its strength is complete and it asks to be cared for, they strike it away.

And among the knowledge they have: when the male wants to mate, he begins by making a call, and the female runs away from him a little, so that he tastes the sweetness of union. Then she obeys him of her own accord, then she refrains somewhat so that his desire and love grow stronger. Then she sways gently, shows indolence, displays her sides to him and shows her beauty. Then there arises between them the courting, love, kissing and sipping that is observed plainly.

And among the knowledge of the female sent out (on a mission): when she travels by night, she is guided by the bottoms of valleys, the courses of water, the mountains, the directions of the winds, and the rising and setting of the sun. She uses these and other signs to find her way if she gets lost. When she knows the route, she passes by like the wind.

And among the knowledge of the lebb, which is a kind of spider: it flattens itself on the ground and gathers itself up, so that the fly thinks it is heedless of it, then it pounces on it like a leopard pounces.

And among the knowledge of the spider: it weaves that fine, tightly woven web and places at its top a thread, then it hangs on to it. When a gnat is entangled in the web, it lowers itself down to it and catches it.

And among the knowledge of the gazelle: it does not enter its lair except backward, so that with its eyes it faces what it fears for itself and for its fawn.

And among the knowledge of the cat: when it sees a mouse in the ceiling, it raises its head as if pointing at it with a stick, then it signals to it to come back down. It only wants to bewilder it so that it slips and falls.

And among the knowledge of the jerboa: it digs its burrow on the slope of a valley, where it is high above the course of the flood, so that it is safe from the trampling of hooves and the flow of water. It deepens the burrow, and in its corners it makes many doors, placing between them and the surface of the ground a thin barrier. When it senses danger, it opens one of them with the least effort and goes out through it. And because it is very forgetful, it digs its burrow only beside a mound or a rock, as a sign for itself of the burrow, in case it gets lost from it.

And among the knowledge of the leopard: when it grows fat, it hides, because movement is burdensome to it, until that fat goes away, and then it appears again.

And among the knowledge of the deer: when its antler falls off, it hides, because its weapon has gone, so it grows fat because of that. When the growth of its antler is complete, it exposes itself to the sun and the wind and moves a great deal, so that its flesh firms up and the fat that prevents it from fleeing disappears.

This is a very broad field, and it suffices for it to cite His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿There is no creature crawling on the earth, nor bird flying on its two wings, but they are nations like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered. And those who denied Our signs are deaf and dumb in darknesses. Whomever God wills, He leaves astray, and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path.﴾

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Were it not that dogs are a nation among the nations, I would have commanded that they be killed." This may have two meanings. One: it is a report about a matter that cannot be done, namely that dogs are a nation whose annihilation is impossible because of their multitude on the earth; if it were possible to eliminate them from the earth, he would have commanded their killing. The second: it is like his saying: "Why, because an ant bit you, have you burned a nation of the nations that glorify God?" Then it is a nation created with wisdom and benefit, so its destruction and annihilation contradicts the purpose for which it was created. And God knows best what His Messenger intended.

Ibn ʿAbbas said, in a narration from ʿAtaʾ: "﴿Nations like you﴾ means: they know Me, they affirm My oneness, they glorify Me and praise Me," like His saying: ﴿And there is nothing but that it glorifies His praise﴾, and like His saying: ﴿Do you not see that God is glorified by whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight? Each has known its prayer and its glorification﴾. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿Do you not see that to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the beasts﴾, and His saying: ﴿And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures﴾. It is also indicated by His saying: ﴿O mountains, echo with him, and the birds﴾, and by His saying: ﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee﴾, and His saying: ﴿A female ant said: O ants﴾, and Solomon's saying: ﴿We have been taught the speech of birds﴾.

Mujahid said: "﴿Nations like you﴾ are classes, classified, recognized by their names."

Al-Zajjaj said: "﴿Nations like you﴾ in that they will be resurrected."

Ibn Qutayba said: "﴿Nations like you﴾ in seeking food, pursuing sustenance, and avoiding destruction."

Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna said: "There is no human on the earth without some likeness to the beasts. Among them is one who struts like a lion, among them one who runs like a wolf, among them one who barks like a dog, among them one who preens like a peacock, and among them one who resembles pigs, which, if food is thrown to them, reject it, but when a man gets up from his dung, they lap it up. Therefore you find among humans one who, if he hears fifty wise sayings, does not remember a single one of them, but if a man makes a slip, he memorizes it and preserves it."

Al-Khattabi said: "How excellent is Sufyan's interpretation of this verse, and how well he drew this wisdom from it. When the speech does not accord with its outward meaning, one must turn to its inner meaning. God has informed us of the existence of a likeness between man and every bird and beast, and this is impossible in terms of creation and form, and absent in terms of speech and knowledge. So it must refer to a likeness in natures and characters. Once this is so, know that you are only mingling with beasts and predators, so let your caution toward them and your distance from them be in proportion to that." End of his words.

God, glorified is He, has made some creatures skillful in earning and cunning, and some reliant and not seeking by cunning. Some insects store up food for their entire year, and some rely on trust that for each day they have their provision as a daily sufficiency, a guaranteed sustenance and a decreed matter. Some store, some do not earn at all. Some males provide for their offspring, and some do not know their offspring at all. Some females take responsibility for their young and do not stray from them, some lay their young and take responsibility for another's young, some do not recognize their young once they are independent of them, and some never stop recognizing them and showing tenderness toward them.

He made some animals complete their young through their mothers, and some through their fathers. Some do not seek offspring, some exhaust their concern in seeking it. Some recognize kindness and thank for it, and some regard it as nothing. Some prefer others over themselves, and some, when they obtain enough for a whole group of their own kind, do not let anyone near them. Some love mating and do it often, some do it only once a year, some are content with their female, and some do not stop at any female, even if she is their mother or sister. Some females do not let anyone but their mate have them, some do not turn away a hand that touches them. Some become familiar with and at ease with the children of Adam, and some are wild with them and flee in extreme aversion. Some eat only good things, some eat only filth, and some combine both. Some harm only those who go to extremes in harming them, and some harm those who do not harm them. Some are resentful and never forget an offense, and some never remember it at all. Some never get angry, and some become very angry and keep being appeased until they are satisfied. Some have knowledge and awareness of subtle matters that most people do not discover, and some have no awareness of any of that at all. Some find ugliness repulsive and flee from it, some regard good and ugly as the same, some learn quickly, some learn slowly, and some never accept learning in any way.

All of this is among the clearest proofs of the Creator, glorified is He, and of the perfection of His workmanship, the wonder of His arrangement and the subtlety of His wisdom. For in what He has placed in them of marvelous knowledge, subtle stratagems, good arrangement, and deliberate pursuit of what they desire, there is what makes mouths speak in glorification and fills hearts with knowledge of Him, of His wisdom and His power. Every intelligent person knows by it that He did not create in vain and did not leave things aimless, and that He, glorified is He, has in every creature a dazzling wisdom, a manifest sign and a decisive proof that He is the Lord and Sovereign of everything, that He alone possesses every perfection apart from His creatures, and that He is powerful over everything and knowing of everything.

(Section)

Let us return to what brought us to this point, which is the discussion of the general guidance, which is the companion of creation in pointing to the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, and to His names, His attributes and His oneness. He, exalted, said, reporting of Pharaoh that he said: ﴿Then who is your Lord, O Moses? He said: Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided﴾.

Mujahid said: "He gave everything its creation: He did not give man the creation of beasts, nor beasts the creation of man." The sayings of most commentators revolve around this meaning. ʿAtiyya and Muqatil said: "He gave everything its form." Al-Hasan and Qatada said: "He gave everything its well-being," meaning he gave it, in creation and shaping, what it needs to fit what it was created for, then guided it to what it was created for, and guided it to what would benefit it in its livelihood, its food, its drink, its mating, its movement and its conduct. This is the sound view on which the majority of commentators agree, and it is like His saying: ﴿He measured, then guided﴾.

Al-Kalbi and al-Suddi said: "He gave the man the woman, the camel the she-camel, and the male the female of his kind." The wording of al-Suddi is: "He gave the male the female, like his own creation, then guided him to intercourse." This is the view chosen by Ibn Qutayba and al-Farra. Al-Farra said: "He gave the male among people a woman like himself, the sheep a sheep, the bull a cow, then inspired the male how to approach her." Abu Ishaq said: "This interpretation is permissible, because we see the male among animals come to the female, and we have not seen a male who had come to a female before him, so God inspired him with that and guided him to it." He said: "The first view encompasses this meaning, because if He guided him to his benefit, then this is included in the benefit." I say: the proponents of this view have diminished the meaning of the verse, for its meaning is more majestic and greater than what they have mentioned. His saying "gave everything" rejects this interpretation, for to restrict "everything" to the males and females of animals alone is impossible and has no basis. How would angels and jinn be excluded from this wording, and humans who have not married, and animals that do not mate? And how is an animal that is approached by the male called its creation? Where is the parallel to this in the Qur'an? When He, exalted is He, wanted to express this meaning they mentioned, He expressed it with the clearest and most explicit wording, saying: ﴿And that He created the pair, the male and the female﴾. So taking His saying "gave everything its creation" to mean this is not correct. Consider this.

There is another view in the verse, said by al-Dahhak, who said: "He gave everything its creation: He gave the hand grasping, the leg walking, the tongue speech, the eye sight, and the ear hearing." The meaning of this view is that He gave each limb what it was created for, and "creation" here means "what is created," that is, He gave each organ its created thing which He created for it. For all these meanings are created by God and placed by Him in the organs. Although this meaning is correct in itself, the meaning of the verse is more general. The first view is the correct one: He, exalted is He, gave everything its particular creation, then guided it to what it was created for. There is no creator besides Him, exalted is He, and no guide other than Him. This creation and this guidance are signs of His lordship and oneness. This is the way of proof against the enemy of God, Pharaoh. For this reason, when Pharaoh knew that this was a decisive argument with no flaw in any respect, he turned to a corrupt question about something irrelevant. He said: ﴿Then what about the former generations?﴾, meaning: what is the case with the former generations, that they did not acknowledge this Lord and did not worship Him, but worshipped idols? The meaning is: if what you say were true, it would not have been hidden from the former generations, nor would they have neglected it. So he argued against him with what he and others observed of the signs of the lordship of the Lord of the worlds. The enemy of God countered him with the unbelief of unbelievers in Him and the polytheism of polytheists. This is the practice of every falsifier, and for this reason this became a standard among his heirs, who counter the texts of the prophets with the sayings of heretics, atheists, the offspring of philosophers, the Sabians, sorcerers, the innovators of this community, and those of them who are people of misguidance.

Moses answered his counter-argument with the best answer, saying: ﴿Its knowledge is with my Lord﴾, meaning: the deeds of those generations and their unbelief and polytheism are known to my Lord. He has counted them, preserved them and deposited them in a Book, and He will recompense them for it on the Day of Resurrection. He did not deposit it in a Book out of fear of forgetting or going astray, for He, exalted is He, does not go astray and does not forget. According to this, "the Book" here is the Book of deeds. Al-Kalbi said: "He means by it the Preserved Tablet." According to this, it is the Book of the prior decree, and the meaning according to this is that He, exalted is He, knew their deeds and wrote them down with Him before they did them. So this is part of the completion of His saying "gave everything its creation, then guided." Consider this.

(Section)

He, exalted is He, often combines creation and guidance in the Qur'an, as in His saying at the beginning of the surah He sent down to His Messenger: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created, created man from a clinging clot. Read, and your Lord is the most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know﴾. And His saying: ﴿The Most Merciful taught the Qur'an, created man, taught him expression﴾. And His saying: ﴿Did We not make for him two eyes, and a tongue and two lips, and guide him to the two paths? But he did not attempt the steep path﴾. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man from a drop of mingled fluid, to test him, and We made him hearing and seeing. Indeed, We guided him to the way, whether grateful or ungrateful﴾. And His saying: ﴿Is He who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down for you water from the sky, by which We caused gardens of delight to grow?﴾, and the verses that follow, then He said: ﴿Or who guides you in the darknesses of land and sea?﴾. So creation is the giving of external, concrete existence, and guidance is the giving of knowledge-based, mental existence. This is His creation, and this is His guidance and His teaching.

(Section)

The second level of guidance is the guidance of direction and explanation for those who are accountable. This guidance does not necessarily entail attaining success and following the truth, even though it is a condition for it or a part of its cause. That does not entail the attainment of the conditioned and the caused. Indeed, the prerequisite may fail to be realized either because the cause is incomplete or because there is an obstacle. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾, and He said: ﴿God would not lead a people astray after He had guided them, until He makes clear to them what they should avoid﴾. So He guided them with the guidance of explanation and indication, but they did not become guided, so He led them astray as a punishment for their refusal to be guided at first.

After they had come to know the guidance but turned away from it, He blinded them to it after He had shown it to them. This is His way with everyone upon whom He has bestowed a blessing and who then disbelieves in it: He strips it from him after it had been his portion and share, as He says: ﴿That is because Allah would never change a favor He had bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves﴾. He also says about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾, meaning they denied Our signs after they were certain of their truth. He says: ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had testified that the Messenger was true and clear proofs had come to them? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾. This is the guidance He affirmed for His Messenger when He said: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾. He negated from him the power over the guidance that necessarily produces its effect, which is the guidance of divine success (tawfiq) and inspiration (ilham), when He said: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾.

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been sent as a caller and a conveyor, and guidance is not in my hands. Iblis was sent as one who adorns and misguides, and misguidance is not in his hands." He says: ﴿And Allah invites to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾. So He combined the two kinds of guidance, the general and the specific. He made the general guidance, the call, universal as a proof, by His will and His justice, and He specified the guidance of success as a blessing, by His will and His grace. This rank is more specific than the one before it, for it is the guidance that concerns the accountable (mukallafun), and it is the proof of Allah over His creation, by which He does not punish anyone except after it has been established against him. He says: ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾.

He also says: ﴿Messengers as bringers of good news and warners, so that people would have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾.

And He says: ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Oh, my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah, and indeed I was among the mockers," or say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous"﴾.

And He says: ﴿Every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did there not come to you a warner?" They say, "Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are not but in great error.'"﴾

If it is asked: how can His proof be established against them when He has prevented them from guidance and placed a barrier between them and it?

It is answered: His proof is established against them by leaving them free to choose between them and guidance, by the messengers' clarification to them, and by showing them the straight path, until it is as though they were seeing it with their own eyes. He also established for them the means of guidance, outward and inward, and did not place a barrier between them and those means. As for those among them who are prevented from those means by the loss of reason, or by childhood without discernment, or by living in a remote part of the earth that the call of His messengers had not reached, He does not punish them until His proof is established against them. So He did not prevent them from this guidance, nor did He place a barrier between them and it. Yes, He cut off His success from them and did not will to help them or to turn their hearts toward it. Thus He did not place a barrier between them and what is within their capacity, though He placed a barrier between them and what is beyond their capacity, namely His act, His will, and His success. That is not within their capacity, and it is what they were prevented from and what was placed beyond them. So reflect upon this point, recognize its weight, and Allah is the One sought for help.

(Section)

The third rank of guidance is the guidance of success (tawfiq) and inspiration (ilham), and the creation of the will which necessarily produces the act.

This rank is more specific than the one before it. It is the guidance which the ignorant Qadariyya (those who deny divine decree and affirm absolute human power) went astray by denying, and against which the early community (salaf) and the people of the Sunna (Ahl al-Sunna) cried out, from every region of the earth, age after age, until our time. But the Jabriyya (those who deny human agency and ascribe all acts to compulsion) wronged them and did not do them justice, just as they wronged themselves by denying causes and powers, denying the servant's action and capacity, and denying that he has any effect upon the act at all. Thus they were not guided by the view of these people. Rather, it increased them in misguidance upon their misguidance, and in clinging to what they were upon. This is the way of the falsifier when he calls another falsifier to abandon his doctrine, since his own doctrine is false. It is like the Christian calling the Jew to the Trinity and the worship of the cross, and to the claim that the Messiah is a complete God, uncreated, and to similar falsehoods which he himself holds.

This rank necessarily involves two matters. The first is the act of the Lord, the Exalted, which is guidance. The second is the act of the servant, which is being guided, and it is the effect of His act. So He is the Guide and the servant is the one guided. He says: ﴿Whom Allah guides is the one truly guided﴾. There is no way for an effect to exist except through its complete cause. If His act does not occur, the servant's act does not occur either. For this reason He says: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide one who leads himself astray﴾.

This is explicit that this guidance is not in the power of the Prophet (ﷺ), even if he were eager for it, nor in the power of anyone other than Allah. Whenever Allah sends someone astray, no one has a way to guide him, as He says: ﴿Whom Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide﴾. He also says: ﴿Whom Allah wills to send astray, He sends astray, and whom He wills, He places upon a straight path﴾. He says: ﴿Then is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him so that he sees it as good [like one who is not misled]? Indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself go to waste in regret over them﴾. He says: ﴿Have you seen one who takes his own desire as his god, and Allah has misguided him knowingly, and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a covering? Who then can guide him after Allah? Will you not be reminded?﴾ He says: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾. He says: ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾. He says: ﴿Have not those who believed despaired that if Allah willed He could have guided all of mankind?﴾ He says: ﴿Whomever Allah wills to guide, He opens his breast to Islam, and whomever He wills to send astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as though he were climbing up into the sky﴾. The people of Paradise say: ﴿Praise be to Allah who guided us to this. And we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us﴾. They did not mean that part of the guidance was from Him and part was from them. Rather, all of the guidance is from Him, and had He not guided them, they would not have been guided.

He says: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant? Yet they threaten you with those other than Him. And whom Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide. And whom Allah guides, for him there is no misleader. Is not Allah Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution?﴾

He says: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, to make clear to them. Then Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾.

He says: ﴿And We had certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid false deities." Then among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was decreed﴾.

He says: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter, and Allah sends astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills﴾.

He says: ﴿Thus Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾.

He says: ﴿By it He misleads many and by it He guides many, and He misleads by it none except the defiantly disobedient﴾.

He says: ﴿By it Allah guides those who follow His pleasure to the ways of peace, and brings them out of darknesses into light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path﴾.

Allah commanded all His servants to ask Him for guidance to the straight path every day and night in the five prayers. That includes guidance to the path and guidance within it, just as misguidance is of two kinds: misguidance from the path, so that one is not guided to it, and misguidance within it. The first is being misguided from knowing it, and the second is being misguided from its details or some of them.

My shaykh said: "Since the servant, in every state, is in need of this guidance in all that he does and abandons, there are matters he has done without guidance, so he needs repentance from them. There are matters in which he was guided to their root but not their details, or was guided to them in one respect and not another, so he needs the completion of guidance in them in order to increase in guidance. There are matters in which he needs to attain in the future the guidance he attained in the past. There are matters about which he has no belief, so he needs guidance in them. There are matters he has not done, so he needs to do them in the manner of guidance. And other kinds of guidance. So Allah has obligated him to ask Him for this guidance in his best states, which is the prayer, repeated several times a day and night." End of his words.

The goal is not achieved except by guidance to the path and guidance within it. The servant may be guided to a path he intends and that is suited to him, yet not be guided to the details of his journey, the times of travel, the provisions for the road, or the dangers of the way. For this reason Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a method﴾, said: "A way and a sunna." This explanation needs explanation. The "way" (sabil) is the road, and this is the minhaj (method). The "sunna" is the shir'a (law), and it is the details of the road, its turns, the manner of traveling it, and the times of travel. On this reading, "a way and a sunna" means the sabil is the minhaj and the sunna is the shir'a, so the earlier term in the verse corresponds to the later term in the explanation. In another wording it is "a sunna and a way," so the earlier term corresponds to the earlier and the later to the later.

(Section)

Among this is His report, the Exalted, that He sealed and stamped the hearts of the disbelievers, and that He made them deaf to the truth and blinded their sight to it, as He says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe. Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing﴾.

The complete pause (waqf tam) is here, then He says: ﴿And over their sight is a covering﴾, like His words: ﴿Have you seen one who takes his own desire as his god, and Allah has misguided him knowingly, and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a covering?﴾

He says: ﴿And their saying, "Our hearts are wrapped," but Allah has set a seal upon them for their disbelief﴾. He says: ﴿Thus Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers﴾, ﴿Thus We seal the hearts of the transgressors﴾, and ﴿We seal upon their hearts, so they do not hear﴾.

He also reports that upon some hearts there are locks that prevent them from opening to let guidance enter. He says: ﴿Say, "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. And as for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness." Such people are called from a distance﴾. This deafness and blindness prevent them from having guidance and healing. He says: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾. He says: ﴿And thus the evil of his deeds was made attractive to Pharaoh, and he was averted from the way﴾. It was recited by the Kufans as "wa-suddu" with a dammah on the sad, taking it as parallel to "zuyyina" (was made attractive). He says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor, a liar﴾. He says: ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾. It is well known that He did not negate the guidance of clarification and indication by which the proof is established, for that is His proof upon His servants.

The Qadariyya reject all of this, referring it to the ambiguous verses (mutashabih) of the Qur'an and treating it as among its ambiguous parts. They interpret it other than its meaning, indeed by interpretations that establish its falsehood and show that the speaker did not intend it. Like the saying of some of them: the intended meaning of this is that Allah names the servant as guided or misguided. They reduced His guiding and misguiding to mere naming the servant by these names. This is known with certainty to be an impossible reading of these verses. When you reflect upon them you find that they do not bear what they claim at all. In no language of any nation, let alone the most eloquent and complete of languages, does "He guided him" mean "He named him guided," or "He misguided him" mean "He named him misguided." Can one say "He made him knowing" meaning "He named him a knower," or "He made him understand" meaning "He named him understanding"? How could this be valid in a verse such as: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾? Did anyone other than the Qadariyya who distort the Qur'an understand from this: "It is not upon you to name them guided, but Allah names whom He wills as guided"?

Did anyone ever understand from His words: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ that it means "you do not name him guided, but Allah names him by this name"?

And did anyone understand from the supplicant's words: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾, or from the saying "O Allah, guide me by Your own means," and similar, that it means "O Allah, name me guided"?

This is a crime of the Qadariyya against the Qur'an, and its meaning is like the crime of their brothers the Jahmiyya (followers of Jahm ibn Safwan, who denied divine attributes) against the texts on the divine attributes, distorting them from their proper places. They opened the door for the heretics (zanadiqa) and the atheists (mulhidun) to commit their crime against the texts on the resurrection and to interpret them with interpretations which, if not stronger than theirs, are not inferior to them. They opened the door for the Qaramita and the Batiniyya (esoteric sects) to interpret the texts of command and prohibition in ways similar to their interpretations. The distorting interpretation that these sects have linked together is the root of the corruption of the world and of religion and the ruin of the world. We will, if Allah wills, devote a book to mentioning the crimes of those who interpret upon this world and religion. When you weigh the interpretations of the Qadariyya, the Jahmiyya, and the Rafida (Shi'a extremists) against those of the atheists, the heretics, the Qaramita, the Batiniyya and their like, you will find no great difference between them. False interpretation entails nullifying what the Messenger brought, lying against the speaker by claiming he intended that meaning, and thereby establishing falsehood, affirming error, attributing to the speaker what is unbecoming of him of deception and riddles, and speaking about him without knowledge that he intended this meaning. The one who interprets must show that the word can bear the meaning he mentions first, and that the speaker used it in that meaning in most instances, so that when he uses it in a sense that could be other than that, it is understood in the sense he is known to use it. He must also establish, with a proof free from opposing evidence, what requires turning the word from its apparent and literal meaning to its figurative and metaphorical meaning. Otherwise it is mere assertion and is not accepted.

Some of them interpret these texts as meaning the guidance of clarification and instruction, not the creation of guidance in the heart. According to this sect, Allah is not able to do that. This interpretation is among the most false of falsehoods. Allah, the Exalted, informs us that He divided His guidance to the servant into two parts: one part that no one but Him can give, and another part that is within the capacity of servants alone. Regarding the part within the capacity of others, He says: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾. Regarding what is not within the capacity of others, He says: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾. And He says: ﴿Whom Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide﴾. It is known with certainty that clarification and indication may be given to such a person, and they are not negated for him.

Likewise His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who misguides himself﴾ cannot be understood as the guidance of call and clarification, for such a person is guided by the call and clarification even if Allah has sent him astray through the call and clarification. Likewise His words: ﴿And Allah has misguided him knowingly, and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a covering. Who then can guide him after Allah?﴾ Can it be permitted to understand this as meaning: "Who then will call him to guidance and make clear to him what establishes the proof of Allah against him?" How will they deal with the texts that state that He is the One who misguided them? Is it permissible for them to interpret them as meaning that He called them to misguidance?

Then if they say: "That is not its meaning. Its meaning is: he found them so (*alfāhum*, or *wajadahum*), or: He informed His angels of their misguidance, or: He placed on their hearts a sign by which the angels know that they are astray." It is said to them: "This is of the same kind as your claim that His guidance and His leading astray mean naming them 'guided' and 'astray.'" So these are four distortions (*taḥrīfāt*) from you: that He named them thus, that He made them known by a sign by which the angels recognize them, that He informed about them thus, and that He found them so. Informing is of the same kind as naming, and we have explained that the language does not bear this, and that whoever reflects on the texts finds them farthest from this meaning. As for the sign, how strange is the sect of distortion, and what harm they have done to the Qur'an and to faith! In what language and what tongue does the Most High's saying, ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾, indicate the meaning that you do not know him by a sign, but rather God is the One who knows him by it? And His saying, ﴿Whomever God leads astray, there is no guide for him﴾: whomever God knows by a sign of misguidance, no one else knows by a sign of guidance. And His saying, ﴿Had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾: We would have known them by the sign of guidance which they themselves created and gave their own souls. And in what language is it understood from the supplicant's saying, "Guide us to the straight path," that "We know you by a sign by which the angels recognize that we are guided"? Or their saying, ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾, that "You do not know them by a sign of the people of deviation"? Or His saying, "O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion," and "O Director of the hearts, turn my heart to Your obedience," and similar texts? In what language and what tongue is it understood from these that "We know by the sign of firmness and turning to Your obedience"? And in what language would the meaning of His saying, ﴿And We made their hearts hard﴾ be "We knew them by a sign of hardness, or found them so"? Indeed, had the Qur'an been revealed in the language of the Qadariyyah, the Jahmiyyah and the people of innovation, it would be possible to interpret it in that way, or the truth would be subject to their desires and its texts would follow the innovations of the innovators and the opinions of the perplexed. You find all these groups bringing the Qur'an down to their doctrines, innovations and opinions. So the Qur'an, according to the Jahmiyyah, is Jahmī; according to the Mu'tazilah, it is Mu'tazilī; according to the Qadariyyah, it is Qadarī; according to the Rafidah, it is Rāfiḍī; and likewise it is according to all the people of falsehood. ﴿They were not its guardians; its guardians are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know﴾.

As for their distortion of these texts and their like by saying that the meaning is "he found them," in what language and what tongue have you found that "I guided the man" means "I found him guided"? And "God sealed his hearing and heart and placed a covering over his sight" means "He found him thus"? This is nothing but pure fabrication against the Qur'an and the language. If they say: "We did not say this in such cases; we said it only in cases like *aḍallahu Allāh*, meaning 'He found him astray,' as one says *aḥmadtu al-rajul* ('I found the man praiseworthy'), *abkhaltuhu* ('I found him stingy'), and *ajanntuhu* ('I found him mad'), meaning 'I found him so' or 'I attributed it to him'," it is said to the sect of distortion: this occurred only in a few rare words, and otherwise this pattern (*bināʾ*) is established to mean that you did that to him, especially when the hamzah is for transitivity from the triliteral, such as *qāma* and *aqamtuhu* ('I made him stand'), *qaʿada* and *aqaʿadtuhu* ('I made him sit'), *dhahaba* and *adhhabtuhu* ('I made him go'), *samiʿa* and *asmaʿtuhu* ('I made him hear'), *nāma* and *anamtuhu* ('I made him sleep'), and likewise *ḍalla* and *aḍallahu Allāh* ('God made him go astray'), *asʿadahu* ('He made him happy'), *ashqāhu* ('He made him wretched'), *aʿṭāhu* ('He gave him'), *akhzāhu* ('He disgraced him'), *amātahu* ('He caused him to die'), *aḥyāhu* ('He gave him life'), *azāgha qalbahu* ('He made his heart deviate'), *aqāmahu ilā ṭāʿatihi* ('He made him stand to His obedience'), *ayqaẓahu min ghaflatihi* ('He awakened him from his heedlessness'), *arāhu āyātihi* ('He showed him His signs'), *anzalahu manzilan mubārakan* ('He caused him to descend to a blessed station'), and *asknahu jannatahu* ('He caused him to dwell in His garden'), and up to many more of this kind. Do you find in these a single word whose meaning is that He found him so? Exalted is God above what the distorters say! Then look in the book *Fa'ala wa-af'ala* (the book on the verb forms), and see whether you find in it *af'altuhu* in the sense of *wajadtuhu* ('I found him'), despite the breadth of the category, except in two or three words transmitted from the lexicographers. Then consider whether any of the earlier or later lexicographers has said that the Arabs coined *aḍallahu Allāh*, *hadāhu*, *khatama ʿalā samʿihi wa-qalbihi*, *azāgha qalbahu*, and *ṣarafahu ʿan ṭāʿatihi*, and similar expressions, for the meaning "he found him so." When He, glory be to Him, wished to explain this meaning, He said, ﴿And He found you lost and guided you﴾, and did not say "and led you astray." And concerning one who opposed the Messenger and disbelieved in what he brought, He said, ﴿and God led him astray with knowledge﴾, and did not say "and God found him astray."

Then what tawhid is praised here, and what knowledge is imparted to the servants, if the whole matter belongs to God and in His hand, and if no one has any share in His command in merely naming, marking, coinciding with His servants in that way, and finding them so with these attributes, without having any action, creation or will in them? Can human beings not do naming, coinciding and finding in this way? Then what praise and what commendation is fitting for the Lord, exalted, by this mere thing? You and your brothers among the Jabriyyah have not praised the Lord with what He deserves to be praised with, nor have you extolled Him with the attributes of His perfection, nor have you measured Him with His true measure. The followers of the Messenger, his party and his elect, are free of you and of them in your falsehood and their falsehood. They are with you and with them in what you hold of truth, but they do not incline to anything other than what the Messenger explained and brought, nor do they deviate from it in support of the opinions of men that differ or the scattered desires of people. That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) taught us the tashahhud in prayer and the tashahhud in need: 'Indeed, all praise is for God; we seek His help and His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in God from the evils of our souls. Whomever God guides, none can mislead; and whomever He leads astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.'" And he recited three verses: ﴿O you who believe, fear God as He should be feared﴾, the verse; ﴿And fear God, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs; indeed God is ever watchful over you﴾; ﴿O you who believe, fear God and speak words of appropriate justice﴾, the verse.

Al-Tirmidhī said: "This is a sound ḥadīth." Abū Dāwūd said: Muḥammad ibn Kathīr narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhā', from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, who said:

"ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb gave a sermon at al-Jābiyah. He praised God and extolled Him, and with him was a *jāthalīq* (a Byzantine ecclesiastical official) who was having his words translated for him. He said: 'Whomever God guides, none can mislead; and whomever He leads astray, none can guide.' The man shook his forehead as one who denies what he says. ʿUmar said: 'What does he say?' They said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, he claims that God does not lead anyone astray.' ʿUmar said: 'You lie, O enemy of God! Rather, God created you, and He has led you astray, then He will cause you to enter the Fire. By God, were it not for a covenant you have, I would strike your neck! Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, created the people of Paradise and what they would do, and created the people of the Fire and what they would do.' So these said: 'This is for this,' and those said: 'That is for that.'" He said: "So the people dispersed and did not dispute about divine decree (*qadar*)."

(Section)

The fourth stage of the stages of guidance is guidance to Paradise and Hell on the Day of Resurrection.

The Most High said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, along with their spouses and what they used to worship besides God, and guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾. And the Most High said: ﴿And those who were killed in the way of God—He will not let their deeds go astray. He will guide them and set right their affairs﴾. So this is guidance after their being killed. It was said that the meaning is: He will guide them to the path of Paradise and set their condition right in the Hereafter by pleasing their adversaries and accepting their deeds.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "He will guide them to the most rightly guided matters, and will protect them during their days of life in this world." This view was questioned, because it reports about those killed in His way that He will guide them. Al-Zajjāj chose it and said: "He will set their affairs right in livelihood and the rulings of this world." He said: "By this He intends to gather for them the good of this world and the Hereafter." According to this view, it is necessary to interpret His saying "killed in the way of God" with a meaning under which the affirmation of guidance and the setting right of affairs is valid.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 1, verse 7 (part 1 of 8):

Then he explained that the path of the people of this guidance differs from the path of those who earn anger and those who are astray. Thus creation is divided, with respect to this guidance, into three categories:
One upon whom it has been bestowed, and whose share of blessings continues in proportion to his share of its details and divisions.
A astray one who has not been given this guidance and has not been granted success in it.
And one who earns anger, who knew it but was not granted success in acting upon its requirements.
The first, the one blessed, stands upon the guidance and the religion of truth in knowledge and in action. The astray one has been stripped of it in knowledge and in action. The one who earns anger knows it in knowledge but has been stripped of it in action. And God is the granter of success to what is correct.
(Benefit)
As for those upon whom favour has been bestowed, they are those whom God has favoured with knowledge of the truth and with submission to it and preference of it over other things in action. These are the people of the path of salvation, and whoever else is on the path of destruction. For this reason God, glorified is He, commanded us to say every day and night, many times: ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned anger or of those who are astray﴾.
A servant is utterly compelled to be one who knows what benefits him in his livelihood and his hereafter, and to be one who prefers and desires what benefits him and avoids what harms him. By the combination of these two, he has been guided to the straight path. If he lacks knowledge of that, he follows the way of those who are astray; and if he lacks the intention and the following of it, he follows the way of those who earn anger. By this one knows the worth of this great supplication, the intensity of need for it, and that the happiness of this world and the next depends upon it.
The servant is in need of guidance at every moment and breath, in everything he does and leaves undone, for he is among matters from which he is never free:
One of them: matters he has undertaken in a way other than the way of guidance, out of ignorance. He needs to seek guidance to the truth in them.
Or one who knows the guidance in them but undertook them in a way other than its proper way, deliberately. He needs to repent of them.
Or matters in which he knew neither the way of guidance, neither in knowledge nor in action, so guidance to knowing and recognising them, and to intending and doing them, has escaped him.
Or matters to which he has been guided in one respect but not in another, so he needs the completion of guidance in them.
Or matters to whose root he has been guided but not to their details, so he needs guidance to the detail.
Or a path to which he has been guided, while he still needs another guidance within it. Guidance to the path is one thing, and guidance within the path itself is another. Do you not see that a man knows that the road to such-and-such a town is such-and-such, yet he does not know how to travel it well? Its travel requires a specific guidance within the journey itself: travelling at one time rather than another, taking water in such-and-such a desert in such-and-such a quantity, and alighting at one place rather than another. This is guidance within the journey itself, which one who knows that this is the road may neglect, and so he perishes and is cut off from the goal.
Likewise, there are matters in which he needs to obtain in the future the same guidance he obtained in the past.
And matters in which he is free of belief in truth or falsehood, so he needs guidance to the correct position in them.
And matters in which he believes himself to be upon guidance while he is in error without realising it, so he needs to be moved from that belief by guidance from God.
And matters which he has done in the way of guidance, yet he needs to guide others to them, advise them and counsel them; his neglect of this causes him to lose guidance in proportion to it. Just as his guiding others, teaching them and advising them opens for him the door of guidance, for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Whenever he guides others and teaches them, God guides him and teaches him, so he becomes a guide who is guided, as in the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ) narrated by al-Tirmidhi and others: "O God, adorn us with the adornment of faith, and make us guides who are guided, not astray nor misleading, a peace to Your friends and a war against Your enemies; we love by Your love whoever loves You, and we oppose by Your enmity whoever opposes You."
God, glorified is He, has praised His believing servants who ask Him to make them leaders whom others follow in guidance. He, exalted is He, said in describing His servants: ﴿And those who say: Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes, and make us leaders for the righteous﴾.
Ibn 'Abbas said: "Guided by us in goodness."
Abu Salih said: "Those who take our guidance as an example."
Makhul said: "Leaders in piety whom the righteous follow."
(Section)
The seventh point: from the knowledge of the one asked, which is the straight path.
The path is not a path (sirat) until it includes five matters: uprightness, delivering to the goal, nearness, breadth for those who pass along it, and its being specified as the path to the goal. It is not hidden that the straight path includes these five matters.
Its description as "straight" includes its nearness, for the straight line is the nearest line joining two points, and whenever it bends it becomes longer and more distant. Its straightness includes its delivering to the goal. Its being set up for all who pass along it necessitates its breadth. Its attribution to those upon whom favour has been bestowed, and its description as differing from the path of those who earn anger and of those who are astray, necessitates its being specified as the path.
The path is sometimes attributed to God, since it is He who legislated and established it, as in His saying: ﴿And that this is My path, straight﴾ [al-An'am: 153], and His saying: ﴿And indeed you guide to a straight path, the path of God﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. Sometimes it is attributed to the servants, as in al-Fatiha, because they are the people who travel it, and it is ascribed to them, and they are those who pass along it.
(The eighth point: on the mention of those upon whom favour has been bestowed, and distinguishing them from the two groups of anger and error.)
Thus people are divided, according to their knowledge of the truth and their acting upon it, into these three categories, because the servant either knows the truth or is ignorant of it. The one who knows the truth either acts according to its requirement or opposes it. These are the categories of the responsible, and they do not go beyond them at all. The one who knows the truth and acts upon it is the one upon whom favour has been bestowed, the one who purified his soul by beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and he is the successful: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it﴾ [al-Shams: 9]. The one who knows it but follows his desire is the one who earns anger. The one ignorant of the truth is the astray one. The one who earns anger is astray from the guidance of action, and the astray one earns anger because of his straying from the knowledge that necessitates action. So each of them is astray and earns anger, but the one who abandons acting upon the truth after knowing it is more deserving of the description of anger and more entitled to it. For this reason the Jews are more entitled to it, and it is intensified regarding them, as in His saying concerning them: ﴿Wretched is what they have sold themselves for, that they disbelieve in what God has sent down, out of resentment that God should send down of His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants; so they returned with anger upon anger﴾ [al-Baqarah: 90]. And He said: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as recompense from God? Those whom God has cursed and upon whom He has become angry, and of whom He made apes and swine, and who worshipped the Taghut; those are worse in position and further astray from the right way﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 60]. The ignorant of the truth is more entitled to the name of error, and for this reason the Christians were described with it in His saying: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion beyond the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and strayed from the sound way﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 77]. The first is in the context of address to the Jews, and the second in its context with the Christians. In al-Tirmidhi and Sahih Ibn Hibban, from the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The Jews are those upon whom is anger, and the Christians are astray."
In the mention of those upon whom favour is bestowed, who are those who knew the truth and followed it, and of those who earn anger, who are those who knew it and followed their desire, and of the astray, who are those who were ignorant of it, there is what necessitates the establishment of the messengership and prophethood, because the division of people into these is the observed reality, and this division is only required by the establishment of messengership.
He attributed the favour to Himself and omitted the agent of anger, for several reasons:
Among them: favour is goodness and bounty, whereas anger is a matter of retribution and justice, and mercy overcomes wrath. So He attributed to Himself the more complete and prior and stronger of the two matters, and this is the Qur'an's method of attributing good things and blessings to Him, and omitting the agent in contrast to them, as in the saying of the jinn who believed: ﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those upon the earth or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾ [al-Jinn: 10]. From this is the saying of al-Khidr concerning the wall and the two orphans: ﴿So your Lord intended that they reach their maturity and extract their treasure﴾ [al-Kahf: 82]. And he said regarding the boat's damage: ﴿So I intended to damage it﴾ [al-Kahf: 79], then he said after that: ﴿And I did not do it of my own accord﴾ [al-Kahf: 82]. Consider His saying: ﴿It is made lawful for you on the night of fasting to go to your wives﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187], and His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3], and His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are your mothers﴾ [al-Nisa': 23], then He said: ﴿And lawful to you is what is beyond that﴾ [al-Nisa': 24].
In His specifying the people of the straight path with favour, there is what indicates that absolute favour is what necessitates lasting success. As for mere favour, it is upon both believer and disbeliever, for all creation is in blessing. This is the decisive resolution of the question: does God have any favour upon the disbeliever or not?
So absolute favour belongs to the people of faith, and general favour is for both believer and disbeliever, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you should count the favour of God, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is oppressive and ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim: 34].
Favour is of the same kind as beneficence; indeed it is beneficence. The Lord, exalted is He, has His beneficence upon the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever.
As for absolute beneficence, it belongs to those who are righteous and those who are good-doers: ﴿Indeed God is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾.
The second aspect: God, glorified is He, is the sole possessor of blessings: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from God﴾ [al-Nahl: 53]. So what He alone possesses is attributed to Him, and if it is attributed to other than Him, it is because that other is a means and channel of the blessing. As for anger against His enemies, it is not exclusive to Him, for His angels, prophets, messengers and friends also become angry with His anger. So in the expression ﴿those who earn anger﴾ [al-Fatiha: 7], there is, through the agreement of His friends with Him, an indication of His singularity in bestowing favour, and that absolute favour comes from Him alone, He being the sole possessor of it, which is not present in the expression "those upon whom favour is bestowed".
The third aspect: in omitting the agent of anger there is an indication of humiliating the one who earns anger, belittling him and diminishing his station, which is not present in mentioning the agent of favour, which honours the one favoured, proclaims his mention and raises his rank, and which is not present in its omission. If you see someone whom a king has honoured, ennobled and raised in rank, and you say, "This is the one whom the sultan honoured, bestowed a robe upon, and gave what he wished," this is more eloquent in praise and exaltation than saying, "This is the one who was honoured, clothed, ennobled and given."
Reflect upon a wondrous secret in the mention of the cause and the recompense for the three groups, in the briefest and most concise wording. The bestowal of favour upon them includes His bestowal of guidance, which is beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and which is the guidance and the religion of truth, and it includes the perfection of favour through the goodness of reward and recompense. This is the completion of favour, and the expression "You have favoured them" includes both matters.
The mention of His anger upon those who earn it likewise includes two matters: the recompense, through anger, whose consequence is the utmost punishment and abasement; and the cause for which they deserved His anger, glorified is He, for He is too merciful and compassionate to be angry without any offence on their part or error. So being angry at them necessitates their error, and the mention of those who are astray necessitates His anger upon them and His punishment of them, for whoever goes astray deserves the punishment which is the consequence of his error and God's anger upon him.
Thus the description of each of the three groups necessitates the cause and the recompense with the clearest necessity, and demands it in the most complete manner, in the utmost brevity, clarity and eloquence, with mention of the agent in the case of the people of felicity, its omission in the case of the people of anger, and the attribution of the action to the cause in the case of the people of error.

I must translate this passage faithfully, so here it is.

Reflect on the contrast between guidance and blessing, and between anger and misguidance. The mention of "those who have earned anger" and "those who are astray" stands in contrast to "those upon whom You have bestowed favour," who are guided. This is frequent in the Qur'an, which pairs misguidance with wretchedness and guidance with success. The second is like His saying ﴿They are upon guidance from their Lord, and they are the successful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 5], and His saying ﴿For them is security, and they are guided﴾ [al-An'am: 82]. The first is like His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness﴾ [al-Qamar: 47], and His saying ﴿Allah has sealed over their hearts and their hearing, and over their vision is a veil, and for them is a great punishment﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7]. He, glorified is He, has gathered the four matters in His saying ﴿So when there comes to you from Me guidance, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer﴾ [Ta-Ha: 123]. This is guidance and happiness. Then He said ﴿But whoever turns away from My reminder, indeed, for him is a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind while I was [once] seeing?" He will say, "Thus came to you Our verses, but you forgot them; and similarly, this Day, you are forgotten"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 124]. Thus He mentioned misguidance and wretchedness.

Guidance and happiness are mutually entailed, and misguidance and wretchedness are mutually entailed.

[Section: He mentioned the Straight Path in the singular, defined in two ways: by the definite article (al-) and by annexation (iḍāfa).]

He mentioned the Straight Path in the singular, defined in two ways: by the definite article (al-) and by annexation (iḍāfa). This indicates that it is specific and exclusive, and that it is one path. As for the ways of those who earned anger and of those who are astray, He, glorified is He, gathers them and makes them plural, as in His saying ﴿And that this is My path, [being] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way﴾ [al-An'am: 153]. He made the word "path" singular and "His way" singular, and He made the deviant ways plural.

Ibn Mas'ud said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew a line for us and said, "This is the way of Allah." Then he drew lines to its right and to its left and said, "These are ways; upon each way is a devil calling to it." Then he recited His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And that this is My path, [being] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way. That has He instructed you, that you may fear Him﴾ [al-An'am: 153].

This is because the path that leads to Allah is one: it is what He sent His messengers with and what He revealed His books with. No one reaches Him except by this path, even if people come from every direction and seek to open every door. The roads are blocked for them, and the doors are closed to them, except this one path, for it is connected to Allah and leads to Allah. Allah, exalted is He, said ﴿This is a path upon Me, [being] straight﴾ [al-Hijr: 41]. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is "a path leading to Me, straight." This may carry two meanings: that it is of the kind of substituting particles for one another, so that the particle "ʿalā" (upon) stands in for "ilā" (to); and second, that he intended an interpretation according to the meaning, which is closer to the method of the early predecessors (salaf): i.e., a path that connects to Me. Mujahid said: the truth returns to Allah, and upon Him is its path; it does not turn aside to anything. This is like the saying of al-Hasan but clearer than it, and it is among the most sound of what has been said regarding the verse. It has also been said that ʿalayya (upon Me) here expresses obligation, i.e., upon Me is its clarification, its explanation, and its indication. The two opinions are analogous to the two opinions in the verse of al-Nahl, which is ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾ [al-Nahl: 9]. The correct view there is like the correct view in the verse of al-Hijr: that the direct way, which is the straight and balanced path, returns to Allah and leads to Him. Tufayl al-Ghanawi said:

They passed away as predecessors; the direction of the way was upon them, and the turning of fates overturns men.

I.e., our passage is over them, and our arrival is to them. Another said:

Then they are deaths; whatever valley I have travelled, my way is upon them, or upon me is their way.

If it is said: if this meaning were intended, the more fitting would be the particle "ilā" (to), which denotes arrival, not "ʿalā" (upon), which denotes obligation. Do you not see that when He intended arrival He said ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return. Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 25–26]? He said ﴿To Us is their return﴾ [Yunus: 70] and ﴿Then to their Lord is their return﴾ [al-An'am: 108]. And when He intended obligation He said ﴿Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 26], and ﴿Indeed, upon Us is its gathering and its recitation﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 17], and ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾ [Hud: 6], and similar examples.

It has been said: in the particle "ʿalā" there is a subtle secret, which is the indication that the one traveling this path is upon guidance, and that it is the truth, as He said regarding the believers ﴿They are upon guidance from their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 5], and He said to His Messenger ﷺ ﴿So rely upon Allah; indeed, you are upon the manifest truth﴾ [al-Naml: 79]. Allah, mighty and majestic is He, is the Truth, His path is true, and His religion is true. Whoever is upright upon His path is upon the truth and guidance. Thus, in the particle "ʿalā," in this sense, there is something that is not in the particle "ilā," so reflect on it, for it is a wondrous secret.

If you say: what is the benefit of mentioning "ʿalā" in this too? And how can the believer be "elevated" above the truth and guidance?

I say: because in it is his elevation and exaltation through the truth and guidance, together with his steadfastness upon it and his uprightness toward it. So the use of the particle "ʿalā" indicates its height, its firmness, and its straightness. This is in contrast to misguidance and doubt, for with these is used the particle "fī" (in), which indicates the immersion of its possessor, his being sunk into it and concealed within it, as in His saying ﴿So they are in their doubt, wavering﴾ [al-Tawbah: 45], and His saying ﴿And those who denied Our verses are deaf and dumb in darknesses﴾ [al-An'am: 39], and His saying ﴿So leave them in their confusion until a time﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 54], and His saying ﴿And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it﴾ [Hud: 110].

Reflect on His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And indeed, either we or you are upon guidance or in clear error﴾ [Saba': 24]. For the path of truth takes its traveller upward, in elevation, to the Most High, the Great; and the path of error takes him downward, falling with its traveller to the lowest of the low.

In His saying, exalted is He, ﴿He said, "This is a path upon Me, [being] straight"﴾ [al-Hijr: 41] there is a third opinion, which is the view of al-Kisa'i: that it is a threat and warning, like His saying ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation﴾ [al-Fajr: 14]. As one says, "Your way is upon me, and your passage is upon me," to one whom you wish to inform that he cannot escape you and cannot outmanoeuvre you. The context rejects this, and it does not suit it for whoever reflects upon it, for He said it in answer to Iblis, who said ﴿I will surely mislead them all, except Your chosen servants among them﴾ [Sad: 82]. So there is no way for me to mislead them, and no path for me over them.

Thus Allah, mighty and majestic is He, established this most completely, and informed that sincerity is a path upon which is straightness. So you have no authority over My servants who are upon this path, for it is a path upon Me. Iblis has no way to this path, nor to hovering around its precinct, for it is guarded and protected by Allah, so the enemy of Allah cannot reach its people.

Let the knowing one reflect on this point with true reflection, and consider this meaning, and weigh it against the other two opinions, to see which is more fitting to the two verses, and closer to the intent of the Qur'an and the sayings of the predecessors.

As for al-Kisa'i's comparison of it to His saying ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation﴾ [al-Fajr: 14], the difference between them in context and in meaning is not hidden, so reflect on it. And one does not say in a threat, "This is a straight path upon me," to one who does not travel it, and the way of the one threatened is not straight; he is not threatened by the straight path of Allah, and his way upon which he is is not straight upon Allah. So this opinion does not stand at all.

As for the one who interpreted it as obligation, i.e., upon Me is the explanation of its straightness and the indication of it, the meaning is sound. But whether this is what is intended by the verse is open to question, because it is a deletion in a place where there is no indicator, and the deleted element mentioned is not one that is composed to be understood when deleted. This is unlike the adverbial governor when it occurs as a qualifier, for that is a familiar and known deletion, to the point that it is never mentioned at all. When you say, "He has a dirham upon me" (lahu dirham ʿalayya), the deletion is known and familiar. But if you intended, "upon me is its payment," or "upon me is its weight and safekeeping," and similar things, and you deleted them, it would not be permissible. This is like "upon me is its clarification," which is assumed in the verse; yet what the predecessors said is more fitting to the context, and is the greater and more magnificent of the two meanings.

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Taqi al-Din Ahmad ibn Taymiyya, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "These two are analogous to His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance, and indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life]﴾ [al-Layl: 12–13]." He said: "These are three places in the Qur'an with this meaning."

I say: Most of the exegetes did not mention in the surah "By the night when it covers" [al-Layl: 1] except the meaning of obligation, i.e., upon Us is the clarification of guidance from misguidance. Some of them did not mention in the surah al-Nahl except this meaning, like al-Baghawi. He mentioned the three opinions in al-Hijr. Al-Wahidi, in his al-Basit, mentioned the two meanings in the surah al-Nahl. Our Shaykh chose the view of Mujahid and al-Hasan in the three surahs.

[Section: The Straight Path is the Path of Allah]

The Straight Path is the Path of Allah. It informs that the path is upon Him, glorified is He, as we have mentioned. It also informs that He, glorified is He, is upon the Straight Path, and this is in two places in the Qur'an: in Hud and in al-Nahl. He said in Hud ﴿There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path﴾ [Hud: 56]. And He said in al-Nahl ﴿Allah presents an example: two men, one of whom is mute and unable to do anything, and he is a burden upon his master; wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who orders justice and is upon a straight path?﴾ [al-Nahl: 76].

This is an example that Allah struck for the idols, which do not hear, nor speak, nor reason; they are a burden upon their worshippers. The idol needs its worshipper to carry it, place it, set it up, and serve it. How, then, do they equate it in worship with Allah, who orders justice and monotheism, who is Capable, Speaking, Self-sufficient, and who is upon a straight path in His saying and His doing? His word is truth, right guidance, sincere counsel, and guidance; His action is wisdom, justice, mercy, and benefit. This is the most correct view regarding the verse, and it is the one that many exegetes did not mention other than it. Whoever mentioned another opinion placed it before the others and then related them afterward, as al-Baghawi did, for he affirmed it and made it the explanation of the verse, then said: al-Kalbi said: "He guides you to a straight path."

I say: His guiding us to the path is part of the necessary consequence of His being upon the Straight Path, for His guidance is by His deed and His word, and He is upon the Straight Path in His deeds and His words. So this does not contradict the saying of one who says that He, glorified is He, is upon the Straight Path.

He said: It was also said: it is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who orders justice, and he is upon a straight path.

I say: This is true and does not contradict the first view. Allah is upon the Straight Path, and His Messenger is upon it, for he does not order or do anything except what it requires and entails. On this view, the example is struck for the leader of the disbelievers and their guide, who is the mute idol that cannot provide guidance or good, and for the leader of the righteous, who is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who orders justice and is upon a straight path.

On the first view, the example is struck for the deity of the disbelievers and the deity of the righteous. The two views are mutually entailed: some of them mentioned this, and some mentioned that, and both are meant by the verse. He said: it was also said: both are for the believer and the disbeliever. This is related by ʿAṭiyya from Ibn ʿAbbas. ʿAṭā' said: the mute one is Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and the one who orders justice is Hamza and ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan and ʿUthman ibn Maz'un.

I say: The verse allows for this, and it does not contradict the two views before it, for Allah is upon a straight path, and His Messenger and the followers of His Messenger are upon it. The opposite of that is the deity of the disbelievers and their guide, and the disbeliever who follows and the one who is followed and worshipped. So some of the predecessors mentioned the highest type, some mentioned the guide, and some mentioned the one who responds and accepts. The verse encompasses all of this, and there are many similar instances in the Qur'an.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 1, verse 7 (part 3 of 8):

As for the verse of Hud: it is explicit and admits of only one meaning, namely that Allah, glorified is He, is upon a straight path (ṣirāṭ mustaqīm), and He, glorified is He, is the most worthy of anyone who is upon a straight path. For His words are all truth, guidance, rightness, justice and wisdom: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am: 115]. His acts are all benefit, wisdom, mercy, justice and good. Evil therefore does not enter into the acts or the words of one who is upon the straight path; it enters only into the acts and words of one who has departed from it.

In his supplication, peace be upon him (ﷺ), he said: "Here I am at Your service, and I am happy to serve You; all good is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You." Nor should one heed the interpretation of those who explained it as: "Evil is not drawn near to You" or "does not ascend to You." The meaning is far greater than that, more exalted and of greater worth. For He, whose names are all beautiful, whose attributes are all perfection, whose acts are all perfection, and whose words are all truth and justice, it is impossible for evil to enter into His names or His attributes, or His acts or His words. So correlate this meaning with His words: ﴿Indeed my Lord is upon a straight path﴾ [Hud: 56]. And reflect how He mentioned this directly after His words: ﴿Indeed I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord﴾ [Hud: 56], meaning: He is my Lord, so He will not neglect me or abandon me; and He is your Lord, so He will not give you power over me or enable you against me, for your forelocks are in His hand. You do nothing without His will, for the forelock of every creature is in His hand; it cannot move except by His permission. He is the one who disposes of it. Yet in His disposing of it and moving it, and in the execution of His decree and destiny concerning it, He is upon a straight path; He does not do what He does of that except with wisdom, justice and benefit. Even if He were to give you power over me, He has in that such wisdom that He deserves praise for it, because it is the empowerment of one who is upon a straight path, who does not wrong and does not do anything in vain without wisdom.

Thus is the knowledge of Allah; not the knowledge of the Qadariyya of the Magians, nor the Jabriyya who deny wisdom, benefit and causation. And Allah is the Granter of success, glorified is He.

[Section: The companions of the seeker of the straight path are those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour]

Since the seeker of the straight path seeks something from which most people turn away, wishing to travel a road whose companions are in the utmost scarcity and honour, and since souls are disposed to the loneliness of being alone and to comfort in companionship, Allah, glorified is He, drew attention to the companion on this path, and that they are those ﴿upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous; and excellent are those as companions﴾ [al-Nisa': 69].
